layers.title: 01 · Human and host surfaces
layers.description: Requests enter through an AI host, VS Code, CLI or MCP. The host owns execution authority; dashboards project operational state.

layers.title: 02 · Workspace and coordination
layers.description: Project identity, activation leases, task claims and handoffs establish who may act on which project.

layers.title: 03 · Discovery and planning
layers.description: Metadata discovery, repository context, capability routing and model selection create bounded plans before activation.

layers.title: 04 · Authority and admission
layers.description: Independent gates bind effects, policy, identity, evidence and lifecycle. A plan, observed action and approved effect are different objects.

layers.title: 05 · Execution and scheduling
layers.description: Separate runtimes execute admitted handlers, agent sessions and typed workflow DAGs. Scheduling and resource controls constrain concurrency.

layers.title: 06 · Memory and canonical knowledge
layers.description: Project memory, structured semantics and canonical knowledge have distinct persistence and promotion paths. Derived indexes do not become truth.

layers.title: 07 · Intake and capability construction
layers.description: External metadata, research mechanisms, verified process records and source documents become bounded candidate artifacts.

layers.title: 08 · Reasoning and adaptation
layers.description: Deterministic reasoning, metacognitive proposals and a governed learning state machine support change without automatic self-authorization.

layers.title: 09 · Observation and assurance
layers.description: Operation streams, evidence assembly, trusted verification and explicit control denominators support claims at different strengths.

layers.title: 10 · Persistence and recovery
layers.description: Locks, write-ahead transactions, lifecycle reconciliation and dependency invalidation preserve authoritative state and reject stale projections.

layers.title: 11 · Delivery and operational proof
layers.description: Ordered repair and release campaigns bind source, tests, package bytes, installed behavior and signed certification.

flows.title: Work from request to verified outcome
flows.description: The bounded single-capability path validates registry and inputs, checks authority, activates one handler, assembles support and evaluates postconditions. Each stage records a checkpoint.

flows.title: Agent planning and actual execution
flows.description: Routing and repository/model context form a plan. Agent admission and preview validate tool/context/authority bindings. Host runs and owned harnesses complete through their respective receipt paths.
flows.limit: Planning and execution have explicit handoffs. Host model, owned deterministic harness and Python provider gateway are different routes; a node being on this map does not prove it is always invoked.

flows.title: Typed workflow execution and recovery
flows.description: A workflow revision is saved, validated/admitted and dry-run. Ready nodes run in bounded conflict-free batches; typed outputs enable branches. Approval, timeout, retry and lifecycle controls produce durable run state.
flows.limit: Diagram is a narrative order, not a claim of one linear function chain. Adapter branches and resource cleanup are parallel responsibilities.

flows.title: Project memory from capture to future context
flows.description: A project-bound capture becomes a candidate record. Lifecycle admission and source/ACL checks determine retrieval eligibility. Structured keys and bounded ranking/materialization select later context.
flows.limit: Index generation and canonical record admission are distinct. The materialization broker consumes supplied records; it does not require an ANN backend.

flows.title: Verified work becomes a process candidate
flows.description: A caller writes an engineering-process record with verified outcomes and recoveries. The process compiler emits inert procedure/decision/tool/execution artifacts, which need separate skill construction/admission before future selection.
flows.limit: The process-record capture/mining and process-candidate-to-Studio adapter are explicit handoff gaps, not proven automatic steps.

flows.title: External knowledge becomes a reusable skill
flows.description: Research and refinery stages offer candidate inputs. Foundry can emit candidate files and export a selected skill to a typed Studio draft object. Physical package conversion, source admission and normal stage_draft remain a separate caller handoff before testing/admission/promotion.
flows.limit: No automatic research-to-refinery-to-Studio pipeline is established. Intake returns an object without saving a draft; calculation-containing export has a producer/consumer field mismatch.

flows.title: Learning changes canonical authority
flows.description: Explicit observations form a signed learning pipeline. Frozen candidates pass statistical comparison, research and final validation, then a separate knowledge proposal verification/approval/promotion. Measured reuse can make a canonical head suspect and invalidate declared dependents.
flows.limit: Metrics and trials are submitted by callers. There is no established automatic bus-to-learning trigger or autonomous experiment execution. This is a real governed state-change loop.

flows.title: Cross-domain principle transfer
flows.description: Mechanisms expose inputs, outputs, invariants, assumptions and limitations. Structural analogy and signature-based theory induction propose transferable patterns; target-domain held-out and boundary evidence must justify reuse.
flows.limit: Proposal construction exists. A fully automated new-algorithm implementation and deployment pipeline is not proven. Multiple research sources do not establish causal validity by themselves.

flows.title: Change propagates into invalidated proof

flows.limit: Propagation coverage depends on the registered graph. This report computes no product revision refresh and runs no release gates.

flows.title: Release bytes become an operational claim

flows.title: Choose what to reason about and test

flows.limit: Strategy output does not execute the kernels; value-of-information output does not launch trials. These are composable operations with caller-owned sequencing.

flows.title: Observe engineering patterns and propose evolution

flows.limit: Current workflow ID/version is not compared to captured pending identity; backend must reject misplaced approval use.

flows.title: Operational walk evidence through repeated status evaluation
flows.description: Walker computes receipt with profile issues; isolated child compares process exit and recomputes; outer launcher derives final status from issue list and closure.
flows.limit: Profile errors can be lost, string helper failures discarded, and scoped completion promoted in nested launcher flag; top-level focused flag separately remains false.

flows.title: Owned host startup and partial finalization
flows.description: Acquire lease, stage current source/fixtures, start isolated host and optional native helper/walker, reconcile handles, evaluate receipt, remove owned root and publish final report.
flows.limit: Path and snapshot intervals, sequential finalizer errors and cleanup-before-publication remain explicit; this audit does not execute these effects.

flows.title: Focused refusal and full coverage accounting
flows.description: Select full or focused predicates, account accepted refusal boundaries separately, normalize issues then calculate terminal status.
flows.limit: Some contracts accept flag-only or empty-chain evidence; an accepted refusal is not execution of the withheld effect.

flows.title: Contained exhaustive control evidence
flows.description: Sample sources, reuse/select records, prepare fixtures, locate and exercise, interpret stages, aggregate and exclusively publish.
flows.limit: Preview scope, weak resume identity, local validation proxies and missing final source equality limit operational claims.

flows.title: Contained form failure and restoration
flows.description: Find first editable field, change/restore, inject and clear custom validity, classify local stages.
flows.limit: DOM field restoration and injected browser validity do not prove product validation or model rollback.

flows.title: Dashboard preview test and screenshot custody
flows.description: Exercise synthetic request/draft boundaries and selected layouts before publishing hashes of screenshot directory.
flows.limit: This is declared test behavior, not a test run; manifest may retain older images and has no source binding.

flows.title: Installed walk admission and profile order
flows.description: Launch child, sample identity, run selected dependent profiles and publish results.
flows.limit: Source verification is not a universal effect gate; timeout is not cancellation; output precedes closure.

flows.title: Installed evidence composition and parent status
flows.description: Builder and profile observations merge into stage records, then child and parent classify status.
flows.limit: Cross-scenario stage union and lost errors can strengthen claims beyond any successful scenario.

flows.title: Native action request and host observation
flows.description: Prepare scenario, observe request, locate or fall back to native input, then await result.
flows.limit: Request type fallback, physical focus and exact effect outcome require distinct proofs.

flows.title: Studio candidate revision and lifecycle evidence
flows.description: Create candidates, edit predecessor-bound revisions, execute lifecycle, combine late-card checks.
flows.limit: Partial content comparison, operation-only result matching and historical closure denominator limit certification.

flows.title: Learning fixture to canonical knowledge
flows.description: Submit declared trials and research reference, admit learning, promote Knowledge proposal and attribute controls.
flows.limit: This demonstrates state transitions, not independently measured learning improvement.

flows.title: Graph and sidebar reconstruction evidence
flows.description: Compare map and selected graph metadata, reconstruct snapshots/preferences and classify faults.
flows.limit: Weighted graph content and latest-state identity are not fully represented by these equality predicates.

flows.title: Owned plugin mutation and recovery boundary
flows.description: Confirm exact preview then use native lifecycle and workbench reconstruction before recovery.
flows.limit: Pending result/version equality does not prove terminal custody; failure cleanup lacks created-this-run ownership.

flows.title: Fixture reclamation and certification order
flows.description: Validation/refusal and cleanup profiles contribute evidence before final publication.
flows.limit: Fixture ownership and exact campaign sequence must be enforced; graph audit performed no such effects.

flows.title: Generated MCP transport to PX effect
flows.description: Launch bundle, frame messages, negotiate protocol, validate input, supply context and invoke authorized PX handler.
flows.limit: Context is lost at wrapper; wire cancellation and schema validity do not imply effect cancellation or domain result correctness.

flows.title: Generated dependency and asset identity
flows.description: Inventory artifact origins, compare copied source syntax, interpret generated runtime and relative assets.
flows.limit: No rebuild or installed-byte certification; preserved syntax can still change __dirname behavior.

flows.title: MCP connection and subscription closure
flows.description: Close subscription records, application instance and wire through the serving handle.
flows.limit: PX does not retain that handle; output drain and cooperative abort do not prove product work reconciliation.

findings.title: Workflow declarations and runtime execution differ
findings.body: workflow_execution_bindings explicitly distinguishes executable_runtime and executable_validator. graph_registry nevertheless emits executes edges from listed project-stream skills. execute_project_stream invokes the registered workflow handler, not each listed skill body. Treat those generated executes edges as declared composition unless the handler proves invocation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D01 Workflow declarations and runtime execution differ.md

findings.title: The original bounded orchestrator has a narrower effect path
findings.body: Orchestrator.run calls enforce without effect_grant_path, signature, trust policy or project/session bindings. enforce requires these for NON_READ_EFFECTS. Consequently this entrypoint cannot establish those non-read executions as written. Agent/Workflow Studio have separate authority paths; this does not mean all PX mutation is blocked.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D02 The original bounded orchestrator has a narrower effect path.md

findings.title: Verification strength depends on the entrypoint
findings.body: Orchestrator imports verify, which is a compatibility alias to evaluate_claims. verify_authoritative instead resolves signed policy and postcondition records against a scope and approved producers. These mechanisms should not be collapsed into one trust level.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D03 Verification strength depends on the entrypoint.md

findings.title: Learning is operationally meaningful but deliberately mediated
findings.body: The signed learning controller has concrete transitions, frozen revisions, statistical comparisons, research/final gates and a linked knowledge proposal. admit_learning_candidate records canonical_writes_performed=false. Separate knowledge verification, approval and promotion are required before reuse measurement can affect canonical authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D04 Learning is operationally meaningful but deliberately mediated.md

findings.title: Decay changes future access, with bounded propagation
findings.body: Measured reuse can write authority_status=suspect and require revalidation. resolve_canonical refuses authoritative access in that state. If no dependency graph is supplied, measure_learning_reuse creates only the knowledge node with no edges: broad downstream invalidation is not established by the default path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D05 Decay changes future access, with bounded propagation.md

findings.title: Saved memory notes describe an earlier architecture
findings.body: An earlier repository-local memory architecture note reported missing typed ontology. Current semantic_memory defines structured payloads, entities, typed relations, namespaces and exact query signals, and MemoryVault projects them into index generations. The report uses current implementation rather than inheriting the earlier gap claim. No private reference content was imported.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D06 Saved memory notes describe an earlier architecture.md

findings.title: Canonical memory and canonical knowledge are separate stores
findings.body: MemoryVault controls project record revisions, lifecycle eligibility and retrieval. KnowledgeCoreController controls signed proposals and canonical knowledge heads. No universally enforced automatic mapping between their identities or lifecycles was established in this inspection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D07 Canonical memory and canonical knowledge are separate stores.md

findings.title: Foundry and cross-domain reasoning have concrete limits
findings.body: Foundry extracts lines/headings/list items and chooses fixed capability templates by term hits. Structural analogy scores supplied mechanism/relationship records, while theory induction groups shared signatures. These are useful deterministic candidate-making operations; arbitrary source understanding, invention and target implementation require additional work.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D08 Foundry and cross-domain reasoning have concrete limits.md

findings.title: Several plausible self-improvement loops lack automatic wiring
findings.body: No automatic driver was established for event-bus-to-learning capture, repeated-run-to-process-record mining, research-method self-rewriting, theory-to-learning payload conversion, canonical knowledge-to-skill implementation, or new capabilities automatically opening research priorities. Those are unresolved caller-mediated boundaries and are excluded from confirmed closed-loop claims.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D09 Several plausible self-improvement loops lack automatic wiring.md

findings.title: Local release prose differs from the current user report
findings.body: README still says v0.7.0 certification/publication are pending and START_HERE defaults to v0.6.3. The user reports Marketplace publication and verification on 2026-09-08. Record this as local-documentation versus user-report discrepancy; Marketplace state was not independently queried.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D10 Local release prose differs from the current user report.md

findings.title: Operational completion is stronger than output presence
findings.body: Project-stream completion checks whether required named outputs exist after the handler and checks elapsed time/lease validity. Signed postcondition verification and installed interaction-denominator evidence are separate mechanisms. A completed stream result should retain its actual evidence scope.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D11 Operational completion is stronger than output presence.md

findings.title: The graph family is an interpretation with auditable boundaries
findings.body: Layers group responsibilities analytically; they are not claimed to be declared deployable services. Every node and edge carries source anchors. Direct means source-level behavior, not a fresh runtime test. Handoff/inferred edges remain visibly distinct. The large catalog inventory is navigation coverage, not proof that every capability was semantically audited.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D12 The graph family is an interpretation with auditable boundaries.md

findings.title: Model execution has two materially different paths
findings.body: Python execute_agent_plan reserves placement capacity and calls supplied GPU/CPU functions; it does not call ProviderInvocationGateway. Agent Studio can instead prepare a VS Code-host model request and validate the returned model/options/token evidence. The host can expose a local Ollama provider. These paths are shown separately; no universal gateway funnel is claimed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D13 Model execution has two materially different paths.md

findings.title: Skill promotion propagates both availability and staleness
findings.body: Skill Studio updates canonical bytes and catalog/index/admission projections in its lifecycle transaction. Cheap semantic metadata is rebuilt from the unpublished after-tree; heavier projections are listed in stale_blocked with a block-until-rebuild policy. Pass 8 narrows the earlier enforcement claim: the world-state reader expects another shape, and the dashboard capability graph reader does not consult this marker. Newly selectable skill metadata and an explicitly stale graph obligation can coexist; universal consumer blocking is not established.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D14 Skill promotion propagates both availability and staleness.md

findings.title: Reasoning recursion and operational learning are different loops
findings.body: Strategy selection recursively orders declared mode dependencies; logic and belief projection iterate to bounded fixed points. Those computational loops do not themselves alter installed capabilities. Capability mutation, practice transfer and optimization produce candidate reports. The signed Learning and Knowledge controllers own the separate persistence boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D15 Reasoning recursion and operational learning are different loops.md

findings.title: The independent panel evaluates artifacts rather than launching agents
findings.body: The panel consumes isolated branch records, flags evidence shared by every branch and reports weighted agreement plus dissent. It always reports rounds_used=1 and authority_granted=False. The max_rounds argument does not establish repeated critique, agent isolation execution or independent source acquisition.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D16 The independent panel evaluates artifacts rather than launching agents.md

findings.title: Analytical uncertainty must survive the handoff
findings.body: Constraint search reports exhaustion and truncation; causal analysis tests a supplied DAG, not its truth; robust decisions depend on caller intervals; belief confidence is explicitly heuristic. A caller that discards these caveats would strengthen conclusions beyond the source contract.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D17 Analytical uncertainty must survive the handoff.md

findings.title: Observed-effects fields have different evidence strength
findings.body: RuntimeLifecycle.run_verified_tool copies declared_effects into observed_effects after a successful callback. That receipt records wrapper-level attribution, not independent OS measurement. Separate operational observers exist. A graph reader must follow the producing path before using an observation field as proof of the actual effect.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D18 Observed-effects fields have different evidence strength.md

findings.title: Canonical and certified are scoped terms
findings.body: Transcript canonical records mean schema-conformant extraction records; Memory Vault admission, signed Knowledge Core heads and Skill Studio canonical bytes each have different owners. Skeptical assurance certified is a metadata-based policy result; a release certificate has separate artifact and operational requirements. Reusing the words across these boundaries would hide material differences.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D19 Canonical and certified are scoped terms.md

findings.title: Declared script names can map to generic behavior
findings.body: The declared suite plans registered procedures, but script execution chooses a handler by tokens in outcome_id. Map names inventory files, rank names rank supplied values, and unmatched names normalize a record. A detailed domain name does not establish a dedicated domain algorithm or execution of every planned step.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D20 Declared script names can map to generic behavior.md

findings.title: Canonical persistence and graph success are deliberately separable
findings.body: persist_with_graph_isolation writes the vault before invoking the graph callback. A failed derived write leaves canonical_persisted=True and requires reconciliation. StateKVGuard bounds the wait and opens a circuit on failures; canceling a Future does not demonstrate that a running callback has ceased effects.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D21 Canonical persistence and graph success are deliberately separable.md

findings.title: A planned lifecycle step is not evidence of its application
findings.body: Memory remediation may mark individual steps apply=true while explicitly returning mutated=False. Durable-goal transitions return state objects without disk writes. Candidate compilation in operational_controls selects record IDs. These are useful decision contracts, but they must remain separate from executors and persistent transition owners.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D22 A planned lifecycle step is not evidence of its application.md

findings.title: Startup and surface health use different projections
findings.body: World state aggregates bounded metadata into GREEN, STALE or BLOCKED and asks for selected hydration. Missing source authority makes startup UNVERIFIED. The registered health evaluator separately derives healthy/degraded/stale/blocked/unknown from lifecycle facts, TTLs and failures. Their states require context rather than direct string equivalence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D23 Startup and surface health use different projections.md

findings.title: The workflow scheduler is richer than its standalone adapter set
findings.body: Workflow Studio has scheduling, branches, approval, joins, retries and typed outputs. The inspected workflow_worker currently executes identity, increment, double, fail and sleep. It rechecks signed task/executor/grant bindings and runs declarative validation checks. Broad catalog composition is therefore not evidence that arbitrary skills execute through this worker.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D24 The workflow scheduler is richer than its standalone adapter set.md

findings.title: A deeper caller sweep found the actual hybrid-retrieval adapter
findings.body: The first runtime-only sweep missed the portable CLI under .px/skills. That adapter imports the source or installed canonical retrieval owner, constructs typed corpus records and calls retrieve. The atlas now links this concrete path and removes the speculative recall-to-generic-kernel connection. No universal Agent Studio or canonical-memory adapter follows from this discovery.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D25 A deeper caller sweep found the actual hybrid-retrieval adapter.md

findings.title: Automatic operation exists where an actual driver is present
findings.body: CanonicalMemoryLeaseController explicitly starts a timer, bounds intervals and coalesces renewals. Durable Studio terminal observation checks worker exit before finalization. These have concrete drivers. By comparison, the inspected learning API accepts externally prepared observations/trials/metrics; no equivalent automatic acquisition-and-promotion driver was found in the scoped caller sweep.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D26 Automatic operation exists where an actual driver is present.md

findings.title: Owner registries and runtime reachability answer different questions
findings.body: Primitive/effect registries validate which owner is canonical. A caller search locates whether and where an operation is actually invoked. Tests establish assertions in source, while exact installed operational receipts establish exercised behavior. The atlas retains these evidence levels instead of treating one as a substitute for all the others.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D27 Owner registries and runtime reachability answer different questions.md

findings.title: The Studio reuse route does not forward the dependency graph
findings.body: measure_learning_reuse accepts dependency_graph and dependency_current_revisions, and direct-controller tests demonstrate downstream projection and release-evidence invalidation. The Studio measure-reuse branch forwards counts and approval only. Consequently its current route uses the singleton fallback; a general propagation claim requires a different caller or an adapter change.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D28 The Studio reuse route does not forward the dependency graph.md

findings.title: Authority restoration exists but has a narrower proof contract
findings.body: revalidate_learning requires a decayed pipeline, explicit approval, a nonempty evidence reference, a 64-hex hash and the expected suspect canonical identity. It updates the pipeline and then the signed head, retaining dependent_rebuild_required. It does not resolve those supplied evidence bytes in this method. The inspected Studio dispatch exposes no restoration operation, so this is a controller-level path with source-test evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D29 Authority restoration exists but has a narrower proof contract.md

findings.title: Theory proposal requirements exceed the fields checked by its validator
findings.body: Induction advertises distinctness, held-out generalization, failure boundary and operational value as required evidence. validate_proposal currently computes the pass rate from supplied held-out passed flags and checks truthy distinctness evidence. It does not explicitly validate failure-boundary or operational-value fields, execute held-out cases, or promote a theory.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D30 Theory proposal requirements exceed the fields checked by its validator.md

findings.title: The deterministic harness does not execute a natural-language objective
findings.body: agent_harness_worker authenticates the task and runs the explicit sha256, json-keys or bounded-delay tool calls. Its result states model_invoked=False and records whether an objective was received plus its hash. The host-model path is where language-model invocation occurs. Treating these as one agent execution capability would conceal a substantial runtime boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D31 The deterministic harness does not execute a natural-language objective.md

findings.title: Host instructions are an operational connection the earlier map understated
findings.body: Active native procedures explicitly prescribe research extraction, foundry compilation and novelty review. The absence of a Python driver is therefore insufficient to call the whole connection missing. These are now explicit instruction-mediated handoffs: source proves a procedure exists, while actual host compliance, effects and promotion require their own evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D32 Host instructions are an operational connection the earlier map understated.md

findings.title: A deferred wrapper is not an active learning engine
findings.body: adapt-human-learning-loop has status mapped_deferred and inactive_external_candidate_wrapper provenance despite a current validation_freshness field and rich capability tags. research-to-capability and forge-skills-from-knowledge have active package records. Preserve status, source type and selection boundary rather than inferring behavior from names.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D33 A deferred wrapper is not an active learning engine.md

findings.title: Coordination has concrete state transitions but completion remains caller reported
findings.body: MCP handlers directly create a DAG, claim scopes, renew leases, record usage/progress and reconcile completed tasks. Progress can mark budget-exceeded work blocked. Reconciliation records supplied evidence and conflicts_resolved and releases claims; it does not itself merge code, run acceptance tests or terminate a worker.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D34 Coordination has concrete state transitions but completion remains caller reported.md

findings.title: Studio commit and UI delivery are separate result boundaries
findings.body: The host rechecks version allocation and source identity before saving. After the backend call, it validates the commit receipt. Invalid receipt yields commit-outcome-unverified; valid commit plus failed cleanup, refresh or notification yields warnings while preserving committed identity. This is more precise than treating a dashboard error as proof that saving failed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D35 Studio commit and UI delivery are separate result boundaries.md

findings.title: Semantic selection has several distinct contracts
findings.body: The cheap semantic index builds profiles and descriptions, while navigate computes weighted lexical evidence and an exact-alias boost. Independent discovery allows candidate metadata; later routing makes active/admitted and policy-filtered items selectable. Working-set dependency recursion rolls back a bundle when it cannot fit. These operations rank and explain metadata; they do not invoke a model or prove task feasibility.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D36 Semantic selection has several distinct contracts.md

findings.title: Persistence guarantees belong to specific publication units
findings.body: Coordination withState publishes deferred files, state, event, receipt and handoff in order. The protected Python ledger publishes event bytes before its head; validation detects head/chain disagreement. Studio directory publication uses a no-replace atomic primitive. These are different guarantees: neither a file lock nor a hash chain makes every related file a single atomic transaction. This is source reasoning about interruption boundaries, not a reproduced crash result.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D37 Persistence guarantees belong to specific publication units.md

findings.title: Task fencing and budget checks need their caller contract
findings.body: Progress checks the owner and active lease, then validates the fencing-token entries supplied by the caller. It accumulates caller-reported usage and marks over-budget work blocked. The inspected tests prove source assertions about stale supplied tokens and blocked state; neither the function nor those assertions establish mandatory complete token submission or worker termination.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D38 Task fencing and budget checks need their caller contract.md

findings.title: Static coverage labels do not establish all runtime effects
findings.body: The source coverage validator checks control labels, available owner/contract/test files and eligible skill statuses. The effect scanner recognizes selected Python AST call spellings and checks a stored inventory. These complement execution evidence; they do not observe JavaScript MCP mutations, arbitrary aliases or the truth of every operational label.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D39 Static coverage labels do not establish all runtime effects.md

findings.title: Generated authority cycles are different from adaptive feedback loops
findings.body: Generated input declarations must be acyclic. Artifact reachability deliberately excludes live evidence/completion/world-state/gap-head projections and engine identity to avoid self-invalidating digest cycles, while retaining independent owners. Runtime learning and control feedback can legitimately be cyclic; applying one graph rule to both would misrepresent the architecture.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D40 Generated authority cycles are different from adaptive feedback loops.md

findings.title: Inspected test assertions corroborate the new host boundaries
findings.body: Coordination tests cover overlap ordering, explicit reconciliation, stale supplied fencing tokens and budget-blocked state. Studio host tests assert that failed post-commit delivery/refresh preserve a created-with-delivery-warning outcome. These are existing test-source assertions; this report does not claim they were freshly executed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D41 Inspected test assertions corroborate the new host boundaries.md

findings.title: Procedural memory naming does not close the process-mining gap
findings.body: The active memory-fabric procedure prescribes explicit capture, lifecycle and retrieval commands. The package named procedural-memory-compiler is mapped_deferred. Its existence cannot establish an active automatic producer for runtime.process_memory records. Host-mediated governance explains operational composition while this specific automation/adapter question remains open. Pass 8 found the separate active trace-to-skill-compiler package, which prescribes host normalization and CLI compilation. Thus a documented capture procedure exists; the remaining gap concerns automation and executable-package construction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D42 Procedural memory naming does not close the process-mining gap.md

findings.title: An active trace procedure closes part of the process-capture explanation
findings.body: trace-to-skill-compiler is active and directs the host to normalize successful and failed traces into the engineering-process schema and call process compile. The earlier review emphasized the differently named mapped-deferred procedural-memory-compiler. That was incomplete: a documented host producer exists. Automatic repeated-run mining, host compliance and the downstream executable package adapter remain separate questions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D43 An active trace procedure closes part of the process-capture explanation.md

findings.title: Process compilation trusts submitted verification and emits a linear execution graph
findings.body: The schema requires an outcome_met boolean, nonempty check/evidence string lists and failure verified booleans. The compiler checks those flags but does not resolve evidence bytes or run checks. decision_graph and tool_graph preserve supplied entries; execution_graph assigns each step only its preceding step as a dependency. Branch discovery and an emitted tested SKILL package are not implemented by this function, despite the richer procedural goals.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D44 Process compilation trusts submitted verification and emits a linear execution graph.md

findings.title: Two generated graph APIs use incompatible edge keys
findings.body: generated_dependency_graph emits source/target edges. adapt_generated_dependency_graph reads only from/to, silently skipping records without both keys; its test explicitly supplies from/to. Directly composing these two APIs would therefore produce no adapted edges or nodes. This is a source-derived contract counterexample, not a claim that a production caller currently makes that direct call.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D45 Two generated graph APIs use incompatible edge keys.md

findings.title: Studio staleness does not match the world-state reader shape
findings.body: Skill promotion writes schema px.skill-promotion-projection-staleness/1.0 with stale_blocked. build_world_state reads projections entries whose stale flag is True. With only the Studio shape, it derives no stale projection IDs and the projections component becomes GREEN. Overall health can still be BLOCKED for ledger reasons. No automatic format bridge was located in the bounded caller sweep.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D46 Studio staleness does not match the world-state reader shape.md

findings.title: A rebuild policy marker is weaker than a consumer gate
findings.body: plan_projection_rebuild classifies work and does not invoke builders. The dashboard capability-graph branch directly reads cognitive_map_index and does not consult projection_staleness. The inspected test named expensive_skill_projection_staleness_is_explicitly_blocking only asserts a constructed dictionary contains the list and policy string. Independent builder equality checks exist during reconciliation, but they do not establish that every graph read is blocked.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D47 A rebuild policy marker is weaker than a consumer gate.md

findings.title: Lifecycle process completion is a metadata presence check
findings.body: record_process_candidate optionally writes a process receipt and appends its relative path to evidence.process_records. lifecycle_status marks process-capture complete from bool(process_records). It does not resolve those receipt bytes in that stage check. Verification-stage checks also distinguish a few sentinel statuses rather than independently rerunning verification. This metadata router must not be treated as a release certificate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D48 Lifecycle process completion is a metadata presence check.md

findings.title: Canonical knowledge has a real browsing consumer
findings.body: KnowledgeCoreController.browse reads signed canonical heads and rollback history and projects authority/revalidation flags. That is a concrete consumer even though the exact-name search found no production resolve_canonical caller. Browsing metadata, resolving authoritative revision bytes and injecting content into an agent remain separate consumption paths.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D49 Canonical knowledge has a real browsing consumer.md

findings.title: A valid Doctor report can describe a blocked system
findings.body: compose_doctor_report requires exactly eight sections and valid states/remediation links, then selects blocked before degraded before healthy. It sets valid=True for the report, operable unless blocked, and ready/certification_ready only when healthy. The inspected tests assert these differences. Those flags belong to diagnostic composition and do not issue a release certificate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D50 A valid Doctor report can describe a blocked system.md

findings.title: Recovery health is bounded by configured authorities
findings.body: RecoveryCoordinator runs configured WAL/state/callback checks. Missing event/session/resource callback groups may be healthy with configured=False. Doctor passes only its known existing WAL roots and apply=False, and downgrades an absence of discovered WALs to degraded. A healthy reconciliation is not a claim that every possible state owner was examined.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D51 Recovery health is bounded by configured authorities.md

findings.title: Failure root grouping is exact evidence matching rather than causal discovery
findings.body: group_candidate_roots groups identical combined evidence/owner/dependency signatures after enforcing the complete unique failure denominator. Merely overlapping signatures remain separate. The discriminating plan proposes removals/substitutions but does not execute them, and caller-confirmed candidate IDs still grant no repair authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D52 Failure root grouping is exact evidence matching rather than causal discovery.md

findings.title: Studio catalog status can change when current projections drift
findings.body: The catalog status reader verifies current projection bytes against the signed committed lifecycle transaction. The inspected test changes only whitespace in skill-index.json and asserts the revision loses promoted status while its admission remains authenticated and a promotion error is retained. The bridge uses that projection, and the UI falls back to candidate when no authenticated status exists. This is a current-proof dependency, not a reversal of historical publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D53 Studio catalog status can change when current projections drift.md

findings.title: Route classification and observed coverage are different denominators
findings.body: validate_route_registry checks declared tier/mechanism pairings and marks the registry certifiable when valid and no advertised Tier D route remains. Doctor also calls reconcile_operation_coverage with health evidence and freshness before assigning its coverage state. A valid declaration alone does not prove current observer health or that the declared mediator ran.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D54 Route classification and observed coverage are different denominators.md

findings.title: Atomic decision functions need a separate persistent owner
findings.body: reserve_budget and atomic_work_checkout compute new records over caller-supplied snapshots. They contain no lock, durable read/commit or worker effect. These are separate from ProviderBudgetLedger and coordination claim persistence. Two callers can evaluate the same prior snapshot; a real persistence owner must serialize acceptance.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D55 Atomic decision functions need a separate persistent owner.md

findings.title: Dependency additions do not update candidate capability coverage
findings.body: optimize_candidate_package updates covered during greedy selection, then appends admitted dependencies without updating covered. Consequently covered_capabilities describes the greedy selection, not necessarily the union of the final package. For example, a selected candidate satisfying required X can pull in a dependency offering additional Y while the report still lists only X. This is source-derived accounting behavior, not an executed product test or a demonstrated false-incomplete result.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D56 Dependency additions do not update candidate capability coverage.md

findings.title: Offline improvement evidence remains supplied input
findings.body: The offline comparison checks distinct actor/optimizer/judge strings and matched held-out score records, requiring an improvement within the regression allowance. It returns quarantined_candidate and requires_independent_promotion=True. It neither runs the experiment nor verifies the independence of those identities.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D57 Offline improvement evidence remains supplied input.md

findings.title: Completed tasks can still contribute zero sidebar completion
findings.body: Sidebar progress counts only reconciled tasks. completed and verifying map to verifying; approved cancelled/skipped tasks are excluded from the weighted denominator. This is a deliberate projection distinction between output delivery and reconciliation, independent of render acknowledgement.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D58 Completed tasks can still contribute zero sidebar completion.md

findings.title: Workflow trace helper tests and browser code have different owners
findings.body: The CommonJS projectWorkflowTrace helper is imported by its unit test, while the dashboard uses a separate projectWorkflowTraceResult implementation. Both inspect workflow/version/run identity and conflicting hashes, but a helper test is not evidence that the actual browser implementation executed. The atlas now anchors the browser producer/consumer too.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D59 Workflow trace helper tests and browser code have different owners.md

findings.title: MCP runtime verified is invocation-scoped
findings.body: observeMcpRuntime requires registration, integrity-valid activity and one fresh successful invocation matching the exact server version; its default window is 24 hours. It retains the matching operation and event. This is stronger than registered metadata but narrower than all-tools behavioral certification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D60 MCP runtime verified is invocation-scoped.md

findings.title: Cleanup reclaimed counts include retained local quarantine
findings.body: Cleanup can move an unchanged staged tree to local quarantine after recycling fails. The final confirmedResults set includes that state when calculating resources_reclaimed and bytes_reclaimed. Those counters describe disposition of the original cache location, not measured disk-space recovery. Errors with disappearance remain disposition-uncertain.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D61 Cleanup reclaimed counts include retained local quarantine.md

findings.title: Rollback identity custody is not an available rollback artifact
findings.body: Extension uninstall retains the exact prior version before native dispatch. Rollback consumes custody only after that version is observed again; command failure, wrong version or pending reload leaves it retained. When no hash-bound local VSIX exists, actual restoration still depends on an available source accepted by VS Code.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D62 Rollback identity custody is not an available rollback artifact.md

findings.title: Host cache metadata contains more than its read gate checks
findings.body: MetadataCache.set records dependency_fingerprints, but get checks the supplied source fingerprint and maximum age; it does not compare each dependency field. PxBridge separately propagates revisions, clears request caches and incorporates revision fingerprints into some keys. Correct cache use depends on that caller wiring.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D63 Host cache metadata contains more than its read gate checks.md

findings.title: A provider isolation harness performs real provider operations
findings.body: run_provider_isolation_suite invokes a supplied factory twice and executes synthetic writes, reads, searches, prompt-log checks, injected failure and correction. It is not merely metadata scoring, but certification remains bounded to those seven probes and the supplied provider/configuration. This report inspected the implementation without executing the harness.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D64 A provider isolation harness performs real provider operations.md

findings.title: Listener coverage can mean registered rather than exercised
findings.body: markRegistered can mark an available enabled listener healthy with events_recorded still zero. snapshot excludes unsupported required APIs from incomplete and can report coverage_complete when the bus is connected. buildActivityAttestation copies the same supplied effect label into declared and observed. Read this as supported listener registration/publication coverage, with explicit limitations, rather than independent observation of every actual effect.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D65 Listener coverage can mean registered rather than exercised.md

findings.title: Activity cancellation and repair have narrower meanings
findings.body: reconcileStaleOperations emits a cancelled activity record without killing a process. repairActivityIntegrity retains exact pre-repair backups, reconstructs predecessor hashes and reseals parsed records. Its postcondition proves internal consistency of that repaired chain, not original event authenticity. recordActivity appends JSONL before atomic state publication; those two files are not one atomic transaction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D66 Activity cancellation and repair have narrower meanings.md

findings.title: Source coverage labels differ from exact execution evidence
findings.body: certify_python_surfaces source mode accepts supplied exact-tool flags, associates tests textually and can assign generic full-suite-and-installed-integration labels. The function does not thereby resolve fresh passing execution receipts for each surface. certify_exact_tools contains an actual bounded execution harness, with its own fixtures and repeat comparison. Both were inspected, not run here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D67 Source coverage labels differ from exact execution evidence.md

findings.title: Enterprise readiness is a write and billable policy is a decision
findings.body: enterpriseDoctor initializes and mutates enterprise state, appends an event and writes a receipt. Its cloud_connectors_ready remains false. evaluateBillableExecution checks caller-supplied spend, cost, resource and approval values without a persistent reservation in that function. Treat configuration, readiness reporting, authorization and actual billing execution as separate owners.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D68 Enterprise readiness is a write and billable policy is a decision.md

findings.title: Studio staging publication and reclamation are separate contracts
findings.body: materializeSkillPackage registers custody before writing files individually to the target and verifies the complete tree before recording published. Failure retains uncertain resources. Reclamation requires a matching durable draft-create receipt, closed lifecycle record and exact inventory, then checks the moved tree before deleting the owned staging resource. This is distinct from canonical immutable revision publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D69 Studio staging publication and reclamation are separate contracts.md

findings.title: A valid installed index may retain partial observation coverage
findings.body: build_index binds current receipt and artifact/engine identities plus platform smoke evidence, including process_tree_closed_verified. Listener coverage_complete false adds a limitation; it is not independently a blocking reason in that branch. Therefore index validity, exact byte identity and complete activity observation are separate claims.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D70 A valid installed index may retain partial observation coverage.md

findings.title: Product validity and whole-tree validity have different denominators
findings.body: classify_tree separates product_errors from all classification errors. Unclassified paths may fail overall valid while product_valid remains true. Control-plane and evidence content hashes are omitted from the product digest, so product identity alone is not a digest of all repository evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D71 Product validity and whole-tree validity have different denominators.md

findings.title: Child exit is not a descendant census
findings.body: terminateProcessTreeAsync first signals the child and resolves on its exit/close, cancelling escalation. That success branch does not independently enumerate surviving descendants. Other callers and reconciliation evidence must establish process-tree closure; this source observation is not a demonstrated live orphan-process incident.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D72 Child exit is not a descendant census.md

findings.title: Candidate test evidence may be supplied rather than executed
findings.body: test_evidence_builder derives proposal admission_ready from supplied case fields. orchestration_builder generates evidence_steps with status current as proposal metadata. Neither establishes independently resolved current execution receipts. Keep those producer fields separate from runtime certification owners.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D73 Candidate test evidence may be supplied rather than executed.md

findings.title: A resumed release can finish its journal while its aggregate remains invalid
findings.body: execute_all starts a new stages list and calls next_pending_step, which skips and verifies earlier passed stages. Its final valid compares this invocation list length to the entire 12-stage STEP_ORDER. Therefore a resumed call with prior passed stages can finish the journal but return valid false and count only newly executed stages. This is source-derived behavior, not a product reproduction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D74 A resumed release can finish its journal while its aggregate remains invalid.md

findings.title: The installed owner has nested parallel and serial order
findings.body: Windows and Ubuntu smoke processes start before either wait; validation results are retained separately. Exhaustive starts afterward even if a parsed smoke result is invalid, while launch/wait exceptions prevent reaching it. All three must pass before settlement advances the campaign.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D75 The installed owner has nested parallel and serial order.md

findings.title: An authoritative-named trace helper uses substring correlation
findings.body: authoritative_runtime_path tests the requested correlation string anywhere in json.dumps(event), skips malformed JSON or TypeError and sorts string timestamp values. Matching rows are useful navigation evidence but do not establish an exact causal trace or full malformed-record accounting.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D76 An authoritative-named trace helper uses substring correlation.md

findings.title: External service templates leave meaningful deployment work
findings.body: The Edge Function checks a header but leaves authentication and idempotent work as comments. The vector schema has RLS enabled without local policies and has no explicit tenant predicate in match_documents. The queue composition retains a pin placeholder. These are concrete scaffold boundaries; they do not establish an exploit or behavior in a deployed system.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D77 External service templates leave meaningful deployment work.md

findings.title: Read-only enterprise MCP routes can persist state without the write gate
findings.body: pacify_enterprise_status and pacify_billable_guardrail_evaluate are read-only annotated but call initializeEnterprise with default persistence. Missing or migrated state causes a write. Middleware authorizes only non-read-only annotations and derives both declared and observed effects from the label. Dashboard callers pass persist false. Existing tests separately check nonpersisting initialization and tool labels but do not cover this composition. This is source-derived, not a fresh execution finding.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D78 Read-only enterprise MCP routes can persist state without the write gate.md

findings.title: Empty MCP context can pass the probe and support runtime_verified
findings.body: Production definition and probe pass an empty context path. contextEnvelope falls back to an empty object; the context snapshot uses a truthiness fallback, so it returns that object. Probe accepts truthy structuredContent. Middleware records success for every resolved handler value, and observed runtime status checks event metadata rather than useful payload content. The evidence proves narrower invocation conditions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D79 Empty MCP context can pass the probe and support runtime_verified.md

findings.title: The structural function denominator includes a generated dependency bundle
findings.body: server/index.js is esbuild output from source.mjs with dependencies, not another independent authored subsystem. Its 4,383 extracted functions remain visible as artifact contents; authored and test functions are counted separately in the semantic ledger. Builder check mode could establish exact byte identity, but was not executed. VSIX packaging separately compiles the extension entry and retains the MCP bundle.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D80 The structural function denominator includes a generated dependency bundle.md

findings.title: Loaded dashboard bridge and navigation registry are not the controller implementation
findings.body: The HTML loads 20-bridge.js and 40-surfaces.js, which define reusable modules. Controller constructs its own VS Code wrapper and visible/advanced arrays and registers its own message listener. The helper spread allows payload.type to override its first argument, but no controller use was found, so that helper behavior is not asserted as a production routing fault.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D81 Loaded dashboard bridge and navigation registry are not the controller implementation.md

findings.title: Enterprise state, event and doctor receipt have separate commit points
findings.body: initialize can persist missing or migrated state. mutate writes sealed state before appending its event; doctor then writes a separate receipt. load substitutes defaults after read/parse errors, which does not itself establish preserved recovery of malformed existing data. No one transaction spans these writes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D82 Enterprise state, event and doctor receipt have separate commit points.md

findings.title: Successor config construction relies on supplied artifact identities
findings.body: The builder transforms predecessor string values and overwrites explicit successor fields from CLI input; it does not independently hash artifact bytes or prove the predecessor terminal state. It writes automation before stage configuration, so a later failure can leave the first output.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D83 Successor config construction relies on supplied artifact identities.md

findings.title: Certification and complete are separate producer fields
findings.body: The UI gives certified plus fresh first precedence. Tracing upstream narrows the initial concern: build_completion_status requires no gate blockers before freshness and certified can become true, so it does not normally emit certified/fresh with current_gates false. complete is separately derived from blocking_reasons, including historical acceptance. Dashboard verifies stored ledger/engine/source bindings and clears green claims on mismatch. Do not label the UI precedence alone a proven certification fault.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D84 Certification and complete are separate producer fields.md

findings.title: Native helper verification and durable state have narrower authority
findings.body: claim-ledger verify assigns a caller-selected status and timestamp without reading evidence. durable-state transition accepts any name and rewrites the JSON; new can replace an existing file. permission-guard matches supplied patterns and prints an approval label without enforcing an effect or approval. Keep these helpers distinct from runtime claim, lifecycle and host admission authorities.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D85 Native helper verification and durable state have narrower authority.md

findings.title: Native memory checking and writing are separate caller steps
findings.body: memory-write-gate checks supplied source/scope/verified and three sensitive patterns. scoped-memory requires a flag for semantic/procedural writes but never calls that gate, authenticates scope or independently verifies evidence. Its delete-scope removes matching rows by direct rewrite. No automatic gate-to-store integration is asserted, and the canonical memory vault remains a distinct owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D86 Native memory checking and writing are separate caller steps.md

findings.title: Helper analytical and replay outputs retain supplied-input limits
findings.body: Context packing uses supplied token costs without requiring nonnegative values; retrieval evaluation scores supplied IDs and accepts the supplied citation flag. Trace recorder hashes stable fields without timestamp, so repeated spans can share IDs. Replay-bundle records paths/hashes and textual instructions; it does not preserve or replay the files.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D87 Helper analytical and replay outputs retain supplied-input limits.md

findings.title: Helper permission changes request tests without invalidating prior evidence
findings.body: recertification-impact adds adversarial and resilience suites for permissions_changed, but invalidate_prior_evidence is computed only from code_changed or dependencies_changed. It computes a proposal over supplied graph/flags and does not execute invalidation. Certification-aggregator only combines PASS/active labels; it explicitly does not replace independent production approval.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D88 Helper permission changes request tests without invalidating prior evidence.md

findings.title: Native protocol metadata is weaker than implemented compatibility
findings.body: protocol-validator tests required-key presence, without values/types/full specification checks. OpenAPI importer creates tool metadata and schema path strings but no schema files; it derives risk/idempotence from method alone. Backend probe lists SGLang installed when python is found, and hardware probe labels an opted-in failed GPU probe completed. These are exact source predicates, not observed deployed behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D89 Native protocol metadata is weaker than implemented compatibility.md

findings.title: Native patch scope omits deleted-file destinations
findings.body: patch-scope-guard adds paths only from +++ b/ headers. A deleted-file header uses +++ /dev/null, so the removed path is absent from denied-file checks; its removed text still contributes to the line count. Empty allowed patterns disable path filtering. The helper reports a decision and does not intercept another executor applying a patch.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D90 Native patch scope omits deleted-file destinations.md

findings.title: Native verification runners test embedded examples and can accept zero cases
findings.body: Differential/metamorphic runners exercise local softmax functions; formula tests exercise one local KV formula; fuzz runner calls Python json.loads. Case counts are not required positive, so no iterations can still yield PASS. Mutation operator only writes a variant, while judge/trajectory helpers score supplied fields and can exit successfully with a negative result field. Their process success must not be read as universal target verification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D91 Native verification runners test embedded examples and can accept zero cases.md

findings.title: Supply-chain helper declarations do not enforce or attest execution
findings.body: Sandbox profile writes desired restrictions; tool policy checks truthy approval_id and rollback_ready. Provenance generator records supplied command strings without running/signing them. SBOM-lite hashes top-level manifests without parsing dependencies. Deterministic archive uses fixed timestamps but does not exclude an output created inside its source tree. Keep these artifacts distinct from enforced runtime boundaries and exact release certificates.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D92 Supply-chain helper declarations do not enforce or attest execution.md

findings.title: Sanitation primary bounds do not constrain its separate secret scan
findings.body: build_sanitation_summary bounds and hashes its first corpus, then calls scan_secret_shapes(root) through a separate os.walk/full-file-read path without explicit count/byte ceilings. That scanner applies shared external-scope checks to directory names, but not file-specific mutable exclusions to file entries. Consequently primary corpus bounds/hash do not alone identify or bound all credential-scan inputs. Matching review classifications also remain supplied dispositions, not independent credential verification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D93 Sanitation primary bounds do not constrain its separate secret scan.md

findings.title: Coordination read routes can publish corruption evidence
findings.body: readAuthoritativeState copies raw corrupt, invalid-shape, workspace-mismatched or hash-mismatched state into quarantine and writes a receipt before throwing. Several MCP read-only tools call it through readCoordination or readMemoryTelemetry. tool_conflict_status catches that error and can return a normal result after the evidence write. The missing-store nonpersisting read test does not establish no-write behavior for damaged existing state.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D94 Coordination read routes can publish corruption evidence.md

findings.title: Expired stored claims are rejected before built-in expiry cleanup
findings.body: withState copies state and calls assertCoordinationState(previous, requireSeal false) before expireClaims. That validator still invokes conformance, which rejects active claims whose expires_utc is at or before now. Thus an otherwise intact stored active lease that has expired prevents the normal mutation path from reaching expiry normalization or its mutator. Read paths expire only in-memory projections. This is a source-derived ordering boundary; no clock-controlled reproduction was run.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D95 Expired stored claims are rejected before built-in expiry cleanup.md

findings.title: MCP retained resume packet bypasses packet hash and freshness checks
findings.body: writeHandoff binds packet.sha256 and verified_state_hash, and its Markdown instructs consumers to verify. pacify_resume_handoff only reads current coordination to get the packet path, then calls generic JSON loading. It does not verify packet.sha256 or equality with current coordination state, so the source route can return a stale or resealed-independent packet. Fresh taskHandoff is a separate derived route.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D96 MCP retained resume packet bypasses packet hash and freshness checks.md

findings.title: Coordination result limits apply after full event and memory reads
findings.body: tailJsonlDetailed reads/parses the full file before slicing up to MAX_EVENTS; readCoordination requests smaller tails after that work. memoryRecords reads all layer/session JSONL files and sorts all matches before slicing. A 100-record API limit therefore does not bound filesystem bytes or parser memory. Malformed event suffixes are reported and mutation checks reject degraded parse health.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D97 Coordination result limits apply after full event and memory reads.md

findings.title: Shared exact-target claims conflict with the global fence invariant
findings.body: Overlap logic permits shared/shared claims on different tasks. claimTask increments one fencing_by_target counter for each exact target without updating earlier active claim tokens. If two shared claims request the identical target string, the prior claim token is now behind the global counter and next-state validation rejects active-claim-fence-not-current. The existing shared-mode test uses ancestor/descendant target strings with different counter keys, so it does not cover this composition.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D98 Shared exact-target claims conflict with the global fence invariant.md

findings.title: Hard-stop state can block an otherwise authorized release transition
findings.body: recordProgress marks exceeded hard-stop usage as blocked. releaseTask sets task.status to released but preserves that budget/usage. assertBudget requires any hard-stop usage to retain blocked status, so the transition guard rejects that release. This concerns ledger transition consistency, not actual worker termination; no runtime reproduction was performed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D99 Hard-stop state can block an otherwise authorized release transition.md

findings.title: Environment writer and reader accept different dataset sizes
findings.body: writeDataset serializes and writes data without a maximum size check; readDataset rejects any shard larger than8MiB before returning records. Thus a produced snapshot can be validly indexed yet have an unreadable graph or subject shard; a small API page limit does not avoid that check because pagination follows full loading. No large-dataset reproduction was executed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D100 Environment writer and reader accept different dataset sizes.md

findings.title: Retained discovery freshness differs by consumer
findings.body: Host memory-only refresh updates currentEnvironment but skips shards; MCP and dashboard subject queries still call stored readers. On a stale stored snapshot, environments deactivates active rows; the graph route returns captured graph properties unchanged with a freshness label. Consumers must interpret that observation metadata rather than treating active graph properties as current liveness.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D101 Retained discovery freshness differs by consumer.md

findings.title: Environment consumer edges are lexical and can span root scopes
findings.body: Environment key names across parsed files form one regex used against source text, including Markdown and JSON. Each matching key accumulates consumer rows across all roots; every declaration of that name receives those rows. semanticGraph uses global name-derived variable IDs and labels edges consumes-variable. These links can arise from comments, documentation or another root and do not prove runtime reads or per-root environment binding. Values and fingerprints are intentionally not retained.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D102 Environment consumer edges are lexical and can span root scopes.md

findings.title: Discovery completeness and deadlines cover different work
findings.body: Tree scanning caps accepted entries/depth and checks time between operations, but prunes selected directories and silently prefilters missing roots in discoverEnvironment. Virtual environment marker reads slice only after full-file reads; .env parsing precedes the consumer-loop deadline checks. The worker45s wrapper covers the combined worker duration but requests termination without waiting for exit. A complete marker describes the bounded scan corpus, not exhaustive host discovery or proven cleanup.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D103 Discovery completeness and deadlines cover different work.md

findings.title: Existing environment shards are trusted by the writer and verified later by readers
findings.body: writeDataset skips an existing target yet returns the digest of the newly serialized intended bytes. It does not verify or repair that target. A corrupted existing file can therefore survive refresh; later readDataset detects a mismatch and rejects it. Current index replacement and event append are separate, so event failure can leave a published current snapshot without its event.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D104 Existing environment shards are trusted by the writer and verified later by readers.md

findings.title: Governor slot release does not establish producer termination
findings.body: _drain races the producer promise against AbortSignal. Abort rejects the race and finally decrements pool.active, removes the entry and drains the next work, even if a noncooperative producer is still running. dispose signals entries without joining them. This bounds governed waiting slots; physical threads/processes need their own shutdown proof. Existing deadline tests use cooperative producers.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D105 Governor slot release does not establish producer termination.md

findings.title: Cancelled half-open circuit trial can leave admission closed indefinitely
findings.body: _admitCircuit sets halfOpenActive true after cooldown. _recordCircuit returns immediately for cancelled work, leaving that flag set. The next call rejects whenever halfOpenActive is true, with no later cooldown transition clearing it. Queued cancellation/displacement also lacks that reset, unlike explicit queue-full rejection. The existing half-open test covers success, not cancellation; this is source-derived, not a live incident reproduction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D106 Cancelled half-open circuit trial can leave admission closed indefinitely.md

findings.title: First persistent snapshot return bypasses the normal short TTL refresh branch
findings.body: snapshot accepts matching persisted metadata up to24h old and immediately returns persistent-hit. Its ordinary cache TTL is5s..5min, but the first restore does not invoke that branch or mark refresh_pending. A later snapshot request can initiate stale-while-revalidate. Matching source identity is not equivalent to current dynamic provider/coordination observations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D107 First persistent snapshot return bypasses the normal short TTL refresh branch.md

findings.title: Canonical lease maintenance can select a project independently of the visible root
findings.body: ensureWorkspaceProjectLease accepts the current shared vscode-dashboard session without comparing projectRoot. If selection is needed it prefers one active project over a basename match, then a sole eligible project. Activation and renewal are separate subprocess calls. The host calls this before visible snapshots and on a timer; it therefore has canonical state effects beyond reading the dashboard.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D108 Canonical lease maintenance can select a project independently of the visible root.md

findings.title: Host bridge disposal covers governed work and fingerprint workers selectively
findings.body: dispose requests termination for tracked fingerprint workers and disposes only an internally owned governor. Direct capture callers for native query/hydrate, workspace operations and verifier description have no shared child registry in PxBridge and receive no disposal signal. Each retains its local timeout; that is a separate lifecycle guarantee from bridge-wide cancellation. Canonical lease stop likewise clears its timer without cancelling an in-flight direct bridge call.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D109 Host bridge disposal covers governed work and fingerprint workers selectively.md

findings.title: Git context conflict count is computed after change capping
findings.body: gitSnapshot retains at most maxChanges rows and then counts conflicts from that retained list. An unmerged path beyond the cap is therefore omitted from conflicts even though staged/unstaged totals scan retained command output. The subprocess wrapper also keeps only the last200000 stdout characters without a truncation flag, potentially losing branch/status prefix. gitConflictDecision depends on that conflicts field and operation markers. This is source-derived, not a reproduced missed-conflict event.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D110 Git context conflict count is computed after change capping.md

findings.title: Authenticated catalog status is not rebound to the JS record read
findings.body: Python verifies lifecycle receipts against current record/tree bytes internally, then emits a row keyed by relative path with status/authenticated/reason but no record digest. PxBridge fetches that projection before studioCatalog reads physical records, and can reuse the status response cache. JS uses authenticated === true to choose displayed status without comparing the projection to its new revision digest. This is an observation-time gap; it does not prove the separate mutation authority accepts changed source.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D111 Authenticated catalog status is not rebound to the JS record read.md

findings.title: Portable context flags describe construction rather than universal policy enforcement
findings.body: buildContextEnvelope includes no file bodies and copies locators, objective and coordination metadata. It labels credentials_included false and supplies a numeric context_injection_cap_tokens, but performs no general secret scan or token calculation over those caller fields. codexPrompt states Git and claim rules as host instructions; the module does not intercept future commands. Its environment filter removes a fixed list of key names.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D112 Portable context flags describe construction rather than universal policy enforcement.md

findings.title: Nominal dashboard reads perform persistent derived work
findings.body: build_snapshot enters RuntimeWorkPlane, which writes lock owners, result cache and start/finish state. Hardware misses also write diagnostics/hardware-dashboard-cache.json. MCP summary, hardware, readiness and enterprise catalog helpers can traverse this composed path while their outer annotation is read-only. This describes actual source effects, not a claim that every call writes every optional cache.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D113 Nominal dashboard reads perform persistent derived work.md

findings.title: Dashboard runnable and coordination totals use weaker evidence than lifecycle catalog status
findings.body: Snapshot agent/workflow runnable totals inspect retained receipt fields without calling Studio receipt authentication. _coordination copies stored state_hash and active status count without hash, workspace or expiry validation. The separate Python Studio catalog projection and JavaScript coordination reader enforce other checks. A displayed count or LIVE provenance label therefore has a different proof basis from those stronger readers.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D114 Dashboard runnable and coordination totals use weaker evidence than lifecycle catalog status.md

findings.title: Graph path and overview do not enforce returned node and edge caps
findings.body: query_graph computes bounded_nodes/bounded_edges for all modes, but overview returns every cluster and aggregate edge, and path performs unrestricted BFS over the loaded graph then returns the entire found path. Both report limits and truncated false. Full mode independently pages nodes/edges so one edge page may reference nodes absent from the current node page. Neighborhood has separate explicit depth/node/edge enforcement.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D115 Graph path and overview do not enforce returned node and edge caps.md

findings.title: Missing capability graph can appear as available empty graph
findings.body: Repository view returns available false for missing, oversized or invalid source. Capability view uses _read_json(...,{}) and then empty records/edges on missing or malformed JSON; later empty-selection response reports available true. Neither branch verifies a projection-staleness marker in query_graph. Unavailable source and a valid empty capability graph are not distinguished by that path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D116 Missing capability graph can appear as available empty graph.md

findings.title: Python work timeout is admission waiting time, not producer execution time
findings.body: RuntimeWorkPlane uses timeout_seconds while acquiring operation lock and later pool slot, each with its own wait clock. Once admitted it calls producer() synchronously with no timer/cancellation wrapper. Thus the dashboard60-second work-plane argument does not itself impose a60-second runtime ceiling; an outer host subprocess timeout is a separate mechanism.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D117 Python work timeout is admission waiting time, not producer execution time.md

findings.title: Python result cache records a digest that reuse does not verify
