findings.body: Producer publication writes result_sha256, but _read_cache only requires an object/result and convertible created_epoch. Fast hits compare input hash/age; concurrent joins compare input hash/new publication time. No reuse branch recomputes result_sha256. authoritative true bypasses the initial TTL path but not concurrent identical-result joining. The malformed-cache test only supplies invalid JSON.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D118 Python result cache records a digest that reuse does not verify.md

findings.title: Work result publication precedes causal finish state
findings.body: execute writes the result cache before _record_finish updates state.json. If finish-state recording fails, the owner records failure/raises while a concurrent joiner may already consume the result cache. Pool and operation locks are released sequentially; a pool-release exception can prevent operation release. These boundaries need separate recovery evidence; no failure injection was executed for the report.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D119 Work result publication precedes causal finish state.md

findings.title: Python budgeted invocation and immutable policy are separate entry points
findings.body: ProviderInvocationGateway.invoke calls _invoke_once directly. execute_provider_request performs supplied immutable policy comparisons before delegating. Repository static symbol search found direct gateway construction/calls and wrapper execution in tests; no production wrapper caller was found. Existing host-model and execute_agent_plan routes remain separately mapped. This is static reachability evidence, not proof against dynamic imports.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D120 Python budgeted invocation and immutable policy are separate entry points.md

findings.title: Provider accounting can commit before terminal event publication fails
findings.body: _invoke_once commits successful settlement before publishing completed. An exception at that publication escapes with accounting already settled and no response receipt returned. Adapter failures burn reservation before publishing failed; failure-event publication errors can replace the original sanitized failure. Budget and event owners have separate WAL transactions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D121 Provider accounting can commit before terminal event publication fails.md

findings.title: Fallback retains primary model and attachment metadata
findings.body: Policy wrapper allows fallback by adapter ID after validating declared fallback metadata. Gateway replace() changes invocation_id and adapter_id only; model_id, revision and attachment remain primary. Returned policy outcome also uses primary request metadata, and exact receipt check expects the primary model ID. Thus a fallback declaration naming a different model is not itself applied by this path. No live fallback was executed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D122 Fallback retains primary model and attachment metadata.md

findings.title: Immutable policy cost ceiling checks expected charge only
findings.body: provider_execution_policy_report compares expected_charge_microunits to policy cost maximum. Actual reserve/settlement limits come from separate budget registry. After invocation, wrapper checks model/adapter and digest shapes but does not compare returned charge with its policy maximum. If those limits differ, the wrapper itself does not enforce its maximum against final usage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D123 Immutable policy cost ceiling checks expected charge only.md

findings.title: Provider observed effects are registry-derived labels
findings.body: Gateway writes identical declared and observed effect arrays from adapter registry mode. Local mode reports model only, although included local HTTP adapters make loopback POST requests. This is an effect-label convention, not independently measured I/O; the local-effects test uses a fake adapter.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D124 Provider observed effects are registry-derived labels.md

findings.title: Provider source scan does not establish universal mediation
findings.body: Scan corpus is runtime/scripts Python; gateway itself is excluded and detector uses selected SDK imports/call suffixes. Cached records reuse prior violations for unchanged source bytes without a scanner-revision check. Current index validates source identity but does not independently recompute its findings. This cannot prove host JavaScript or arbitrary adapter/network calls are mediated.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D125 Provider source scan does not establish universal mediation.md

findings.title: Memory append has several publication points before its returned receipt
findings.body: Lifecycle event, anchor and head are published before record JSON and Markdown note. No transaction wraps all these files, and records/lifecycle readers do not take the writer lock. A failure or concurrent read can observe intermediate state; underlying FileLock serializes writers only.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D126 Memory append has several publication points before its returned receipt.md

findings.title: Memory revision validation follows filesystem path order
findings.body: records iterates sorted recursive paths and requires the next per-ID revision immediately. append chooses category/address/directory from current type/title/key and does not require those fields unchanged. A revision whose new path sorts before its predecessor can therefore fail subsequent chain reads; prior_payloads[-1] also depends on path order. Existing tests exercise different IDs and duplicate revision rejection, not title-changing same-ID history. This is a source-inferred branch, not an executed reproduction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D127 Memory revision validation follows filesystem path order.md

findings.title: Active memory index and canonical search are separate paths
findings.body: Index validation checks entries against all historical records, without requiring every latest record to be represented. Reconciliation selects generation from retained activation events but does not compare event manifest_sha256 with current validated manifest. Direct vault.search reads canonical eligible records and workspace search uses a separate ranker; neither consults active index entries.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D128 Active memory index and canonical search are separate paths.md

findings.title: Memory monitor healthy and eligible fields omit some retrieval and activation checks
findings.body: healthy checks absence of orphan generations and queue.valid, while nested index.activation_error is not in that predicate. eligible_record_count sums certified/trusted states without checking expiry, actor visibility or supersession. These summary labels therefore do not equal query eligibility or valid active-index authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D129 Memory monitor healthy and eligible fields omit some retrieval and activation checks.md

findings.title: Three retrieval paths have different filters and scoring
findings.body: Vault search uses candidate_memories exact semantic/SimHash selection then structured/lexical/relationship scoring. Workspace search first checks lease and actor, obtains vault retrieval_records, and calls rank_memories with lexical and optional caller scores/fixed bindings. Generic retrieve uses seven fixed weighted signals and visibility. Its strategy is a label and its byte counter includes excerpts only. No shared ranking equivalence is established by their names.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D130 Three retrieval paths have different filters and scoring.md

findings.title: Certified supersession is decided before expiry and actor filtering
findings.body: Vault retrieval_records builds superseded IDs from all certified/trusted latest records, then filters individual records by expiry and actor ACL. An expired or inaccessible certified correction can suppress a prior record even when that correction is not returned. The standalone candidate_memories helper is broader still: it collects supersedes from every supplied record before filtering. No live retrieval reproduction was run.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D131 Certified supersession is decided before expiry and actor filtering.md

findings.title: Memory context and compaction budgets have distinct practical limits
findings.body: assemble_context sums block lengths but joins blocks with extra newline separators omitted from used_chars. compact_tool_results preserves protected tail and only offloads eligible older large tool results, so output may remain above max_chars. Preview returns pointers without ensuring object persistence; restore checks digest but does not verify path containment or project.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D132 Memory context and compaction budgets have distinct practical limits.md

findings.title: Write-intent deduplication does not make handlers execute exactly once
findings.body: Queue key binds project/operation/payload, but flush calls handler(operation,payload), then writes receipt and moves pending intent. There is no queue lock or atomic commit spanning handler and receipt. A handler effect followed by receipt failure leaves replayable pending work, and concurrent flushes can call the same handler. No failure/concurrency injection was executed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D133 Write-intent deduplication does not make handlers execute exactly once.md

findings.title: Integration health loads all valid registered targets
findings.body: validate_integrations imports handler and healthcheck even with smoke false, despite returning a loading_rule that says metadata startup then explicit selection. Smoke true invokes all active checks. Current checks are one noop scheduling simulation, one public retrieval fixture, and metacognitive registry denominators/references; they do not prove external service or complete workflow operation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D134 Integration health loads all valid registered targets.md

findings.title: Memory lifecycle primitives rely on caller evidence authority
findings.body: append accepts a valid record with supplied certified/trusted state; transition requires allowed state change and nonempty evidence strings, and reinstatement requires revoked plus supplied evidence. These primitive functions do not invoke decide_promotion or authenticate evidence receipts themselves. Stronger workspace admission must be traced at its own call boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D135 Memory lifecycle primitives rely on caller evidence authority.md

findings.title: Memory materialization does not supply current revision freshness checks
findings.body: validate_memory_query_plan can compare current source/dependency revisions when explicitly passed. materialize_memory_context calls it without those arguments, and agent preview passes only plan, supplied records and clock. Therefore the shown path checks plan integrity but does not establish that its retained source/dependency revision values are current.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D136 Memory materialization does not supply current revision freshness checks.md

findings.title: Governed execution binds memory and handoff hashes without forwarding their contents
findings.body: preview_governed materializes memory and validates acknowledged handoffs, but _resolved_preview returns their hashes. execute_governed_plan includes those hashes in request/receipt and calls execute_agent_plan with task plan, placement, run ID and CPU/GPU callbacks only. The integration test CPU lambda returns a constant answer without consuming context. This establishes receipt binding; content injection requires a separate caller path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D137 Governed execution binds memory and handoff hashes without forwarding their contents.md

findings.title: Semantic required and excluded context are declarations in reviewed retrieval paths
findings.body: Envelope validates and preserves required_context/excluded_context, but semantic_query_signals takes only query/envelope and uses keys, aliases, tags, entities and predicates. Reviewed vault candidate search, workspace ranker and memory materializer do not evaluate these context maps. Invalid nonmapping context inputs are also normalized to empty objects by mapping conversion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D138 Semantic required and excluded context are declarations in reviewed retrieval paths.md

findings.title: Agent structural admission and launch readiness are different gates
findings.body: test_candidate labels its receipt structural_preflight_not_behavioral_certification and excludes memory_runtime_resolved/handoff_runtime_resolved from admission_ready. _new_session later calls plain preview, which blocks unresolved memory/handoff bindings. Governed preview accepts additional broker/handoff inputs through a different API. A passed preflight or admitted catalog row therefore does not imply an ordinary launch can run.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D139 Agent structural admission and launch readiness are different gates.md

findings.title: Host preparation does not repeat the instruction byte identity check
findings.body: Creation and structural identity test compare instruction bytes with spec.instruction_sha256. _admitted_context checks saved record/builder/admission/live authority; it does not rehash instructions.md. prepare_host_run and host resume then read that file directly into a newly signed prepared request. This describes the Python boundary; host acceptance and filesystem protection are separate controls requiring their own evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D140 Host preparation does not repeat the instruction byte identity check.md

findings.title: Agent terminal state can precede its signed run receipt
findings.body: Host completion and governed callback execution publish terminal durable state before signing and writing the final run receipt. Signing or receipt publication failure can therefore leave terminal state without that artifact. Host preparation has explicit best-effort compensation for preparation failure; these later commit boundaries are different.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D141 Agent terminal state can precede its signed run receipt.md

findings.title: Deterministic worker setup and cleanup have failure paths outside terminal handling
findings.body: _execute_session transitions running before creating the task workspace/signing task outside its guarded supervisor try. After supervision it parses last stdout JSON without asserting an object, then reclaims task content before terminal transition; cleanup errors raise first. These source paths can leave nonterminal state requiring owner reconciliation, rather than guaranteeing immediate terminal publication on every exception.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D142 Deterministic worker setup and cleanup have failure paths outside terminal handling.md

findings.title: Memory broker receipt authority is scoped to supplied records
findings.body: Materialization maps supplied records by ID with last duplicate winning, checks metadata predicates and provenance hash shape, then returns a digest. It does not load vault records, authenticate lifecycle history, recompute source bytes or call full MemoryRecord.validation_errors. Future effective times are not rejected by the age comparison; context token count is ceil(serialized item bytes/4), not a model tokenizer.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D143 Memory broker receipt authority is scoped to supplied records.md

findings.title: Detached launch acceptance does not require a running live worker
findings.body: launch_studio_worker returns accepted true and live_worker_observed true whenever durable state differs from launch_state, before checking process.poll. A failed/finalizing/cancel transition also satisfies this branch. The returned state must be interpreted directly; these booleans are not independent worker-liveness or successful-start proof.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D144 Detached launch acceptance does not require a running live worker.md

findings.title: Detached worker last-resort diagnostics are discarded by launcher
findings.body: _retain_publication_failure tries two filesystem paths then os.write(2,...), with a comment that launcher supervises stderr. launch_studio_worker sets stderr DEVNULL. The unit test mocks os.write and proves the call, not retention through the actual launcher. When both diagnostic writes fail, this final fallback is discarded on this path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D145 Detached worker last-resort diagnostics are discarded by launcher.md

findings.title: Finalizer and Agent runtime use different run-receipt locations
findings.body: Agent _execute_session writes the signed receipt to record_path.parent/runs/run_id.json, below its immutable revision. finalize_studio_run_if_worker_exited checks state_root/runs/run_id.json and updates it only if present. The detached session wrapper does not copy the Agent receipt there. Therefore terminal durable state can be updated while the existing revision receipt remains finalizing. This source path was not executed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D146 Finalizer and Agent runtime use different run-receipt locations.md

findings.title: Resume observer handoff is run-bound rather than launch-generation-bound
findings.body: launch_studio_worker reuses sessions/run_id/worker-request-cleanup.json across resumes. Observer waits only for its existence, and finalizer filters worker history by the retained resource/PID when present. Until the new worker overwrites it, an old binding can identify an exited prior worker. Path reconciliation also returns early when multiple historical worker records share the run. This race requires a targeted reproduction before claiming an observed premature terminal transition.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D147 Resume observer handoff is run-bound rather than launch-generation-bound.md

findings.title: Handoff consumption checks fewer acknowledgment fields than construction
findings.body: acknowledge_handoff checks receiver ID/revision when creating the value. consume_handoff checks accept, acknowledgment digest and packet ID/hash, then validates packet receiver against supplied context; it does not compare acknowledgment receiver fields, schema or time again. Hashes are unkeyed and persistence is exclusive creation, not independently authenticated receiver approval.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D148 Handoff consumption checks fewer acknowledgment fields than construction.md

findings.title: Handoff consumed view omits hypotheses and open questions
findings.body: Packet creation retains hypotheses and open_questions, but consume_handoff returns evidence, authority, budgets and identity without those two fields. Agent governed preview subsequently returns only packet hashes. Transferring these reasoning contents requires an additional consumer path; presence in a persisted packet is not proof the receiving executor sees them.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D149 Handoff consumed view omits hypotheses and open questions.md

findings.title: Deterministic Agent worker is a closed tool adapter
findings.body: The owned inner worker only dispatches sha256, json-keys and delay and returns an objective digest. It reports model_invoked false and does not read the Agent instruction body. This is a real process/tool boundary with a bounded repertoire; completing it does not establish model reasoning or execution of arbitrary declared agent capabilities.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D150 Deterministic Agent worker is a closed tool adapter.md

findings.title: Snapshot list and cancellation polling prove different things
findings.body: read/read_snapshot verify complete signed ancestry under lock. list_snapshots reads without that lock and caps 500 lexical random run IDs before sorting by updated time; its has_more excludes omitted roots. DurableControlSignal authenticates only head and returns true for pause_requested/cancel_requested, not interrupted or terminal states.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D151 Snapshot list and cancellation polling prove different things.md

findings.title: Stale reconciliation has no expected-heartbeat compare at transition
findings.body: reconcile reads state and tests heartbeat age, then calls separately locked transition without expected sequence/heartbeat. A concurrent fresh heartbeat can therefore be followed by an interruption based on the older observation. This is a source-inferred interleaving, not a reproduced incident.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D152 Stale reconciliation has no expected-heartbeat compare at transition.md

findings.title: Authority transaction is compensated multi-file publication
findings.body: register_authority_transaction prevalidates records and locks writers, but _resolve readers do not take that lock. Records and history are published sequentially; exception rollback is another sequence of writes and can fail. Initial project/key creation also has no shared initialization lock. Authentication does not imply atomic authority-set visibility.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D153 Authority transaction is compensated multi-file publication.md

findings.title: Approval is consumed before downstream operation outcome
findings.body: Both RSA host approval and workflow approval create an exclusive marker before returning to the executor. A subsequent marker write/signing or downstream operation failure does not unconsume the proof. Retries need the caller to distinguish consumed authorization from successful operation evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D154 Approval is consumed before downstream operation outcome.md

findings.title: Resource reconciliation dry run can terminate owned processes
findings.body: When a process record has an in-memory Popen handle, reconcile calls terminate_owned_process without checking apply. Thus apply=False can signal/terminate that process and publish state/receipt while the returned summary says dry_run true. Other cleanup dry-run branches also write receipts. The reviewed dry-run test covers failed path cleanup, not this process branch.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D155 Resource reconciliation dry run can terminate owned processes.md

findings.title: Owned process starts before its registration is retained
findings.body: spawn_owned_process calls Popen, constructs its record, then upserts the ledger and finally stores the handle in _processes. No compensation surrounds upsert failure here. Registration failure can leave a running child without a returned owned handle or retained resource record on this source path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D156 Owned process starts before its registration is retained.md

findings.title: Cleanup effect ledger and receipt are separate commits
findings.body: reclaim checks a record and dependencies, inventories the path and links, removes it, updates the ledger and finally writes the receipt with direct write_text. No shared lock spans that sequence. Receipt failure can follow successful removal, and promotion checks use caller validated boolean plus file presence rather than retained content hashes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D157 Cleanup effect ledger and receipt are separate commits.md

findings.title: Generic process closure labels exceed the observed boundary
findings.body: complete_current_process marks itself reclaimed while executing. terminate_owned_process labels process_tree_terminated when the parent Popen is exited, including an already-exited parent branch; it does not separately enumerate and verify all descendants. A selected test checks one child, while ProcessSupervisor owns additional tree containment elsewhere.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D158 Generic process closure labels exceed the observed boundary.md

findings.title: Resource valid and pressure counters have separate meanings
findings.body: resource_status returns valid true regardless of active resources or cleanup failures. storage_status valid depends on optional stored-counter alerts; critical disk pressure alone does not make it false. Owned bytes/files come from ledger counters, not a fresh inventory; workspace count includes all unreclaimed ephemeral resource types.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D159 Resource valid and pressure counters have separate meanings.md

findings.title: History pruning needs producer concurrency evidence beyond WAL
findings.body: prune_operational_history reads and validates current history, computes a suffix and later commits it with anchor/receipt through WAL. This method shows no history-owner lock or expected-before-hash comparison across read and commit. Atomic multi-artifact publication alone does not establish preservation of an intervening producer append.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D160 History pruning needs producer concurrency evidence beyond WAL.md

findings.title: Output and deadline budgets cover distinct work
findings.body: Capture retains a prefix and counts dropped bytes while continuing to drain; excess output does not terminate the child. Supervision time begins after spawn, ledger identity, containment and thread setup. Initial/full disk traversal and sampling have no internal deadline; errors skip entries. Float NaN passes the timeout range comparisons, so finite timeout validity is not fully established here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D161 Output and deadline budgets cover distinct work.md

findings.title: Registration error can become an inaccurate spawn-failure receipt
findings.body: ProcessSupervisor catches OSError from the entire manager.spawn_owned_process call and reports not_started/tree_closed true with no resource ID. ResourceManager can raise that error from ledger upsert after Popen has started. The wrapper does not recover the child handle on this path; the existing missing-executable test covers only failure before child creation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D162 Registration error can become an inaccurate spawn-failure receipt.md

findings.title: Unexpected supervision callback failure skips normal terminal publication
findings.body: The main finally closes Job/liveness handles and joins capture threads, but does not itself call POSIX shutdown. An exception from cancellation polling, disk accounting or another loop operation can propagate before resource closure and receipt creation. Post-spawn identity update and thread startup also precede this try. Thread join timeout is not followed by an alive check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D163 Unexpected supervision callback failure skips normal terminal publication.md

findings.title: Owner-loss fixture does not demonstrate supervisor-death recovery
findings.body: The liveness owner is os.getpid: the supervisor checks its own kernel handle/fingerprint while running. The owner-loss test mocks that fingerprint becoming unavailable and disables the handle; it does not kill the supervisor. Windows kill-on-close Job is a separate mechanism. POSIX polling alone cannot keep running after supervisor death.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D164 Owner-loss fixture does not demonstrate supervisor-death recovery.md

findings.title: WAL recovery consistency is not concurrent reader isolation
findings.body: Targets are replaced sequentially under a per-journal writer lock. Crash tests recover then assert the complete before/after set. A reader outside that lock can see a mixed generation while applying; another journal does not share the writer lock. The durable guarantee depends on retained manifest recovery, not one filesystem operation for all targets.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D165 WAL recovery consistency is not concurrent reader isolation.md

findings.title: A rejected WAL commit can still finish previous transactions
findings.body: commit calls _recover_locked before before-image validation, optional precommit validation and reused transaction-ID rejection. Old pending transactions may therefore be rolled forward/archived even when the requested new transaction later fails. Reusing an ID is rejection, not an idempotent successful result.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D166 A rejected WAL commit can still finish previous transactions.md

findings.title: WAL before-image guard begins after caller intent was computed
findings.body: WAL compares current targets with before/after images captured during commit. It can detect later external writes, but without an owner precommit validator it accepts a newly captured value as before even if the caller computed its after value from an older read. RetentionManager constructs JsonWal without a validator, confirming the boundary documented in D160.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D167 WAL before-image guard begins after caller intent was computed.md

findings.title: WAL inspection and byte bounds exclude some preceding work
findings.body: Desired payloads are serialized before the64MiB aggregate check; existing before images have no corresponding byte cap. Inspection enumerates sorted paths before count checking and reads each file before total-byte checking. Its two fingerprints cover pending journal contents, not a stable snapshot of external target bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D168 WAL inspection and byte bounds exclude some preceding work.md

findings.title: Archive verification does not recheck source tree before removal
findings.body: Both archive scripts verify ZIP membership, manifest and member hashes, then recheck selected top-level containment before direct rmtree. They do not compare current source file inventory/bytes with the archived manifest immediately before removal, and do not hold a producer lock or use ResourceManager. A newly added/changed source entry after archive verification is a source-inferred preservation gap. Receipt follows all deletions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D169 Archive verification does not recheck source tree before removal.md

findings.title: Archive latest and recovery labels have narrower implementations
findings.body: Both keep_latest options retain the lexical filename suffix; generic WAL tx UUID names do not establish chronological order. The archive test uses simple synthetic manifest files, checks ZIP integrity/hash and directory count, and never restores/runs WAL recovery. JsonWal does not automatically read ZIP archives; receipt supplies manual extraction guidance.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D170 Archive latest and recovery labels have narrower implementations.md

findings.title: Assurance certification labels derive from supplied metadata
findings.body: certify_skeptically compares caller evidence class labels, equal positive coverage and supplied revisions; both absent revisions compare equal. audit_runtime uses declared benchmark/drift and top-level fields. Neither runs tests or authenticates evidence receipts. These labels must remain distinct from governed repository certification and observed runtime health.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D171 Assurance certification labels derive from supplied metadata.md

findings.title: Commissioning blocked and implementation-authorized outputs can disagree
findings.body: commission_project includes facts_without_evidence in decision reasons, but implementation_authorized checks only missing sections, high-risk unknowns and human_acceptance. With complete answers and acceptance, a fact lacking evidence can produce blocked plus implementation_authorized true. Consumers need an explicit decision precedence; no execution was performed to exercise this branch.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D172 Commissioning blocked and implementation-authorized outputs can disagree.md

findings.title: Lock finalization can fail after protected work committed
findings.body: FileLock retains heartbeat I/O error until __exit__, writes released metadata, unlocks/closes and raises release_error if the body succeeded. Thus a caller may receive an exception after its protected state writes completed. A failed release write can retain held metadata naming a still-live process and block later acquisition even though the OS lock is free.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D173 Lock finalization can fail after protected work committed.md

findings.title: Version allocation observes occupancy without reserving it
findings.body: Allocation reads physical versions/source and returns an envelope; no lock or reservation is performed here. Revalidation recomputes hashes and candidate but checks observed_utc format/calendar only, not elapsed age. Source identity excludes top-level runs. External-authenticated skill mode validates caller hash shapes; source authentication is a caller obligation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D174 Version allocation observes occupancy without reserving it.md

findings.title: Generic record immutability is narrower than full revision immutability
findings.body: write_versioned_record accepts kind/identity/version separately from model and does not compare them with model fields. Existing revision replay compares only record.json with normalized envelope; undeclared sibling files are not inspected. Agent/Workflow specialized publishers supply additional full-tree and receipt checks, so this generic helper alone must not stand for them.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D175 Generic record immutability is narrower than full revision immutability.md

findings.title: Studio frozen records validate metadata rather than operational evidence
findings.body: Lifecycle true flags require nonempty evidence strings; operational combines flags without resolving evidence. Agent schemas require object root and byte bound, not full schema verification. Frozen records retain mutable nested maps. Workflow DAG validation checks type, unique drivers, cycles, branch/join structure; it does not run nodes or establish current capability authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D176 Studio frozen records validate metadata rather than operational evidence.md

findings.title: Execution grant trigger differs from operation mutation vocabulary
findings.body: operation_authority treats effects outside READ_EFFECTS, including process and workspace-write, as non-read. execution_contract.NON_READ_EFFECTS contains only write_workspace/install_tool/network/run_service/secret_access/migration/destructive. Given declared manifest and approved policy, the other recognized mutation spellings do not trigger its signed-grant checks or requires_verification. The outer owner gate still requires its IDs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D177 Execution grant trigger differs from operation mutation vocabulary.md

findings.title: Authority composition does not resolve scope claim or idempotency evidence
findings.body: AuthorityRequest.scopes is accepted but unused by decide. User/policy/claim/idempotency strings and active status are checked for presence/declared values, without store lookup or reservation. The signed-policy wrapper authenticates policy separately but passes caller claim fields onward. Downstream owners must establish those independent truths.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D178 Authority composition does not resolve scope claim or idempotency evidence.md

findings.title: Physical bounded reads do not establish an immutable content snapshot
findings.body: read_bounded_regular_file opens once, checks descriptor regular type/size and reads size+1 at most, rejecting length change. This bounds retained bytes and catches growth/shrink but does not detect a same-size concurrent modification. Root containment and ancestor checks are outside this helper; O_NOFOLLOW is used only where provided.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D179 Physical bounded reads do not establish an immutable content snapshot.md

findings.title: Studio atomic JSON replacement has a different durability contract from WAL
findings.body: write_json_atomic writes a unique prepared file then os.replace without file/directory fsync or cleanup on replacement failure. Its name describes replacement visibility, not the staged-image recovery protocol in JsonWal. Durable controller signs event and head, but each uses this separate helper.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D180 Studio atomic JSON replacement has a different durability contract from WAL.md

findings.title: Freshness policies differ across evidence consumers
findings.body: TrustedEvidenceResolver rejects records older than max_age but not future timestamps; its now is captured at construction. Effect grants require expiry after issue and current before expiry, without current at or after issue. Pure evidence assembler explicitly rejects future evidence. These are three distinct temporal contracts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D181 Freshness policies differ across evidence consumers.md

findings.title: Effect grant validation depends on complete caller target inventory
findings.body: Network hosts, secrets and writable targets are checked only when supplied. A network effect does not itself require a nonempty host inventory. Nonce and idempotency are nonempty/same-value checks with no consumed store; repeating a valid same-key grant can pass. Actual target enumeration, replay policy and execution interception belong to callers.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D182 Effect grant validation depends on complete caller target inventory.md

findings.title: Verified postcondition collisions follow caller reference order
findings.body: verify_authoritative assigns each verified record result into observed_checks by name. Later verified values overwrite earlier values without contradiction rejection or newest-time selection. Thus reversing conflicting authenticated records can alter the final required-check result. Source-derived behavior; no operational reproduction performed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D183 Verified postcondition collisions follow caller reference order.md

findings.title: Authenticated receipts do not universally bind evaluated source content
findings.body: Outcome required-check contract is a caller-selected local file without hash binding to signed evidence in this function. Admission scopes its four receipts to project/candidate ID without version/source digest. Resolver artifact integrity is optional and nonempty expected scope fields alone are compared. A signature authenticates supplied record content, not every external interpretation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D184 Authenticated receipts do not universally bind evaluated source content.md

findings.title: Admission security fact extraction treats absent true flag as safe input
findings.body: After a security record is authenticated, malicious_or_unsafe is derived using is True. An empty result supplies false rather than an explicit failed assessment-schema check. Other required provenance/license/test facts and classification still apply. Authoritative restrict can be accepted, which is distinct from unrestricted admit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D185 Admission security fact extraction treats absent true flag as safe input.md

findings.title: Signature verification and readiness probes carry process and filesystem effects
findings.body: Signed evidence, grant and certificate verification create temporary allowed-signers material and invoke ssh-keygen. Signing readiness generates keys and performs three sequential bounded subprocesses per probe. Probe resolves executable once but later signer helpers use bare PATH name. These verification owners are not pure metadata functions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D186 Signature verification and readiness probes carry process and filesystem effects.md

findings.title: Resolver integrity does not impose a complete evidence record schema
findings.body: Resolver parses unbounded JSON and accesses mapping methods without a root mapping guard; malformed roots can raise outside selected catches. It does not compare evidence_id with reference filename or require a full record schema. Signer trust and caller producer allowlist are checked separately without a signer-to-producer authorization mapping.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D187 Resolver integrity does not impose a complete evidence record schema.md

findings.title: Orchestrator completed can carry nonauthoritative verification
findings.body: Orchestrator imports verify, the compatibility evaluate_claims alias, and computes completed from verified status plus no unsupported claims. It does not require verification.authoritative. Signed authoritative outcome verification is a separate entry point and is not called by this path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D188 Orchestrator completed can carry nonauthoritative verification.md

findings.title: Contradiction warnings do not block orchestration completion
findings.body: Assembler marks support when any usable supports link exists and retains usable contradictions as warnings without clearing support. Orchestrator ignores package warnings in its completed decision and collects all usable attachment IDs, including context/contradiction relations. These records are caller descriptions, not resolved signed artifacts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D189 Contradiction warnings do not block orchestration completion.md

findings.title: Single-handler activation does not enforce execution duration or teardown
findings.body: Orchestrator checks requested timeout/tool-call numbers against contract, then calls handler directly without watchdog or ProcessSupervisor. Finally assigns handler None; unloaded does not prove processes/resources stopped. Handler resolution and activation checkpoint occur before execution try. Retry helper exists separately and is not invoked here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D190 Single-handler activation does not enforce execution duration or teardown.md

findings.title: Workflow scheduling claims and attempt authority are different snapshots
findings.body: execute checks admitted hashes through dry_run, then caches authority_claims once. _run_node resolves current binding/executor/grants again and signs those hashes without comparing them to original admission or cached scope claims. Worker validates fresh hashes. A later admitted authority change can therefore alter scope/adapter assumptions after scheduling; this interleaving was not reproduced.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D191 Workflow scheduling claims and attempt authority are different snapshots.md

findings.title: Workflow conflict serialization is local lexical batching
findings.body: Scopes normalize slashes/case/trailing separators and overlap by equality or slash prefix; absent scope uses wildcard exclusive. Selection compares only nodes in the current batch. It does not acquire cross-run/project claims or normalize physical aliases and dot segments. shared_effects_serialized describes this local policy.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D192 Workflow conflict serialization is local lexical batching.md

findings.title: Workflow retries reuse inputs and one consumed approval
findings.body: Approval is consumed before _execute_node, and the same signed host-consumed metadata is passed to every retry. retry_limit repeats failed attempts without new evidence or idempotency reservation. Output name/type validation follows the retry loop, so those errors do not receive the same retry policy.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D193 Workflow retries reuse inputs and one consumed approval.md

findings.title: Workflow fail-closed handling waits for the selected batch
findings.body: All futures are awaited and successful outcomes checkpointed before failed_closed, lifecycle signals or worker errors are handled. A sibling may continue through its attempts after another has failed. This preserves settled sibling progress, but fail-closed is a batch boundary rather than immediate cancellation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D194 Workflow fail-closed handling waits for the selected batch.md

findings.title: Finalizing workflow cancellation bypasses worker-exit publication gate
findings.body: request_lifecycle directly transitions finalizing to cancelled on cancel/stop and changes terminal_target. It does not verify worker exit or update run receipt there. The normal observer finalizer returns early for already-terminal state, so terminal label in this shortcut does not establish normal closure evidence. Existing test uses synthetic finalizing state without a live worker.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D195 Finalizing workflow cancellation bypasses worker-exit publication gate.md

findings.title: Closed workflow adapters run before approval marker and node-config checks
findings.body: Worker authenticates task and current authority before execution, but executes the selected closed adapter before checking node kind/config and host_consumed approval marker. Parent normally consumes approval before signing. The worker independently establishes current grant hashes, while relying on parent for earlier approval order.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D196 Closed workflow adapters run before approval marker and node-config checks.md

findings.title: Workflow effect fields are not an aggregate execution ledger
findings.body: Run receipt initializes attempted/completed/denied effects empty and effects_executed false, without updating them as supervised workers run. Worker likewise emits empty effect lists despite arithmetic/sleep and process activity. Declared grants are metadata; the actual adapter set is identity/increment/double/fail/sleep and does not dispatch arbitrary declared capabilities.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D197 Workflow effect fields are not an aggregate execution ledger.md

findings.title: Workflow head and final run receipt publish separately
findings.body: execute transitions running before writing initial run receipt outside its main try. Final success/lifecycle state is committed before separate signed run receipt replacement. Initial write failure can leave running state; final write failure can leave terminal head with stale receipt. Resource/observer closure is another owner and cannot be inferred from receipt label alone.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D198 Workflow head and final run receipt publish separately.md

findings.title: Disabled workflow edges and continued failures change dataflow differently
findings.body: A required port with incoming but no enabled edge becomes skipped only if no explicit input supplied it. Explicit input can satisfy disabled-edge port; enabled upstream value overwrites explicit input. Skipped or failed-continued nodes retain empty result maps and count completed, allowing downstream readiness while missing source ports can still fail later.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D199 Disabled workflow edges and continued failures change dataflow differently.md

findings.title: Custody reconstruction rereads verified chunks without rebinding bytes
findings.body: verify_evidence_custody hashes chunks; reconstruct_evidence_custody then reads them again into a ZIP without comparing that second read or final ZIP digest to receipt. Archive path/type/size checks still apply. Publication wrapper independently hashes critical subjects afterward, but the helper result retains the first verification digest. Source-derived race, not reproduced.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D200 Custody reconstruction rereads verified chunks without rebinding bytes.md

findings.title: Custody builder binds subjects after taking archive bytes
findings.body: Build reads each source into ZIP, writes chunks, then rereads certificate and subjects to calculate bindings. No source snapshot equality spans those observations. A changing source can yield a binding that differs from its archived bytes; publication subject checks can reject that later. chunk_size is not required positive, with zero yielding no chunks and negative reading all.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D201 Custody builder binds subjects after taking archive bytes.md

findings.title: External evidence verified means manifest and inventory hashes
findings.body: The validator checks contained outer manifest and inventory digest/bundle ID, without parsing listed payload contents. Inventory path comes from manifest and is joined without the same traversal/containment check. Strict mode requires available manifests, but an empty records list is not rejected by this function.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D202 External evidence verified means manifest and inventory hashes.md

findings.title: Feature acceptance verified is a metadata comparison
findings.body: Feature acceptance requires exact declared revisions/criteria, evidence-class and test-name coverage, and authority label equality. Evidence references and optional digests are validated syntactically; no file lookup, signature resolution, actual test result or time validation follows. The included fixture passes with an arbitrary SHA reference.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D203 Feature acceptance verified is a metadata comparison.md

findings.title: Portability projection excludes the main evidence trees by default
findings.body: PRODUCT_STRUCTURED_ROOTS excludes evidence and extension/evidence; historical/capture/ledger families have further exclusions. validate_evidence_portability uses that projection. A separate release preflight scan covers broader roots, and tests explicitly show an external evidence locator passing product projection while failing broader audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D204 Portability projection excludes the main evidence trees by default.md

findings.title: Current evidence index permits partial smoke coverage
findings.body: Installed smoke must bind expected artifact, engine identity and closure flag, but coverage_complete false and limitations remain nonblocking. Cross-platform dashboard fields are compared for equality, not individually required true/nonempty. The fixture intentionally returns valid with coverage tier B partial.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D205 Current evidence index permits partial smoke coverage.md

findings.title: Index publication and source identity are separate observations
findings.body: Engine identity hashes a filtered sequential tree, excluding mutable state/evidence and other named families. Index reads stat/hash/parsed metadata separately and publishes registry then versioned projection through fixed prepared filenames without shared lock/WAL. Invalid index is still publishable; failure or concurrent writers can leave projections different.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D206 Index publication and source identity are separate observations.md

findings.title: Publication verification mutates restored evidence and can fail after commit
findings.body: verify_publication extracts output before later subject validation and finally copies release tree into repository. Replacement moves old target to backup, publishes new target, then deletes backup. If deletion fails, exception path restores only when target absent, so failure can follow successful publication. Extracted output remains after later checks fail.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D207 Publication verification mutates restored evidence and can fail after commit.md

findings.title: Packaging and publication authenticate different certificate boundaries
findings.body: Package script requires inner certificate signature file presence, cross-checks installed proof metadata and signs/verifies outer custody. It does not verify inner certificate signature there. Publication wrapper verifies both signatures and exact critical artifacts before repository restore. Both boundaries belong in the release flow.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D208 Packaging and publication authenticate different certificate boundaries.md

findings.title: Fusion package dependencies bypass initial candidate policy filters
findings.body: build_minimum_package selects ranked selectable records, then appends dependencies from records after existence/kind/total budget checks only. It does not rerun lifecycle/risk/reviewer/input policy on dependencies. Conflict checks follow, but complete/executable may include a dependency that initial ranking would keep discovery-only.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D209 Fusion package dependencies bypass initial candidate policy filters.md

findings.title: Package completeness is narrower than requested task coverage
findings.body: complete equals nonempty selected and no collected errors, even if required capability terms remain uncovered. Selection is greedy, not a globally minimum cover. Contract/validator names are collected rather than resolved. Discovery drops navigator missing_inputs, while route constraints are retained in envelope but only max_risk is passed to discovery.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D210 Package completeness is narrower than requested task coverage.md

findings.title: Routing graph and corpus bounds do not establish semantic completeness
findings.body: Graph expansion seeds are inserted before max_nodes checks and sorts adjacency before elapsed checks; discovered graph-only nodes are not added to ranking. Corpus certification checks selectable IDs/precision with thresholds defaulting to zero, so absent returned results can pass absent stronger thresholds and forbidden failures. It does not test package execution or complete task coverage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D211 Routing graph and corpus bounds do not establish semantic completeness.md

findings.title: Task plan validity is self-consistency unless current values supplied
findings.body: Compiler does not reject incomplete/nonexecutable route packages. Validator allows empty selected capabilities and checks authority/effect containers without resolving strings. Source/projection freshness checks are optional arguments; execution envelope, Agent and hardware consumers shown call without them. Paired model/ranking maps only compare selected hash here; separate model validator is stronger.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D212 Task plan validity is self-consistency unless current values supplied.md

findings.title: Task plan persistence can retain partial final target after write failure
findings.body: persist_task_execution_plan opens final identity path with xb and writes directly, without prepared replacement/fsync/failure cleanup. A failed write may leave an incomplete file that subsequent exact-byte replay rejects as collision. This differs from atomic replacement and WAL protocols elsewhere.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D213 Task plan persistence can retain partial final target after write failure.md

findings.title: Capacity ledger corruption can erase accounting and crashes can retain leases
findings.body: PlacementCapacityLedger._read maps OSError/JSON error or malformed active container to empty state. Reserve can then overwrite with new accounting. Normal reserve/release is locked, but leases have no owner PID, expiry, heartbeat or restart recovery; a dead callback owner can retain reservations indefinitely. Matching groups omit device_index.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D214 Capacity ledger corruption can erase accounting and crashes can retain leases.md

findings.title: Placement promotion gates consume supplied evidence metadata
findings.body: Promotion functions accept predecessor hash shapes and passed/sealed/approval/reuse counts without resolving actual artifacts or recomputing predecessor digest. Observed decision does check observation self-hash, but later tiers have different checks. Tier4 production_authorized remains a metadata decision with automatic_migration_authorized false; tier5 still requires learning promotion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D215 Placement promotion gates consume supplied evidence metadata.md

findings.title: Placement publication chooses identity field by insertion order
findings.body: publish_placement_artifact scans reversed artifact items for any valid sha256-suffixed field and uses the first found as filename; it need not be the whole artifact digest. Existing file comparison detects mismatch, but absent-file check then replacement does not atomically reserve an immutable name across writers. Work-plane admission supplies scheduling, not file identity authentication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D216 Placement publication chooses identity field by insertion order.md

findings.title: Placement baseline selection can retain an ineligible current option
findings.body: decide_placement requires one keep_current candidate, then selects it when no eligible alternative exists or the best alternative fails minimum improvement. Current eligibility is not required for this fallback. Output is a keep-current recommendation with migration_authorized false, not proof that current configuration satisfies all hard gates.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D217 Placement baseline selection can retain an ineligible current option.md

findings.title: Decoded model validation omits constructor path and revision checks
findings.body: Builder contains resolved local path, requires .gguf and validates fallback revision strings. validate_model_attachment hashes root/path without the same containment/suffix checks, does not validate fallback revisions, and does not enforce schema_version. A self-consistent decoded attachment can therefore satisfy different conditions than one built through constructor.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D218 Decoded model validation omits constructor path and revision checks.md

findings.title: Duplicate model IDs can separate ranking winner from selected record
findings.body: select_model_attachment ranks model capability rows but selects next eligible_rows item matching winner model_id. eligible_rows includes rows that rank_models later rejects for unavailable/context/traits/privacy. Duplicate IDs can therefore bind the first different row rather than the row that earned winning score. No uniqueness check exists here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D219 Duplicate model IDs can separate ranking winner from selected record.md

findings.title: Explicit CUDA has a different benchmark gate than automatic routing
findings.body: route_workload requires benchmark validity only when policy.require_benchmark and requested_device equals auto. Explicit CUDA can route after compatibility/resource checks without benchmark/correctness evidence; test explicitly expects this. required_checks still contains benchmark_current/correctness_validated labels. Wrapper benchmark_current derives label presence and correctness flag rather than full benchmark_valid.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D220 Explicit CUDA has a different benchmark gate than automatic routing.md

findings.title: Optional accelerator discoverability is treated as executor availability
findings.body: _discover_hardware_details adds cupy/cudf/tensorrt backends from find_spec alone and may mark CUDA executor available. Those specs are checked even when probe_libraries false. Torch/ONNX child probes provide stronger observations, but arbitrary chosen backend still must support the actual workload. hardware_report valid remains true with unavailable probes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D221 Optional accelerator discoverability is treated as executor availability.md

findings.title: Hardware probe timeout does not bound every parent operation
findings.body: Child commands have timeouts and run up to three concurrently, but parent psutil import/sensor call, module find_spec and future result waits have no independent overall deadline. Subprocesses use subprocess.run directly without ResourceManager custody. Timeout test mocks TimeoutExpired and checks text, not actual descendant closure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D222 Hardware probe timeout does not bound every parent operation.md

findings.title: Fallback device telemetry follows callback branch rather than measured execution
findings.body: execute_with_fallback labels actual_device cuda whenever gpu_fn returns, without querying what hardware it used. RuntimeError text containing cuda/cudnn/out of memory triggers retries and batch halving, then unconditional CPU callback. No rollback, callback equivalence or RoutingPolicy.fallback_to_cpu check occurs here. Other RuntimeError propagates.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D223 Fallback device telemetry follows callback branch rather than measured execution.md

findings.title: Benchmark records bind software identity without routing comparison
findings.body: benchmark_devices runs CPU once, GPU warmup then one measured GPU call, with optional synchronization and caller compare/peak-memory callbacks. Software fingerprint is hashed into benchmark revision but route_workload does not compare it with current software. Correctness and timing are as trustworthy as caller callbacks; benchmark collection has no own timeout.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D224 Benchmark records bind software identity without routing comparison.md

findings.title: Local server start verifies self-consistency without repeating plan construction checks
findings.body: start accepts a ServerPlan whose unkeyed hash matches and whose declared model/executable bytes match, but executes plan.command without reconstructing it from executable/model/host/port fields. It does not repeat allowed roots or numeric bounds. A caller-created self-consistent plan can therefore have command semantics different from plan_server output. This is a caller authority boundary observed in source, not an executed exploit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D225 Local server start verifies self-consistency without repeating plan construction checks.md

findings.title: Readiness callback and started-event failures can bypass startup cleanup
findings.body: After ResourceManager spawn, start runs readiness_probe and _append started outside a try/finally. Exceptions in either leave the normal timeout termination branch unreached. An event-head write failure may occur after the durable event append, producing a different partial state than a probe failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D226 Readiness callback and started-event failures can bypass startup cleanup.md

findings.title: Healthy loopback response is not bound to the owned server process
findings.body: Health accepts a 2xx response at the chosen port while spawned process poll remains None, without checking socket ownership, loaded model or server session. A different listener can satisfy this check. Readiness and inference openers disable proxies but retain standard redirect handling; final response origin is not revalidated here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D227 Healthy loopback response is not bound to the owned server process.md

findings.title: Local inference session and model identity remain caller assertions
findings.body: LlamaCppHttpAdapter validates origin syntax, session prefix and digest shape, then checks request model equals supplied digest and sends a session header. It does not load lifecycle/ownership evidence or verify response model identity. Authored source search found constructor references in tests only, with no production joining caller from LocalModelRuntime to this adapter. Dynamic external consumers remain outside that search claim.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D228 Local inference session and model identity remain caller assertions.md

findings.title: Local lifecycle chain verification is narrower than its declared event shape
findings.body: Event loading reads the full log and verifies previous hash plus content hash, without enforcing sequence/schema/event type. The replaceable head is not consulted. Append fsyncs event before separately writing/replacing head, so head failure follows a committed event and can strand a temporary file. The eight-thread test verifies normal append order and unrehashed tampering, not all these branches.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D229 Local lifecycle chain verification is narrower than its declared event shape.md

findings.title: Local model compatibility does not prove runnable tensor or resource compatibility
findings.body: The bounded GGUF parser reads metadata and checks a nonzero tensor count but does not validate tensor payloads. inspect_model compatibility accepts supported architecture and any non-None context value. plan_server bounds context/GPU numbers without comparing model context limit or hardware benchmark/capacity evidence. Resolving input path before link checks also loses original-link traversal history.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D230 Local model compatibility does not prove runnable tensor or resource compatibility.md

findings.title: Local model status and recovered tree closure use different evidence
findings.body: status labels running from active resource record and last started event, without checking live PID or health. recover checks persisted root exit and completes its record before appending tree_closed true, without separately enumerating descendants. Normal stop selects manager or ProcessSupervisor based on retained handle; failed-start tree_closed uses reclaimed count without cleanup errors.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D231 Local model status and recovered tree closure use different evidence.md

findings.title: I/O paths require one matching type rather than all capability prerequisites
findings.body: find_io_paths advances when current type appears in consumes and adds each provided type. Other consumed types, dependencies, conflicts, authority and lifecycle readiness are not required. It limits returned paths but can explore a large frontier; rank_io_paths only evaluates first 4*limit candidates, so metadata ranking is not a global optimum.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D232 I/O paths require one matching type rather than all capability prerequisites.md

findings.title: Declarative parallel effect checks use inconsistent defaults
findings.body: validate_orchestration checks requested effects using contract effects when step effects omitted, but serial_steps scan defaults omitted effects to empty. Conversely, any two explicitly serial-effect steps with max_agents greater than one are rejected without checking if depends_on serializes them, despite error text requiring a serial chain. Runtime scheduling is a separate owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D233 Declarative parallel effect checks use inconsistent defaults.md

findings.title: Registry graph publication and source hashing are separate phases
findings.body: Graph builders read source metadata, construct output bytes, then reread source paths for manifest hashes. Concurrent source changes can bind output to later source bytes. Writer publishes six files sequentially without a shared reader/writer lock or atomic directory swap; validator later detects stale or extra files by rebuilding. Declared executes stage edges do not prove an invocation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D234 Registry graph publication and source hashing are separate phases.md

findings.title: Count coverage does not itself enforce unique owner records
findings.body: Registry envelope coverage compares sets of path/count_key pairs, allowing duplicate owner records to collapse. Schema, builder and consumer are checked only for nonempty values. The test adds record-count equality against discovered fields, but the validator alone does not. Discovery is top-level only with seven explicit exclusions; counts prove declared collection arithmetic, not record semantics.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D235 Count coverage does not itself enforce unique owner records.md

findings.title: Service golden validity can disagree with routing validity
findings.body: evaluate_service_golden_queries tests only missing must_include and present must_exclude IDs. It ignores routed valid and denials; a case may satisfy ID expectations while its route is refused. Empty case set also produces valid true. Production tests require configured twenty cases but evaluator does not enforce that denominator itself.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D236 Service golden validity can disagree with routing validity.md

findings.title: Service hydration budgets bound returned bodies after complete reads
findings.body: hydrate_service_skills first materializes all IDs, then reads each full file and hashes it before checking cumulative max_bytes. It does not validate positive max_records/max_bytes or require a successful route result. Body identity comes from catalog SHA; catalog validates counts/status but not contained ID syntax. These are trusted catalog and caller boundaries, not observed external execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D237 Service hydration budgets bound returned bodies after complete reads.md

findings.title: Project-map query freshness depends on its caller
findings.body: query_project_map directly reads retrieval index and manifest with a path/mtime/size cache and does not verify sealed artifact hashes or current source tree. CLI query calls it directly. route_task separately validates freshness first, then queries and rereads manifest; those separate reads are not sealed into one immutable revision. Stat-preserving replacement can reuse cached metadata.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D238 Project-map query freshness depends on its caller.md

findings.title: Project retrieval result caps are not full computation or context-byte bounds
findings.body: top_k and relation_depth are validated, but entire JSON is read/scored, relation expansion has no frontier cap, and returned summaries/relations have no byte cap. Hydration files/context lines are not range-validated. Duplicate IDs overwrite relation lookup; negative posting indices are not rejected. These inputs come from the promoted index and are not fully schema-checked here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D239 Project retrieval result caps are not full computation or context-byte bounds.md

findings.title: Impact traversal limits do not bound every reported consequence
findings.body: _walk initializes every start before checking max_nodes and marks truncated only when adding beyond node budget, not when stopping at max_depth. analyze_project_impact runs separate call and file traversals, then aggregates all related tests/routes/contracts/services. A valid result with truncated false may therefore omit deeper dependencies or exceed max_nodes across seeds and result categories.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D240 Impact traversal limits do not bound every reported consequence.md

findings.title: Impact invalidation adapter loses path detail and accepts missing revisions
findings.body: as_invalidation_inputs requires valid true and nonempty resolved_target, then emits a star from target to affected file/test nodes. It does not require freshness, nontruncated analysis, receipt hash or nonempty revision bindings. Affected contracts/routes/services and original traversal direction/path are omitted. Downstream graph admission remains a separate owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D241 Impact invalidation adapter loses path detail and accepts missing revisions.md

findings.title: Decision frontier is an unclaimed proposal rather than reserved work
findings.body: Frontier excludes closed states and truthy claimed_by but does not otherwise distinguish open, blocked and in_progress when blockers are closed. It hashes only ready rows, not complete blocker/closure evidence, and acquires no claim. Recursive cycle detection includes closed tickets; no frontier/input cap or finite priority validation exists.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D242 Decision frontier is an unclaimed proposal rather than reserved work.md

findings.title: Reasoning workflow validity proves quoted name presence only
findings.body: validate_reasoning_orchestration checks twelve quoted skill identifiers in raw workflow text. It does not parse stage order/dependencies or verify current package admission. Names in irrelevant text can satisfy this check. The project change-intelligence validator is stronger about four exact step tuples but still does not execute their owners.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D243 Reasoning workflow validity proves quoted name presence only.md

findings.title: Glossary no-issue validity can have no inspected files
findings.body: audit_glossary skips nonfiles/oversize files and returns valid whenever issues empty, even if files_checked zero. Alias lists/cross-canonical collisions are not fully validated; max-file-size stat occurs before unrestricted read and there is no aggregate byte/issue cap. Report consumers must inspect skipped and coverage fields.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D244 Glossary no-issue validity can have no inspected files.md

findings.title: Module depth evidence is a specific unbounded AST proxy
findings.body: inspect_python_module reads/parses whole source and counts public functions and public class methods only. Private/dunder methods are excluded; implementation nodes include nested definitions, annotations and docstrings. No byte/AST/time bound exists in this helper despite a test using bounded in its name. Returned metric boundary correctly requires call-graph and change-history evidence before architecture action.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D245 Module depth evidence is a specific unbounded AST proxy.md

findings.title: Incremental map facts trust prior cache and ignore changed text limits
findings.body: Mapper reuses previous file-facts row when declared sha256 matches current full file hash and adapter_version matches. It does not validate prior receipt/fact semantics and does not include max_text_bytes in reuse key. Increasing scan limit can therefore preserve earlier truncated facts; modified cache facts can be resealed when their stored source hash/version still match.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D246 Incremental map facts trust prior cache and ignore changed text limits.md

findings.title: Project call resolved flags encode lexical guesses
findings.body: _call_graph indexes each file by short symbol name, overwriting equal method names, and resolves callee leaf against local or imported symbols without receiver binding. Unresolved plain calls often do not enter external summary. Python relative imports from __init__ lose package context, JS relative resolver does not collapse parent segments, and duplicate Python module paths can overwrite via set iteration. These limits propagate into impact and test associations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D247 Project call resolved flags encode lexical guesses.md

findings.title: Source inventory hashes and parsed facts are not captured atomically
findings.body: bounded_walk records file size before _sha_file streams content, then _scan_file separately opens text and stats again. There is no before/after identity check or final two-tree source equality check before promotion. Staged validation checks map artifacts with freshness disabled. Concurrent source changes can therefore separate inventory metadata, recorded hash and derived facts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D248 Source inventory hashes and parsed facts are not captured atomically.md

findings.title: Full map validation omits checks present in quick receipt validation
findings.body: validate_project_map hashes only entries supplied by receipt.file_sha256 without requiring every required file be listed; it does not verify receipt self-hash or recompute map_revision. It checks fact/inventory path sets without matching each fact source hash. project_map_status quick mode additionally verifies receipt self-hash and required hash names, but not file bytes. Thus full and quick checks are different sets rather than a strict stronger/weaker pair.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D249 Full map validation omits checks present in quick receipt validation.md

findings.title: Requested map freshness can be skipped while validity remains true
findings.body: When check_freshness true and recorded project_root is unavailable, validator appends a warning instead of an error. Impact analysis checks valid and later reports freshness_checked from requested require_fresh flag, so the result can label freshness checked although source walk was skipped. Task-routing root/revision feature checks impose additional caller conditions but do not change this validator behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D250 Requested map freshness can be skipped while validity remains true.md

findings.title: Map replacement and final receipt are separate publication boundaries
findings.body: After staged validation, builder moves old output into history, then moves stage into output, then rewrites promoted receipt in place. If new promotion fails, old output is not restored; if receipt write fails, new output already exists. Exception path preserves remaining stage but not an atomic rollback. Exclusive lock uses file existence with no liveness recovery and is written before the main try/finally.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D251 Map replacement and final receipt are separate publication boundaries.md

findings.title: Git discovery failure changes mapper corpus and captures before bounding
findings.body: Git command captures complete stdout/stderr with subprocess.run before checking stdout byte/file limits; timeout is 30 seconds and process is not directly registered with ResourceManager. Any captured-limit/command failure falls back to PX default exclusions, potentially adding Git-ignored paths that are not otherwise excluded. Manifest records fallback and freshness reuses that recorded policy.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D252 Git discovery failure changes mapper corpus and captures before bounding.md

findings.title: Scanner language coverage and retained text vary across adapters
findings.body: Python AST records include nested scope approximations; JS/other-language regex can match comments/strings and captures declaration-span rather than full function body. C/C++/Swift are classified source but have no symbol scanner here. Compose parser falls back on any exception without a dedicated parse-warning signal. Origin URLs/config key values are constrained, but Docker entrypoint text, Compose image/build/ports and headings are retained and are not universally content-redacted.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D253 Scanner language coverage and retained text vary across adapters.md

findings.title: Filesystem walk limits exclude directory count and pre-limit listing memory
findings.body: bounded_walk materializes/sorts each directory before checking per-entry file/depth/stat-byte limits, and has no directory count or global time cap. Link policy uses DirEntry.is_symlink without explicit all-reparse classification. Returned logical paths are opened later by consumers, so containment checks do not pin later file identity. Positive limits are not strict integer/finite validation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D254 Filesystem walk limits exclude directory count and pre-limit listing memory.md

findings.title: Project retrieval relations are entity links rather than the full project graph
findings.body: _retrieval_index accepts dependency_graph and architecture but does not consume their edges. It links files to contained symbols/routes and shared configuration/integration entities. Service IDs are based only on service name; equal names across Compose files collapse in graph/index dictionaries. Whole-file documents span the full scanned line count and can produce broad hydration ranges despite a small top_k.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D255 Project retrieval relations are entity links rather than the full project graph.md

findings.title: Core navigation risk can differ from declared contract risk
findings.body: navigation_index assigns R1 when effects subset read_local and R2 otherwise, ignoring contract risk. Skill adapter instead uses declared risk when present. Routing the same capability through different metadata adapters can therefore expose different risk information; adapter calls do not themselves invoke validate_registry.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D256 Core navigation risk can differ from declared contract risk.md

findings.title: Discovery source convergence includes shared semantic metadata
findings.body: skill_navigation_index loads semantic index and merges its description/synonyms/concepts and relationship fields. skill_discovery_sources also returns semantic_navigation_index as a separate source. Source-count agreement downstream is therefore partially correlated; it is not four independent observations of capability quality.
