findings.note: 05 Findings/D257 Discovery source convergence includes shared semantic metadata.md

findings.title: Navigation quality scores encode declarations and file presence
findings.body: Skill validation_coverage becomes 1 when package tests path is a file; evidence_quality needs truthy evidence plus current label. Agency validation/contract coverage are constant 1 and evidence quality only needs body/manifest hash fields present, without fetching those bytes. These values contribute metadata ranking rather than passed validation receipts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D258 Navigation quality scores encode declarations and file presence.md

findings.title: Installed declared-file availability intentionally accepts omitted source assets
findings.body: resolve_declared_path returns None for extension/tests/scripts in non-source layout and declared_file_available treats None as available. Runtime/builders redirect to installed module locations. Tests explicitly require the exemption. Consumers must not interpret this result as proof the referenced file shipped; navigation adapters that directly root-join paths have different behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D259 Installed declared-file availability intentionally accepts omitted source assets.md

findings.title: Operational source coverage can pass without behavioral evidence
findings.body: validate_source_coverage checks state labels, IDs and only listed owners/contracts/tests/skills. Empty lists and empty controls have no independent rejection, allowed state vocabulary is supplied by document, and no execution receipt is resolved. Required controls need operational/operational_bounded label, which alone is not demonstrated behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D260 Operational source coverage can pass without behavioral evidence.md

findings.title: Startup configuration does not validate every policy field
findings.body: Config enforces exact safety booleans, positive integer budgets and nonnegative retries, but leaves default effect and effect collections without vocabulary/type validation. Missing retry_requires_new_evidence becomes false; ID/version/mode and deferred set may be empty. Actual budget and policy enforcement remain consumer responsibilities.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D261 Startup configuration does not validate every policy field.md

findings.title: Schema constant and uniqueness checks use different Python comparisons
findings.body: Instance const/enum use Python equality, where boolean True compares equal to numeric 1; uniqueItems compares JSON-serialized representations, distinguishing numeric 1 and 1.0. Explicit integer type rejects booleans, as tested, but that does not change const/enum rules without such type constraints. Unruled additional values are not recursively checked for nonfinite or non-JSON Python values.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D262 Schema constant and uniqueness checks use different Python comparisons.md

findings.title: Schema reference admission and use are separate unsealed reads
findings.body: Schema admission restricts local reference paths, links/junctions, cycles and reference depth, but _errors reloads external documents during evaluation. contract_digest also rereads bytes after dependency discovery. No immutable snapshot binds these phases, and reference depth64 does not bound object nesting, repeated-reference expansion, full-file bytes or regex execution time.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D263 Schema reference admission and use are separate unsealed reads.md

findings.title: Contract corpus fixtures are narrow checks with shared implementation
findings.body: Corpus generates a minimal positive and checks it using the same interpreter, plus empty-object negative only where required fields exist. Ownership records keyed by path overwrite duplicates and referenced producer/test lists need not be nonempty. build_minimal_instance itself returns an unvalidated candidate; integer fixture generation casts multipleOf to int, so an admitted positive fraction can become zero. These are source-observed limits, not a fresh conformance test.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D264 Contract corpus fixtures are narrow checks with shared implementation.md

findings.title: Management state and human templates have different acceptance projections
findings.body: Generator accepts any nonempty all-true human_acceptance mapping and can mark brief accepted while generic markdown retains pending/unconfirmed text. Validator checks required documents exist and selected state/schema invariants, not their content agreement or live repository identity. Commissioning may enforce stronger questionnaire rules upstream.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D265 Management state and human templates have different acceptance projections.md

findings.title: Lease and switch checks describe controls rather than performing them
findings.body: authorize_lease checks existing writable foreign project leases only in the same session and does not persist reservations or compare path conflicts across sessions. Switch checks caller truthy teardown flags and same workspace/different projects. switch_project appends an active event without performing actual rebind; workspace manager is a separate owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D266 Lease and switch checks describe controls rather than performing them.md

findings.title: Signed transfer receipts are not bound to the bytes copied
findings.body: Four signed references require transfer ID, source/destination project, producer/type/freshness and accepted result. No package content digest is compared. import_transfer checks both paths lie inside workspace, not that they belong to the named projects, and hashes actual content after copy. A receipt for the same transfer/project IDs does not by itself identify those copied bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D267 Signed transfer receipts are not bound to the bytes copied.md

findings.title: Promotion source containment does not contain constructed release target
findings.body: promote_capability validates staged source and hash, then joins shared_root with caller capability_id and version without rejecting absolute/parent components or checking final containment. Source validation and destination namespace validation are separate obligations. No operational reproduction was performed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D268 Promotion source containment does not contain constructed release target.md

findings.title: Copy acceptance and final event publication are separate effects
findings.body: Guarded change, promotion and transfer check destination absence before copy2; no exclusive destination creation or transaction spans the collision check, copy, verification and event append. A concurrent target creation can be overwritten and later event failure can leave copied files. Approval/test strings and booleans in change/promotion are caller evidence, unlike transfer reference resolution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D269 Copy acceptance and final event publication are separate effects.md

findings.title: Quarantine verifies known files rather than exact current tree equality
findings.body: quarantine_candidates inventories files once and rehashes those known entries before moving each candidate. New directory members and empty directory changes are not added to that comparison. expected_sha256 is optional and partial; the stream wrapper omits it. This function does not implement two matching full-tree snapshots or a fresh exact pre-move denominator.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D270 Quarantine verifies known files rather than exact current tree equality.md

findings.title: Quarantine rollback stops before final event and commit marker
findings.body: Move/hash/moved-journal failures enter compensation, but project event and committed journal are written afterward. Their failure can leave a moved tree without committed marker. Replay trusts existing marker presence and current inventory hashes, and its early path precedes accumulated rejection checks. The interruption-named test only repeats caught synchronous move rollback, not process death or final publication failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D271 Quarantine rollback stops before final event and commit marker.md

findings.title: Recovery compensation does not span final preservation and evidence
findings.body: After prepared-copy verification and replacement, recovery leaves its try block before moving rollback artifact into quarantine and publishing event/commit. Failures there do not restore old destination. Existing interrupted transaction restores rollback only when destination absent, then escalates even if no restoration occurred. With no previous destination, a failure after replacement can retain the new file. Commit replay checks marker presence and destination hash without authenticating marker body.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D272 Recovery compensation does not span final preservation and evidence.md

findings.title: Stream checkpoint writes precede effect approval
findings.body: execute_project_stream writes preflight checkpoint before checking handler effects or explicit approval. _append_checkpoint joins caller correlation_id directly, counts files for sequence, uses exclusive open but has no chain/fsync or primitive-level containment. Workspace caller supplies a governed context; direct primitive does not independently provide that boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D273 Stream checkpoint writes precede effect approval.md

findings.title: Stream timeout is observed after synchronous handler returns
findings.body: timeout_seconds is range-checked but no timer preempts handler. Only after handler returns does elapsed time or expired lease produce failed result; prior side effects remain. The test sleeps beyond budget and asserts failure after return. Handler lookup uses workflow ID and optional replacement mapping; binding handler string is a report label rather than callable identity verification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D274 Stream timeout is observed after synchronous handler returns.md

findings.title: Nested rejected operation can still yield completed stream
findings.body: Final reducer asks whether workflow outcome names are present, not whether their nested decisions accepted. Wrappers always return expected key around guarded-change rejected, incident escalated, health score or other result. Workspace run_workflow_request then maps completed to valid. This is structural completion and must remain distinct from semantic operation success.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D275 Nested rejected operation can still yield completed stream.md

findings.title: Resume comparison does not authenticate or resume the operation
findings.body: validate_checkpoint_resume compares identity, four repository values and effect set plus lost approval, with absent repository fields comparing equal. It does not check workflow ID, payload digest, lease/timeout, tool/skill revisions or record authentication. The function is not called by execute_project_stream and no authored-runtime caller was found; it returns a comparison result, not continuation execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D276 Resume comparison does not authenticate or resume the operation.md

findings.title: Certifying health and passed resilience retain metadata-only scope
findings.body: project_health sets certifying when none of six metrics are unknown, so complete zero scores still satisfy that flag. evaluate_resilience checks supplied digital-twin/approval/rollback/outcome assertions and evidence labels; it does not inject faults. dispatch_workstreams creates a fresh scheduler each call and returns assignments without executing workers.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D277 Certifying health and passed resilience retain metadata-only scope.md

findings.title: Candidate memory publication is sequential across stream completion
findings.body: memory_ingest_distill compiles bundle, skips existing memory IDs and appends candidate notes one by one; later append or outer checkpoint failure leaves earlier notes. Maintenance separately builds, validates and promotes index; candidate retrieval remains disabled pending certification. These boundaries connect foundry, vault and stream status without a single all-or-nothing ingest transaction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D278 Candidate memory publication is sequential across stream completion.md

findings.title: Workspace caller strengthens transfer path ownership
findings.body: JSON materializer looks up registered source project, requires active project as destination and resolves source/destination beneath those separate roots. This closes the direct import_transfer workspace-only path gap for this entrypoint. Four receipts still do not bind content bytes. Dedicated lifecycle commands bypass generic stream workflow routes intentionally.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D279 Workspace caller strengthens transfer path ownership.md

findings.title: Workspace recovery and cleanup defaults conflict with primitive roots
findings.body: For project workspace/projects/alpha, materializer chooses transaction_root workspace/projects_tracking/transactions/projectID and quarantine beneath workspace/repo_quarantine. Control primitives require transactions below active_root.parent, which is workspace/projects; quarantine applies the same sibling-tree requirement. The ordinary JSON route therefore rejects/escalates before mutation. Wrapper retains required output name, allowing structural stream completion despite rejection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D280 Workspace recovery and cleanup defaults conflict with primitive roots.md

findings.title: Workspace context reset is partly asserted rather than measured
findings.body: activate_project requires context_reset_confirmed for live project switch, writes checkpoint/revocation/new lease and evaluates one synthetic ContextObject denial against new scope. It sets other seven SwitchEvidence fields true. No host cache/tool teardown or physical root rebinding operation is performed by that evidence construction; host confirmation is an external handoff.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D281 Workspace context reset is partly asserted rather than measured.md

findings.title: Workspace event and projection publication can diverge on failure
findings.body: Session creation/renewal/release event precedes projection replacement; admission and lifecycle registry replacement precede their event. Registry and seal also replace separately. Readers do not share mutation lock and may see mismatch. Decorators detect changed config after function returns, with no rollback of completed effects; the test checks the raised error only.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D282 Workspace event and projection publication can diverge on failure.md

findings.title: Registry and repeated session reads do not share one pinned snapshot
findings.body: Config reader compares original bytes and seal again, but registry reader parses bytes then separately hashes path and compares seal. Session active-set path validates full event history, then calls _verified_session for each session which validates full history again. A short status result can therefore perform repeated whole-history reads and combine separate observation times.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D283 Registry and repeated session reads do not share one pinned snapshot.md

findings.title: Workspace preview and idempotency do not precommit an operation
findings.body: run_workflow_request returns preview before payload shape/path/timeout checks. It writes idempotency receipt only after handler returns, so failure before receipt publication permits retrying effects. Existing receipt replay compares request hash and trusts recorded result; it does not verify checkpoint hashes, current handler revision or receipt authentication. Current active session is required before replay.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D284 Workspace preview and idempotency do not precommit an operation.md

findings.title: Projection rebuild compensation is narrower than atomic publication
findings.body: Rebuild replaces registry, seal and sessions sequentially and restores only targets that existed before call. Unexpected session files remain; newly created session targets are not removed on rollback. Final committed record, recovered-intent events and dashboard follow the compensating block. The atomic-named test verifies bytes after caught exception, not reader isolation or process-kill recovery.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D285 Projection rebuild compensation is narrower than atomic publication.md

findings.title: Workspace rebuild and normal replay interpret some lifecycle fields differently
findings.body: Normal session replay verifies renewal lease ID and pending operations remain unresolved after session-revoked. Rebuild renewal omits lease-ID check and counts session-revoked/expired operation IDs completed; revision also increments for renew/revoke unlike normal registry update path. Rebuild is therefore a separate interpretation, not exact replay of every normal projection counter and pending-intent rule.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D286 Workspace rebuild and normal replay interpret some lifecycle fields differently.md

findings.title: Canonical browser trusts active sessions and shadows source filter output
findings.body: browse_canonical_memory has no caller actor/session argument; it searches each active session as its stored agent, allowing same-project multi-session duplicate rows. It loads/inspects up to 10,100 ranked results per session before global pagination. Local source variable is overwritten with a record source mapping, so returned filters.source can cease to be the requested string although wanted_source filtering uses the original normalized value.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D287 Canonical browser trusts active sessions and shadows source filter output.md

findings.title: Orphan memory classification occurs before the lock protecting moves
findings.body: reconcile_memory obtains orphan generation list before acquiring vault lock, then checks only that each directory still exists. It does not reclassify under lock against a possibly changed index head. Moves/manifest/outer event have no compensation across generations or final publication. Source inference exposes a race with direct vault index promotion; no reproduction performed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D288 Orphan memory classification occurs before the lock protecting moves.md

findings.title: Project event append can publish event before protected head fails
findings.body: append_chained_event replaces fsynced event before _publish_head writes exclusive anchor/history/prepared head. Failure in later phase leaves event/head mismatch, and next append refuses invalid ledger. Readers do not hold append lock. Adjacent authority is a filesystem trust location, not signed host identity or ACL setup enforced by this module.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D289 Project event append can publish event before protected head fails.md

findings.title: Empty event set bypasses retained ledger head checks
findings.body: validate_event_ledger checks head only when event_paths is nonempty, so removing every event yields valid empty chain even with old authority files. read_event_tail returns missing before checking head. Existing tests remove one event from two or rewrite an event while leaving head; they do not cover total event-set loss. No files were removed for this report.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D290 Empty event set bypasses retained ledger head checks.md

findings.title: Tail and intake limits have narrower scopes than their result labels
findings.body: read_event_tail reads and retains all valid events before slicing output limit. Intake walker max_files+1 allows a truncation result only for one extra file; additional files raise instead. Walked size limit is based on stat before later whole-file hash reads. Workspace substantive rglob is separate and not bounded by intake max_files.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D291 Tail and intake limits have narrower scopes than their result labels.md

findings.title: Workspace health depth depends on selected caller and transitive reads
findings.body: workspace_status runs project_check only when source_root is supplied; otherwise project validity covers listed hashes/bindings and session state. workspace_monitor adds all-vault scans, index and queue health plus validate_integrations(smoke=True). Its no-mutation docstring does not itself prevent transitive vault/workplane setup effects; read-only status and live service operational proof remain distinct.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D292 Workspace health depth depends on selected caller and transitive reads.md

findings.title: Questionnaire schema closes missing acceptance keys but not unresolved content
findings.body: commission and apply_project_brief validate exact eight human acceptance booleans and required ten answer keys. All answer values permit null/empty string, and accepted state depends on flags rather than unresolved contradictions/unknowns/pending decisions. This strengthens direct template key validation while leaving semantic acceptance a caller assertion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D293 Questionnaire schema closes missing acceptance keys but not unresolved content.md

findings.title: Commissioning preview reads complete skill bodies and can reuse stale inventory
findings.body: _skill_registry reads every active/admitted body to derive hash/byte metadata, though project scaffold copies only metadata. _existing_inventory trusts saved JSON without current-tree comparison. Metadata-only startup and commissioning preview therefore have different I/O scopes; the latter is not purely compact catalog loading.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D294 Commissioning preview reads complete skill bodies and can reuse stale inventory.md

findings.title: Scaffold collision checks do not form a concurrent creation transaction
findings.body: commission plans absent/conflicting files, then checks exists and calls write_bytes for absent paths without exclusive open, final nested-link containment or a project-wide lock. Concurrent creation/replacement between checks can change target ownership; later map/event/receipt failure leaves earlier writes. Existing owner preservation is demonstrated for stable fixtures, not all interleavings.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D295 Scaffold collision checks do not form a concurrent creation transaction.md

findings.title: Framework binding records certificate identity without verifying trust
findings.body: _framework_binding records authoritative version, optional certificate path/hash and revocation existence/hash. project_check compares this metadata with receipt but does not verify certificate contents/signature or reject revoked true. A matching binding means same current metadata; admission/certification trust requires another owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D296 Framework binding records certificate identity without verifying trust.md

findings.title: Commissioning checker accepts matching historical receipt anchor
findings.body: Receipt validation finds any event matching commissioning_event_sha256 and payload digest, not necessarily latest event. Producer publishes event before replacing receipt. A failure after event or restoration of an older still-file-compatible receipt can leave project_check accepting prior binding. It checks listed managed files without regenerating their full expected denominator; producer manifest coverage test is a separate guarantee.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D297 Commissioning checker accepts matching historical receipt anchor.md

findings.title: Brief update preserves history but publishes three uncoordinated files
findings.body: apply_project_brief archives existing state/questionnaire/dashboard then replaces questionnaire, state and dashboard using fixed next names without lock, fsync, rollback or commissioning event linkage. Regex can leave dashboard unchanged when Current state section shape does not match. Accepted state can coexist with pending approvals; returned applied does not independently verify all document agreement.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D298 Brief update preserves history but publishes three uncoordinated files.md

findings.title: Framework rebind valid status excludes unrelated project errors
findings.body: rebind_commissioning_framework filters project_check errors to receipt-related prefixes, permits sole framework-binding drift, and can return valid when other project errors remain. It intentionally preserves managed artifacts but does not revalidate whole project after replacement. History/event/current receipt are separate writes with no compare-and-swap on prior receipt.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D299 Framework rebind valid status excludes unrelated project errors.md

findings.title: Portable profile validation checks keys rather than routing values
findings.body: validate_profile requires local_models/cloud_models/sensitive_data keys without validating their values. Set validation collects IDs into a set and rejects missing known IDs but permits duplicates. Heavy-lane1 is a checked declaration, not runtime serialization; machine-path check is only selected substrings and reads file separately from parsed payload.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D300 Portable profile validation checks keys rather than routing values.md

findings.title: Missing world-state inputs can still produce overall GREEN
findings.body: Builder _read maps missing or JSON-invalid source files to empty objects. Overall health uses blocker count0 and empty stale list, independent of authority component UNVERIFIED or absent project/model/release inputs. Supplied source revision is attached without validating each source revision. GREEN therefore describes this reduction, not complete verified system health.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D301 Missing world-state inputs can still produce overall GREEN.md

findings.title: Startup loses world-state authority warning at caller boundary
findings.body: Without current_source_revision, loader compares stored revision with itself and returns wrapper UNVERIFIED/source_authority_not_supplied. bounded_startup retains only world_state and hydrate fields; CLI calls without revision and omits those fields entirely while returning valid true. No-current-revision startup does not establish freshness of the stored world projection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D302 Startup loses world-state authority warning at caller boundary.md

findings.title: World-state validation covers self-consistency and selected top-level rules
findings.body: Validator checks schema label, revision equality, self hash, detail flag, encoded size and forbidden top-level names. It does not validate all field types/counts/health vocabulary, nested private payload or external revision syntax. Loader reads full bytes before64KiB cap; builder reads all source JSON before producing compact output. Private-payload-named test only exercises stale revision.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D303 World-state validation covers self-consistency and selected top-level rules.md

findings.title: Startup count and worker bounds are not whole-operation resource bounds
findings.body: Capability, policy and catalog limits are checked after materialization; model/project data have no analogous count cap. Explicit tool_names bypass default candidate limit8. ThreadPoolExecutor limits parallel workers but waits for all callbacks without deadline, including at context exit. Configured coordination startup also reads retained events/memory, despite no skill-body hydration.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D304 Startup count and worker bounds are not whole-operation resource bounds.md

findings.title: Tool discovery returns locations rather than verified executable capability
findings.body: Alias loader drops nondict records, candidate values are stringified and family maximum has no1..8 validation. Probes catch OSError and return optional resolver path; no version/trust/function test or timeout. Startup default list is bounded, but selected-family resolver and caller override have distinct bounds.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D305 Tool discovery returns locations rather than verified executable capability.md

findings.title: Lazy hydration guarantees retained-state atomicity after full reads
findings.body: prepare recursively reads body/reference text before checking total active count and byte footprint. Failure leaves active map unchanged under RLock, as tests cover, but huge inputs can allocate beyond retained budget before rejection. This is an in-memory context commit guarantee, not a pre-read byte/time bound.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D306 Lazy hydration guarantees retained-state atomicity after full reads.md

findings.title: Catalog loader omits dependency closure and hash admission
findings.body: from_catalog initializes dependencies empty for every descriptor and only reads package references. Hydration checks descriptor active/admitted status and root containment, not declared body hashes, version, package admission or selected-task authority. Custom descriptor dependencies tested separately do not prove catalog dependencies are wired.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D307 Catalog loader omits dependency closure and hash admission.md

findings.title: Active skill cache does not upgrade references or recheck current source
findings.body: hydrate returns active entry immediately by ID, even when a later request enables references or source/status changed. unload can remove a dependency while dependent remains active. A selected-body cache and lifecycle/dependency authority therefore need distinct owners; no automatic refresh follows file mutation here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D308 Active skill cache does not upgrade references or recheck current source.md

findings.title: Classifier labels are substring routing hints
findings.body: ASCII normalization and term-in-text checks do not implement token boundaries or negation. Missing task-class matches default read-only and confidence is fixed arithmetic. Capability routing consumes these labels but they cannot establish allowed effects or semantic understanding.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D309 Classifier labels are substring routing hints.md

findings.title: Frozen package identity omits execution-relevant fields
findings.body: Requirement fingerprint excludes goal, dependency map and deferred work. Duplicate/empty IDs and dependency existence/cycles are not checked. Existing requirements can produce complete nodes while missing capabilities also mark them blocked. load_work_package reconstructs fields without verifying ID/fingerprint/frozen semantics. No production builder caller was found.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D310 Frozen package identity omits execution-relevant fields.md

findings.title: Scheduler pressure and ownership are caller-fed transient facts
findings.body: Missing pressure becomes0; NaN bypasses threshold comparisons and caller agents count replaces internal heartbeat count. Path normalization is lexical and omits canonical alias/traversal resolution. Maps lack synchronization or persistence, while project dispatch instantiates a new scheduler each time. This is local admission bookkeeping, not durable cross-owner capacity custody.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D311 Scheduler pressure and ownership are caller-fed transient facts.md

findings.title: Worker reassignment and loss do not prove released physical ownership
findings.body: Reassigning a worker can retain its old work ownership; multiple workers may reference one work. release removes assignments but leaves heartbeat entries used for agent counts. recover_lost releases the whole work and other assignments without stopping or verifying live workers. A timestamp threshold is not child-process closure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D312 Worker reassignment and loss do not prove released physical ownership.md

findings.title: Durable persistence can remove current state before replacement succeeds
findings.body: persist_state validates existing source version, moves it into history, then writes replacement exclusively. It does not validate the new dataclass payload before writing and lacks owner lock, rollback or fsync. A replacement failure can leave only history, and a newly written malformed payload can fail subsequent load.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D313 Durable persistence can remove current state before replacement succeeds.md

findings.title: Migration WAL does not pin the originally decoded source
findings.body: migrate_state invokes WAL recovery before decoding source or rejecting a downgrade. Exact original bytes are backed up, but no owner lock or expected-source compare-and-swap spans decode through WAL commit; concurrent replacement can be overwritten. Unsupported target versions are rejected before WAL construction, which is a separate earlier check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D314 Migration WAL does not pin the originally decoded source.md

findings.title: Resume metadata ignores pending approvals and selected capability freshness
findings.body: reconcile_resume checks evidence-reference membership, interrupted steps and completed idempotency keys. It does not enforce pending approvals, package goal binding, selected skill current versions or authenticated evidence contents. The positive resume test contains a pending approval and still expects allow.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D315 Resume metadata ignores pending approvals and selected capability freshness.md

findings.title: Recovery fallback precedes retry budget and idempotence checks
findings.body: After policy/irreversibility and circuit/rollback handling, an eligible fallback is selected before retry logic and without current capability/effect authorization. Trace repetition counts matching signatures throughout supplied trace. Retry backoff tops at32 seconds under exponent cap5. Decisions are explicitly non-authorizing and have no authored runtime caller found.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D316 Recovery fallback precedes retry budget and idempotence checks.md

findings.title: Coordinator healthy is limited to configured callback reports
findings.body: Empty configuration can report healthy. Event/agent callback dictionaries default missing valid to true; callbacks have no coordinator deadline or independent postcondition check. Dry-run version errors become migration-required even when version may be unsupported for migration. CLI and doctor configure different authority sets; healthy is not global runtime closure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D317 Coordinator healthy is limited to configured callback reports.md

findings.title: Shared coordination vectors prove only a seven-rule subset
findings.body: Node runner and Python comparison call coordinationConformanceReport/coordination_conformance_report, not complete validators. JavaScript transition checks project identity, actor, operation, event predecessor and exact operation-specific memory increments. Python candidate checks monotonic counters and hashes but not all those fields; startup performs different retained-chain checks. Equality on the shared vectors is narrower than full semantic parity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D318 Shared coordination vectors prove only a seven-rule subset.md

findings.title: Python WAL coordination guard is optional and only test-wired in inspected callers
findings.body: CoordinationPreCommitGuard has a definition and test constructor use; no authored production caller was found. JavaScript coordinationManager directly invokes its own guard before deferred/state/event/receipt/handoff publications. Python startup uses retained-state validation. These are separate paths, so a precommit guard class cannot be treated as universal production enforcement.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D319 Python WAL coordination guard is optional and only test-wired in inspected callers.md

findings.title: Python guard checks role presence without validating all artifact semantics
findings.body: Guard requires one exact state target, one event and presence of state/event/receipt/handoff roles. Receipt and handoff bodies/paths are not bound to candidate/event. Candidate validator checks before/after hashes and event self digest but not predecessor event head, operation, actor or project continuity. Startup event audit adds other checks, after any publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D320 Python guard checks role presence without validating all artifact semantics.md

findings.title: Coordination structured rejection does not cover every malformed shape or depth
findings.body: Reduced conformance iterates candidate tasks before full array validation, so tasks=null can raise TypeError rather than produce the intended report. Dependency DFS is recursive without explicit depth bound. Target ownership uses lexical normalization rather than canonical path identity, and actor equality does not require a matching active session registry record. These limits coexist with substantive cycle, budget and fencing checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D321 Coordination structured rejection does not cover every malformed shape or depth.md

findings.title: Retained coordination memory seals are optional and revisions are sorted
findings.body: Memory record SHA is checked only when non-null. Per-ID revisions from all stores are sorted and compared to1..N, allowing physical reordering while preserving continuity. Count, project and layer checks establish other useful invariants, but they do not prove authenticated append order or record origin.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D322 Retained coordination memory seals are optional and revisions are sorted.md

findings.title: Python startup audit does not acquire a coherent store snapshot
findings.body: State, memory and events are stat-checked then read separately without a shared coordination lock or final identity pin. Missing state returns valid configured=false. Byte caps bound observed sizes and event count5000, while session file enumeration and recursive DAG depth have different resource limits. Concurrent publication can yield a mixed observation or grow files between stat and read.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D323 Python startup audit does not acquire a coherent store snapshot.md

findings.title: Architecture invariant names can exceed their underlying predicate scope
findings.body: Tree helper conformance/task-model checks require files to exist, empty projection arrays satisfy all predicates, and release identity check only rejects a particular active/certified mapping lacking source digest. Parent-child-NA reuses evidence compatibility result. No authored tree-helper caller was found; registry names it as bypass detector. Boolean unit tests cover aggregation rather than these tree semantics.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D324 Architecture invariant names can exceed their underlying predicate scope.md

findings.title: Authority topology checks declarations rather than effect interception
findings.body: Python owner inspection accepts any unqualified matching AST definition, including nested names; JavaScript checks substring presence. Runtime labels are not vocabulary-validated and multi-runtime vectors only need to exist. Non-contract receipt identifiers are nonempty strings. No authored executing resolve_effect_authority caller was found; a declared rollback owner is not proof it rolls back.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D325 Authority topology checks declarations rather than effect interception.md

findings.title: Primitive resolution does not inherit exception expiry validation
findings.body: Primitive registry requires nonempty expiry/rationale and matching declared exception IDs, but date/wildcard checks live in primitive_lint.validate_primitive_exceptions. resolve_primitive_owner calls only registry validation. Names establish static ownership metadata, not actual route discovery or mandatory dispatch through that owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D326 Primitive resolution does not inherit exception expiry validation.md

findings.title: Duplicate primitive scan has a bounded syntactic denominator
findings.body: Default scope is runtime/scripts Python. Canonical leaf-name dictionary can overwrite collisions. Walker omits class declarations themselves, nested functions and definitions under conditionals; only constant bare getattr is considered dynamic ambiguity. Bare assignment aliases are allowed and federated owners are not exception entries. No clean scan can establish absence of every equivalent or bypass implementation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D327 Duplicate primitive scan has a bounded syntactic denominator.md

findings.title: Maturity evaluator trusts evidence metadata rather than authenticating it
findings.body: Highest contiguous level requires valid=True, exact caller source/dependency revisions and sufficient authority label. It does not verify evidence artifact, signature, subject capability, producer or timestamp. SkillStudio generates L0-L3 labels and forwards caller higher rows; its separate signed admission and tree binding remain real checks, but do not authenticate these higher rows.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D328 Maturity evaluator trusts evidence metadata rather than authenticating it.md

findings.title: Maturity level semantics depend on the supplied policy
findings.body: Installed policy requires installed-host evidence at L5 and external-authority at L6. General policy validator checks ordered levels, unique nonempty evidence types and nondecreasing rank, so a custom policy may weaken those requirements. Architecture helper adds an L5/L6 stronger-authority predicate, but evaluator does not invoke that helper. verified means at least L0, not all operational levels.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D329 Maturity level semantics depend on the supplied policy.md

findings.title: Semantic profile source backing is declared text and ID normalization
findings.body: Minimal ID text creates a positive intent and synonym even with no behavioral provides. Owner may fall back to admission_record string; evidence_sources are locator labels. Validator checks vocabulary/conflicts/guards but not source existence, owner implementation or maturity evidence. Effects/paths are normalized into ASCII phrases, not retained authority tokens.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D330 Semantic profile source backing is declared text and ID normalization.md

findings.title: Semantic index overlay and hash reads can describe different source observations
findings.body: Catalog/body/contracts honor byte overlays; aliases/workflows read disk directly. Contract JSON and contract digest come from separate reads. Catalog paths are joined without canonical containment. Builder reads whole bodies before compact output and stored loader does not verify freshness; exact-rebuild validator is separate and has no source snapshot lock.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D331 Semantic index overlay and hash reads can describe different source observations.md

findings.title: Golden query complete proves only supplied metadata expectations
findings.body: Each case checks required/forbidden IDs and result equality after reversing input order. Empty case corpus fails, but nonempty cases with no expectations can pass with deterministic empty results; duplicate IDs and string-valued expectation collections are not rejected. Report does not bind signed corpus identity or verify actual capability behavior. Builder/certifier scripts publish JSON by direct overwrite.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D332 Golden query complete proves only supplied metadata expectations.md

findings.title: Skill Studio construction and promotion preflight can recover prior effects
findings.body: Constructor creates authority/resource owners and enters lifecycle recovery. promote also recovers lifecycle and legacy projection journals before checking new approved/admitted fields. These are retained prior-transaction effects, so constructing this owner or invoking a rejected promotion is not necessarily filesystem-read-only.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D333 Skill Studio construction and promotion preflight can recover prior effects.md

findings.title: Strong skill tree framing is not a single immutable read snapshot
findings.body: Attestation has explicit path/count/depth/byte bounds, rejects links/reparse and empty/unowned directories, and length-frames ordered path/body bytes. Descriptor reads reject changed length but do not pin every directory/member for the full traversal or detect all same-size concurrent content changes. Verified copy rechecks source/target identity at later points.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D334 Strong skill tree framing is not a single immutable read snapshot.md

findings.title: Skill behavioral validation executes limited declarative assertions
findings.body: Runner accepts required-files, JSON/YAML object parsing and text-contains cases. It does not run skill scripts. Python leaf names such as get/run can classify unrelated methods as network/process; unknown dynamic aliases and unsupported suffixes are outside selected scans. Signed independently_derived receipt authenticates this checker result, not arbitrary operational capability.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D335 Skill behavioral validation executes limited declarative assertions.md

findings.title: Skill admission copies signed validation without rechecking current draft
findings.body: admit verifies receipt signature and passed flag plus caller approval/approver, then copies validation digests. It does not rehash current draft or check those digests against current package in this method. promote separately compares manifest and payload tree before accepting new promotion. A displayed admitted state can therefore precede currentness rejection at promotion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D336 Skill admission copies signed validation without rechecking current draft.md

findings.title: Promotion projections can retain different lifecycle and effect metadata
findings.body: Package/admission projections take effects from package.permissions, while validation allows package.effects or permissions. Existing TOML entry updates version/tags but leaves status/body/contract/admission fields unchanged, whereas native/package/admission rows are rebuilt active. Denominator equality checks IDs, not all corresponding state/locator semantics. Staleness marker is a declaration requiring consumer enforcement.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D337 Promotion projections can retain different lifecycle and effect metadata.md

findings.title: Lifecycle recovery is roll-forward rather than reader-atomic publication
findings.body: Canonical directory is displaced/replaced and verified before _bounded_lifecycle_artifacts validates all images. Artifacts then publish individually, including receipt in sorted path order, before final committed manifest. Corrupt image or conflicting projection can leave changed canonical with incomplete projections and an applying journal. Tests exercise synchronous exceptions and successful restart with intact custody, not actual process-kill at every boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D338 Lifecycle recovery is roll-forward rather than reader-atomic publication.md

findings.title: Prepared canonical after-image is not rebound to the earlier admission digest
findings.body: promote checks current_tree_sha256 against signed admission, then builds projections and calls preparation. Preparation freshly attests/copies canonical_source and records its new digest without requiring equality to the earlier current_tree_sha256 embedded in promotion receipt. A source change between checks can produce canonical/projection/receipt observations from different moments; lifecycle lock does not freeze external draft bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D339 Prepared canonical after-image is not rebound to the earlier admission digest.md

findings.title: Rollback backup rehash is not checked against original pre-promotion tree
findings.body: Rollback verifies current canonical equals promoted_tree_sha256 and authenticates committed promotion journal. It then computes restored_sha from current backup contents and uses those contents as new canonical_source without comparing to promotion_manifest.canonical.before_tree_sha256. A changed but structurally valid backup can therefore be re-attested as rollback output. This source path has not been executed as a reproduction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D340 Rollback backup rehash is not checked against original pre-promotion tree.md

findings.title: Rollback can overwrite post-promotion projection changes
findings.body: Current rollback reads authenticated old before-images, but does not require live projections to match the promotion after digests. New preparation snapshots current live projection bytes as its own before state, then writes historical bytes. Later unrelated valid changes can be replaced. The older _restore_projection_transaction helper checks before/after conflicts, but current rollback uses the lifecycle path instead.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D341 Rollback can overwrite post-promotion projection changes.md

findings.title: Lifecycle preparation retention differs from registered draft workspace closure
findings.body: Draft staging registers its temporary workspace and preserves committed-create truth through cleanup warnings. Lifecycle preparation creates .preparing and canonical .lifecycle directories directly; recovery retains .preparing entries and does not register/reclaim these through ResourceManager. _atomic_bytes write-loop failure precedes its prepared-file cleanup block. Retention can therefore include incomplete preparation debris distinct from durable signed journal custody.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D342 Lifecycle preparation retention differs from registered draft workspace closure.md

findings.title: Universal cycle policy and cone validation have separate gaps
findings.body: Graph builder compares DFS back-edge node subsets to allowed_cycle_components regardless cycle_policy reject/declared_components. Those subsets are not full SCCs. compute_invalidation_cone does not validate graph/policy and only examines supplied current revisions; omitted nodes cannot seed drift. Generated adapter retains edge endpoints only and expects from/to rather than generated SCC source/target.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D343 Universal cycle policy and cone validation have separate gaps.md

findings.title: Projection rebuild plan groups work without ordering or execution
findings.body: Plan returns stale records in input order split by cost/gate, with usable meaning no blocked list. Cheap stale outputs can still need rebuilding. It does not topologically sort or call builders. Registry cycle check deduplicates adjacency but increments indegree per duplicate dependency entry, causing some duplicate entries to look like cycles.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D344 Projection rebuild plan groups work without ordering or execution.md

findings.title: Projection reconciliation can refresh unknown output hashes without builder equivalence
findings.body: Only four known projection IDs are rebuilt for equality before revisions refresh; others receive current hashes. All-current staleness builder merely projects supplied metadata as stale=false. Known registry inventory builder uses no supplied root. Reconciliation reads separate observations and replaces metadata without owner lock/fsync; it must remain governed by the external ordered rebuild owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D345 Projection reconciliation can refresh unknown output hashes without builder equivalence.md

findings.title: Graph authority validates output digest but not current source revisions
findings.body: Graph manifest requires source revision strings to look like SHA-256 but does not compare them with current source bytes. Output digest and two-directory graph inventory are checked. Reconciliation updates graph/source hashes without rebuilding graphs, so these functions alone cannot prove output was derived from those sources.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D346 Graph authority validates output digest but not current source revisions.md

findings.title: Affected proof completion checks names rather than authenticated exact plan evidence
findings.body: Validator does not recompute/bind plan_sha256, authenticate test/section receipts or require focused_vectors. Negative proof is checked per card, not every negative case. Extra completion names are accepted, and an empty plan/completion can pass. Tests named exact plan acceptance provide lists without hash or vector proof. No authored runtime caller was found.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D347 Affected proof completion checks names rather than authenticated exact plan evidence.md

findings.title: Generated dependency helper loses one-shot inputs and fails self-loop formatting
findings.body: Declared Iterable values are traversed to collect nodes then traversed again for edges, so generators can be exhausted. Self-loop insertion yields an extra nested list; subsequent string join for failure message raises TypeError instead of structured RP-GEN-002. Tests cover reusable-list DAG/two-node cycle only. Casefold-only edge sort also leaves tied case variants without a full tie-break.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D348 Generated dependency helper loses one-shot inputs and fails self-loop formatting.md

findings.title: Dependency audit misses producer declared_required vocabulary
findings.body: Inventory builder emits declared_required for runtime YAML. validate_dependency_closure checks only required when enforcing presence in project runtime dependencies, so the generated classification skips that branch. Tests assert valid counts and separately assert declared_required, without removing YAML declaration. This is a concrete producer-consumer vocabulary mismatch.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D349 Dependency audit misses producer declared_required vocabulary.md

findings.title: Lock hash count does not prove unique artifacts for every platform
findings.body: Dependency audit counts --hash=sha256 marker occurrences and compares counts to Python/OS matrix sizes. It does not validate digest syntax/uniqueness or bind each hash to a platform wheel. Requirement names are parsed by equals splitting and workflow authority by substring checks. Actual package installation and resolved dependency closure are outside these checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D350 Lock hash count does not prove unique artifacts for every platform.md

findings.title: Generated equality gate can accept a matching invalid graph report
findings.body: validate_generated_artifacts marks its generated dependency check valid when stored JSON equals computed report, without requiring report.valid. A stored two-node-cycle report can therefore match an invalid expected result at this check. Release preflight separately evaluates the helper valid flag; these gates should not be conflated. Installed profile comparison can also be vacuously true when owner glob is empty.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D351 Generated equality gate can accept a matching invalid graph report.md

findings.title: Revision tree hashing and import classification have bounded scope assumptions
findings.body: revision_for_path resolves the requested root target but does not independently contain every nested file symlink and reads full tree contents without count/byte bounds. Import inventory uses stored packaged surface membership, AST static imports and current interpreter stdlib names, omitting dynamic imports. Distinct source denominators must be retained when interpreting revision or dependency coverage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D352 Revision tree hashing and import classification have bounded scope assumptions.md

findings.title: Learning validates typed commitments but accepts unresolved evidence hashes
findings.body: Controller evidence snapshots accept bare sha256 references without bytes, while path-plus-hash checks only identity. Trials accept caller winner labels; research independence defaults true; final validation checks reference/hash rather than interpreting a result. The typed parser recomputes records and ancestry, so consistency is stronger than independent provenance. Tests deliberately use hash-only evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D353 Learning validates typed commitments but accepts unresolved evidence hashes.md

findings.title: Direct decay can mutate the canonical head before rejecting approval
findings.body: measure_learning_reuse writes the suspect canonical head before calling _transition_learning, which checks approved, actor and revision CAS. Thus a direct method call with approved false can reach a write before denial when decay criteria pass. Studio API consumes host proof before dispatch, so this is a direct-controller boundary, not an established unauthenticated Studio route.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D354 Direct decay can mutate the canonical head before rejecting approval.md

findings.title: Decay and restoration have opposite nontransactional failure windows
findings.body: Decay writes canonical head then learning event/head; restoration writes learning event/head then canonical head. Pipeline CAS failure can follow decay mutation. Restoration head failure leaves a canonical pipeline that the decayed-only revalidation method cannot normally retry; final write also reuses a pre-transition head without canonical CAS. These interleavings are source-inferred, not reproduced here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D355 Decay and restoration have opposite nontransactional failure windows.md

findings.title: Revalidation does not resolve its fresh evidence claim
findings.body: revalidate_learning checks approval, a nonblank reference and lowercase SHA shape. It does not call _evidence_snapshots, verify bytes, validate producer/result or establish freshness. The positive test uses an unmaterialized evidence:fresh-validation reference. dependent_rebuild_required reports a condition but executes no rebuild.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D356 Revalidation does not resolve its fresh evidence claim.md

findings.title: Studio reuse cannot supply the richer dependency graph
findings.body: studio_operation forwards cumulative counts and actor to measure_learning_reuse, but omits dependency_graph and dependency_current_revisions. That route therefore computes the singleton default cone. Authored runtime/script/extension call-site search found revalidate_learning and resolve_canonical only in their definitions and tests; availability of their methods is not proof that ordinary consumers enforce them.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D357 Studio reuse cannot supply the richer dependency graph.md

findings.title: Signed learning readers and recovery enforce different history rules
findings.body: The normal learning reader verifies signed event/hash chains and typed nested state, but recovery additionally binds event pipeline identity, state sequence, initial evidence state, directory identity and legal transitions. Proposal history has a similar normal-reader versus recovery difference. A valid signature does not itself establish every lifecycle invariant.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D358 Signed learning readers and recovery enforce different history rules.md

findings.title: Knowledge source limits follow materialization and signed histories are read whole
findings.body: Source snapshot traversal sorts/materializes all files before checking count and reads each file before checking cumulative bytes. Signed JSON/history readers have no pre-read total budget; learning publication bounds projected state/history after materialization. Original source links are resolved before later symlink checks. These are bounded output policies rather than fully bounded input acquisition.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D359 Knowledge source limits follow materialization and signed histories are read whole.md

findings.title: Canonical knowledge commit precedes final proposal actor validation
findings.body: Promotion validates approval/base/source identities, writes canonical revision and head, then calls _publish where actor.strip is checked. Empty direct-call promoted_by can therefore fail after publication. Recovery rolls forward a signed retained revision without resnapshotting source evidence; that treats revision creation as the recoverable commit point.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D360 Canonical knowledge commit precedes final proposal actor validation.md

findings.title: Knowledge rollback replaces status metadata before its receipt exists
findings.body: Rollback CAS-checks current candidate and verifies the retained signed target, writes a fresh head, then separately writes receipt. It does not carry suspect/revalidation metadata forward; an unchanged candidate hash can still permit status replacement. Actor emptiness and target hash grammar are not early explicit guards. No rollback receipt recovery transaction is present.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D361 Knowledge rollback replaces status metadata before its receipt exists.md

findings.title: Pure promotion helpers are weaker than the typed pipeline parser
findings.body: promote_revision checks record_type, immutable/passed flags, validation hash shape and dependency equality, without independently recomputing every supplied gate or binding comparison to revision. The controller typed parser adds exact reconstruction. Standalone compare_revisions permits repeated evidence hashes, as its tests demonstrate; controller trial capture rejects phase-local duplicates.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D362 Pure promotion helpers are weaker than the typed pipeline parser.md

findings.title: Typed learning validation validates present fields rather than complete lifecycle states
findings.body: validate_learning_pipeline_state recomputes nested records that are present but does not require the outer state-specific set or enforce transition history. Missing optional components can pass this parser alone. Failed promotion decisions receive weaker semantic reconstruction than passed decisions; reuse reconstruction does not itself enforce cumulative history. Controller transition methods supply additional checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D363 Typed learning validation validates present fields rather than complete lifecycle states.md

findings.title: Learning candidate and admitted pipeline are separate commits
findings.body: admit_learning_candidate scans proposal heads for a matching pipeline/decision, otherwise proposes the candidate, then CAS-transitions the pipeline. A conflict can leave a linked proposal without an admitted pipeline; retry scanning supports reuse but accepts a matching proposal independently of its current lifecycle state. No atomic joint commit exists.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D364 Learning candidate and admitted pipeline are separate commits.md

findings.title: Cleanup learning compiler derives wins from selected success labels
findings.body: The compiler requires at least two failed and six successful receipts across two lanes, but does not pair observations or bind each receipt to the declared incumbent/challenger implementation. Only successful rows become challenger-winning trials; all reuse is labelled successful. It hashes the audit and section files without validating their contents and asserts research independence. Synthetic receipts satisfy its source test.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D365 Cleanup learning compiler derives wins from selected success labels.md

findings.title: Canonical authority and browse labels have limited enforcement scope
findings.body: resolve_canonical rejects suspect or revalidation_required true, but does not require authoritative true or a recognized current status and trusts the signed revision locator without a local semantic identity/containment recheck. Browse derives authoritative from status alone and returns bounded subsets with no pagination. read_only constructor mode avoids initialization but is not retained as a mutator prohibition.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D366 Canonical authority and browse labels have limited enforcement scope.md

findings.title: Summary cursor consumes omitted facts and does not enforce terminal closure
findings.body: summarize stops selecting at max_facts but advances end_event_id across every pending event. Later calls cannot recover omitted later facts through this cursor. Source hash excludes created_at; SessionEnd only marks final when it is last, and later events after a final record are still accepted. Number allocation and cursor read have no common lock or history authentication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D367 Summary cursor consumes omitted facts and does not enforce terminal closure.md

findings.title: Summary namespace sanitization retains dot segments and collisions
findings.body: Session directory names replace unsupported characters but allow dots; a session ID of .. can resolve to the parent directory. Different IDs can normalize to the same name and share an unvalidated cursor. This is a direct helper boundary; source search found no production caller exposing it as an external route.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D368 Summary namespace sanitization retains dot segments and collisions.md

findings.title: Memory timeout bounds waiting but not callback effects or aggregate concurrency
findings.body: StateKVGuard creates a new executor per call and shutdown(wait=False) cannot stop an already-running callback. Breaker state has no lock and uses invocation-start time for failures, so long calls can consume the cooldown before failure is recorded. Concurrent calls can race success/failure resets; no central worker or resource custody bound is present.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D369 Memory timeout bounds waiting but not callback effects or aggregate concurrency.md

findings.title: Graph clustering bounds retained nodes after consuming the full iterable
findings.body: build_graph_clusters materializes every node before slicing max_initial_nodes and iterates every edge. Duplicate IDs overwrite in lookup while enumerated_nodes counts the original selected rows. BFS treats edges as undirected, splits components at cluster size and retains first32 lexical terms rather than semantic novelty. Missing endpoints include nodes excluded by truncation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D370 Graph clustering bounds retained nodes after consuming the full iterable.md

findings.title: Memory repair steps are not ordered by the computed dependency order
findings.body: Planner computes a topological node list but sorts repairs by defect class then node ID. Every node remaining after Kahn traversal is labelled dependency_cycle, including acyclic descendants blocked behind a cycle. Citation values need only a nonempty collection and temporal values need no date semantics. apply is planning data; no mutation occurs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D371 Memory repair steps are not ordered by the computed dependency order.md

findings.title: Process verification and execution graphs are supplied flags and a linear projection
findings.body: Compiler trusts schema-valid outcome_met and failure verified booleans; evidence/checks are strings. It constructs each step dependency as previous index, while decisions and tools are ordered lists, not reconstructed causal trace graphs. Jaccard comparison uses every catalog ID/tag without active status filtering and chooses lexical greatest ID on equal scores.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D372 Process verification and execution graphs are supplied flags and a linear projection.md

findings.title: Process receipt identity omits mutable compilation inputs
findings.body: Receipt filename hashes the process record only, while compilation also reads current catalog and stores project/apply metadata. Repeating after catalog changes can trigger receipt drift under the same process hash. Receipt write precedes project state parse/schema validation/write; no joint transaction, lock or state CAS protects that update. Project commissioning is checked by file existence first.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D373 Process receipt identity omits mutable compilation inputs.md

findings.title: Research independence is citation-string diversity
findings.body: canonicalize_research counts distinct casefolded citation strings, not distinct verified publications, authors or evidence hashes. It checks source SHA length but not hexadecimal content. The positive test assigns identical source hash to two citation strings and receives multi_source. Bundle hash follows input order even though groups are sorted.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D374 Research independence is citation-string diversity.md

findings.title: Blocked research bundles still emit experiment-state candidate rows
findings.body: Source validation errors block the bundle but each grouped row still has candidate_experiment state. admission_experiment checks only that row state plus nonempty positive/negative test collections; it does not consume parent errors or bind bundle identity. Blank test-name strings satisfy collection presence. Result remains candidate-only and performs no test execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D375 Blocked research bundles still emit experiment-state candidate rows.md

findings.title: Clean-room workflow validation checks membership without matching each binding
findings.body: Validator requires exact operation set and unique step IDs, but each runtime_binding need only belong to the allowed set rather than correspond to that step operation. Contracts are tested for file existence, not schema contents or containment. Duplicate operations under distinct step IDs and dependency/order defects are not excluded. Dispatcher independently uses its explicit handler map.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D376 Clean-room workflow validation checks membership without matching each binding.md

findings.title: Refinery novelty precedence can classify changed same-ID artifacts as duplicates
findings.body: After explicit conflict and ambiguity, matching ID immediately yields DUPLICATE before supersession/quality checks. Canonical identities need not be unique; only the highest-ranked target is considered for conflict/supersedes relationships. Similarity is weighted supplied metadata, and quality uses caller evidence/validation scores, not measured content equivalence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D377 Refinery novelty precedence can classify changed same-ID artifacts as duplicates.md

findings.title: Refinery portable inventory separates walk snapshot from later byte reads
findings.body: bounded_walk captures file metadata and applies traversal limits; portable_inventory later reads entire files for hashing and rereads small files for secret scanning without a retained snapshot identity. Files over max_text_bytes are not scanned for secrets, yet valid means no detected findings. Digest and scan can observe different contents; size counters retain walk metadata.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D378 Refinery portable inventory separates walk snapshot from later byte reads.md

findings.title: Refinery retrieval validity omits failed no-result expectations and empty denominators
findings.body: evaluate_retrieval valid depends only on zero forbidden hits; incorrect no-result cases and no expected results can remain valid. Duplicate returned expected IDs can inflate binary NDCG beyond1. Calibration trusts supplied metrics/case IDs, need not require nonempty train/holdout sets, and can accept empty mappings at default zero improvement.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D379 Refinery retrieval validity omits failed no-result expectations and empty denominators.md

findings.title: Refinery certification and workflow checks do not prove execution
findings.body: certify_refinery_run checks supplied component valid flags, count parity, no forbidden hits and accepted calibration; it hashes the mapping without reconstructing reports or producer provenance. Its positive test passes tiny green dictionaries. Workflow validation searches quoted step names anywhere in text, without parsing dependencies, bindings or execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D380 Refinery certification and workflow checks do not prove execution.md

findings.title: Refinery staging does not refresh target fingerprints or require certification
findings.body: stage_merge_plan verifies self-hash and valid flag plus commissioned-state file existence and nonempty approval strings. It does not validate project state, authenticate approval, recheck target_fingerprint or require certify_refinery_run. Exclusive receipt write can leave a partial file on failure; replay compares exact bytes. It remains explicitly inert and grants no authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D381 Refinery staging does not refresh target fingerprints or require certification.md

findings.title: Foundry bundle identity does not commit all generated artifacts
findings.body: compile_foundry_bundle hashes only source records and merged knowledge. Calculations, registry capability exclusions, emitted skills/schemas/benchmarks and compiler revision do not enter bundle_id. Distinct outputs can share destination identity; materialization rejects any existing directory instead of reconciling it.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D382 Foundry bundle identity does not commit all generated artifacts.md

findings.title: Foundry confidence and relationships are heuristic line projections
findings.body: Repeated normalized statements add0.1 confidence even when repetitions come from the same source. Every source-wide wiki relation attaches to each extracted statement. Capability detection is substring matching over all statements, and emitted procedures/tests are fixed generic templates. Evidence coverage means a reference exists, not support was independently verified.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D383 Foundry confidence and relationships are heuristic line projections.md

findings.title: Candidate certification checks structure and Python syntax rather than tests
findings.body: certify_foundry_bundle trusts retained certification_errors, requires nonempty knowledge/skill fields and parses generated Python. It does not recompute source/bundle identities, execute named tests/examples, parse JavaScript, validate schema alignment or require at least one skill. Manually supplied dataclasses can bypass compiler-generated identity assumptions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D384 Candidate certification checks structure and Python syntax rather than tests.md

findings.title: Foundry materialization has partial publication and duplicate output identities
findings.body: Materializer creates destination/bundle_id before rendering/writing sorted files and publishes receipt last. Failure leaves an unregistered partial directory that normal retry refuses. Duplicate calculation IDs overwrite entries in the file map while bundle metadata retains both. Supplied bundle/skill IDs are used as path components without separate validation; compiler-produced slugs are narrower than direct dataclass inputs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D385 Foundry materialization has partial publication and duplicate output identities.md

findings.title: Generated calculation functions omit interpreter runtime controls
findings.body: evaluate_calculation checks numeric nonboolean finite inputs, exact variable set, AST64/depth16, magnitude1e100 and exponent16. Emitted Python directly returns the expression and JavaScript directly evaluates it with a modulo helper. Neither emitted function contains these guards; JavaScript division by zero and overflow differ from interpreter rejection. Tests inspect strings and execute only the interpreter.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D386 Generated calculation functions omit interpreter runtime controls.md

findings.title: Calculation units establish dimensions without scale or offset conversion
findings.body: Known units km/cm/mm all map to L, time variants to T, and kelvin/absolute Celsius/delta Celsius to Theta. Values are never converted before arithmetic. Dimension compatibility alone can accept mixed scales or physically invalid absolute-temperature operations. Unit parser also tolerates repeated/trailing operators rather than a strict unit grammar.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D387 Calculation units establish dimensions without scale or offset conversion.md

findings.title: Generated calculation identifiers are not fully validated
findings.body: Compiler checks the slugged function name with isidentifier but not reserved keywords; supplied variable names are joined directly into both function signatures without unique/identifier/keyword validation. AST validates names used in the expression, leaving unused declared variables outside that check. Compilation can return malformed generated source; later candidate certification only parses Python.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D388 Generated calculation identifiers are not fully validated.md

findings.title: Calculation-bearing Foundry export mismatches its producer contract
findings.body: CalculationPackage defines equation and normalized_dimension as a string. export_foundry_candidate reads item.expression and converts item.normalized_dimension with dict. Nonempty calculations therefore encounter an attribute mismatch before a usable candidate export. Existing bridge tests compile no calculation specs and do not cover this branch. Source-established mismatch, no product execution performed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D389 Calculation-bearing Foundry export mismatches its producer contract.md

findings.title: Foundry lineage signature is an unkeyed integrity digest
findings.body: lineage_signature is SHA256 of a public domain prefix plus candidate hash; signed_by is a fixed string. Validation recomputes the digest but authenticates no external signer. This supports content consistency, while source hashes/citations and candidate-only authority remain separate claims. Export filters missing source references rather than requiring complete reference membership.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D390 Foundry lineage signature is an unkeyed integrity digest.md

findings.title: Foundry Studio intake returns an object without staging a package
findings.body: SkillStudio.intake_foundry_candidate delegates to build_skill_studio_draft and returns its dataclass. Neither method writes a physical draft or calls stage_draft. Studio construction can initialize/recover other lifecycle state, but that is not persistence of this candidate. Authored runtime/scripts/extension search found no caller invoking export or intake beyond definitions. Earlier map wording has been narrowed accordingly.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D391 Foundry Studio intake returns an object without staging a package.md

findings.title: Formula registration executes supplied examples but treats property authority as text
findings.body: Executable registration requires assumptions, authoritative_source, validation, expected_examples and property_cases; only examples are evaluated. Example inputs are float-coerced and bypass runtime domain min/max validation. Infinite tolerance is not explicitly rejected. Unknown non-executable status is retained reference metadata, while evaluate requires exact executable status.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D392 Formula registration executes supplied examples but treats property authority as text.md

findings.title: Formula evaluation always computes perturbations and has distinct numeric limits
findings.body: FormulaEngine accepts float-coercible finite values, including booleans/strings, and has no input magnitude cap; bare Name return bypasses intermediate-result bounds. It computes sensitivities even without requested uncertainty. Declared bounds guide perturbation, but implicit sqrt/log/division domains can still fail at an otherwise evaluable point.
