findings.title: Object and array descriptor checks are asymmetric
findings.body: Plain object properties require enumerable data descriptors and reject dangerous keys. Array density/key count/symbol checks do not inspect element descriptors before every/iteration accesses them. Real webview structured transport limits expressible values; this helper alone is not a hostile-object sandbox.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D893 Object and array descriptor checks are asymmetric.md

findings.title: Encoded working drafts get shallow parsed validation
findings.body: Each encoded kind capped at 512KiB and total one MiB, then JSON parsed and envelope/schema/kind/draft-object checked. Inner draft structure is not recursively passed through inspectValue. View-state allowed keys also lack full type/enum checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D894 Encoded working drafts get shallow parsed validation.md

findings.title: Numeric and request-identity rules differ by operation
findings.body: Generic numeric fields need finite numbers but not universal integer/range checks. Some Studio operations permit missing requestId, while run controls/skill operations require one; start/test agent examples intentionally accepted without it. Handler correlation and semantic validation remain separate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D895 Numeric and request-identity rules differ by operation.md

findings.title: Studio and extension version grammars differ
findings.body: Studio caps numeric components at signed 32-bit maximum and validates suffix rules; extension grammar lacks that component cap. Enablement/uninstall exact targets check prefix/suffix at message layer rather than parsing full middle version; retained host token supplies stronger equality check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D896 Studio and extension version grammars differ.md

findings.title: Message validation returns the original object
findings.body: Accepted message is neither cloned nor deeply frozen. Static CONTRACTS freeze only outer object and nested arrays remain shared with action metadata. Normal transport may supply isolated JSON, but validator itself does not create immutable authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D897 Message validation returns the original object.md

findings.title: Host dispatch and view restoration are concrete separate callers
findings.body: Host validates before switch and request observation; panel deserializer validates saved view state and clears cached state on failure. Neither validation callback by itself grants a work admission or proves a later effect.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D898 Host dispatch and view restoration are concrete separate callers.md

findings.title: Action metadata describes intended boundaries
findings.body: UI-only and HOST maps label authority/effects/outcomes; build checks host message existence only. Some UI actions described as opening an editor can cause later controller queries or view-state publication. Metadata is not an exhaustive runtime effect detector.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D899 Action metadata describes intended boundaries.md

findings.title: Literal action discovery is lexical
findings.body: Regex finds literal data-action attributes in JavaScript files, including possible comments/dead branches, and cannot discover arbitrary computed action names. Exact missing/stale reconciliation proves agreement between declarations and that lexical set, not actual DOM coverage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D900 Literal action discovery is lexical.md

findings.title: Action artifact currentness omits source content identity
findings.body: Artifact stores action names/source filenames/contracts but not hashes of implementation files. A source change preserving literal actions can leave artifact bytes unchanged. Current control manifest later hashes referenced source files independently.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D901 Action artifact currentness omits source content identity.md

findings.title: Control source manifest authenticates bytes rather than handler semantics
findings.body: Checks exact lexical inventory path, schema, per-surface ordered-ID hash and unique IDs; resolves source files and hashes them. Source reference symbols/handler backend are copied or described, not AST-validated. Filesystem containment uses resolve/stat without realpath alias rejection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D902 Control source manifest authenticates bytes rather than handler semantics.md

findings.title: Control contracts have descriptive fallbacks
findings.body: Unknown actions and non-action control kinds can use source-owned-semantic fallback with label-derived effects. Host handler text is synthesized as extension.js plus message name. These relationships need caller inspection rather than assuming the string is a callable path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D903 Control contracts have descriptive fallbacks.md

findings.title: Interaction profiles and mutation classification use labels
findings.body: Supplied surface/control profiles can override inference. Otherwise regexes classify labels such as remove/run/config, even when an action only edits a draft. This is conservative metadata, not actual effect observation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D904 Interaction profiles and mutation classification use labels.md

findings.title: Exact action resolver can represent many instances
findings.body: No suffix means all same-action matches form exact class; row variant accepts any dataset key containing id/index/row/key. Multiple named matches can also be exact. This does not mean unique element identity or every instance exercised.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D905 Exact action resolver can represent many instances.md

findings.title: Attempted control IDs can imply visibility without a match
findings.body: Base record sets rendered to exact resolver OR attempted ID; visible follows rendered and enabled uses every over matches, which is true for empty array. Open/display stages then become observed. Caller must supply trustworthy attempt evidence; base projection does not prove DOM presence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D906 Attempted control IDs can imply visibility without a match.md

findings.title: Interaction completeness does not validate stage identity
findings.body: isCompleteInteractionChain checks thirteen entries and allowed statuses only, not exact names/order/uniqueness, evidence, hashes or timestamps. A malformed thirteen-entry list can satisfy this local predicate. Broader consumers need their own validation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D907 Interaction completeness does not validate stage identity.md

findings.title: Installed mismatch is caller-supplied to base chain builder
findings.body: hostSourceMismatch defaults false. A true flag blocks every stage; absent false does not establish current installed/source identity. Real walker separately composes source identity and many probe observations after these initial records.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D908 Installed mismatch is caller-supplied to base chain builder.md

findings.title: Contained walk covers only action controls and first match
findings.body: Manifest filtered to kind action. Each control opens fresh preview; only first matching visible enabled element clicked even when match_count exceeds one. DynamicRepair labels are specially unwrapped here, unlike base manifest locator/resolver.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D909 Contained walk covers only action controls and first match.md

findings.title: Contained before and after hashes are narrow UI projections
findings.body: Hashes cover first forty-thousand body-text characters, message count, dialog count and active identifier. They do not bind complete DOM, posted payloads, runtime effects or persistence. A changed hash is not necessarily intended successful action.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D910 Contained before and after hashes are narrow UI projections.md

findings.title: Contained exit success does not mean full interaction success
findings.body: Missing/invisible/disabled controls produce statuses but only interaction_error sets failure exit. Fixed 140ms post-click delay can miss late response/error. Receipt explicitly sets operationally_complete false, preserving correct non-certification boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D911 Contained exit success does not mean full interaction success.md

findings.title: Contained browser cleanup starts after context and page creation
findings.body: Browser launch, context and page creation precede try/finally, so setup failures can bypass browser.close. No whole-run timeout or network interception is supplied in this file. Receipt is exclusive-written after close; fixture resource ownership depends on surrounding runner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D912 Contained browser cleanup starts after context and page creation.md

findings.title: Installed smoke checks selected live surfaces and cardinalities
findings.body: Driver checks sidebar ready/render acknowledgment, nonzero graph geometry and selected live versus Python snapshot counts. These are concrete host observations when executed, but count equality is not semantic equivalence and geometry does not prove all graph interactions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D913 Installed smoke checks selected live surfaces and cardinalities.md

findings.title: Installed Studio smoke partly bypasses editor interaction
findings.body: Requires installed source modules directly, creates bridge/approval material and calls setup/creation functions with confirmCreate true. It checks catalog reopening and run outcomes, but receipt knowledge_ui_bridge_cli_backend true is not evidence of an actual webview editor click path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D914 Installed Studio smoke partly bypasses editor interaction.md

findings.title: Installed smoke assumes isolated ownership from runner
findings.body: Local driver requires receipt path and a workspace folder but does not prove disposable ownership, exact source hash or receipt-path containment. It mutates files/configuration/Studio state and starts host work. External runner owns admission and cleanup; audit did not invoke it.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D915 Installed smoke assumes isolated ownership from runner.md

findings.title: Smoke wait helper cannot bound a hanging predicate
findings.body: waitFor checks elapsed time between awaited predicates. A predicate consuming shell execution stream can itself hang past the nominal timeout. Debug wait result is not checked before exercised-live label; task timeout rejects but listener cleanup only occurs on expected event.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D916 Smoke wait helper cannot bound a hanging predicate.md

findings.title: Smoke event verification matches names rather than exact attempted correlation
findings.body: Operation Set comes from recent activity events; required names may have been produced by other activity. Test/debug/shell/SCM/extensions are reported but not all required complete. Extensions registration is checked while live mutation intentionally omitted.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D917 Smoke event verification matches names rather than exact attempted correlation.md

findings.title: Smoke cleanup and receipt publication are not one closure transaction
findings.body: Bridge disposal and key-env restoration have a local finally; test controller, terminal, task listener and configuration restoration are not enclosed by a global cleanup finally. Receipt write uses overwrite mode and occurs only after assertions; failed runs may leave no final receipt.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D918 Smoke cleanup and receipt publication are not one closure transaction.md

findings.title: Broad extension contract tests are mostly source assertions
findings.body: Many test titles describe live/governed paths but assertions match source strings or relative positions. A few normalization/context/path tests execute helpers with synthetic data; their evidence is stronger only for those bounded cases.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D919 Broad extension contract tests are mostly source assertions.md

findings.title: Hardening fixtures test selected boundaries rather than all host outcomes
findings.body: Coordination corruption and locks use local trees, process termination uses injected fake processes, and message tests validate supplied objects. Protocol-copy equality is source currentness, not installed-host execution. No fresh tests run for this report.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D920 Hardening fixtures test selected boundaries rather than all host outcomes.md

findings.title: Action inventory tests prove declared denominator agreement
findings.body: Compare generated bytes, source handler strings, metadata presence and synthetic row matches. Manifest hash-format assertions do not prove a clicked control reached backend effect or durable receipt.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D921 Action inventory tests prove declared denominator agreement.md

findings.title: Contained walker unit tests do not run the walker
findings.body: Tests exercise actionIdentity/matchesVariant and status predicate only. They do not launch browser, inspect repeated instances, validate exact stage names or verify receipt custody.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D922 Contained walker unit tests do not run the walker.md

findings.title: Transcript adapter planning does not run extraction
findings.body: Profile validates schema and optional tool root; adapter plan binds runner hash and argv but returns execution_authorized false. CLI ingest independently dispatches without loading profile, so profile input formats are not its enforcement source.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D923 Transcript adapter planning does not run extraction.md

findings.title: Transcript source link check follows resolution
findings.body: Explicit input is resolved before is_symlink, hiding original alias. Directory child links are excluded, but ancestor aliases and later replacements are not locked. File count/byte budget follow enumeration and precede full hashing/copying.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D924 Transcript source link check follows resolution.md

findings.title: Transcript identifiers can collapse distinct source relationships
findings.body: Source ID derives from first twenty digest characters, so identical bytes in different files have same source ID. Conversation ID is filename stem, so separate source names/extensions can share conversation. Writer/export dictionaries collapse those keys without uniqueness checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D925 Transcript identifiers can collapse distinct source relationships.md

findings.title: Ingest verifies copied bytes but publishes without exclusive final target
findings.body: Copies are hashed against plan before os.replace stage to target. Existence checked earlier, no final exclusive reservation, no fsync and no aggregate size recheck during copy. Failure retains stage under failed name; output parent aliases are not independently rejected.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D926 Ingest verifies copied bytes but publishes without exclusive final target.md

findings.title: Transcript span validation is numeric rather than textual
findings.body: Schema requires positive line bounds and runtime rejects end before start. It never checks source line count or whether record text/label is supported by the cited span. The immutable source copy preserves evidence for a separate reviewer.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D927 Transcript span validation is numeric rather than textual.md

findings.title: Verified transcript states rely on declared evidence strings
findings.body: Verified completion/outcome needs ASSERTED plus nonempty validation_evidence array. Strings may be empty and are not resolved/authenticated. Certain unconfirmed action states cannot be verified outcomes, but this is consistency logic rather than verification execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D928 Verified transcript states rely on declared evidence strings.md

findings.title: Canonical record writing trusts manifest before checking provenance
findings.body: Writer loads run manifest without verifying its digest/source-copy bytes first, then binds records against its supplied sources/queue. Records and manifest write separately using overwrite-capable write_text after earlier exists check; no lock/reservation protects concurrent writers.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D929 Canonical record writing trusts manifest before checking provenance.md

findings.title: Later run validation omits writer relationship checks
findings.body: validate_run checks source schemas/copy hashes and individual record schemas plus digests. It does not repeat record-ID uniqueness or source/conversation/queue binding. Resealed malformed relationships can pass this local integrity check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D930 Later run validation omits writer relationship checks.md

findings.title: Run source paths are not constrained by source schema
findings.body: ingested_copy is only nonempty string, then joined with run_dir without containment check. A supplied absolute/traversal path in a resealed manifest can make validation read outside run. Manifest itself lacks a complete schema validation here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D931 Run source paths are not constrained by source schema.md

findings.title: Export validates then rereads mutable files
findings.body: Run validation is followed by fresh records and manifest reads, so checked bytes are not retained throughout export. Unknown requested conversation IDs yield blank rows; duplicate conversation sources use last mapping. Output uses existence check then ordinary write without atomic reservation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D932 Export validates then rereads mutable files.md

findings.title: Transcript summary labels can overgeneralize a mixed conversation
findings.body: Any record with VERIFIED or VERIFIED_COMPLETED selects verified outcome for entire conversation, even when other records report failure/uncertainty. CSV quotes syntax through DictWriter but does not neutralize spreadsheet formula-leading values.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D933 Transcript summary labels can overgeneralize a mixed conversation.md

findings.title: Queue normalization and transcript workflow checks are structural
findings.body: Cross-queue transfer matches declared queue/term; reviewer/evidence are strings, not authenticated receipts. Workflow check compares step-ID set and unknown dependencies only: duplicates, missing intended dependencies and cycles/order are not rejected.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D934 Queue normalization and transcript workflow checks are structural.md

findings.title: Transcript fixtures do not prove extraction accuracy
findings.body: Tests cover dry-run, source copying, selected state/queue refusals, stable CSV and tampered copy. They supply invented canonical text and do not validate text spans, authenticated validation evidence, resealed relationships or publication races.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D935 Transcript fixtures do not prove extraction accuracy.md

findings.title: Audit archive exclusions are filename policy rather than secret scanning
findings.body: Inventory excludes selected directories/environment filenames by case-sensitive names. Root resolution hides original root aliases, traversal materializes before filtering, and payload bytes are retained in memory. No aggregate byte/file bound establishes bounded packaging.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D936 Audit archive exclusions are filename policy rather than secret scanning.md

findings.title: Portable audit includes prerequisites without proving readiness
findings.body: Prerequisite JSON must be an object, but no valid/ready result is enforced. Optional attestation need only parse as JSON; signature/trust not verified. Empty eligible payload can still produce archive. These are packaged claims, not certification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D937 Portable audit includes prerequisites without proving readiness.md

findings.title: Archive and checksum are separate publications
findings.body: Temporary ZIP replaces destination, then destination read/hash and checksum temp replace follow. Failure can leave new ZIP with old/missing checksum. Output roots excluded from inputs, but prerequisite/attestation output collisions are not comprehensively excluded; no pair rollback/fsync.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D938 Archive and checksum are separate publications.md

findings.title: Audit verifier establishes internal consistency only
findings.body: Checks outer hash, duplicate/unsafe names, declared per-file hashes and exact member set/count. It does not validate full manifest schema, payload byte totals, unique manifest rows, exclusion semantics or nonempty payload. Recomputed unkeyed hashes do not authenticate origin.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D939 Audit verifier establishes internal consistency only.md

findings.title: Portable archive verification has resource and shape limits
findings.body: Whole archive hashed before verification try and members read without decompression/aggregate cap. Unsafe-name checks are not an extraction engine; some malformed shape or encrypted-member exceptions fall outside caught types. No extraction performed by verifier.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D940 Portable archive verification has resource and shape limits.md

findings.title: Bundle CLI is a dispatcher rather than certification owner
findings.body: Unique label=path arguments dispatched to runtime builder/verification, printed result determines exit status with missing valid default true. Build has no dry-run mode here. Audit only inspected this entrypoint.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D941 Bundle CLI is a dispatcher rather than certification owner.md

findings.title: Exact lock parsing is narrower than package semantics
findings.body: Requires exact pin and lowercase SHA-256 syntax, handles continuations and rejects interrupted continuation. Name normalization lowercases and replaces underscore only; versions are nonwhitespace strings, not fully parsed package-version semantics. Empty lock returns invalid with possibly empty errors.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D942 Exact lock parsing is narrower than package semantics.md

findings.title: Wheelhouse hash membership does not bind wheel identity
findings.body: Top-level wheel bytes compared to union of allowed hashes; package metadata, filename/version and platform compatibility not parsed. One allowed hash can satisfy multiple pins sharing it. Caller may receive valid true for empty wheelhouse/empty invalid lock when no errors exist.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D943 Wheelhouse hash membership does not bind wheel identity.md

findings.title: Environment scrub does not itself isolate network or executable search
findings.body: Allowlist retains PATH/system locations and sets pip offline/config flags. Empty mapping uses ambient environment because of source-or-os.environ fallback. Offline argv construction returns a list and does not execute or apply a network boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D944 Environment scrub does not itself isolate network or executable search.md

findings.title: Toolchain identity can combine two different interpreter identities
findings.body: Optional executable path is hashed, but Python version/platform fields come from current running process. Filesystem case-sensitivity field is based on path normalization behavior rather than probing actual target filesystem.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D945 Toolchain identity can combine two different interpreter identities.md

findings.title: Support matrix validation uses declarations and text presence
findings.body: Compares project requires-python/classifiers to policy, then checks CI text for expected minor/runner strings. It does not execute CI jobs or validate parsed job matrix topology. Certificate platform fields are checked as supplied strings, not cryptographically measured platform identity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D946 Support matrix validation uses declarations and text presence.md

findings.title: Release environment validity and lock validity can diverge
findings.body: Validator copies lock errors but not false lock.valid as error, checks installed distribution versions and declared support/current minor. Empty lock can therefore yield valid true with lock_valid false when other checks pass. It does not verify installed package bytes or require current OS in the environment path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D947 Release environment validity and lock validity can diverge.md

findings.title: Portable audit tests exercise tiny byte fixtures
findings.body: Source relocation verifies archive independence; tamper test adds duplicate ZIP entry and exclusion test checks known names. No independent signature proof, zip bomb bound, pair failure or full manifest semantics established.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D948 Portable audit tests exercise tiny byte fixtures.md

findings.title: Release environment tests do not execute offline installation
findings.body: Tests named installation/network check generated argv/environment and fake wheel byte hashes. Support tests compare declared metadata; one local FileLock fixture does not prove all advertised platforms. This audit ran none of these product tests.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D949 Release environment tests do not execute offline installation.md

findings.title: External catalog checks are partial structural checks
findings.body: Loader checks schema/count/ID and selected deferred-state invariants, but does not validate all record schemas, candidate/bundle ID uniqueness or cross-record references. License data is returned rather than semantically verified.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D950 External catalog checks are partial structural checks.md

findings.title: External metadata limits follow full loading and ranking
findings.body: Catalogs are fully read, tokenized and sorted before output limits. Hydration deduplicates the complete input iterator before slicing; full record serialization precedes byte-budget rejection. Top-level body/content/raw_source removal does not remove nested payloads.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D951 External metadata limits follow full loading and ranking.md

findings.title: Metadata truncation can obscure requested identities
findings.body: Missing IDs consume selected positions. First oversized record stops processing, so later requested IDs may never be examined or reported missing; valid can be true with no returned record. max_records has no fixed ceiling.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D952 Metadata truncation can obscure requested identities.md

findings.title: External stage commissioning check does not bind project identity
findings.body: Plan requires commissioning file existence, not its schema/content or project identity. Caller project_id is not bound to resolved root. Source body containment/hash is checked, but no expected catalog hash or aggregate body budget is enforced.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D953 External stage commissioning check does not bind project identity.md

findings.title: Stage dependency closure omits unknown identifiers
findings.body: Dependency rejection concerns known candidate IDs not selected; unknown dependency strings are not comprehensively rejected. Plan digest binds chosen identities/hashes/collisions/dependencies, not full project root, current catalog and approval evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D954 Stage dependency closure omits unknown identifiers.md

findings.title: Direct stage apply trusts plan while CLI plans freshly
findings.body: Apply does not recompute plan hash, source body hashes, commissioning or dependencies. Frozen plan object contains mutable dictionaries. CLI stage calls planner immediately, so direct forged/stale-plan behavior must not be represented as inevitable CLI behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D955 Direct stage apply trusts plan while CLI plans freshly.md

findings.title: Stage receipt labels are not authenticated approvals
findings.body: Supplied evidence values are stringified and truthiness-filtered, rather than resolved and signature-verified. Candidate receipt is written without body installation, active registry admission or authority grant. No fsync or full cross-step transaction closes publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D956 Stage receipt labels are not authenticated approvals.md

findings.title: Stage and revoke plan IDs need caller boundary distinction
findings.body: Direct apply builds target from supplied plan.plan_id. Revoke accepts raw plan_id from CLI and interpolates it into path without portable ID or resolved containment guard. A crafted ID may select paths outside expected candidate directory; audit did not execute this path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D957 Stage and revoke plan IDs need caller boundary distinction.md

findings.title: Existing revocation marker is trusted without equivalence check
findings.body: Revoke requires source is_file but does not authenticate source receipt. Existing marker returns valid true/applied false without checking marker content or new evidence equivalence. Source receipt remains retained.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D958 Existing revocation marker is trusted without equivalence check.md

findings.title: External hook token is context rather than authority
findings.body: Hook checks enabled/event/evidence labels/reentry/depth. Token hashes hook/event/chain but not full profile, authenticated evidence or expiry; no consumption or execution follows. CLI valid envelope does not mean allowed hook decision.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D959 External hook token is context rather than authority.md

findings.title: Portable session filtering is shallow
findings.body: Sensitive-key regex examines top-level keys, not nested values. Retained fields can stringify arbitrary supplied objects and reference strings can be iterated as characters. No aggregate byte budget or authenticated session identity is established.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D960 Portable session filtering is shallow.md

findings.title: Session parity can pass while authority differs
findings.body: Comparator valid is based on selected semantic fields and excludes authority equality. It separately returns authority_equal, so consumers must inspect both fields. Empty or weakly shaped mappings can compare equal without normalized session provenance.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D961 Session parity can pass while authority differs.md

findings.title: Route rank trusts supplied measurements and nonfinite values
findings.body: Threshold checks and weighted score use supplied floats without finite/range checks. NaN can bypass comparisons; negative cost/latency can improve score. Authority/safety booleans are required declarations, not authenticated grants. Quality threshold then weighted score is not strict highest-quality ordering.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D962 Route rank trusts supplied measurements and nonfinite values.md

findings.title: External workflow validation checks quoted names
findings.body: Required workflow step strings are searched in source text, not parsed into executable dependency graph. Presence of inventory/license/search/stage/admission/certification names proves neither ordering nor successful operation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D963 External workflow validation checks quoted names.md

findings.title: External provider fixtures stop at candidate semantics
findings.body: Tests use empty commissioning JSON and fake evidence labels; selected schema checks occur inside tests rather than all runtime paths. They do not establish installed skill bodies, authenticated approval, hostile plan-ID safety, concurrent writes or finite route metrics.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D964 External provider fixtures stop at candidate semantics.md

findings.title: Security catalog count checks do not validate every relationship
findings.body: Loader checks provider/source declarations, 817 records, domain counts, risk classes and selected lifecycle/high-risk fields. Optional graph load checks count, not endpoint/relation uniqueness; without graph load, reported edge count is expected constant. Full schemas and all risk-count declarations are not enforced here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D965 Security catalog count checks do not validate every relationship.md

findings.title: Security discovery scores correlated metadata signals
findings.body: BM25, domain aliases and framework boosts come from the same catalog; they are not independent verification. All records are processed before top-k. Descriptions are opt-in, but other external metadata remains untrusted candidate text.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D966 Security discovery scores correlated metadata signals.md

findings.title: Security golden routes measure expected-domain retrieval
findings.body: Each case repeats catalog search and succeeds when expected domain appears in top-k. This does not measure top-one precision, authority soundness, archive custody or successful security operations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D967 Security golden routes measure expected-domain retrieval.md

findings.title: Security risk decisions are engagement declaration checks
findings.body: R0 allows nonempty non-denied targets; R1 requires allowlist and read-only/advisory. Higher risks require supplied authorization labels, date window, human flag and mode-specific fields. No evidence signature, target identity normalization or actual host grant is authenticated; authority_granted remains false.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D968 Security risk decisions are engagement declaration checks.md

findings.title: Security environment labels are exact policy inputs
findings.body: Active production exception tests exact production string. R4 requires exact isolated_lab and lab_simulation. Caller-supplied environment labels are not independently measured environment containment. Tests exercise these declarations with synthetic broad-date engagement.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D969 Security environment labels are exact policy inputs.md

findings.title: Security graph input seeds can exceed node budget
findings.body: Initial seed set is built before traversal and is not trimmed to max_nodes. Depth zero can return too many seeds without truncation. Entire graph and all seed input are loaded before output budgets. Positive parameters lack fixed upper limits.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D970 Security graph input seeds can exceed node budget.md

findings.title: Capped security graph may return dangling edges
findings.body: Outgoing edge is appended before target-node cap check. At cap, target may be omitted while edge remains, so returned edge endpoints need not all appear in returned nodes. One-seed tests assert counts only.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D971 Capped security graph may return dangling edges.md

findings.title: Security package ranks before filtering authority
findings.body: Despite docstring and test naming, build calls search with limit 100 before risk/engagement checks. Eligible candidates below that cutoff cannot be selected. Selection stops once max_bodies is filled; rejected list is not exhaustive.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D972 Security package ranks before filtering authority.md

findings.title: Security execution package is candidate context only
findings.body: Package contains selected metadata and declaration decisions, not hydrated bodies or executed scripts. Catalog is loaded separately from search, allowing changed metadata between reads. Package digest omits full engagement scope/authorization and exact body identity. Runtime authority remains false.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D973 Security execution package is candidate context only.md

findings.title: Security reference hydration pins bytes but reopens archive
findings.body: Whole archive digest is checked before opening ZIP separately, so exact checked handle is not retained. Selected body is matched by source-path suffix, hashed and returned as untrusted text; no extraction or provider script execution occurs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D974 Security reference hydration pins bytes but reopens archive.md

findings.title: Security archive byte limits follow expensive reads
findings.body: Whole archive hash precedes body budget, all input IDs deduplicate before slice, and selected ZIP member is decompressed/read before byte-cap comparison. No total archive/decompression resource cap is established. Empty selection can succeed without bodies.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D975 Security archive byte limits follow expensive reads.md

findings.title: Verified security finding requires labels rather than proof
findings.body: Required keys are checked for presence; verified status requires nonempty evidence list of mappings with truthy reference and sha256. Hash grammar/file bytes, severity/confidence/assets/actions and evidence authority are not authenticated. Canonical promotion remains false.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D976 Verified security finding requires labels rather than proof.md

findings.title: Security workflow step text is not executed ordering
findings.body: Validator searches quoted names for normalize/authority-filter/discover/rank/hydrate/validate-outcome/record-learning. It does not parse dependencies or run them. Its stated authority-before-ranking order differs from candidate package implementation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D977 Security workflow step text is not executed ordering.md

findings.title: Security archive test substitutes a fixture trust pin
findings.body: Hydration test patches expected archive SHA and catalog loader for tiny ZIP. It proves chosen fixture hash and no extraction/script load, not actual production archive identity or reopen/decompression race safety.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D978 Security archive test substitutes a fixture trust pin.md

findings.title: Security tests do not observe claimed filter ordering
findings.body: Package test checks allowed risk outputs and some rejections, not call order or eligible candidates beyond top 100. Graph test uses one seed and does not check endpoint closure. Finding test supplies invented hash string; it does not resolve evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D979 Security tests do not observe claimed filter ordering.md

findings.title: Security CLI exposes independent authority and reference routes
findings.body: Authority result wraps valid true around the decision, while package, hydrate, graph and finding validation are separate commands. Reading reference content does not imply engagement approval or security execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D980 Security CLI exposes independent authority and reference routes.md

findings.title: Readiness version parsing is a bounded numeric subset
findings.body: First numeric substring supplies three-part version and ignores prerelease semantics. Caret ceiling always increments major, so zero-major constraints differ from full semver. Alternatives short-circuit, potentially leaving unsupported later alternatives unexamined. This is local comparison logic, not package-manager resolution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D981 Readiness version parsing is a bounded numeric subset.md

findings.title: Readiness resolves executable paths without byte identity
findings.body: Explicit relative/absolute paths and PATH candidates resolve to files; no digest/ownership or expected tool identity is checked. Windows batch dispatch selects ambient COMSPEC. A parseable version string is not proof of the intended binary or its launch functionality.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D982 Readiness resolves executable paths without byte identity.md

findings.title: Probe output is bounded after subprocess capture
findings.body: subprocess.run captures complete stdout/stderr before joining and truncating to 4096 characters. Individual deadlines bound direct waits, not aggregate work or descendant lifetime. Scrubbed environment does not impose network or filesystem isolation; read_only/not-used fields are declarations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D983 Probe output is bounded after subprocess capture.md

findings.title: Browser readiness can use file version without launch
findings.body: Windows browser file-version metadata yields ready with no version requirement or process launch. Other platforms use --version. Neither path checks that the browser can render the certification app or that required automation features work.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D984 Browser readiness can use file version without launch.md

findings.title: Readiness dependency parity is version-label parity
findings.body: Lock v3 root name/version/direct dependency mappings must match and direct pins must look exact. Installed direct package.json version is compared, but bytes/integrity hashes, transitive installed closure and executable scripts are not verified. Registry package names are joined as paths without additional containment grammar.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D985 Readiness dependency parity is version-label parity.md

findings.title: Managed readiness consumes phase without receipt authentication
findings.body: Managed campaign at validated or later with intake closed and no unresolved entries returns ready. repair_campaign_status validates state shape/phase, not current full-profile/validation receipts or source digest. This avoids rerunning ordered validation but is a weaker local evidence check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D986 Managed readiness consumes phase without receipt authentication.md

findings.title: Unmanaged readiness launches validation and parses truncated combined output
findings.body: Unmanaged path invokes runtime.cli validate and requires exit success plus valid true JSON. Probe combines stderr with stdout and truncates before JSON parsing, so otherwise valid noisy/large output may be rejected. Nested malformed metadata or nonobject payload can escape handled exceptions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D987 Unmanaged readiness launches validation and parses truncated combined output.md

findings.title: Readiness tests mock tool execution
findings.body: Tests use invented executable paths/version strings and synthetic late-phase campaign JSON without validation receipts. They prove selected classifications and no managed validation rerun, not actual browser startup, executable authenticity or network isolation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D988 Readiness tests mock tool execution.md

findings.title: Readiness entrypoints have different failure exits
findings.body: CLI release readiness returns normal CLI invalid status while bootstrap wrapper returns 2 for unready. Both call same assessor; bootstrap label read-only does not change effects of child tools or unmanaged validation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D989 Readiness entrypoints have different failure exits.md

findings.title: Exact certification fixtures are concrete but narrow
findings.body: Harness defines tiny repository, policy, memory, benchmark, JSON and archive fixtures for 56 helper IDs. Positive case coverage is set equality against registry, which does not separately reject duplicate admitted IDs; each helper has one main positive scenario.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D990 Exact certification fixtures are concrete but narrow.md

findings.title: One negative argument case produces multiple coverage labels
findings.body: Eleven explicit denial examples are supplemented by generic --pacify-x-invalid-boundary for other tools. Every negative ToolCase is labeled malformed_input, wrong_type and boundary_denial; later booleans reuse the same passed flag. These are not three separately exercised scenarios.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D991 One negative argument case produces multiple coverage labels.md

findings.title: Exact helper isolation is working directory and environment convention
findings.body: Runner copies ambient environment and sets only no-bytecode/no-user-site flags. It does not create an OS filesystem/network sandbox or use governed process/workspace custody here. Absolute source scripts execute outside fixture tree; selected interpreter is supplied directly.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D992 Exact helper isolation is working directory and environment convention.md

findings.title: Exact filesystem comparison misses deletions and outside effects
findings.body: Snapshot hashes files under temp except __pycache__. Changed list iterates only after entries, so deleted files are absent and unreported. Writes outside temp, metadata-only changes and effects in excluded caches are not observed. Symlink targets may be followed by is_file/read_bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D993 Exact filesystem comparison misses deletions and outside effects.md

findings.title: Exact output pass does not enforce semantic result schema
findings.body: Pass requires expected exit, parseable JSON when requested, output existence and no observed unexpected local additions/changes. Parsed JSON need not be object or valid true; json_object is reported but not checked. Expected output may be directory, and semantic contents are not asserted by ToolCase.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D994 Exact output pass does not enforce semantic result schema.md

findings.title: Exact timeout branch loses observed effect information
findings.body: Timeout returns failed result with empty effect lists and all declared outputs missing without taking an after snapshot. Direct subprocess timeout does not prove descendant closure. OSError/decoding failures outside TimeoutExpired handling can abort aggregate and skip terminal receipt.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D995 Exact timeout branch loses observed effect information.md

findings.title: Repeat normalization can remove meaningful differences
findings.body: JSON keys containing time, created, updated, duration or timestamp are removed recursively, in addition to selected volatile names. This can hide timeout/runtime or other semantically meaningful fields. Fixture-root redaction is case-insensitive substring replacement, not path-token equivalence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D996 Repeat normalization can remove meaningful differences.md

findings.title: Shared fixture state differs from the repeat tree
findings.body: Positive and negative cases for all tools share one temp tree; repeat cases share its repeat-run child. Earlier helper outputs persist for later cases, while repeat has separate accumulated history. The comparison is not independent fresh-tree execution per helper/case.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D997 Shared fixture state differs from the repeat tree.md

findings.title: Helper source hash precedes a separate execution open
findings.body: Each registry target hash is checked once before subprocess runs or cache reuse. No immutable copy/handle binds the executed script bytes to that hash across four cases. Target path is joined from registry without containment guard; registry is trusted input at this layer.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D998 Helper source hash precedes a separate execution open.md

findings.title: Exact cache identity omits selected interpreter and dependencies
findings.body: Cache key binds tool, complete registry, harness and current Python process platform/version, but not python_executable argument bytes/version, dependency/import trees, environment variables or wrapper implementation. Reusing cache across those changes is not excluded by this key.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D999 Exact cache identity omits selected interpreter and dependencies.md

findings.title: Cache seal detects corruption but is not authenticated provenance
findings.body: Persistent receipt seal is SHA-256 of canonical JSON, recomputable by a writer. Loader checks key/seal/result.passed/repeat presence but not complete nested schema. Tests flip passed without resealing; they do not test a coherently forged seal.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1000 Cache seal detects corruption but is not authenticated provenance.md

findings.title: Exact aggregate timeout is a between-tool check
findings.body: Deadline is checked at beginning of admitted-tool loop only. Up to four case deadlines and snapshot work follow; wrapper loop runs even after aggregate break and has no aggregate check. Fixture creation, hashing, output capture and temp cleanup are outside a hard aggregate deadline.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1001 Exact aggregate timeout is a between-tool check.md

findings.title: Wrapper certificate strength differs from exact helper checks
findings.body: Seven wrappers run one positive JSON fixture; there is no wrapper expected source hash check before execution, negative case or deterministic repeat here. Report hashes wrapper afterward. Their count should not imply equivalent coverage to admitted exact helper cases.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1002 Wrapper certificate strength differs from exact helper checks.md

findings.title: Harness progress and caches use ordinary overwrite publication
findings.body: Progress rewrites whole receipt in_progress with accumulated events/results; final overwrites it after temporary directory context exits. Cache files similarly write directly. No atomic commit/fsync/locking or guaranteed terminal write on exception protects these publications.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1003 Harness progress and caches use ordinary overwrite publication.md

findings.title: Certification strength label does not include every tool-pass condition
findings.body: negative-path-certified label depends on denial and repeat, while tool_passed also requires direct load and positive behavior. A row may retain stronger label despite failing another required case. Final aggregate correctly checks all tool conditions; consumers must not rely only on label.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1004 Certification strength label does not include every tool-pass condition.md

findings.title: Python surface direct label consumes only positive case
findings.body: Classifier direct_paths selects positive_behavior.passed and wrapper behavior.passed without requiring full exact result valid or negative/repeat success. CLI combines final valid flags separately; map builder still writes projection before returning failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1005 Python surface direct label consumes only positive case.md

findings.title: Ownership map current flag is publication intent rather than success proof
findings.body: Builder unconditionally sets map_current true, writes normal overwrite, then returns combined validity. It does not reread/hash the published map or refuse write on failed certification. Clean source export likewise sets this flag in its projection sequence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1006 Ownership map current flag is publication intent rather than success proof.md

findings.title: Exact harness tests mostly assert its own aggregate projections
findings.body: Tests run fixtures then assert counts, inferred coverage fields, local effect lists and normalized repeat. Timeout test is one direct sleeping child; cache test observes simple corruption rejection and may reuse process cache. No deletion/outside effect, resealed cache, alternative interpreter or hard aggregate deadline coverage is established.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1007 Exact harness tests mostly assert its own aggregate projections.md

findings.title: Canonical owner index silently keeps first duplicate identity
findings.body: Records deduplicate by object_type/object_id and ignore later competing owner metadata. Registry extraction visits top-level lists only; workflow IDs use filename stems. Index digest seals projected records, not source file hashes or runtime implementation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1008 Canonical owner index silently keeps first duplicate identity.md

findings.title: Disposition ownership is path and alias inference
findings.body: Large first-match rule table assigns known packs to canonical files/skills based on names, suffixes and path markers. Rationale strings such as reviewed/implemented/admitted are fixed text, not results of semantic comparison or admission checks. Unknown code falls back to merge into capability_routing.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1009 Disposition ownership is path and alias inference.md

findings.title: Source inventory does not compare expected tree digest
findings.body: expected_tree_sha256 is copied to output only. inventory_sha256 hashes enumerated relative path/size/content rows, but no equality condition compares the two fields. CLI expected-tree flag therefore does not enforce source snapshot identity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1010 Source inventory does not compare expected tree digest.md

findings.title: Disposition zero-unaccounted count is not independent closure
findings.body: Builder sets unaccounted_count=0 after is_file enumeration. Nonfiles/empty directories are not represented; symlink files can be followed. No second matching snapshot or immediate equality check establishes stable full-tree inventory. File size is read after content hash, allowing mixed-time metadata.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1011 Disposition zero-unaccounted count is not independent closure.md

findings.title: Overlay classification checks current target bytes without durable binding
findings.body: Existing matching bytes yield retain, existing differing target merge, absent target admit. Target may be directory or alias; no target expected hash is retained in differing case. No actual merge/admission or owner existence verification occurs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1012 Overlay classification checks current target bytes without durable binding.md

findings.title: Disposition validator accepts some weakly shaped resealed records
findings.body: Path check detects nonobject/duplicates but never tests nonempty string, so one empty path can pass. Owner/hash need truthiness only. Byte totals, digest syntax, inventory digest recomputation, disposition counts and expected-tree identity are unchecked; recomputed report seal can cover malformed values.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1013 Disposition validator accepts some weakly shaped resealed records.md

findings.title: Disposition report seal authenticates no external evidence
findings.body: Self-digest establishes consistency with supplied report fields, not provenance authenticity or equality to current source. Report validation never reads source or selected owners. Empty records with matching count/zero-unaccounted and seal can be valid.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1014 Disposition report seal authenticates no external evidence.md

findings.title: Disposition writer has separate unconstrained output publications
findings.body: Owner report writes before disposition report with ordinary overwrite. Outputs may coincide with each other or source paths; no containment/collision guard, atomic pair or readback is shown. Failure can leave one new report and one old or absent report.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1015 Disposition writer has separate unconstrained output publications.md

findings.title: Disposition tests cover labels rather than completed integration
findings.body: Fixtures exercise new overlay, cache exclusion and direct/wrapped external defer. They do not compare expected tree hash, test owner implementation, or execute a merge. Invalid owner fixture also changes report digest, so it does not isolate every semantic check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1016 Disposition tests cover labels rather than completed integration.md

findings.title: Structural closed-world scope is explicitly selective
findings.body: Duplicate inventory excludes external environments, evidence, __pycache__, committed WAL and selected derived/custody directories; links are skipped. Walker limits are 100000 files, depth128 and 2GiB and raise on excess. Other checks independently scan folders, so one inventory denominator does not cover every subcheck.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1017 Structural closed-world scope is explicitly selective.md

findings.title: Exact duplicate exemption can misname nonempty package files
findings.body: All matching paths ending __init__.py are classified empty-package-markers without testing empty content in classifier. Group byte equality proves they match each other, not that they are empty. Other classes likewise rely on fixed path sets and names.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1018 Exact duplicate exemption can misname nonempty package files.md

findings.title: Logic duplicate signature omits decorators and short functions
findings.body: Only functions with at least three body statements are hashed. Root function name/decorators and all type_comment/type_params fields are removed, while local identifiers remain. Decorated or generic functions with different semantics can normalize together; short or renamed-local equivalence can be missed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1019 Logic duplicate signature omits decorators and short functions.md

findings.title: Duplicate review metadata is not behavioral execution
findings.body: Function/path patterns assign digest adapters, CLI boilerplate, progress helpers and other reviewed categories after normalized equality. Their behavioral-parity/regeneration descriptions are labels; classification does not run those behaviors or regeneration commands.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1020 Duplicate review metadata is not behavioral execution.md

findings.title: Import graph resolves first matching ancestor rather than most specific module
findings.body: For each candidate, next module satisfying equality-or-prefix is selected in insertion order. A package ancestor can be chosen before exact submodule. From-import aliases are not expanded into submodule candidates, and package __init__ relative context uses parent calculation. Cycle graph therefore approximates actual imports.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1021 Import graph resolves first matching ancestor rather than most specific module.md

findings.title: Import cycle traversal can revisit many paths
findings.body: Cycle detection recursively explores paths from every node with active-set detection but no global visited/SCC reduction. Dense acyclic or cyclic graphs can cause large repeated work and recursion depth; no explicit time/node output budget bounds this stage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1022 Import cycle traversal can revisit many paths.md

findings.title: Callable reachability executes imports in current process
findings.body: Entrypoint resolver import_module uses current sys.path/cache and checks callable attributes. It does not load from audited root, authenticate module bytes or call workflow. Import side effects and exceptions other than ImportError/AttributeError can escape.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1023 Callable reachability executes imports in current process.md

findings.title: Workflow and skill set equality can hide duplicate declarations
findings.body: Catalog, semantic skill IDs, workflow definitions/handlers and binding maps are compared as sets/dictionaries. Duplicate IDs or repeated binding paths can collapse. Skill orchestration dependency graph catches unknown edges/cycles but not duplicate step IDs or intended operational order beyond supplied dependencies.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1024 Workflow and skill set equality can hide duplicate declarations.md

findings.title: Policy consistency does not establish enforcement reachability
findings.body: Policy index body paths must equal top-level JSON files excluding index files, and startup IDs must be known. This does not check complete policy semantics or runtime enforcement callers; duplicate IDs/bodies collapse into sets.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1025 Policy consistency does not establish enforcement reachability.md

findings.title: Structural release claims depend on selected text and lifecycle label
findings.body: release_open is lifecycle.status != complete, then selected document strings/version patterns/count tables are checked. Forbidden claims are exact substrings after limited formatting removal. This does not authenticate the lifecycle completion claim or semantically inspect all documentation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1026 Structural release claims depend on selected text and lifecycle label.md

findings.title: Documented CLI checker uses an independent static command list
findings.body: Only lines starting engineering-bootstrap space in README/START_HERE are tokenized. Hand-maintained top-level/nested names omit newer commands such as release readiness; flags and deeper parser semantics are not exercised. Valid examples can be rejected or malformed options missed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1027 Documented CLI checker uses an independent static command list.md

findings.title: Structural marker check dynamically executes scanner module
findings.body: Loader suppresses bytecode while exec_module runs and restores process-global flag afterward, then calls audit. No module digest is authenticated here. It is executable local analysis rather than pure text scanning, and concurrent threads share bytecode flag.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1028 Structural marker check dynamically executes scanner module.md

findings.title: Structural aggregation can lose delegated invalid state
findings.body: Five delegated validator results contribute errors lists; their valid fields are not required true. A false valid with empty errors can contribute no failure, and generated failed fallback is used only if errors key absent. Final valid is not errors. Other top-level stages lie outside checked exception wrapper.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1029 Structural aggregation can lose delegated invalid state.md

findings.title: Policy audit-item coverage is supplied category membership
findings.body: Audit-item IDs form dictionary, so duplicates overwrite. Empty categories pass all vacuously; category names are indexed without schema check here. Required item count reflects surviving IDs rather than an independent expected list.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1030 Policy audit-item coverage is supplied category membership.md

findings.title: Structural release composition can run the same audit twice
findings.body: Release certification calls audit_framework, which itself calls structural audit, then calls structural audit again in its checks mapping. These are repeated local inspections, not independent evidence owners or an atomic snapshot.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1031 Structural release composition can run the same audit twice.md

findings.title: Structural fixture tests do not execute named parity or regeneration
findings.body: Tests with behavioral-parity/regenerate names inspect equivalence-rule strings and classifications. Selected mutation tests exercise orphan/declaration drift. Cached root audit is reused across assertions; fixture clone uses hardlinks and explicit detach before changing known files.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1032 Structural fixture tests do not execute named parity or regeneration.md

findings.title: Doctor validity and operational readiness are separate
findings.body: Composer returns valid true after section-shape checks even when overall blocked. operable means not blocked; ready and certification_ready mean all eight states healthy. CLI defaults operable and exits 2 when unmet; --require syntax can succeed on blocked report.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1033 Doctor validity and operational readiness are separate.md

findings.title: Doctor composer trusts supplied section states
findings.body: Exact section-key set, known state, remediation mapping and px:// prefix are checked. It does not authenticate evidence, verify full section schema or validate evaluation timestamp. Public composer intentionally supports fixtures; certification_ready remains a derived diagnostic label.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1034 Doctor composer trusts supplied section states.md

findings.title: Doctor Git budget follows full subprocess capture
findings.body: Git commands use five-second direct timeouts and capture entire output before byte checks. Status excludes untracked then separately counts nonignored untracked files. No ignored-file inventory, process-tree cleanup, aggregate deadline or environment scrub is provided by this helper.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1035 Doctor Git budget follows full subprocess capture.md

findings.title: Doctor local JSON size check precedes separate read
findings.body: is_file/stat byte cap precedes read_text, leaving a change window; symlink/ancestor identity is not checked. Returned fields such as snapshot_hash/phase may retain arbitrary values even though secret_values_retained is fixed false. This is projection policy, not value scanning.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1036 Doctor local JSON size check precedes separate read.md

findings.title: Near-future Doctor evidence can be healthy but fresh false
findings.body: Age between minus300 and zero seconds sets fresh false but adds no problem; section state uses problems only. More than five minutes future adds clock skew. A caller comparing fresh flag and section state can therefore observe disagreement.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1037 Near-future Doctor evidence can be healthy but fresh false.md

findings.title: Doctor handoff freshness compares declared hashes
findings.body: Old handoff age is removed as problem when its verified_state_hash equals nonempty coordination state_hash. Neither hash is recomputed or authenticated. Absent coordination state leaves no current-state proof, and weak string checks accept empty handoff hash when no state comparison applies.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1038 Doctor handoff freshness compares declared hashes.md

findings.title: Doctor provider readiness does not pair budget and adapter
findings.body: Healthy requires some admitted ready adapter, some enabled budget and no scan violations. It does not match budget provider/model/scope to a ready adapter or check remaining allowance/live connectivity. Counters report declaration availability.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1039 Doctor provider readiness does not pair budget and adapter.md

findings.title: Doctor integrity consumes booleans as well as errors
findings.body: Unlike structural error-list-only aggregation, integrity requires every selected check valid. It also checks current sections and three named release groups. Exceptions are normalized for selected operations; this remains bounded control-plane status rather than certification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1040 Doctor integrity consumes booleans as well as errors.md

findings.title: Doctor transaction coverage is a fixed existing-root list
findings.body: Only operations/provider-budget/resource-lifecycle/coordination/diagnostics WAL directories are configured when present. Other owners are outside this list; recovery uses apply false. No discovered roots degrades even if remaining recovery checks healthy.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1041 Doctor transaction coverage is a fixed existing-root list.md

findings.title: Doctor extension claim selection and clocks are asymmetric
findings.body: First extension.activity-projection claim is assessed; later matching claims are ignored. Assessment uses health owner default clock, while supplied evaluated_at is passed to environment/handoff and report. max_age_seconds routes to coverage only; environment defaults one day.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1042 Doctor extension claim selection and clocks are asymmetric.md

findings.title: Doctor coverage wording can differ from blocked registry state
findings.body: Coverage section state blocks if route registry or reconciliation invalid, but human summary selects all-routes-current text solely from report.certifiable. Inconsistent delegated flags can therefore produce reassuring summary inside blocked section.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1043 Doctor coverage wording can differ from blocked registry state.md

findings.title: Doctor report retention does not validate incoming report seal
findings.body: Retention accepts report_sha256 string of length64, without hex syntax, recomputation or full report schema verification. It embeds supplied report and seals new receipt; a valid receipt can preserve a caller-supplied inconsistent report. Path/transaction safety remains delegated to JSON WAL.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1044 Doctor report retention does not validate incoming report seal.md

findings.title: Doctor digest covers base report before later fields
findings.body: run_px_doctor appends diagnostic_receipt after compose hashes report; CLI then appends requested_contract and contract_satisfied. Hashing the entire returned object minus report_sha256 will differ from base digest. Retained nested report captures original base before those additions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1045 Doctor digest covers base report before later fields.md

findings.title: Doctor receipt identity is digest-named rather than authenticated immutability
findings.body: Receipt target uses report hash and transaction ID uses first24 characters. Existing path immutability/idempotence relies on WAL behavior; helper has no existing-receipt equivalence check. Returned byte digest is a separate read after commit, not signed provenance.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1046 Doctor receipt identity is digest-named rather than authenticated immutability.md

findings.title: Doctor tests measure five WAL roots rather than every effect
findings.body: Live test compares snapshots of five known WAL roots and checks section fields. It does not inventory all filesystem/process/network effects. Freshness fixtures use arbitrary matching hash strings; receipt test starts from valid composer output rather than tampered reports.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1047 Doctor tests measure five WAL roots rather than every effect.md

findings.title: Doctor CLI tests intentionally distinguish syntax from operability
findings.body: Selected CLI test supplies blocked report and expects default exit2 but syntax exit0. Lazy-loading subprocess test likewise asks syntax while simulating two unrelated import failures. These do not establish healthy/ready installed system.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1048 Doctor CLI tests intentionally distinguish syntax from operability.md

findings.title: Doctor execution has no aggregate diagnostic deadline
findings.body: Serial validators/recovery/Git/health collection can perform substantial work before compose. Only selected local probes catch failures or use direct subprocess timeouts; an exception in unwrapped coverage/runtime/health/recovery can prevent any final report.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1049 Doctor execution has no aggregate diagnostic deadline.md

findings.title: Manifest expansion models a subset of build declarations
findings.body: Supports include/exclude and recursive-include/exclude, collecting exclusions independently of directive order. Wheel source packages use longest declared package-dir prefix; data-file target uses source basename. This is a custom projection model, not complete setuptools interpretation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1050 Manifest expansion models a subset of build declarations.md

findings.title: Projection source paths have uneven link checks
findings.body: Python package glob reads source without explicit symlink rejection; package/data/license branches differ. Resolving source paths can hide ancestor aliases, while bytes and size are read separately. No aggregate file/byte budget or locked source snapshot is established by generator.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1051 Projection source paths have uneven link checks.md

findings.title: Projection collision checks miss same-source duplicate and case aliases
findings.body: Collision key is exact package target/installed path and errors only when prior source differs. Repeated record for same source/path survives; case-only installed-path collisions remain distinct. Later expected dictionary can collapse exact duplicate paths.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1052 Projection collision checks miss same-source duplicate and case aliases.md

findings.title: Source-only skill policy also skips sdist requirement
findings.body: For allowed source-only skill file, helper rejects wheel projection then continues before sdist checks. Thus source-only path may be omitted from sdist while skill projection remains valid. Unknown projected skill paths not present in enumerated source are not separately rejected.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1053 Source-only skill policy also skips sdist requirement.md

findings.title: Frozen artifact manifest validation is shallow
findings.body: Record validation requires keys and package target but not path safety, field types, required/generated booleans, digest grammar, byte-size values or unique records. Empty record list and arbitrary skill_projection mapping can pass with valid flags and correct self-digest.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1054 Frozen artifact manifest validation is shallow.md

findings.title: Manifest self-digest is consistency rather than authenticity
findings.body: Digest excludes errors/valid/digest fields; validator separately checks generation errors/valid. A coherent rewritten manifest can be resealed. Higher release certificate owner binds expected manifest digest; direct intrinsic checker does not authenticate author or source.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1055 Manifest self-digest is consistency rather than authenticity.md

findings.title: Built-artifact checker does not invoke intrinsic manifest validation
findings.body: verify_built_artifact trusts supplied record/allowed-generated mappings, checks required only when exactly True and compares hashes for present records. It ignores manifest.valid and source sizes. bind_artifact_set adds intrinsic validation when manifest supplied; direct verifier is weaker.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1056 Built-artifact checker does not invoke intrinsic manifest validation.md

findings.title: Generated archive members are allowed by path rather than semantic contents
findings.body: Expected generated metadata paths can appear without matching source bytes; wildcard policy permits matching extras. Inspector only obtains metadata Version, not package Name, wheel tags, entrypoint correctness or RECORD hash closure. This requires higher-level checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1057 Generated archive members are allowed by path rather than semantic contents.md

findings.title: Archive inspectors have format and resource limits
findings.body: Wheel reads every file payload and sdist materializes member list then reads payloads with no aggregate/member/decompression cap. Duplicate names are detected, but case/normalized aliases are not. Tar links rejected; ZIP Unix link mode is not checked. Other nonfile tar entries are ignored.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1058 Archive inspectors have format and resource limits.md

findings.title: Archive metadata version can come from multiple matching members
findings.body: Every matching dist-info/METADATA or PKG-INFO updates version; no exact-one metadata check. Last matching member wins. Version existence is checked, but archive package identity is not bound to filename/project metadata by inspector.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1059 Archive metadata version can come from multiple matching members.md

findings.title: Build once is local invocation accounting
findings.body: Helper checks output directory empty then calls backend once; no exclusive reservation or campaign claim occurs inside it. Concurrent calls or later new output directories are not globally prevented. Caller release campaign provides ordered ownership separately.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1060 Build once is local invocation accounting.md

findings.title: Build helper can succeed without projection manifest
findings.body: If pyproject or MANIFEST.in absent, manifest generation/verification is skipped. A successful runner producing exactly one wheel/sdist can return valid with null manifest; synthetic once-build test uses this path. Actual certification staged source supplies declarations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1061 Build helper can succeed without projection manifest.md

findings.title: Build snapshots are collected after backend execution
findings.body: Artifact file hashes and source manifest are read after build, then archive inspection rereads artifacts. No immutable source/artifact handles span these steps. Extra unrelated files in output do not affect one-wheel/one-sdist count. Backend failure can still proceed through verification/custody handling.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1062 Build snapshots are collected after backend execution.md

findings.title: Intermediate custody does not verify moved bytes afterward
findings.body: Pre-move inventory checks links and hashes files, then each directory moves independently to supplied custody. Existing destinations cause partial movement/errors; no group rollback or post-move equality check. Receipt writes normally afterward. This dependency was inspected only; quarantine cleanup remains skipped.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1063 Intermediate custody does not verify moved bytes afterward.md

findings.title: Artifact record verification checks provided records only
findings.body: Verifies portable basename uniqueness, selected file/hash/size equality, but permits empty record list, arbitrary type labels and extra unlisted directory files. Type is copied from supplied record into actual result, so this check does not infer file format.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1064 Artifact record verification checks provided records only.md

findings.title: Artifact binding requires presence rather than exactly one of each type
findings.body: Binding uses next wheel and next sdist; despite error wording it does not reject additional same-type records with different names. All supplied records receive byte checks, but only first wheel/sdist receive version/projection inspection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1065 Artifact binding requires presence rather than exactly one of each type.md

findings.title: Record errors do not prevent subsequent archive access
findings.body: After verify_artifact_records returns errors, bind still opens first wheel/sdist paths from supplied records. Invalid filename, missing file or malformed archive can cause further reads or exceptions rather than a clean early refusal. No effect executed in audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1066 Record errors do not prevent subsequent archive access.md

findings.title: Manifest-free artifact binding does not prove source snapshot
findings.body: Without source_root or frozen manifest, binding checks supplied bytes and metadata versions then echoes source_product_digest. Same-source test uses arbitrary a-times64 digest. Certification callers pass current source or frozen manifest, adding stronger projection checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1067 Manifest-free artifact binding does not prove source snapshot.md

findings.title: Wheel installation uses before and after hashes around separate pip read
findings.body: Wheel path is resolved and hashed, pip later reads it, then helper hashes again. Byte replacement and restoration during that window is not detected by endpoint hashes. No immutable copy/handle binds exact installed bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1068 Wheel installation uses before and after hashes around separate pip read.md

findings.title: Install result does not verify installed package bytes
findings.body: EnvBuilder may reuse existing environment; pip no-deps/no-index can report success without fresh replacement of an already installed same version. Helper checks process exit and wheel endpoints, not installed RECORD/files/import origin. Environment creation uses current process interpreter and occurs outside runner timeout.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1069 Install result does not verify installed package bytes.md

findings.title: Distribution tests combine real builds with mocked installs
