findings.body: Module fixture truly builds copied source for manifest omission/extra/member tests if executed. Exact install test uses fake wheel bytes and mocked venv/pip runner, proving argv/env/hash handling rather than successful package installation. No product tests were run by this audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1070 Distribution tests combine real builds with mocked installs.md

findings.title: Frozen-manifest tests preserve intended historical binding
findings.body: Test modifies live completion state after build, verifies live manifest changes, and validates old archive against original frozen manifest. Separate tests reject simple manifest tampering and simultaneous source/frozen authority. This is meaningful snapshot-projection coverage, not proof against coherently resealed claims.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1071 Frozen-manifest tests preserve intended historical binding.md

findings.title: Installed test can build unless certified wheel variable is supplied
findings.body: Certified-wheel branch checks supplied hash and no-build flag. If wheel variable absent, test builds regardless of no-build flag. Test-local install uses --no-deps without explicit --no-index and inherits environment; higher owner may supply offline configuration.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1072 Installed test can build unless certified wheel variable is supplied.md

findings.title: Installed scenario covers selected commissioning and memory flows
findings.body: Runs installed validation/helper certification, preserves existing AGENTS bytes, creates/discovers/activates workspace projects, promotes/corrects memory and checks corrected visibility plus foreign-project denial. These concrete checks exceed pure metadata tests, but memory evidence strings and health metrics are fixtures.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1073 Installed scenario covers selected commissioning and memory flows.md

findings.title: Installed parallel sessions are sequential actions
findings.body: Second project/session activates after earlier commands, then count two is asserted and session released/switched. No simultaneous process race or concurrent writes are exercised. Per-command waits exist, but no single aggregate test deadline or process-tree ownership is shown.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1074 Installed parallel sessions are sequential actions.md

findings.title: Installed Doctor check proves syntax only
findings.body: Installed test invokes doctor --require syntax and checks valid. It does not require operable/ready, verify extension host health or certify all external services. Installed CLI bytes/import origin are not separately attested by this test.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1075 Installed Doctor check proves syntax only.md

findings.title: Source limit is defined on an unused export helper
findings.body: The 128MiB limit is enforced by _snapshot, which actual create_clean_export does not call. Actual materialization copies then hashes staged files without that aggregate limit. _snapshot also reads source twice, so its two digest fields would not be an atomic snapshot even if used.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1076 Source limit is defined on an unused export helper.md

findings.title: Clean export selection preserves only selected custody state
findings.body: Shared repository scope plus local filters exclude environments/builds/evidence and most bootstrap state, while retaining selected project/commissioning/test receipt paths. File symlinks are skipped; resolving root/ancestor aliases is not equivalent to rejecting them. Selection does not establish source stability.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1077 Clean export selection preserves only selected custody state.md

findings.title: Export preflight checks stage after candidate work
findings.body: Package processing-stage check lives in _preflight, invoked after candidate materialization and optional projection/test operations. It is not an admission before all export effects. Separate release-stage owner run() checks exact campaign phase before using rebuild directly.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1078 Export preflight checks stage after candidate work.md

findings.title: Cross-platform export condition is a digest-cardinality check
findings.body: Preflight accepts at most one distinct artifact digest, including zero artifacts. This is not observed equivalent behavior across operating systems. Stored completion is compared with fresh completion, while detailed component errors collapse to named check validity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1079 Cross-platform export condition is a digest-cardinality check.md

findings.title: Rebuild includes executable helper certification
findings.body: Projection rebuild does not merely format JSON: it runs exact-tool certification then writes Python ownership and other projections. Subsequent writes proceed in sequence, with engine identity near end and classification checks afterward. Failures leave earlier staged mutations; lock release does not roll them back.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1080 Rebuild includes executable helper certification.md

findings.title: Rebuild static inventory helper is intentionally rootless
findings.body: build_inventory() supplies declared count-computation records and does not inspect a source root. Calling it without root in candidate rebuild is not by itself a live-root leakage defect. Other builders explicitly receive candidate root.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1081 Rebuild static inventory helper is intentionally rootless.md

findings.title: Export command success is process exit rather than structured verdict
findings.body: _run_command inherits ambient environment while adding no-bytecode/no-user-site/PYTHONPATH, captures complete stdout/stderr, and checks returncode. It does not parse a JSON valid field or use ProcessSupervisor tree/capture accounting. Each timeout is separate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1082 Export command success is process exit rather than structured verdict.md

findings.title: Candidate check order has no encompassing rollback or deadline
findings.body: Certification runs stale sections, requires current section status, runs stale groups, then one full profile and validation before publishing evidence/completion. These commands have separate deadlines and mutate staged evidence; no total transaction/deadline restores previous candidate on later failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1083 Candidate check order has no encompassing rollback or deadline.md

findings.title: Git provenance samples independent mutable observations
findings.body: HEAD, commit time and porcelain status are separate subprocess reads. Empty successful status is converted to None, causing clean state to become unknown rather than false. Revision/mtime/provenance are not bound by one tree snapshot.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1084 Git provenance samples independent mutable observations.md

findings.title: Frozen records exclude the export manifest itself
findings.body: _candidate_records excludes every file whose basename is AUDIT_EXPORT_MANIFEST.json, along with links. Equality therefore cannot detect changes to those bytes or link/directory state. The ZIP still includes the manifest. Tests cover added pyc but not manifest mutation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1085 Frozen records exclude the export manifest itself.md

findings.title: Staging overwrites reserved output names without a source reservation check
findings.body: Materialization writes audit README, SHA256SUMS, replay contract and manifest into copied tree. Optional VSIX artifact names are checked for case-insensitive uniqueness and extension, but archive format and aggregate payload size are not validated there. Copies and hashes occur at separate times.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1086 Staging overwrites reserved output names without a source reservation check.md

findings.title: Deterministic ZIP metadata does not freeze concurrent bytes
findings.body: Archive writer fixes timestamps and derives executable mode from shebang, sorting files case-insensitively. It rereads bytes after equality check; there is no immutable file handle spanning freeze and archive. Actual filesystem permission/empty directory differences are not preserved.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1087 Deterministic ZIP metadata does not freeze concurrent bytes.md

findings.title: Uncertified export receipts use skipped-valid checks
findings.body: Library can auto-detect certification mode, while CLI defaults to requiring it unless allow-uncertified. Skipped candidate/replay preflight values are valid true. Manifest explicitly refuses certification claim and filenames containing certified are rejected, even when that substring appears in uncertified.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1088 Uncertified export receipts use skipped-valid checks.md

findings.title: Resource registration failures can precede export finally
findings.body: Workspace and both prepared file records are registered before try begins. A later registration error can leave earlier owned resource unreconciled by this function. Resource ledger is written under original source root although candidate work occurs in stage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1089 Resource registration failures can precede export finally.md

findings.title: Replay checks a self-produced archive rather than independent acceptance
findings.body: Certified branch extracts prepared ZIP, compares selected records, and reruns preflight. This is useful transport replay but shares implementation/inputs with producer. Prepared archive can change between writes/reads; no external signature or independent verifier authority is established here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1090 Replay checks a self-produced archive rather than independent acceptance.md

findings.title: Archive and receipt publication can be partial
findings.body: Archive is replaced/promoted before receipt construction and replacement. A later sidecar failure leaves published archive without completed pair. Initial existence checks are not exclusive reservations, so concurrent publication may be overwritten by os.replace. No pair rollback or fsync boundary is shown.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1091 Archive and receipt publication can be partial.md

findings.title: Export cleanup does not gate successful return
findings.body: Finally catches selected reclaim exceptions and ignores reclaim result validity. Completion state is marked before cleanup, allowing apparent success with incomplete reclamation. A failure during failure-marking can also mask original error. hard_delete false in summary does not mean owned temporary cleanup was absent.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1092 Export cleanup does not gate successful return.md

findings.title: Returned archive hash is another later read
findings.body: Sidecar binds hash read after publication; returned summary rereads archive afterward. Concurrent replacement can make returned hash differ from receipt without a final equality check. No final sidecar readback is performed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1093 Returned archive hash is another later read.md

findings.title: Clean export tests do not run the full certified export sequence
findings.body: Tiny uncertified fixtures check deterministic bytes, modes, CRLF, preserved custody and exclusions. Preflight is patched all-valid and candidate command runner is mocked. POSIX extraction test has platform gating and external subprocesses without timeout. No archive/sidecar failure, manifest mutation or size cap test.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1094 Clean export tests do not run the full certified export sequence.md

findings.title: Git worktree attributes are distinct from working-tree contents
findings.body: Archive command uses selected revision, default HEAD. --worktree-attributes controls attribute interpretation but does not include dirty/untracked source bytes. Report keeps revision string without resolving commit or retaining archive SHA256.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1095 Git worktree attributes are distinct from working-tree contents.md

findings.title: Tar membership checks ignore nonregular entries
findings.body: Inspector skips links/directories/special entries and checks only limited case-sensitive forbidden prefixes plus four required regular names. It does not reject duplicate names, traversal/normalized aliases or malicious link targets. No extraction occurs in auditor, so these are proof limits rather than an extraction exploit claim.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1096 Tar membership checks ignore nonregular entries.md

findings.title: Tar size checks do not establish content authenticity
findings.body: Physical tar cap and declared regular-byte cap bound size, but file content is not hashed or semantically checked. No member-count cap is applied, and declared byte sum is checked after member traversal. Required-name existence can be satisfied with arbitrary bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1097 Tar size checks do not establish content authenticity.md

findings.title: Owned Git process requires actual tree closure
findings.body: ProcessSupervisor applies startup/idle/total limits, grace/force shutdown and 64KiB captures. Result requires exited/zero and tree_closed, then archive existence. Dropped stderr is recorded but not invalidating. This is stronger lifecycle evidence than bare subprocess exit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1098 Owned Git process requires actual tree closure.md

findings.title: Archive workspace cleanup affects final validity
findings.body: Auditor reclaims in finally and marks result invalid unless exactly one resource reclaimed without errors. Registration occurs before try and cleanup exceptions can mask earlier errors. No archive payload survives cleanup, while process receipt is retained through manager.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1099 Archive workspace cleanup affects final validity.md

findings.title: Git archive tests exercise real supervised synthetic children
findings.body: Tests run a tiny Python tar creator, a timeout sleeper and 200000-byte stderr writer, asserting closed process tree and reclaimed workspace. These are meaningful lifecycle checks when executed, but do not exercise actual Git revision/attributes or forbidden member policies. Source-name assertions are structural only.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1100 Git archive tests exercise real supervised synthetic children.md

findings.title: Git revision and custom command interfaces assume trusted callers
findings.body: Revision is appended as a raw argv item without separator or revision resolution; option-like values may be interpreted by Git. Custom command_builder can return an arbitrary fixture command. Timeout check only requires positive value; caller still owns authorization and acceptable bounds.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1101 Git revision and custom command interfaces assume trusted callers.md

findings.title: Contract ownership can preserve prior declarations
findings.body: Unknown contract paths fall back to existing ownership records, preserving owner/producers/enforcement/tests without independently deriving them. generated_artifacts compares to build(root), which rereads that same registry. Coherent changes in fallback metadata can therefore regenerate consistently; corpus consumer separately checks declared files/schema.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1102 Contract ownership can preserve prior declarations.md

findings.title: Contract routing tables classify rather than prove enforcement
findings.body: Directory basename and schema filename select tables; some directories use generic owners, others index known names and raise on unknown. Builder stamps version 1.0.0, packaged true and universal runtime/contracts.py consumer. It reads schema ID/title without establishing actual owner call coverage or test success.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1103 Contract routing tables classify rather than prove enforcement.md

findings.title: Contract corpus consumer adds limited independent checks
findings.body: Corpus auditor validates schema structure/IDs/references and generated positive/empty negative fixtures, verifies ownership file paths, nonempty enforcement and labels. It does not execute every listed producer/test or demonstrate claimed runtime enforcement merely from ownership registry.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1104 Contract corpus consumer adds limited independent checks.md

findings.title: Count inventory is a static declaration set
findings.body: build_inventory returns an explicit table, not filesystem-discovered completeness. It handles varied count rules and assigns fallback builder label to undeclared producer paths. Runtime consumer independently discovers count fields and checks rule results, while metadata fields are tested for nonemptiness rather than actual producer execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1105 Count inventory is a static declaration set.md

findings.title: Count inventory check is canonical text equality
findings.body: CLI renders static table and compares read_text, which normalizes newline differences. It reports valid true after successful write/check; actual count values are validated only by runtime envelope consumer, not this script.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1106 Count inventory check is canonical text equality.md

findings.title: Proof matrix binds inventory bytes rather than probes
findings.body: Matrix records SHA256 of input JSON and canonical plan plus explicit authority that no probe ran. Source references and declared action_count are copied; underlying source bytes and operation outcomes are not verified by builder.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1107 Proof matrix binds inventory bytes rather than probes.md

findings.title: Proof matrix denominator check is aggregate
findings.body: Control IDs must be unique and total count equal sum of expected surface counts. It does not compare each surface count, so offsetting per-surface discrepancies can pass. Duplicate action keys collapse in dictionary, and action_count is not checked against its list length here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1108 Proof matrix denominator check is aggregate.md

findings.title: Action policy comes from mode and effect labels
findings.body: Action chosen from first label token or dynamicRepair second token. Navigate and sidebar controls can receive synthetic contracts; sidebar host-ui-or-read is outside nonmutating allowlist and thus marked disposable/restart. Mode other than exact host is treated as UI for these decisions. No schema validation precedes interpretation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1109 Action policy comes from mode and effect labels.md

findings.title: Indicator roles are inferred from words
findings.body: Failure tokens take priority over progress then empty tokens; camel-case splitting and specific phrases determine state. Semantic meaning, negation and actual reachable UI state are not independently derived. All requirement variants mark real external authority false.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1110 Indicator roles are inferred from words.md

findings.title: Restart flags and stage requirements are separate tables
findings.body: Editor configuration sets requires_restart true, but persistence/reload_reopen stages are not required by the later kind set. Consumers that only use stage_policy can have different obligations from consumers using restart flag. This is a declaration inconsistency to account for, not evidence a restart happened.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1111 Restart flags and stage requirements are separate tables.md

findings.title: Selected installed branch infers three stages from acknowledgement
findings.body: For contained_host_interaction with attempted and acknowledged probe, required authorization/backend_dispatch/runtime_effect stages are set present with the same receipt reference. Response/live-view change supports an observation, but does not independently expose each internal stage. Whole large operational walk remains under review.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1112 Selected installed branch infers three stages from acknowledgement.md

findings.title: Proof matrix tests establish metadata consistency
findings.body: Tests compare build output with stored matrix, check unique aggregate counts/stage vocabulary, source-name presence and four indicator labels. They do not execute controls or test malformed action entries, offset surface counts or restart-stage inconsistency.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1113 Proof matrix tests establish metadata consistency.md

findings.title: Current evidence index apply publishes before validity return
findings.body: CLI calls publish_index then returns 0/2 according to value.valid. Core publisher writes both locations regardless of validity using separate prepared replacements. One target can update before failure of second; CLI invalid result does not undo publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1114 Current evidence index apply publishes before validity return.md

findings.title: Thin projection wrappers have different success meanings
findings.body: Effect and historical writers print valid true after write; graph core writer returns valid true; test-group and engine wrappers return zero without a validator. Provider-route writer returns nested report validity only after writing scan. These results are not interchangeable validation receipts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1115 Thin projection wrappers have different success meanings.md

findings.title: Graph writer leaves stale extra artifacts in place
findings.body: Core writer creates output and writes expected files, without removing preexisting extras or post-write validation. Separate validate_graph_artifacts requires exact JSON file set and expected bytes. Wrapper success can therefore precede a later stale-extra failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1116 Graph writer leaves stale extra artifacts in place.md

findings.title: Writer root options select data rather than imported code
findings.body: Thin wrappers prepend their own repository path for imports, then some pass caller-selected root to core builder. Others pin both data and implementation to script ROOT. This is an important portable/candidate invocation distinction, not an execution sandbox.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1117 Writer root options select data rather than imported code.md

findings.title: Agency output can fail reporting after an outside-root write
findings.body: Wrapper accepts absolute --output and writes it, then output.relative_to(root) for JSON summary raises if outside root. There is no pre-write containment check. Check-only mode can also fail at summary. No such operation was executed here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1118 Agency output can fail reporting after an outside-root write.md

findings.title: Historical locator publication does not retrieve historical bytes
findings.body: Writer records dispositions discovered within PRODUCT_STRUCTURED_ROOTS and prints valid true. It does not dereference nonportable locators or establish evidence authenticity; generated gate only compares freshly discovered record list.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1119 Historical locator publication does not retrieve historical bytes.md

findings.title: Profile apply reports success while extra profiles remain
findings.body: Profile reconciler detects projected names absent from owners, but does not remove them. Apply result is always true after writes, even with extras; check mode rejects them. Missing source/projection directories can yield empty successful result because glob returns no names.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1120 Profile apply reports success while extra profiles remain.md

findings.title: Byte projection fixed denominators do not inspect all extras
findings.body: Wrapper reconciler checks seven hardcoded destinations; suite template reconciler checks 3 by 7 paths. Neither discovers unexpected additional copies nor validates Python/JSON semantics. Each records pre-write stale list and returns true in apply mode after sequential normal writes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1121 Byte projection fixed denominators do not inspect all extras.md

findings.title: Projection writes have separate path and publication limits
findings.body: Profile/domain/suite helpers follow ordinary file operations with no explicit symlink/ancestor containment guard, predecessor comparison or group rollback. Suite helper does not create missing parents. A failure leaves earlier writes intact; no final readback proves exact published bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1122 Projection writes have separate path and publication limits.md

findings.title: Active hash apply intentionally retains pre-write invalid result
findings.body: Active helper returns valid not stale after computing stale before writes. First successful repair may return false; dedicated test asserts false on apply then true on check. Export ignores the return and later derives other projections, so false there is not automatically write failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1123 Active hash apply intentionally retains pre-write invalid result.md

findings.title: Active hash map allows collapsed contracts and trusted paths
findings.body: Paths from map are joined without relative containment or symlink checks. Multiple active entries targeting same contract overwrite output dictionary; active_count counts distinct outputs, not entries. Empty active list passes. Rehashing current bytes does not itself prove those bytes admitted or behavior verified.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1124 Active hash map allows collapsed contracts and trusted paths.md

findings.title: Active contract replacement is atomic per file only
findings.body: All outputs calculated before mutation, then unique prepared names replace each file, even unchanged outputs. No compare-against-predecessor or group transaction; implementation may change between hashing and later use, and concurrent contract edits can be overwritten.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1125 Active contract replacement is atomic per file only.md

findings.title: Declared owner reconciliation assigns verification labels without tests
findings.body: Exact_authoritative_recovery state triggers authoritative_implementation_verified, supplied_and_revalidated and authoritative labels while helper only hashes SKILL.md. These metadata assignments must not be interpreted as a freshly executed verification receipt.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1126 Declared owner reconciliation assigns verification labels without tests.md

findings.title: Owner hash reconciliation gates group write on missing bodies
findings.body: Any missing owner body prevents writing all in-memory changes. Check mode detects label/hash drift; apply writes one normal JSON file if changed and no errors. Owner path/source identities have no containment/uniqueness proof here and no final readback.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1127 Owner hash reconciliation gates group write on missing bodies.md

findings.title: Declared tool reconciliation maintains a three-level hash chain
findings.body: Target bytes update registry source_sha256 and reference authoritative_source_sha256; newly rendered reference bytes determine owner scripts-index sha256. This establishes computed consistency at read time, not admissibility or behavioral success of changed code.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1128 Declared tool reconciliation maintains a three-level hash chain.md

findings.title: Tool hash reconciliation assumes valid layout and IDs
findings.body: Owner derived from target path third component, IDs interpolated into reference path, and existing index records selected by ID. No containment/schema/duplicate validation is performed; duplicate IDs/maps can collapse and malformed shapes raise. CLI writes outputs sequentially without rollback/readback.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1129 Tool hash reconciliation assumes valid layout and IDs.md

findings.title: Rebuild order binds copied owners before derived discovery
findings.body: Export invokes wrappers, templates, profiles, skills, active hashes and tool hash outputs before semantic/cognitive/agent graph rebuilding. This causal order is explicit. It does not call declared-owner hash reconciler in the inspected sequence; that remains a separate entrypoint.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1130 Rebuild order binds copied owners before derived discovery.md

findings.title: Recovery tests prove declared metadata and routing reachability
findings.body: Test checks fixed 260 identity count, active owner hashes, metadata freshness labels, evidence/test file presence and top-three navigation inclusion. It does not run each recovered owner, verify referenced receipt contents or prove no body hydration by instrumenting reads.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1131 Recovery tests prove declared metadata and routing reachability.md

findings.title: Byte stability test uses check mode only
findings.body: Generated-artifact test snapshots templates before/after check=True calls, establishing check-mode nonmutation when current. It does not exercise actual generation followed by byte-identical regeneration. Separate wrapper fixture does detect one injected drift.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1132 Byte stability test uses check mode only.md

findings.title: Engine identity wrapper delegates one-file replacement
findings.body: Core writer prepares a PID-named file then replaces identity; CLI prints count/tree hash and returns zero without running validate_engine_identity. Concurrent same-process calls can share prepared name, and filtered identity scope/installed equivalence remain core consumer concerns.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1133 Engine identity wrapper delegates one-file replacement.md

findings.title: Candidate queue merges by ID with uneven requirements
findings.body: CSV duplicate skill IDs overwrite earlier rows. Manifest-only IDs start with candidate/defer but omit CSV required_before_promotion list. Multiple unsorted manifest glob entries may overwrite same fields. No duplicate/schema/digest validation establishes one authoritative source.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1134 Candidate queue merges by ID with uneven requirements.md

findings.title: Manifest scalar extraction is not YAML semantics
findings.body: Anchored regex reads matching key line from anywhere in manifest and strips quotes; comments, block scalars, nested structure and duplicate keys are not parsed as YAML. Priority sorting is lexical, so numeric-looking priority strings may not follow numerical order.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1135 Manifest scalar extraction is not YAML semantics.md

findings.title: Specialty count deduplication differs from category rows
findings.body: Every queue entry is appended, while represented IDs and top-level counts use sets. Duplicate IDs across rows/categories can remain visible while counts understate rows. Active/mapped state is catalog membership alone; loading_rule prose does not enforce admission or lazy reading.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1136 Specialty count deduplication differs from category rows.md

findings.title: External promoted bundles bypass candidate regeneration
findings.body: Bundles already active/admitted in skill catalog are omitted from generated deferred manifests. One fixed active intake controller is always assigned; duplicate bundle IDs collapse and an ID collision with controller is overwritten. Promotion status is trusted from catalog, not independently authorized by this builder.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1137 External promoted bundles bypass candidate regeneration.md

findings.title: External package freshness and validation counts are authored constants
findings.body: Manifests stamp validation_freshness current and test source path as evidence; ledger sets failed zero/passed eight for active and deferred records. No tests run here. clean_room is a fixed active-control declaration or determined from source-license marker.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1138 External package freshness and validation counts are authored constants.md

findings.title: External catalog marker can suppress reconciliation
findings.body: Append decision searches raw TOML text for exact id marker. Existing entry with wrong body/status/version is not repaired; marker in comment can suppress missing entry. ID/version/body interpolation is not TOML-escaped except tags. Core registry later adds identity/status/file consistency checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1139 External catalog marker can suppress reconciliation.md

findings.title: External reconciliation is a sequence of partial writes
findings.body: Catalog rewrite occurs before package files, ledger and catalog additions. Later failure leaves prior changes. Trusted body/ID paths lack containment checks; source rereads can race, duplicate ledger IDs collapse when update occurs. Return valid reflects initial drift, while apply CLI exits zero despite false result.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1140 External reconciliation is a sequence of partial writes.md

findings.title: Security archive pin does not bind companion pack
findings.body: Builder hashes archive against fixed expected value, but reads catalog, graph, YAML, workflows and pack inventory from separate source files. It checks catalog/graph nonempty line counts before projection, not derivation from archive or a signed companion manifest.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1141 Security archive pin does not bind companion pack.md

findings.title: Security source metadata is copied without comparing to verified archive
findings.body: source.json archive hash/entry count/size come from source_archive.json rather than the already measured archive. A mismatch may publish successfully then fail runtime declared-hash check. Catalog hash is of original source JSONL, while published catalog is transformed/sorted JSON; digest scopes differ.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1142 Security source metadata is copied without comparing to verified archive.md

findings.title: Security metadata count check is weaker than runtime validation
findings.body: Builder line-count checks can accept duplicate IDs or malformed graph lines; graph is copied without parsing here. Runtime adds unique IDs, domains, risks and deferred-state checks; graph loading checks only edge count in inspected loader. Neither uses source catalog/graph hashes to authenticate projected payloads.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1143 Security metadata count check is weaker than runtime validation.md

findings.title: Security source projections are unbounded separate reads
findings.body: Archive hashing reads full file; catalog is counted, reread into full transformed bytes, hashed later and parsed again for candidate rows. YAML uses safe_load but without size/depth budget. No stable source snapshot or per-file/aggregate resource budget binds all steps.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1144 Security source projections are unbounded separate reads.md

findings.title: Security provider publication keeps external scripts inert
findings.body: Registration explicitly sets discovery enabled, execution disabled, provider_scripts_admitted zero and source_archive null/not bundled. Actual archive hydration is separate and verifies pinned bytes. Builder itself does not extract or execute provider scripts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1145 Security provider publication keeps external scripts inert.md

findings.title: Security operational schemas use local required-field definitions
findings.body: Source YAML supplies contract name/purpose; local OPERATIONAL_CONTRACTS supplies actual required/properties and additionalProperties false. Constants such as approved, immutable, cleanup_verified or selected hashes valid describe accepted claims, not real authorization/evidence verification. Unknown names raise; missing source contract files are not independently counted here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1146 Security operational schemas use local required-field definitions.md

findings.title: Security golden queries are derived from domain declarations
findings.body: Golden cases use each canonical domain name as query and expected domain, top_k ten. This is correlated vocabulary coverage rather than independent diverse evaluation. No golden-query execution occurs during generation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1147 Security golden queries are derived from domain declarations.md

findings.title: Security skill and workflow merging is recorded metadata
findings.body: Native bodies provide frontmatter; workflows provide ID/output labels; each receives merge_into_existing and fixed owner. duplicate_active_skills_created zero is assigned. No implementation equivalence or execution is established by these records.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1148 Security skill and workflow merging is recorded metadata.md

findings.title: Security admission publishes fixed test success
findings.body: Active control manifest is current with fixed evidence path, and admission ledger records sixteen passed/zero failed. Builder does not run tests or validate cited receipt. Existing catalog text marker prevents field reconciliation; multiple normal writes can partially publish.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1149 Security admission publishes fixed test success.md

findings.title: Security workflow binding admits a validator rather than executing operations
findings.body: Binding mode executable_validator points to validate_security_orchestration. Workflow JSON is loaded from a .yaml-named file and copied into orchestration registry after removing version/loading_rule/bounds/scenarios. Source workflow execution and retained bounds are not proved by this projection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1150 Security workflow binding admits a validator rather than executing operations.md

findings.title: Security pack unaccounted zero is based on supplied rows
findings.body: Every supplied pack manifest row gets a prefix-based owner/disposition, with fallback fragment_only. unaccounted_count is fixed zero; builder does not enumerate actual pack files, verify row hashes/sizes or compare missing/extra files. Merge label does not show target bytes received source behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1151 Security pack unaccounted zero is based on supplied rows.md

findings.title: Security apply result retains pre-write drift
findings.body: _write_or_check records drift then performs normal writes; final valid is not drift. Apply CLI exits zero regardless of that false result. No final all-output comparison, group rollback or stale-extra removal closes publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1152 Security apply result retains pre-write drift.md

findings.title: Health snapshot denominator is four fixed routes
findings.body: ROUTES is a hardcoded list and platform listener path chooses Windows otherwise Linux. All four receipt files must exist even if route is not active. Build does not enumerate current active tier routes; downstream coverage detects missing required route states.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1153 Health snapshot denominator is four fixed routes.md

findings.title: Remote health is configuration readiness rather than live invocation
findings.body: Remote route healthy requires any OpenAI adapter admitted true/status ready. Local route additionally needs Ollama adapter, enabled budget and any settled successful invocation without policy_overrun. No recent specific model/endpoint smoke is measured by builder; local adapter and budget files are not included in route receipt hash.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1154 Remote health is configuration readiness rather than live invocation.md

findings.title: Environment health is a shallow declared shape
findings.body: Healthy requires expected schema string, any string snapshot_hash and credential_values_persisted exactly false. Hash format/content, inventory status/age and actual credential handling are not verified here; malformed boundaries value can raise instead of returning unknown.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1155 Environment health is a shallow declared shape.md

findings.title: Listener route health and canonical readiness differ
findings.body: Route helper prefers top-level listener_health over host fallback and only requires healthy/coverage_complete. Canonical projection requires host listener plus engine connection, bus, closed-tree and unchanged-artifact flags and zero drops. Same receipt can therefore produce different results without contradiction in their distinct predicates.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1156 Listener route health and canonical readiness differ.md

findings.title: Canonical extension facts trust supplied envelope labels
findings.body: Configured/detected derive from truthy artifact name/VS Code version, authority from supplied flags, and finished time needs only nonempty text. Artifact hash, running host identity and process tree are not independently checked. int conversion of dropped_events accepts some coercions and can raise for malformed input; last_failure is always null.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1157 Canonical extension facts trust supplied envelope labels.md

findings.title: Observation time fallback can follow filesystem rewrite time
findings.body: Valid timezone-aware receipt times are preserved; malformed/naive/missing times fall back to file mtime. Rewriting or touching old evidence can thus advance fallback observation time. Builder does not reject future/stale timestamps; optional coverage enforces age/future bounds separately.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1158 Observation time fallback can follow filesystem rewrite time.md

findings.title: Receipt payload and bound hash are separate reads
findings.body: Build parses receipt text, derives health/time, then rereads bytes for SHA256. Concurrent replacement can bind hash of different payload from one interpreted. Optional health claims reread installed receipt again after writing snapshot, without cross-output equality.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1159 Receipt payload and bound hash are separate reads.md

findings.title: Snapshot write success does not mean healthy or certifiable
findings.body: CLI first writes snapshot and sets valid true even with unknown/unconfigured routes. Only optional coverage changes validity/certifiable fields; missing/malformed optional inputs can fail after initial write. Output paths can alias each other or input evidence, with no preflight collision check or transactional rollback.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1160 Snapshot write success does not mean healthy or certifiable.md

findings.title: Coverage validates freshness and bytes without rederiving route semantics
findings.body: For active tier A/B routes, consumer checks kind, healthy label, time window, contained receipt path and SHA256 equality. It does not rerun health producer or bind local auxiliary policy files in that branch. A hash-correct receipt supports byte identity but not every derived healthy claim.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1161 Coverage validates freshness and bytes without rederiving route semantics.md

findings.title: Health tests cover helper transformations rather than full observation
findings.body: Synthetic dictionaries prove selected listener/remote/environment labels, canonical facts and timestamp preservation. Installed receipt test checks nonzero size or skips. No full build/CLI/local branch or fresh live provider/host observation is exercised by this module.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1162 Health tests cover helper transformations rather than full observation.md

findings.title: Control source binding covers matrix-referenced files only
findings.body: Source manifest strips numeric/semantic anchors and hashes whole referenced files after resolved containment. It does not verify anchor existence, all repository code or current matrix/inventory bytes unless those happen to be source refs. Changed policy with unchanged referenced files can preserve source manifest equality.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1163 Control source binding covers matrix-referenced files only.md

findings.title: Assembler trusts matrix metadata beyond a deduplicated count
findings.body: Requirements dictionary length must equal control_count, but duplicate rows can collapse if declared count also collapsed. Matrix schema/self-digest and inventory-to-matrix equality are not checked. Test fixture deliberately has minimal matrix and empty inventory controls.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1164 Assembler trusts matrix metadata beyond a deduplicated count.md

findings.title: Allowed direct evidence kind is a declaration
findings.body: Assembler checks schema/kind allowlist and exact current source manifest. It does not authenticate producer, observed host, underlying artifact, timestamp or claimed measurement process. A permitted evidence_kind label alone does not establish direct observation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1165 Allowed direct evidence kind is a declaration.md

findings.title: Stage evidence references are rewritten without dereferencing
findings.body: Present stage requires nonempty detail and evidence list with nonblank string representations. Values are replaced by indexed fragment pointers into input receipt; original targets are not opened or checked here. Arbitrary nonstring objects can stringify nonempty.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1166 Stage evidence references are rewritten without dereferencing.md

findings.title: Assembler merges monotonic success across receipts
findings.body: Flags OR across inputs; present stages overwrite earlier present details, while missing stages never remove prior presence. There is no common run/host/time identity or contradiction check. A complete chain may combine distinct observations with last-present precedence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1167 Assembler merges monotonic success across receipts.md

findings.title: Assembly timestamps are publication time
findings.body: Every output control and aggregate observed_at is datetime.now rather than retained source observation time. Old source-compatible receipts can receive fresh assembly timestamps. No input evidence age or maximum skew is checked here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1168 Assembly timestamps are publication time.md

findings.title: Assembled inventory hash names a different digest scope
findings.body: control_chains.inventory.path names operational_surface_inventory.json, while its sha256 is source manifest source_sha256, not inventory file SHA256. This field must be interpreted with that specific schema convention, not assumed to authenticate named inventory bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1169 Assembled inventory hash names a different digest scope.md

findings.title: Assembler source and receipt identities use separate reads
findings.body: Input receipts parsed before per-record receipt hashing; same file can be reread and hashed once for each control. Concurrent edits may bind different bytes, and large receipts amplify read cost. Source manifest is not rechecked after merge. Input root containment occurs after input load.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1170 Assembler source and receipt identities use separate reads.md

findings.title: Exclusive evidence output prevents overwrite but not partial new file
findings.body: All three CLIs resolve output below root and open with x. This refuses existing outputs, but JSON serialization/write failure can leave partial newly created file. No prepared replacement, fsync or final readback shown. Input paths are contained only late in some builders.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1171 Exclusive evidence output prevents overwrite but not partial new file.md

findings.title: Installed smoke adapter checks retained bytes without inspecting VSIX contents
findings.body: Artifact before/after SHA256 must match supplied file; file format and packaged-source-to-current-source equality are not examined. Engine identity is a separate receipt declaration matched to local identity and selected control files. A test uses arbitrary non-ZIP bytes and coherent fake tree hash.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1172 Installed smoke adapter checks retained bytes without inspecting VSIX contents.md

findings.title: Installed smoke flags are not independent process proof
findings.body: Adapter checks receipt engine connection/worker exit/tree closed and Studio/sidebar labels, many by truthiness. It does not authenticate receipt producer, age, full engine manifest self-digest or actual process records; bool exit_code false can compare equal to zero.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1173 Installed smoke flags are not independent process proof.md

findings.title: Installed smoke maps one scenario into fixed stage sets
findings.body: Agent/workflow success/admission/reopen labels populate persistence and reload controls on both Studio and list surfaces plus lifecycle stages. Sidebar counters populate six stages. Missing policy stages remain missing, but progress/authorization/dispatch/effect are inferred from summary labels rather than separate per-stage observations here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1174 Installed smoke maps one scenario into fixed stage sets.md

findings.title: Optional Skill save changes installed adapter denominator
findings.body: Skill persistence record added only for created and content_bound true. Other fixed Studio/sidebar requirements can raise before any output. Expected maximum is twelve records, but missing Skill save can yield eleven; retained test expects twelve when adaptation succeeds.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1175 Optional Skill save changes installed adapter denominator.md

findings.title: Installed adapter identity reads are not one snapshot
findings.body: Receipt, VSIX, identity and control files are read at separate times; final receipt hash rereads after interpretation. No final identity revalidation binds all artifacts atomically. receipt/vsix relative_to(root) checks happen at output assembly after earlier reads.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1176 Installed adapter identity reads are not one snapshot.md

findings.title: Owned probe adapter lets caller choose installed evidence label
findings.body: Evidence kind allows direct_current_source_host_measurement or direct_installed_host_measurement, supplied by caller. It checks source/bridge/host-error declarations but no VSIX or installed host identity/process closure. Thus installed label has weaker binding than separate smoke adapter.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1177 Owned probe adapter lets caller choose installed evidence label.md

findings.title: Optional profile counts need not prove full expected profile coverage
findings.body: Absent profiles accepted; present profile requires schema and record length equal declared eligible count. No independent eligible-ID denominator, profile completion status or unique record check exists before duplicate merge. Matrix dictionary also collapses repeated IDs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1178 Optional profile counts need not prove full expected profile coverage.md

findings.title: Owned probe stages merge complementary claims into complete chain
findings.body: Present beats missing; present/present combines detail/evidence; applicability conflict rejected. Duplicate controls across or within profiles are merged, without common run/target/correlation checks. Test explicitly combines setup missing failure and edit missing runtime into both stages present.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1179 Owned probe stages merge complementary claims into complete chain.md

findings.title: Probe adapter does not resolve evidence strings
findings.body: Present requires detail plus nonempty list, but no nonblank item/dereference/provenance check. Assembler later rejects blank-string items, adding a stronger shape check. Profile dictionary-valued evidence can also fail dedup hashing if duplicate stages combine; malformed fields can raise.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1180 Probe adapter does not resolve evidence strings.md

findings.title: Adapter tests prove transformation with synthetic receipts
findings.body: Host fixture uses fake artifact and engine digest; probe fixture authors verified/bridge/stage labels. Tests meaningfully reject stale source, endpoint mismatch, host errors and policy/count conflicts, but do not establish real installed operation. Retained host test may skip or accept a specific stale result.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1181 Adapter tests prove transformation with synthetic receipts.md

findings.title: Assembler tests retain gaps but do not authenticate origins
findings.body: Tests show incomplete control remains observed_only, one exact synthetic direct record completes it, and observed true can complete without attempted. They reject contextual kind, outside IDs and stale source, but not replayed timestamps, policy-only changes, conflicting runs or fabricated nonempty references.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1182 Assembler tests retain gaps but do not authenticate origins.md

findings.title: Historical aliases can substitute different current artifacts
findings.body: Resolver maps conversation aliases to retained report or whole ledger, one old JS path to Python implementation, and installed extension package locator to source package.json. This resolves a current representative, not necessarily original observed bytes. Installed package special branch returns relative Path before root normalization, depending on process cwd.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1183 Historical aliases can substitute different current artifacts.md

findings.title: Historical token parsing chooses first resolvable file
findings.body: Command regex extracts one whitespace-delimited script token; semicolon alternatives return first existing file. Numeric anchors/fragments stripped. File paths can be outside root; resolve hides leaf symlink before later is_symlink check, so physical-file wording does not reject all aliases.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1184 Historical token parsing chooses first resolvable file.md

findings.title: Same-card later evidence need not correspond to original claim
findings.body: Helper takes first hash/size-bearing evidence from history entries after first, regardless of target reference identity or relative chronology of target being attested. It does not read/verify correlated artifact. Same-card correlation can bind a different supporting event than original claim.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1185 Same-card later evidence need not correspond to original claim.md

findings.title: Retained semantic alias proof is a card-ID substring
findings.body: For selected semantic aliases, raw retained artifact must contain gap ID bytes. This is not structured claim matching, exact token boundary or authorization verification. Nonsemantic aliases skip this check. Hashing entire current ledger/report binds current bytes rather than original authority text.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1186 Retained semantic alias proof is a card-ID substring.md

findings.title: Exact gap-event fallback hashes first matching raw event
findings.body: If direct file missing, helper scans ledger lines, skips malformed JSON and hashes stripped text of first matching event ID. It does not independently validate event chain in that function or require matched event to support same card. Earlier snapshot validation is a separate read.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1187 Exact gap-event fallback hashes first matching raw event.md

findings.title: Historical attestation completeness has narrow meaning
findings.body: Skips evidence with any artifact_sha256 truthy or hash-looking reference prefix. check complete means no resolver failures, even when candidate attestations have not been appended. Both unresolved check/apply return zero; callers must inspect complete/unresolved fields.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1188 Historical attestation completeness has narrow meaning.md

findings.title: Attestation append can partially complete across chunks
findings.body: Candidates derive from one snapshot and current reads, then append in MAX_BATCH_EVENTS chunks. Duplicate/concurrent target change or later failure can leave earlier chunks committed. No final snapshot audit or retry reconciliation occurs in script. Ledger validates each batch under its own lock.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1189 Attestation append can partially complete across chunks.md

findings.title: Ledger attestation validates binding shape rather than historical truth
findings.body: Consumer requires existing card/target evidence, valid hash/size/nonempty method and no prior target attestation. It does not open artifact or constrain method to proof semantics in this branch. Attested target is removed from unbound denominator; no automatic behavioral proof follows.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1190 Ledger attestation validates binding shape rather than historical truth.md

findings.title: Typed gap links bind fixed reviewed proposal bytes
findings.body: Script pins exact proposal SHA256 before interpreting assignments; it does not rederive source trace against current files. Retired controls are skipped explicitly, existing gap sets preserved/unioned, and operational controls can be changed to gap. It reports zero operational claims.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1191 Typed gap links bind fixed reviewed proposal bytes.md

findings.title: Typed proposal aggregate assertion is check-only
findings.body: Expected proposal candidate count compared only inside --check branch. Apply defaults to effects and appends even without that total assertion. Known surfaces/control IDs checked, but duplicate proposal assignments can create conflicting predecessor revisions because all planned from same snapshot.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1192 Typed proposal aggregate assertion is check-only.md

findings.title: Typed updater delegates meaningful predecessor validation to ledger
findings.body: Revisions bind hash of existing disposition. Ledger rejects stale predecessor, unknown gap cards, empty gap targets, invalid transition and semantic no-op. Append prepares entire bounded batch before authoritative append under lock; multiple script chunks still lack one all-proposal transaction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1193 Typed updater delegates meaningful predecessor validation to ledger.md

findings.title: Typed proposal evidence is bound again at append time
findings.body: Script hashes proposal before planning, while ledger _bind_evidence rereads referenced evidence during append preparation. If source proposal changes between reads, pinned planning bytes and retained event reference hash can differ; no script-side immediate equality recheck spans that gap.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1194 Typed proposal evidence is bound again at append time.md

findings.title: Ledger event integrity is distinct from actor authentication
findings.body: Reducer verifies sequence, predecessor and unkeyed canonical content hashes. Actor and authority are supplied strings; these checks establish internal consistency, not authenticated identity or independent truth of evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1195 Ledger event integrity is distinct from actor authentication.md

findings.title: Replay and new append admission deliberately differ
findings.body: New event preparation binds discovery actor/time, report physical manifest, work checkpoint predecessor/new-branch denominator and exclusive mutating owner. Historical replay retains weaker legacy envelopes so repair remains possible. A replay success alone does not prove every event satisfies current append policy.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1196 Replay and new append admission deliberately differ.md

findings.title: Ordinary transition branch bypasses undeclared feature requirement
findings.body: append_event delegates to append_events; eligible ordinary transitions use bulk preparation even for one event. Bulk reducer validates declared acceptance when present but does not set require_declared_feature_acceptance=True. An undeclared integrated card with complete chain can become operationally_verified. Pure memory probe confirmed strict branch rejects the same input and public dispatch branch accepts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1197 Ordinary transition branch bypasses undeclared feature requirement.md

findings.title: Feature acceptance regression fixture does not exercise absent declaration
findings.body: The test named new operational transition requires declared acceptance begins with card() that already supplies requirements. It checks missing acceptance evidence and stale revision, leaving the undeclared-card bulk branch untested by that case.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1198 Feature acceptance regression fixture does not exercise absent declaration.md

findings.title: Gap-switch invalidation can disappear from compact work history
findings.body: Guard searches retained checkpoints newer than admission for another active gap. Projection retains only eight checkpoint details and keeps unclosed admissions indefinitely. After A to B to A and enough same-A checkpoints, original A session passes again. Pure memory replay agrees with incremental projection; no live session was switched.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1199 Gap-switch invalidation can disappear from compact work history.md

findings.title: Guard omits permanent closed-admission hash index
findings.body: Projection retains closed admission hashes for all history, but guard checks only recent closure rows. With nine concurrent read sessions, closing newest then eight older sessions drops newest closure detail while its recent admission remains. Pure memory guard first rejected then accepted that closed session although closed hash remained. Append-time exclusivity does consult the permanent index.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1200 Guard omits permanent closed-admission hash index.md

findings.title: Existing work admission guard does not check current card closure
findings.body: New admission requires known non-closed card. guard_work_admission checks active gap/session/effect/scope but never current card state. Pure memory example closes card while session remains unclosed and same checkpoint active; guard still accepts existing read admission. No live card closure performed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1201 Existing work admission guard does not check current card closure.md

findings.title: Work owner exclusivity treats expired sessions as open until explicitly closed
findings.body: Append-time conflict check permits overlapping reads but refuses any new mutating admission against existing open read or mutating ownership on the gap. It does not check session expiry or gap-switch invalidation; explicit closure is required to release that owner. Guard separately rejects expired work.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1202 Work owner exclusivity treats expired sessions as open until explicitly closed.md

findings.title: Work checkpoint new-branch check does not carry every old unresolved branch
findings.body: Append verifies exact newly discovered cards since previous checkpoint and requires their unresolved members except active/closed/superseded. It does not require every still-open ID from previous unresolved_branch_gap_ids to remain. Thus this check protects new intake denominator, not complete branch-history conservation by itself.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1203 Work checkpoint new-branch check does not carry every old unresolved branch.md

findings.title: Closed-card outgoing handoff condition does not count prior handoffs
findings.body: Validator allows a closed active card when previous checkpoint has same active gap and switching_to is nonempty. It does not reject a second same-card outgoing checkpoint after the first. The test checks absent target, refusal of new work and one valid switch, not repeated outgoing emission.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1204 Closed-card outgoing handoff condition does not count prior handoffs.md

findings.title: Session scope equality is textual normalization under host authority
findings.body: Guard strips whitespace, normalizes slash direction, rejects duplicate/empty scopes and compares sorted sets. It does not resolve path aliases or execute effects. Actor ownership is not compared with a requesting identity because guard accepts no requester parameter. Host security retains execution authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1205 Session scope equality is textual normalization under host authority.md

findings.title: Historical work tests cover immediate refusal rather than compaction combinations
findings.body: Tests verify same-gap continuity, explicit close, expiry, higher-risk rejection and active gap mismatch; separate compaction case checks session-ID reuse. They do not guard a retained closed admission after closure detail evicts, or return to original gap after switch history eviction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1206 Historical work tests cover immediate refusal rather than compaction combinations.md

findings.title: Control ownership resolution is independent of lifecycle completion
findings.body: Non-visible source metadata can resolve ownership without reading path/symbol. Explicit typed bindings can remain resolved after operational disposition removes gap links. Aggregate parents resolve when child ownership resolutions do, regardless of child card state. This is deliberate ownership accounting, not repair completion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1207 Control ownership resolution is independent of lifecycle completion.md

findings.title: Card relationships record typed links without enforcing acyclic execution order
findings.body: Relationship reducer requires distinct known cards, supported relation and unique triple. It does not enforce global acyclicity or synchronize links with card dependencies/blockers. Aggregate resolution uses bounded fixed-point passes; cycles can remain unresolved rather than becoming execution ordering guarantees.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1208 Card relationships record typed links without enforcing acyclic execution order.md

findings.title: Current typed observation is a shape and supplied-source predicate
findings.body: Observation validates stages, flags, kind/mode and completeness; observed_at is nonempty text, not an age check. current_source and source hash are supplied assertions here rather than compared with repository bytes. Read-only observed operation may intentionally have attempted=False.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1209 Current typed observation is a shape and supplied-source predicate.md

findings.title: Inventory reconciliation examination and operational proof are separate
findings.body: Known-versus-disposed controls can reconcile inventory without any typed current observation. Examined requires all current controls have current_typed proof status, while operationally proven additionally requires operational disposition. surface_examined event alone does not satisfy these derived predicates.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1210 Inventory reconciliation examination and operational proof are separate.md

findings.title: Same-ID control metadata revision retains prior disposition observation
findings.body: Inventory revision predecessor binds sorted control IDs. If IDs stay the same while kind/label/source refs change, retained control_dispositions are preserved rather than invalidated or revalidated against new kind. Old current_typed status can survive the metadata change. Retiring/removing an ID does remove its live disposition while retaining history.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1211 Same-ID control metadata revision retains prior disposition observation.md

findings.title: Revised disposition detail history omits old typed observation
findings.body: Disposition revisions preserve prior disposition/gap/evidence/actor/time and predecessor binding, but historical detail row does not copy prior observation or proof_status. Full append-only JSONL remains required to recover that older typed observation; compact history retains only a latest detail plus hashes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1212 Revised disposition detail history omits old typed observation.md

findings.title: Evidence binding identifies current bytes without verifying supplied hashes
findings.body: _bind_evidence reads resolvable referenced local file only when artifact_sha256 absent. Caller-supplied digest is not compared with file bytes. Reference prefix sha256 or fragment presence can satisfy some bound checks without reopening immutable storage. These are binding metadata, not independent claim verification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1213 Evidence binding identifies current bytes without verifying supplied hashes.md

findings.title: Ledger evidence-path handling has different bounds from report admission
findings.body: Generic evidence resolution strips line suffixes and resolves contained paths before physical checks, so contained aliases can resolve to a physical target. _bind_evidence uses unbounded read_bytes; report manifest admission instead uses a 16MiB physical-file read and exact finding denominator/hash comparison.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1214 Ledger evidence-path handling has different bounds from report admission.md

findings.title: Historical admission backfill is append-only but changes effective replay payload
findings.body: Full replay validates exact earlier event target then overlays admission fields supplied by later backfill before validating the old transition. Dedicated writer requires full replay and appends one new event without rewriting original bytes. The resulting historical validation is assisted by later evidence, not proof of what the original event carried.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1215 Historical admission backfill is append-only but changes effective replay payload.md

findings.title: Compact head and dashboard API disagree on feature-aware open count
findings.body: _dashboard_index treats closed/operationally_verified/superseded as resolved only if declared feature acceptance verifies. dashboard_api both compact and full paths recomputes open_count from lifecycle states alone and derives source_status from it. Missing feature acceptance can remain in head critical blockers while punch-card API reports status-only resolved count.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1216 Compact head and dashboard API disagree on feature-aware open count.md

findings.title: Compact dashboard rows and detailed history are intentionally bounded
findings.body: Head retains first 100 priority-sorted cards, clips display fields and lists first 25 progress IDs with total/truncated flags. Full snapshot has bounded per-card history as well, so full-history investigation still needs JSONL. Unfiltered dashboard uses compact head only within its cached window; filtered/detail queries use snapshot.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1217 Compact dashboard rows and detailed history are intentionally bounded.md

findings.title: Checkpoint read verifies cross-file hashes rather than replaying all semantics
findings.body: Reader compares portable ledger size/hash, validates tail digest and links, verifies snapshot/delta hashes when requested, and rereads head for optimistic coherence. read_head intentionally omits snapshot. Unkeyed self-consistent head/snapshot replacement is not independently authenticated by a trusted external anchor or full replay on this path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1218 Checkpoint read verifies cross-file hashes rather than replaying all semantics.md

findings.title: Ledger digest cache trusts device inode size and mtime
findings.body: Fingerprint caches whole-ledger digest by device/inode/size/mtime_ns and extends it from admitted append bytes. Same-identity same-size content mutation with restored mtime can evade this cache; source has no post-hash fstat consistency check. Existing same-length mutation test changes file normally and does not restore metadata. This edge is source-derived, not reproduced here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1219 Ledger digest cache trusts device inode size and mtime.md

findings.title: Prepared events precede fsync but projection publication follows commit
findings.body: Entire bounded request is semantically prepared before ledger append. Opened file must match expected size/device/inode/mtime and writes loop to completion then fsync. Snapshot/delta/head publish afterward. Later publication error does not roll back JSONL; caller retry of same discovery can hit duplicate identity. Tests prove original event survives snapshot/head failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1220 Prepared events precede fsync but projection publication follows commit.md

findings.title: Atomic publication applies per file rather than across all checkpoint files
findings.body: Writer uses exclusive prepared filename, flush/fsync, os.replace and directory fsync where supported, then removes prepared file. Multiple files publish separately; optimistic readers retry three times and then report unavailable. A failure during prepared-file cleanup can also propagate after replacement.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1221 Atomic publication applies per file rather than across all checkpoint files.md

findings.title: Large-snapshot fallback can reuse the stale artifact that caused replay
findings.body: After append-base checkpoint failure, fallback returns full replay with predecessor=None. Publication subsequently rereads existing snapshot unbounded and, if at least 8MiB, uses it as delta base without requiring a verified predecessor. Corrupt JSON can raise after append; stale well-formed base plus only new appended rows can produce unreadable delta checkpoint. Source-derived path; normal forced-delta test uses valid base.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1222 Large-snapshot fallback can reuse the stale artifact that caused replay.md

findings.title: Delta checkpoint preflight and retention have separate limits
findings.body: Preappend preflight builds ordinary head. Delta-specific head fields are added and bounded after authoritative append. Cumulative delta is content-addressed; existing path is reused without reading equality in writer, though reader later verifies it. Old cumulative deltas are not reclaimed here, and compaction occurs only when delta bytes exceed 16MiB.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1223 Delta checkpoint preflight and retention have separate limits.md

findings.title: Automatic recovery distinguishes malformed suffix from semantic corruption
findings.body: Recovery only considers non-newline-terminated final suffix within event bound and first validates complete prefix. Invalid UTF8/JSON suffix is retained as exact base64/hash receipt before truncation. Syntactically complete but semantically invalid event is preserved and rejected. Valid complete event missing delimiter gets receipt then newline. No recovery executed by this audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1224 Automatic recovery distinguishes malformed suffix from semantic corruption.md

findings.title: Append fallback may perform recovery before requested event is admitted
findings.body: _load_append_base_unlocked is invoked under lock before preparing new requested event. Its recovery can write a receipt and alter final delimiter/torn suffix even if later payload validation fails. project/write_snapshot also invokes recovery; the read-only head/snapshot APIs do not.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1225 Append fallback may perform recovery before requested event is admitted.md

findings.title: Segment migration is a separate historical projection with partial publication
findings.body: Migration reads events under read_events lock then releases it before fingerprinting and writing segments/manifest. Concurrent append can change legacy identity; final equivalence validation can fail after new files exist. Existing differing manifest refuses overwrite. Legacy JSONL is retained and remains active authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1226 Segment migration is a separate historical projection with partial publication.md

findings.title: Segment validation verifies content equality but not every manifest range claim
findings.body: Validator checks manifest digest, segment byte/hash/count, combined exact legacy event equality, reducer validity and global legacy/head identity. It does not compare per-segment first_sequence/last_sequence/predecessor/head fields or enforce declared segment_event_limit against rows; manifest schema and read bounds are also not validated here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1227 Segment validation verifies content equality but not every manifest range claim.md

findings.title: Historical bootstrap conflicts with current provenance and chain admission
findings.body: Historical cards set discovered_by to historical-operational-surface-audit but record actor is bootstrap actor. Fixed current cards also carry fixed 20260816 time/actor while append timestamp defaults current; chain_for creates present/partial stages with empty evidence. Current append rejects these before writing batch. The script is historical producer evidence, not a working current initializer claim.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1228 Historical bootstrap conflicts with current provenance and chain admission.md

findings.title: Bootstrap surface union and dated findings must not become current truth
findings.body: Regex action collection unions whole files for several surfaces, then filters Studio action names heuristically. Fixed rows PX-OS-068..094 retain dated source narratives and conversation approval text, with selected transitions through implementing. Those statements describe original bootstrap context and authorize nothing in this audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1229 Bootstrap surface union and dated findings must not become current truth.md

findings.title: Live-size benchmark clone omits current delta projection files
findings.body: Benchmark copies JSONL/snapshot/head only after reading source head separately. A delta head points outside those three files; bounded read_snapshot on copy can fail before append fallback. Sequential source copy has no frozen identity check. Small non-delta clone test does not prove this copy works for delta checkpoints.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1230 Live-size benchmark clone omits current delta projection files.md

findings.title: Benchmark memory and rewrite metrics have narrower meaning than their labels
findings.body: Without psutil RSS is zero and budget passes. RSS sampling covers cold decode only; no process-isolated baseline. projection_rewrite_bytes_per_append compares snapshot endpoints, excludes head and cumulative delta writes, and is not divided by append count. All samples are few warm observations, not tail-latency population guarantees.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1231 Benchmark memory and rewrite metrics have narrower meaning than their labels.md

findings.title: Benchmark recovery and custody are explicit limits
findings.body: Recovery benchmark removes newline from valid final event rather than writing malformed suffix. TemporaryDirectory and threads are managed by language contexts without local owned workspace/process registration. Optional output permits external/overwriting path; source-size and source-head identities are sampled separately. This report only reviews its source and does not execute benchmark or cleanup.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1232 Benchmark recovery and custody are explicit limits.md

findings.title: Every-event test title exceeds actual exercised event list
findings.body: The equality test covers initialization/inventory/surface aliases/cards/annotations/one transition/dispositions/examination/report/relationship/checkpoint/revision. It does not enumerate all EVENT_TYPES and omits sessions/closures/attestations/backfill/scope revisions and other transitions in that case. Other tests cover many separately, but title is not exhaustive coverage evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1233 Every-event test title exceeds actual exercised event list.md
