findings.title: Scaling tests force representation rather than demonstrate production scale
findings.body: Scaling fixtures use one initial event and a one-byte threshold override; concurrency test appends eight surface events. They establish normal-path delta behavior, ordering and segment corruption handling on tiny inputs. Production-sized capacity, delta fallback after corrupt base and concurrent segmentation remain separate obligations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1234 Scaling tests force representation rather than demonstrate production scale.md

findings.title: Operator guard and mutation are separate APIs
findings.body: CLI exposes guard-work as explicit read_snapshot plus guard_work_admission call. Other mutation commands directly append and do not invoke guard themselves. JSON payload may come from unbounded stdin or arbitrary existing file. This interface assumes host orchestration supplies prior authorization/governance; actor flag alone is not proof.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1235 Operator guard and mutation are separate APIs.md

findings.title: Pinned review registration lacks the current embedded manifest
findings.body: Registration derives finding_ids from four review classification dictionaries and pins source bytes. The retained pinned JSON has neither finding_ids nor findings. Current ledger _validate_report_manifest requires embedded nonempty finding_ids exact equality, so fresh registration fails despite check planning successfully. Existing historical registration may be reused. Metadata observation is retained in historical-reconciliation-inputs.json.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1236 Pinned review registration lacks the current embedded manifest.md

findings.title: Registration check reports projected zero without append validation
findings.body: Check mode only constructs entries; it does not run ledger admission or recalculate final snapshot. Output unreconciled_after_apply is literal zero in both modes. Existing registered findings are checked for exact card disposition and IDs, but the displayed zero remains a planned result rather than current audited count.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1237 Registration check reports projected zero without append validation.md

findings.title: Historical binding compatibility accepts typed inventory class drift
findings.body: Same inventory ID rejects reviewed count below current control count; differing IDs are accepted whenever both share pacify-x-typed-surfaces- prefix. No inventory source digest or numeric revision ordering comparison. Exact referenced controls must exist, but that proves identity membership rather than unchanged source meaning.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1238 Historical binding compatibility accepts typed inventory class drift.md

findings.title: Reviewed bindings preserve gaps but can downgrade operational disposition
findings.body: For each reviewed control script unions missing card IDs and revises current operational or gap disposition to gap with exact predecessor hash. It requires a current disposition and creates no initial one. This deliberately records ownership uncertainty; it is not a new operational observation and it never advances card lifecycle.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1239 Reviewed bindings preserve gaps but can downgrade operational disposition.md

findings.title: Existing non-visible scope rerun checks only kind and path ID
findings.body: A matching non_visible_path/path_id skips before rechecking source refs, authority, reason or review overrides. New scopes filter source refs for nonempty strings but do not resolve symbols. Aggregate ready compares ordered child list, whereas split tool later compares sets/supersets. Different rerun predicates can disagree.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1240 Existing non-visible scope rerun checks only kind and path ID.md

findings.title: Reference repair fills all empty present stages from one existing path
findings.body: Quality reconciler selects first existing discovery/source path or entire ledger fallback and inserts that same reference into each empty present/partial stage, retaining stage state and claiming restored support. It checks file existence rather than each stage claim. This can clear required-reference denominator without new interaction evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1241 Reference repair fills all empty present stages from one existing path.md

findings.title: Owner and symbol quality repair is a fixed metadata assignment
findings.body: Only unassigned/unknown owner labels become codex-primary. Six card IDs have fixed path-to-symbol fill rules only for empty symbol lists. No ownership acknowledgment, symbol existence or current source hash is checked by this script; incorrect nonempty metadata is left unchanged.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1242 Owner and symbol quality repair is a fixed metadata assignment.md

findings.title: Reference selection and ledger binding have different containment rules
findings.body: Quality helper permits absolute existing paths and strips the final colon suffix heuristically; generic ledger evidence binder hashes only resolved contained files. A helper-selected external path can therefore remain unbound. Fallback ledger file is mutable and each independently committed chunk may bind a different prefix.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1243 Reference selection and ledger binding have different containment rules.md

findings.title: Accepted punch-card refresh changes proof binding without re-execution
findings.body: Reconciler replaces stale hashes with current artifact bytes and updates accepted record timestamp, preserving accepted status. It runs no acceptance tests. Operation coverage checks the newly current digests, so digest drift can clear while original behavior remains un-reverified. Open modern records are intentionally skipped.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1244 Accepted punch-card refresh changes proof binding without re-execution.md

findings.title: Punch-card refresh can partially write before later error
findings.body: Errors list is shared across sorted records. Dirty records are written only when no errors have yet accumulated; a later malformed/missing record prevents subsequent writes but does not roll back earlier ones. Final valid=False can coexist with earlier accepted-record mutations. Writes are direct and have no retained revision/atomic group.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1245 Punch-card refresh can partially write before later error.md

findings.title: Punch refresh input checks are weaker than coverage acceptance
findings.body: Empty or non-list artifacts can produce zero checked rows without error; nonobject list entries are silently skipped. accepted_record_count counts all immediate JSON files including skipped open/unsupported/unreadable ones. Coverage requires nonempty list and validates each artifact object/unique path. Reconciler valid is not coverage acceptance validity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1246 Punch refresh input checks are weaker than coverage acceptance.md

findings.title: Duplicate modern artifact paths update only their first occurrence
findings.body: Rows are captured before mutation. On mismatch, next(...) finds first artifact with matching path, so later duplicate entries can retain stale digest while apply reports valid when no errors. Coverage separately rejects duplicate resolved paths. Existing tests do not include duplicate entries.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1247 Duplicate modern artifact paths update only their first occurrence.md

findings.title: External re-audit importer pins denominator rather than source authority
findings.body: Parser requires exact Markdown row syntax, unique A-Z/three-digit IDs, exactly 113 rows and fixed severity/family totals. Other lines are ignored. It hashes original bytes and initializes every finding open with no owner/acceptance evidence. Correct counts do not validate truth or completeness outside this fixed table grammar.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1248 External re-audit importer pins denominator rather than source authority.md

findings.title: Re-audit import is standalone and its portability substitution is narrow
findings.body: Output is a separate remediation schema, not operational ledger events. Home substitution replaces only current native/doubled-backslash home spellings; it is not general path redaction. CLI directly writes arbitrary supplied output after creating parents, with no exclusive creation or source/output distinction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1249 Re-audit import is standalone and its portability substitution is narrow.md

findings.title: Live-walk mapping creates fixed feature families independent of report membership
findings.body: Nine CARD_SPECS are proposed before iterating actual report findings. Existing features are indexed globally by name, with last duplicate winning, without matching surface/control/evidence. New IDs are allocated from a snapshot outside append lock; concurrent discovery can cause collision rejected at append.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1250 Live-walk mapping creates fixed feature families independent of report membership.md

findings.title: Live-walk historical report registration has the same manifest mismatch
findings.body: Retained walk reports have findings arrays but no top-level finding_ids. Script derives IDs from findings and later hashes a separate reread, while current ledger physical report validator requires embedded IDs. Fresh registration fails current contract; existing report IDs bypass registration. No live walker was run.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1251 Live-walk historical report registration has the same manifest mismatch.md

findings.title: Live-walk rerun skips existing mappings without verifying their binding
findings.body: If report ID already registered its source hash/finding denominator is not compared to current retained file. If finding ID already reconciled its disposition/gap IDs are not checked, unlike pinned review registration. New mapping relies on fixed dictionaries and unknown IDs raise; historical source claims remain discovery-only.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1252 Live-walk rerun skips existing mappings without verifying their binding.md

findings.title: Aggregate splitter rejects new children before creating them
findings.body: _parent_child_set always includes new_children IDs. main computes unknown=set(children)-set(cards) and exits before the later loop that would append missing card_discovered events. Therefore new_child_cards cannot become nonzero through this path; script presently reconciles only already-existing allocated IDs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1253 Aggregate splitter rejects new children before creating them.md

findings.title: Split rerun treats allocated ID existence as prior application
findings.body: Any planned ID already in cards is accepted as pre-applied without comparing parent, feature, discovery source or payload. Frontier check only requires current maximum at least historical last_existing. Allocation count/uniqueness/min/max are checked but not contiguous sequence or absence of collision with unrelated existing cards.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1254 Split rerun treats allocated ID existence as prior application.md

findings.title: Aggregate selector membership varies with current gap dispositions
findings.body: Selectors enumerate current disposition rows, filter typed kind/label/regex, and union gap_ids. Operational promotion can remove those gap IDs and change desired child set despite fixed plan bytes. This makes historical plan plus current state the real input, not plan SHA alone.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1255 Aggregate selector membership varies with current gap dispositions.md

findings.title: Aggregate scope revision preserves extras only in the superset branch
findings.body: When current children already include every required child, script keeps prior extras. If one required child is missing, it revises to exactly ordered_children, dropping prior extra scope children although relationship history remains. Thus preservation depends on whether a missing child triggers revision.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1256 Aggregate scope revision preserves extras only in the superset branch.md

findings.title: Dormant split discovery payload conflicts with append-time timestamp
findings.body: Child payload uses fixed DISCOVERED_AT, but queued card_discovered event has no matching timestamp. If missing-child guard were repaired, current ledger requires discovered_at exactly match generated event time, creating a second independent incompatibility. This is source-derived dormant-path analysis.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1257 Dormant split discovery payload conflicts with append-time timestamp.md

findings.title: Review and split dry runs do not invoke ledger admission
findings.body: Check computes planned entries but does not project them through strengthened reducer/append-time validators. Apply uses independent bounded chunks; validation protects each chunk but no all-proposal transaction or final semantic denominator recomputation. A check count is a plan, not guaranteed applicable change.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1258 Review and split dry runs do not invoke ledger admission.md

findings.title: Stream reconciliation turns implementation labels into executable handler claims
findings.body: Child capability labels partition skills into operational versus deferred. Every handler is then marked executable regardless of missing enhancement count. No function loading, test invocation or receipt check occurs. Runtime uses executable status for admission after its separate preflight, so this writer affects activation metadata rather than merely display titles.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1259 Stream reconciliation turns implementation labels into executable handler claims.md

findings.title: Stream missing denominator is moved and two files publish separately
findings.body: Writer sets missing_capabilities=[] and retains nonoperational entries under deferred_capabilities, labels source adapted-bounded-runtime and chooses one of seventeen fixed titles. Unknown orchestration IDs fail. Sequential direct writes can leave orchestration and handler views inconsistent on second-write failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1260 Stream missing denominator is moved and two files publish separately.md

findings.title: Studio reconciliation validates byte projection rather than protocol
findings.body: Writer reads owner once and copies raw bytes to two targets without parsing JSON, schema or operation kinds. Apply reports valid whenever writes return; no immediate postwrite/source stability check. Import-time studio_protocol performs schema check, and generated_artifacts later compares bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1261 Studio reconciliation validates byte projection rather than protocol.md

findings.title: Studio projection writes are not a combined atomic publication
findings.body: Targets are fixed paths but writer uses normal path operations, no resolved target containment/physical-file check, exclusive temp replacement or rollback. Existing links can redirect writes; second target failure can leave first updated. This audit only maps behavior and does not reconcile source projections.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1262 Studio projection writes are not a combined atomic publication.md

findings.title: Reference candidate partial coverage is a fixed mapping declaration
findings.body: Fifteen canonical IDs receive predetermined skill/symbol unions and partial_semantic_coverage. No actual symbol availability, source digest or tests are verified. Existing active_composed rows are skipped entirely, preserving their claims. Broader source capability is explicitly still unadmitted.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1263 Reference candidate partial coverage is a fixed mapping declaration.md

findings.title: Reference reconciliation marker is historical text rather than fresh certification
findings.body: Helper writes runtime_reconciliation=2026-08-02-structural-recertification and recomputes delivery/canonical/duplicate counts. CLI overwrites registry directly. Neither the marker nor counts are a certification receipt or proof that referenced functions implement broader candidate semantics.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1264 Reference reconciliation marker is historical text rather than fresh certification.md

findings.title: Punch refresh tests establish narrow preservation and containment cases
findings.body: Tests assert accepted digest refresh, untouched open digest and escaping artifact rejection. They do not execute or validate original accepted behavior, timestamp meaning, duplicate or empty artifact handling, malformed records or multi-record partial commit. Their assertions should support only those narrow helper contracts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1265 Punch refresh tests establish narrow preservation and containment cases.md

findings.title: Inventory reconciliation covers incoming surfaces rather than whole-surface retirement
findings.body: Only incoming known surfaces are reconciled. Identical control IDs and records skip the revision without comparing source_files. Entire old surfaces absent from input are not retired here. Expected inventory checks exact source metadata and predecessor, but are a separate event.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1266 Inventory reconciliation covers incoming surfaces rather than whole-surface retirement.md

findings.title: Receipt classification validates claimed source flags rather than source bytes
findings.body: Current source requires host_source_mismatch false and source_identity.state verified; the control manifest digest is checked for SHA grammar. This helper does not recompute the inventoried source identity or establish receipt age.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1267 Receipt classification validates claimed source flags rather than source bytes.md

findings.title: Duplicate chain stages collapse before exact-denominator validation
findings.body: Stage rows become a dictionary keyed by stage, so later duplicates replace earlier values. Equality of resulting keys to CHAIN_STAGES does not require exactly one row per stage. Generated receipt fragment references can fill stage evidence without a raw evidence artifact.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1268 Duplicate chain stages collapse before exact-denominator validation.md

findings.title: Observation fallback and ledger normalization have different semantics
findings.body: A visible clean complete indicator can enter fallback whether observed is omitted or explicitly false. The produced v1 observation can retain observed=false, while ledger v1 normalization derives observed from rendered and drops extra fields. Conversely a nonvisible observed=true/rendered=false planner result may fail ledger operational admission.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1269 Observation fallback and ledger normalization have different semantics.md

findings.title: Recovered authority boundary is a narrow explicit disposition class
findings.body: Only ten named controls with required boundary metadata, observed failure/recovery and an incomplete stage can qualify. These remain gap dispositions with gap IDs, observed-only outcomes and v2 evidence; accepting their boundary does not establish execution of the protected operation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1270 Recovered authority boundary is a narrow explicit disposition class.md

findings.title: Unobserved foreign rows can pad receipt cardinality before membership checks
findings.body: Receipt total, record length and globally unique IDs must equal known control count. A record yielding no observation is skipped before known surface/control membership checks, so cardinality alone does not guarantee exact receipt membership. Full completion additionally requires every expected observation, limiting the effect on final valid status.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1271 Unobserved foreign rows can pad receipt cardinality before membership checks.md

findings.title: Prior operational state suppresses contrary error observations
findings.body: When a newly classified result would be gap and the current disposition is operational, the planner unconditionally continues. The condition includes new errors and failure results, not just harmless partial metadata. An explicit separate path must therefore correct an old operational disposition.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1272 Prior operational state suppresses contrary error observations.md

findings.title: Dry simulation retains fields and history that live projection discards
findings.body: Observation simulation copies raw observations and extends full prior history. The live ledger normalizes typed observations and compacts retained history. Proposal equality and card-binding reachability can consequently differ between simulation, first apply and repeated apply.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1273 Dry simulation retains fields and history that live projection discards.md

findings.title: Historical card advancement depends on retained compact history
findings.body: Binding discovery enumerates current dispositions and retained history only, then tests current disposition outcome. Older gap bindings evicted by ledger compaction disappear from this planner even though original events remain in the durable JSONL. Explicit card control scopes are not an alternate binding source here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1274 Historical card advancement depends on retained compact history.md

findings.title: Special feature acceptance copies requirements into synthesized evidence
findings.body: For unverified-operational-control cards, synthesis copies requirement revision, criteria, dependency keys, classes, authority and tests into verified evidence backed by one aggregate receipt, then invokes the metadata verifier. It does not independently demonstrate that the receipt exercised every copied required test or evidence class.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1275 Special feature acceptance copies requirements into synthesized evidence.md

findings.title: Card planner reuses aggregate proof across lifecycle transitions
findings.body: Eligible primary-state cards receive merged chain evidence and forward transitions through operational verification. The same aggregate receipt supports multiple lifecycle steps. The helper does not execute implementation, tests or integration work, and current outcome checks do not independently revalidate full chain/current source proof.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1276 Card planner reuses aggregate proof across lifecycle transitions.md

findings.title: Nonprimary card states can abort reconciliation planning
findings.body: The planner skips selected terminal, host-owned and excluded cards, then calls CARD_PRIMARY_STATES.index(state). A bound eligible card in blocked, deferred or reopened state can raise rather than produce a controlled nontransition result.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1277 Nonprimary card states can abort reconciliation planning.md

findings.title: Completion can accept recovered boundaries with no operational controls
findings.body: Status distinguishes current operational controls from acceptable recovered authority boundaries. A discovered gap card bound to an accepted boundary can be excluded from nonterminal cards. The test fixture demonstrates valid status with zero operational receipt controls; this is boundary accounting rather than complete execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1278 Completion can accept recovered boundaries with no operational controls.md

findings.title: Completion checks terminal labels rather than feature acceptance again
findings.body: Status counts only cards found through current/retained disposition bindings and regards terminal card states as complete without repeating feature acceptance validation. Unbound cards are outside this denominator; boundary-linked cards can be exempted even if their broader bindings remain.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1279 Completion checks terminal labels rather than feature acceptance again.md

findings.title: Inventory changes can commit before receipt rejection
findings.body: CLI apply submits inventory revisions before it loads and validates the optional live receipt. It later submits discovery, initial disposition, observation and card batches separately. A bad receipt or later invalid completion result can follow already committed mutations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1280 Inventory changes can commit before receipt rejection.md

findings.title: Discovery identity and requirements can drift across inventory revisions
findings.body: Missing-card allocation uses a sampled maximum ID outside the append lock and existing cards are indexed by control_action without surface identity. Initial feature requirements pin the discovery inventory hash; later synthesis can retain that old requirement revision with newer aggregate evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1281 Discovery identity and requirements can drift across inventory revisions.md

findings.title: Check-mode completion is based partly on uncommitted plans
findings.body: Check simulates raw dispositions, and planned reconciled card IDs are excluded from final nonterminal count without applying their transition events through the reducer. The printed valid result is proposal validity under that simulation, not a current committed state. operational_claims also counts observation revisions, excluding direct initial operational bindings.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1282 Check-mode completion is based partly on uncommitted plans.md

findings.title: Reconciliation tests omit live normalization and failing apply sequences
findings.body: Tests cover important planner branches and mocked status, but do not run full ledger append normalization, history compaction, duplicate stage rows, error-based demotion suppression, nonprimary card states or multi-phase partial commits. Their source does not prove those paths safe.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1283 Reconciliation tests omit live normalization and failing apply sequences.md

findings.title: Installed owner plan is command-shape validation only
findings.body: Plan reports effects=false after command validation. Campaign activity, exact artifact hash/size/mtime, package/install receipts, engine manifest and fresh output paths are checked only by execute. Plan success is not operational readiness.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1284 Installed owner plan is command-shape validation only.md

findings.title: Installed command validation leaves executable and shell latitude
findings.body: Windows/exhaustive commands check node basename, script and selected flags while allowing extra arguments. Ubuntu checks fixed wsl prefix and shell-string markers rather than parsing or proving command equivalence; markers can occur alongside other shell content. These are caller-controlled commands within host authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1285 Installed command validation leaves executable and shell latitude.md

findings.title: Installed preflight validates upstream receipt claims without redoing their audit
findings.body: Package/install receipt schema, artifact identity, counts, cleanup and stage fields are checked. Engine manifest shape and digest are read. The owner does not itself inspect ZIP contents, reconstruct the installed tree or verify engine tree contents against the manifest. Those remain upstream owner obligations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1286 Installed preflight validates upstream receipt claims without redoing their audit.md

findings.title: Fresh output paths are not checked for mutual uniqueness
findings.body: Execute rejects existing summary/log/receipt/lifecycle/report paths, but does not require all configured paths be distinct. Resolved contained aliases are accepted by path construction. Collisions can fail after the stage claim rather than during freshness checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1287 Fresh output paths are not checked for mutual uniqueness.md

findings.title: Process timeout and interruption closure differ
findings.body: Process wait timeout attempts Windows tree termination or POSIX group termination and verifies the leader has stopped. Other BaseException paths close the log but do not terminate the child. POSIX leader polling is not a complete descendant inventory. Owner wrapper itself does not register its launched processes in resource lifecycle.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1288 Process timeout and interruption closure differ.md

findings.title: Parallel launch uses sequential wait budgets
findings.body: Windows and Ubuntu are started before either wait, but each timeout begins at its own wait call. The second process may run during the entire first wait and then receive its full timeout. Launch/wait errors are retained after waiting existing children. Ordinary smoke result failures still allow the exhaustive member to run.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1289 Parallel launch uses sequential wait budgets.md

findings.title: Smoke receipt checks do not establish all host status semantics
findings.body: Smoke result validates artifact hashes, platform, engine identity and embedded/separate lifecycle equality. Host receipt is primarily schema-checked; broader host readiness or listener state is not independently established here. Fresh paths provide run isolation, not authentication of every reported fact.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1290 Smoke receipt checks do not establish all host status semantics.md

findings.title: Exhaustive result trusts aggregate fields rather than enumerating controls
findings.body: The exhaustive member checks reported completion, issues, normalized counters, scope/process/cleanup and artifact fields. It does not enumerate every profile/control chain or bind report and receipt through source, engine or campaign identities. Recursive counter coercion accepts several noninteger input forms.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1291 Exhaustive result trusts aggregate fields rather than enumerating controls.md

findings.title: Final artifact failure can publish and advance a passed stage
findings.body: After all three members pass, execute sets passed=true and then rechecks the artifact. The catch stores the exception without resetting passed. Summary can contain all_passed=true plus error; finish receives true and repair phase advances before OwnerBlocked is raised. Confirmed using the actual execute flow with all effects faked; retained probe at data/semantic-closure/installed-owner-order-probe.json.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1292 Final artifact failure can publish and advance a passed stage.md

findings.title: Post-claim summary construction can skip release finish
findings.body: Fresh package/install artifact references are computed outside the main catch and before the guarded summary write. A reference read failure there propagates before effects.finish, leaving claim closure to external recovery. Final source/engine identity and upstream receipt bytes are not revalidated as one stable snapshot.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1293 Post-claim summary construction can skip release finish.md

findings.title: Summary publication release finish and repair advance are separate effects
findings.body: Exclusive prepared summary publication uses a prior existence check then replacement; concurrent target creation can race that check. Finish runs before a separate repair-state rewrite. Finish or advance failure is not rolled back by this owner, and advance does not use a shared predecessor-bound transaction with the release stage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1294 Summary publication release finish and repair advance are separate effects.md

findings.title: Installed owner tests use synthetic artifacts and effects
findings.body: The tests validate launch order, preflight gates and selected ordinary failures with fake VSIX bytes, fake receipts and fake processes. They do not establish real timeout/descendant closure, final artifact drift handling, summary failure recovery, command equivalence or full installed-host compatibility.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1295 Installed owner tests use synthetic artifacts and effects.md

findings.title: Frozen DAG inventory does not make every list exact
findings.body: The validator enforces 43 distinct node records and 86 distinct dependency edges, matching known cards and a topological dependency order. Topological_order is checked by set equality without list length/uniqueness, so a duplicate terminal entry passes; confirmed with a pure synthetic 43-node/86-edge graph. Consumer lists must include reverse dependencies but may contain extra known consumers without reverse dependency.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1296 Frozen DAG inventory does not make every list exact.md

findings.title: Checksum inventory binds expected projection names rather than all directory files
findings.body: SHA256SUMS must list exactly cards, DAG and README and match their bytes. Additional directory files are not part of that inventory. Evidence readers resolve paths before checking symlinks and hash/stat separately; contained aliases and concurrent content changes are not excluded as one stable physical snapshot.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1297 Checksum inventory binds expected projection names rather than all directory files.md

findings.title: Historical evidence validates receipt fields without executing behavioral criteria
findings.body: The fixed freeze, final99 full/validation and repair12 receipts are validated and selected referenced files are hashed. Focused-test logs and installed focused receipts/reports are retained by hash rather than interpreted for each card criterion. Benchmark budget_results only requires all supplied values truthy, including the empty dictionary case; full-profile group count equality does not itself establish positive exact counts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1298 Historical evidence validates receipt fields without executing behavioral criteria.md

findings.title: Card evidence requires some implementation file rather than every declared file
findings.body: Live references are limited to recognized evidence families or one external orchestration path. Source cards need nonempty criteria/test/symbol strings, but symbols are not resolved and missing declared files are skipped as long as one exists. External anchor validation uses card ID substring presence. These checks establish traceability shape rather than complete implementation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1299 Card evidence requires some implementation file rather than every declared file.md

findings.title: Cohesion successor syntax is broader than numerical successor order
findings.body: Installed proof accepts any positive final number/date matching the campaign pattern. Close binds the exact repair12 predecessor through the release kernel, but does not compare the candidate number/date to final99. The word successor therefore carries a caller ordering obligation beyond this regex.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1300 Cohesion successor syntax is broader than numerical successor order.md

findings.title: Installed proof consumer accepts selected summary facts and retained bytes
findings.body: The consumer requires all_passed, concurrency flags, exact three member names, zero exits, artifact/process flags and exhaustive aggregate counters; it verifies hashes for member logs/receipts/lifecycle/report. It does not parse those member artifacts or check each member valid field, and does not reject a top-level summary error. Actual artifact drift still fails its hash checks; this is not a claim that every owner error bypasses closure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1301 Installed proof consumer accepts selected summary facts and retained bytes.md

findings.title: Release timing is checked without proving admission event authenticity
findings.body: Close requires exact release and automation stage insertion order, passing labels, sequential UTC windows and automation windows enclosing release windows. Admission/gap IDs are checked only as nonempty strings, not against ledger work admissions. Source digests bind the release kernel but are not recomputed from current repository bytes here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1302 Release timing is checked without proving admission event authenticity.md

findings.title: Installed proof timestamp is not joined to the release window
findings.body: finished_utc is valid UTC syntax and becomes the default card close timestamp. It is not compared with the installed release stage finish, automation finish, earlier card history or explicit --at. A syntactically valid override can therefore predate the evidence it purports to reconcile.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1303 Installed proof timestamp is not joined to the release window.md

findings.title: Lifecycle history is synthesized from one reconciliation event
findings.body: All intermediate lifecycle entries between current and target receive the same timestamp, reason and evidence references. This is an evidence-backed projection of claimed progress, not a record showing separate admitted implementation, test and integration executions. Existing at-target/closed cards return without refreshing evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1304 Lifecycle history is synthesized from one reconciliation event.md

findings.title: Project-state projection replaces broader state with fixed campaign claims
findings.body: The writer clears degraded_components, replaces failures/open circuits/unknowns, sets branch main without querying branch, fixes revision at least 44 and clears active card. Counts are derived from requested target rather than actual mixed retained card states; existing closed cards can coexist with a downstream target reporting zero closed in management state.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1305 Project-state projection replaces broader state with fixed campaign claims.md

findings.title: Cohesion WAL validates after-images without a planning predecessor
findings.body: Cards/evidence/state are read and projected before commit. JsonWal captures before-images under its own lock; custom precommit reads transition.after only and does not compare transition.before with the previously validated planning snapshot. A concurrent valid change before lock acquisition can be overwritten by the older proposal while still becoming the transaction before-image.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1306 Cohesion WAL validates after-images without a planning predecessor.md

findings.title: WAL recovery precedes fresh reconciliation evidence checks
findings.body: Apply invokes recover before card checksums, current evidence and close gates. Check only inspects and fails if recovery is needed. A previous committed proposal may therefore be completed during apply before the new request passes its evidence checks; recovery and new admission are distinct stages.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1307 WAL recovery precedes fresh reconciliation evidence checks.md

findings.title: Control and cohesion apply are not one atomic operation
findings.body: The release driver requires check-control, check-cohesion, apply-control, apply-cohesion in exactly that order. Control events use append batches while cohesion uses a separate WAL. A failure after control apply can leave control changes committed without cohesion closure; driver final status separately checks both denominators.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1308 Control and cohesion apply are not one atomic operation.md

findings.title: Closed cohesion is deliberately short of certification
findings.body: Close requires certify pending and active release identity, plus prior installed stage pass. Management state and README explicitly retain certification/publication obligations. A later check after certification changes these conditions, so repeated close is not an unconditional post-certification verifier.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1309 Closed cohesion is deliberately short of certification.md

findings.title: Cohesion tests prove useful recovery and metadata cases within synthetic evidence
findings.body: Tests cover deterministic plans, checksums, dependency disagreement, explicit idempotent apply, interrupted fifth-target publication/recovery, exact member identity, stage chronology, resource status and repeat close. Synthetic artifacts can be arbitrary bytes; tests do not prove member contents or each acceptance criterion, planning race safety, summary-error handling or duplicate topology rejection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1310 Cohesion tests prove useful recovery and metadata cases within synthetic evidence.md

findings.title: Typed inventory fuses historical semantics and current declarations
findings.body: One historical surface overlay replaces the base surface after base SHA validation. Current action contracts and two controller navigation arrays add declarations; fixed mappings add structural/native/variant controls. The output is a hybrid provenance baseline, not a fresh rendered or executed inventory.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1311 Typed inventory fuses historical semantics and current declarations.md

findings.title: Current action coverage is only at the base action name
findings.body: Every action contract must appear somewhere among historical/current typed action label prefixes. It does not require each rendered surface or template variant to be mapped. Historical actions absent from current contracts are retained, and structural/native controls are hardcoded rather than derived from current handlers/package commands.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1312 Current action coverage is only at the base action name.md

findings.title: Action inventory duplicate rows can collapse before count validation
findings.body: Action records are keyed by action name and compared only with declared action_count. Duplicate rows can be hidden if the declared count matches unique keys. Navigation parsing uses regex over two specific const-array forms, so source formatting or commented text can affect discovery independently of runtime rendering.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1313 Action inventory duplicate rows can collapse before count validation.md

findings.title: Typed inventory source provenance is incomplete for generated controls
findings.body: Top-level hashes bind overlay, action inventory and dashboard controller, but not builder source or extension package bytes used by the fixed native-command list. Per-surface source_files come from historical source_refs rather than the union of current per-control rendered references. Source refs and base_report paths are consumed without an overall containment or immutable snapshot check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1314 Typed inventory source provenance is incomplete for generated controls.md

findings.title: Inventory lifecycle IDs depend on historical list position
findings.body: Lifecycle identities use path.1, path.2 and so on. Reordering or inserting historical lifecycle labels changes identity-to-meaning association. Stable names for actions coexist with positional lifecycle IDs; consumers must evaluate metadata revisions rather than assuming identical ID preserves semantics.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1315 Inventory lifecycle IDs depend on historical list position.md

findings.title: Typed inventory generation writes directly and tests only a narrow exclusion rule
findings.body: Default CLI overwrites registry bytes; check compares exact bytes with regenerated output. It is not an atomic publication across its input sources. The sole test verifies five hidden fields stay excluded and total count equals unique IDs, not current rendered completeness or negative malformed-source cases.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1316 Typed inventory generation writes directly and tests only a narrow exclusion rule.md

findings.title: Heuristic catalog does not retain a complete discovery error denominator
findings.body: Catalog prunes named dependency/build directories, silently continues on stat/read failures and uses os.walk without onerror. It emits no file hashes. Its file_count is successful selected rows rather than all physical files. Optional summaries read at most nominal 1 MiB files but only return a short heuristic description.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1317 Heuristic catalog does not retain a complete discovery error denominator.md

findings.title: Catalog redaction and classification are narrow lexical transformations
findings.body: Three source terms are substituted, not arbitrary private paths or secrets. Classification follows ordered path/name/size rules, with governance before skills before tests and other categories. These recommendations are not capability admission or semantic review. Existing output files under the root can enter later runs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1318 Catalog redaction and classification are narrow lexical transformations.md

findings.title: Hash-backed inventory accounting excludes traversal failures and configured omissions
findings.body: Selected file failures are retained and cause CLI failure, but os.walk has no onerror and pruned directories/root-files-only entries never enter files_discovered. Thus discovered=records+errors can hold despite an unreadable or excluded subtree. File symlinks are not rejected before stat/read/hash.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1319 Hash-backed inventory accounting excludes traversal failures and configured omissions.md

findings.title: File identity text structure and hash can describe different versions
findings.body: Inventory stat, sample read, optional full text read and final streaming SHA are separate operations without before/after identity verification. Concurrent edits can produce old size/structure with new hash. Full-tree freeze likewise stats before hashing each file and does not lock or compare a second snapshot.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1320 File identity text structure and hash can describe different versions.md

findings.title: Inventory text structure is bounded lexical evidence rather than parser semantics
findings.body: Text detection uses a 64 KiB sample, suffix/MIME or UTF-8. Structure extraction uses regex headings, fences, links, command prefixes and declaration lines over text below a size threshold. Normalized digest uses sanitized casefolded whitespace; SimHash takes at most 100000 tokens. Large text remains text with empty structure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1321 Inventory text structure is bounded lexical evidence rather than parser semantics.md

findings.title: Structure projection trusts upstream format and identity
findings.body: extract copies selected metadata from rows labeled text and derives format from path suffix. It does not parse any source file or verify the source hash. The test proves only Markdown/JSON retention and binary exclusion from declared input labels.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1322 Structure projection trusts upstream format and identity.md

findings.title: Exact duplicate groups trust supplied hashes and can contain only one distinct ID
findings.body: Grouping uses declared sha256 and int(bytes), without reading source contents. It requires two input rows before deduplicating IDs, so repeated same-ID rows can emit a count-one group. Group IDs truncate SHA and omit size, though grouping key includes size.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1323 Exact duplicate groups trust supplied hashes and can contain only one distinct ID.md

findings.title: Duplicate classification implicitly chooses the lexicographically first ID
findings.body: Exact groups sort IDs; classifier marks members[1:] duplicate. That makes the first hash-derived ID canonical by position without reviewed provenance or quality. A missing optional duplicate file silently disables this stage. Duplicates are classified before executable-extension checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1324 Duplicate classification implicitly chooses the lexicographically first ID.md

findings.title: Near-duplicate prefix bucketing loses close neighbors
findings.body: SimHash candidates are only compared within equal extension and equal first four hex digits. A one-bit difference in that prefix prevents comparison even when full Hamming distance is within threshold. Normalized-hash equality is a separate exact grouping path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1325 Near-duplicate prefix bucketing loses close neighbors.md

findings.title: Greedy SimHash clusters are not pairwise or transitive equivalence
findings.body: Each unassigned anchor collects later candidates within distance, then all are assigned. Members need not be close to each other and transitive neighbors can be split. Confidence is computed from configured max_hamming rather than actual measured distances. Large same-prefix buckets can require quadratic comparisons.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1326 Greedy SimHash clusters are not pairwise or transitive equivalence.md

findings.title: Zero unknown classification comes from forced fallback labels
findings.body: The first matching path/heading rule wins; confidence is a fixed lexical score. Remaining records become not_applicable, knowledge_reference_only or clean_room_required, then summary hardcodes unknown_count=0. This does not establish reviewed applicability, safe execution or correct semantic ownership. Quarantine is only a review-state string.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1327 Zero unknown classification comes from forced fallback labels.md

findings.title: Review cluster identity binds grouping attributes rather than members
findings.body: Clusters group class/domain/review_state and select the shortest lexical path as representative. ID hashes a pipe-joined tuple, without member-list identity or delimiter escaping. Member duplicates are not rejected and representative choice is not evidence quality ranking.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1328 Review cluster identity binds grouping attributes rather than members.md

findings.title: Partition merge assumes sorted inputs and keeps a global ID set
findings.body: heapq.merge is applied to streams without checking each stream is ordered. It avoids retaining all rows but stores every seen ID, so memory is still proportional to corpus identity count. Output input-aliasing is not rejected; lazy input iterators can open after output truncation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1329 Partition merge assumes sorted inputs and keeps a global ID set.md

findings.title: Partition merge failure can replace a good result with a partial file
findings.body: Output is opened directly before row validation. A duplicate ID or malformed later record raises after earlier rows have been written, and summary is not updated as a transaction. Input file existence alone is checked before output mutation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1330 Partition merge failure can replace a good result with a partial file.md

findings.title: Partition campaign can reconcile an empty or partially omitted campaign
findings.body: Immediate directories missing summary or inventory are skipped; explicit exclusions further reduce scope. Reconciliation trusts summary counts and root flags, including empty roots/list vacuous truth. Inventory contents, supplied hashes and error-log rows are not read, and logged errors can intentionally count as reconciled files.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1331 Partition campaign can reconcile an empty or partially omitted campaign.md

findings.title: Map digest refresh does not restore source evidence validity
findings.body: Rehash updates inventory_sha256 from current map bytes and replaces an existing Markdown hash line. It does not validate records, source hashes, counts or the claimed preceding sanitization. Multiple partitions and JSON/Markdown writes can partially finish.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1332 Map digest refresh does not restore source evidence validity.md

findings.title: Freeze helper captures one file view rather than an immutable full topology
findings.body: Snapshot includes paths recognized as files with content hash, size and mtime, omitting directory and other entry identity. File links can dereference content, casefold-only sorting can tie, and no scan budget or second matching snapshot is enforced. Output under the scanned root changes future manifests; timestamp also changes output bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1333 Freeze helper captures one file view rather than an immutable full topology.md

findings.title: Source comparison misses normalized matches of different byte lengths
findings.body: Workspace candidates are prefiltered by source raw byte sizes before both exact and normalized comparison. Whitespace-only changes that alter length can therefore be absent from normalized matches. Normalization casefolds code/text and collapses whitespace, which is not semantic equivalence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1334 Source comparison misses normalized matches of different byte lengths.md

findings.title: Source comparison scope and completeness are heuristic
findings.body: Traversal excludes selected names and quarantine by resolved roots, but does not reject external file links or establish a stable snapshot. Reads are unbounded. active_implementation is assigned from fixed path prefixes, so matching bytes in that scope do not establish current runtime usage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1335 Source comparison scope and completeness are heuristic.md

findings.title: ZIP hazard inventory inspects central-directory claims without payload validation
findings.body: Archive hash is computed, but member bodies are never opened; CRC values, sizes and ratios are metadata. Nested archives are only listed and do not themselves trigger danger. Traversal/encryption/link/ratio findings produce recommendations, not extraction, move or deletion. CLI returns zero after writing even when archives contain recorded errors.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1336 ZIP hazard inventory inspects central-directory claims without payload validation.md

findings.title: Archive thresholds flag metadata after its allocation rather than bound parsing
findings.body: ZipFile loads infolist before max_entries and aggregate thresholds are checked. Optional maps and hazard sets can grow with all entries; no bound limits the archive byte hashing or central-directory parse. Floating NaN thresholds satisfy the simple positivity check but disable greater-than ratio comparisons.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1337 Archive thresholds flag metadata after its allocation rather than bound parsing.md

findings.title: Sanitized archive identity can collide and old maps remain
findings.body: Sanitization collapses path separators, control characters, drive syntax, colons, source terms and parent markers. Hazard sets deduplicate sanitized names, and map IDs hash sanitized root/path, so distinct originals can collapse or overwrite one map. No old map cleanup occurs when an archive disappears.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1338 Sanitized archive identity can collide and old maps remain.md

findings.title: Archive metadata and content digest are read at different times
findings.body: Both archive tools hash then independently parse/stat archive bytes, without a stable before/after check. A changing archive can yield a content digest paired with later metadata. The simple catalog reads whole archive bytes into memory; hazard inventory streams its digest but loads metadata.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1339 Archive metadata and content digest are read at different times.md

findings.title: Deduplicated archive tree hash binds metadata rather than member contents
findings.body: Simple catalog entry trees use path hash, uncompressed/compressed sizes and CRC, sorted by path hash. It does not read payloads or reject duplicate entry paths/hazards. Identical archive bytes share stored maps, but every occurrence is still parsed. Invalid ZIP occurrences remain and CLI still exits successfully.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1340 Deduplicated archive tree hash binds metadata rather than member contents.md

findings.title: Corpus report writers do not publish one atomic evidence set
findings.body: Catalog, file inventory, classification and partition outputs use direct writes and independently written summaries. Different tools permit arbitrary caller output paths, without common input-output identity checks or retained rollback. A successful earlier file can remain alongside stale or absent later summaries.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1341 Corpus report writers do not publish one atomic evidence set.md

findings.title: Corpus tests establish fixture accounting rather than broad semantic closure
findings.body: Tests use tiny synthetic files to check repeatability, structure fields, one exact group, class count, merge duplicate rejection and reconciled logged error accounting. They do not exercise near-duplicate search completeness, full tree error handling, mutation races or output aliasing. Subprocess helper has no timeout.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1342 Corpus tests establish fixture accounting rather than broad semantic closure.md

findings.title: Archive tests support metadata behavior and non-extraction only
findings.body: Tests verify deterministic maps, hazards, configured thresholds, bad ZIP retention and identical-archive deduplication using small fixtures. They do not test payload corruption, sanitized collisions, stale map removal, stable source identity, metadata allocation limits or NaN thresholds. No product archive tests were run in this audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1343 Archive tests support metadata behavior and non-extraction only.md

findings.title: Legacy map wrappers expose different validation and exit contracts
findings.body: Build forwards traversal budgets/exclusions/incremental mode and exits zero when the runtime returns, without checking a valid field. Validation opts into freshness only with --fresh and maps valid to exit status. Query forwards top-k and exits zero on a returned result. Their runtime owners, not wrappers, enforce operational behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1344 Legacy map wrappers expose different validation and exit contracts.md

findings.title: Portable routing and transcript wrappers delegate authority to selected runtime
findings.body: They prepend local source only when a runtime directory exists, otherwise use imported installed modules and framework_root. Specialist routing returns recommendations and valid-based exit, not spawned agents. Transcript export forwards explicit apply and exits zero if the underlying call returns.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1345 Portable routing and transcript wrappers delegate authority to selected runtime.md

findings.title: Legacy bootstrap reporter is not an independent certification owner
findings.body: audit_framework performs the work; reporter renders all supplied checks and uses valid for exit. External manifest strictness is opt-in. JSON and Markdown writes use caller paths without creating parents or joint atomic publication. Rendering PASS does not add new evidence beyond the runtime report.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1346 Legacy bootstrap reporter is not an independent certification owner.md

findings.title: Service discovery heuristic uses whole-file keyword suppression
findings.body: A selected config file warns only when an IPv4 address pattern appears and no discovery/resolver/TTL/registry keyword occurs anywhere. Unrelated comments can suppress a real stale-address concern; hostname-only or IPv6 paths are outside the detector. No service resolution or expiry is observed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1347 Service discovery heuristic uses whole-file keyword suppression.md

findings.title: Static service audit completeness omits skipped files and traversal errors
findings.body: Unreadable/oversized/unsupported/link files are skipped without an error denominator; os.walk has no onerror. stat occurs outside the read catch and may abort. complete is hardcoded true, and CLI exits zero with review findings. The test covers only one IPv4 config and an added resolver line.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1348 Static service audit completeness omits skipped files and traversal errors.md

findings.title: Import audit matches source strings rather than resolved dependencies
findings.body: Python uses AST import names; JS uses a literal regex missing side-effect imports, dynamic imports and runtime resolution. Selection casefolds suffix but parser branch tests exact .py, so .PY takes JS scanning. Any target beginning three dots is marked escape even when package-relative syntax is legitimate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1349 Import audit matches source strings rather than resolved dependencies.md

findings.title: Import mirror policy can point outside the project
findings.body: Canonical and mirror strings are joined to root without resolve/containment checks; absolute paths or parent segments can redirect reads. Mirror verification is byte equality only. Source traversal omissions remain outside findings, while parse failures become findings and fail CLI.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1350 Import mirror policy can point outside the project.md

findings.title: Scanner aggregation complete means parse completion rather than all-pass security
findings.body: Every finding carries its envelope status; complete is simply not errors, so fail/blocked/skipped/uncertain scanner results can coexist with complete=true. Missing or empty input directory can also complete. The focused test explicitly expects aggregation completeness while preserving a fail count.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1351 Scanner aggregation complete means parse completion rather than all-pass security.md

findings.title: Scanner aggregation can lose malformed finding rows without an error
findings.body: Non-dictionary findings are skipped, but a nonempty all-invalid list suppresses the empty-summary fallback and yields no records. Non-object JSON roots can raise AttributeError outside the catch. Tool/location strings remain raw while messages are hashed; hashing messages alone is not general payload sanitization.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1352 Scanner aggregation can lose malformed finding rows without an error.md

findings.title: Text repair ordering permits cascades and empty search strings
findings.body: Mappings sort by descending search length then lexical key and apply sequentially. Replacement text may be changed by a later mapping, and empty search keys insert text between characters. JSON repair changes values only and always reserializes, so changed can be true with no replacements while object keys stay unchanged.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1353 Text repair ordering permits cascades and empty search strings.md

findings.title: Text repair CLI does not enforce separate or immutable output custody
findings.body: Pure repair returns bytes, but CLI accepts arbitrary output and receipt paths without alias checks, allowing input/mapping overwrite or one output replacing another. Receipt binds input/output hashes and version text, not mapping bytes. The test checks only the pure helper leaving input unchanged.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1354 Text repair CLI does not enforce separate or immutable output custody.md

findings.title: Retrieval readiness can pass without resource measurements
findings.body: Missing p95/memory and missing maxima all default to infinity; infinity <= infinity passes. A pure probe with one perfect case and empty thresholds/metrics/state confirms complete=true with no resource measurements. This is evaluator behavior, not measured performance.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1355 Retrieval readiness can pass without resource measurements.md

findings.title: Retrieval readiness quality and calibration remain caller assertions
findings.body: Reference/candidate collections are coerced to strings/sets, recall is an unweighted mean with no precision/rank/top-k requirement, and forbidden exposure covers only supplied denied IDs. Numeric bounds/types and finiteness are not fully validated. Compressed readiness checks lifecycle strings and equal fingerprints rather than actual calibration evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1356 Retrieval readiness quality and calibration remain caller assertions.md

findings.title: Incomplete detector collapses all same-file pass sites into one identity
findings.body: ID includes path, rule and normalized semantic_source; for ast.Pass that source is always Pass(). Line and function context are absent. Multiple pass nodes in one file therefore share an ID and the unique dictionary keeps the last locator. Confirmed in memory with two separate functions. source_hash argument is unused.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1357 Incomplete detector collapses all same-file pass sites into one identity.md

findings.title: Incomplete signal detection is broader and narrower than unfinished behavior
findings.body: Pass can be deliberate control flow, and lexical TODO/unimplemented strings include tests/documentation. Bare raise NotImplementedError is not the AST Call branch but can match lexical text; ellipsis detection requires a one-statement body. Signal review is necessary and absence is not proof of fully implemented behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1358 Incomplete signal detection is broader and narrower than unfinished behavior.md

findings.title: Incomplete audit omits excluded and oversized sources from completion
findings.body: Custody/generated directories and nonselected/large/link files are skipped without full physical denominator. os.walk traversal failures are unreported; stat and initial raw read occur outside the catch. Python AST reparses the file in a second read, while lexical rules use prior bytes, allowing version mismatch during mutation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1359 Incomplete audit omits excluded and oversized sources from completion.md

findings.title: Incomplete review matching validates labels rather than the review condition
findings.body: Reviews bind ID/path/rule while ignoring line movement, require an allowed class plus nonempty rationale/condition, and reject stale IDs. They do not evaluate review_condition, verify an accountable owner or bind whole source bytes. A same-ID new pass site can inherit an earlier classification because of the context-free ID.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1360 Incomplete review matching validates labels rather than the review condition.md

findings.title: Historical incomplete disposition can complete with missing source
findings.body: First matching path-glob rule supplies arbitrary disposition and targets. Missing source is a recorded flag, not an unresolved condition. Any assigned disposition except literal unresolved can satisfy completion if row count matches; empty targets are accepted. No fresh detector or original-content comparison is run.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1361 Historical incomplete disposition can complete with missing source.md

findings.title: Historical incomplete reconciliation trusts paths and later input hashes
findings.body: Source path is joined without containment/physical-file checks, and current hashes are cached by path. Report/policy are loaded before later hashing for output, with no stability check. Default CLI can exit zero on incomplete accounting unless require-complete is supplied.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1362 Historical incomplete reconciliation trusts paths and later input hashes.md

findings.title: Source audit coverage digest has three explicit evidence strengths
findings.body: Included source binds content SHA. Ordinary excluded generated boundaries bind path/size metadata with bounded scandir and errors. Opaque external/preserved/explicit exclusions bind only boundary path identity without recursion. Equal-byte-size changes under metadata exclusions intentionally preserve that digest; opaque contents are not counted as files.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1363 Source audit coverage digest has three explicit evidence strengths.md

findings.title: Included source traversal is less strict than excluded metadata traversal
findings.body: Ordinary excluded metadata walk retains scandir errors and rejects a linked boundary. Main included os.walk has no onerror, and later nonregular/disappeared paths can silently continue. Included symlinks increase a skip count but do not enter the inventory digest like nested excluded symlinks do. An opaque boundary is selected before the ordinary symlink check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1364 Included source traversal is less strict than excluded metadata traversal.md

findings.title: Source audit nominal max bytes is a review threshold not an I/O cap
findings.body: Text above max_bytes but <=8MiB is still line-scanned; above fixed 8MiB is content-hashed only. Those hash-only files still increment text_scanned. Nontext files are hashed without mechanism analysis. No total file/byte/depth/time cap bounds the included walk and retained path list.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1365 Source audit nominal max bytes is a review threshold not an I/O cap.md

findings.title: Mechanism scan uses combined lexical matches rather than semantic independence
findings.body: Combined regex emits nonoverlapping matches and alternation order can hide a second mechanism matching the same span. It scans line by line with replacement decoding, so cross-line patterns are not found. Declared prefilter/individual-regex/overlap tables are not used by the active _scan_text path. Metadata names/descriptions inspect only the first 12000 bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1366 Mechanism scan uses combined lexical matches rather than semantic independence.md

findings.title: Source audit records retain candidates rather than every hashed file
findings.body: Only score/skill/oversize-positive text produces records; other included file identities contribute only to aggregate inventory hash. Duplicate candidate groups are limited to those retained records. candidate_count counts review dispositions, and complete only means no retained errors even when candidates remain. Catalog match uses token Jaccard similarity, not semantic equivalence or admission.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1367 Source audit records retain candidates rather than every hashed file.md

findings.title: Source progress complete is positional rather than final validity
findings.body: Progress can mark complete when last selected content iteration finishes even with retained errors. Early continues for nontext/skipped paths can bypass updates, leaving stale incomplete progress when the last path is skipped. No final unconditional receipt corrects this. Progress file created under source before walking can enter and change during its own audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1368 Source progress complete is positional rather than final validity.md

findings.title: Source audit progress replacement is atomic per file but not a durable transaction
findings.body: Progress uses a deterministic .tmp path and os.replace without exclusive creation, fsync, lock or finally cleanup. Final report writes directly. Stat/hash/metadata reads are not an immutable snapshot. CLI allow-errors can exit zero while complete remains false, and printed excluded count uses a key not populated by the coverage counters.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1369 Source audit progress replacement is atomic per file but not a durable transaction.md

findings.title: Excluded entry budget is checked after each directory is materialized
findings.body: Excluded scanner sorts the entire scandir iterator before incrementing visited_entries and applying its million-entry bound. It limits processed entries but does not cap a single directory listing allocation. Its metadata methods can race directory replacement; no stable physical handle or second tree equality is retained.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1370 Excluded entry budget is checked after each directory is materialized.md

findings.title: Legacy helper tests support bounded cases rather than universal completion
findings.body: The full capability-mining test module checks meaningful preserved-custody, excluded-body nonread, error, hidden-lock, symlink, progress and historical disposition cases. It does not cover main included traversal failure, self-mutating progress, ID collisions, broad detector precision or policy semantic authority. Retrieval tests similarly omit missing measurement defaults.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1371 Legacy helper tests support bounded cases rather than universal completion.md

findings.title: Historical hash matches override current owner inspection
findings.body: Historical evidence is indexed by any 64-character source hash, without validating disposition, owner, path or original bytes. A matching hash is accepted before examining a current owner, including historical unresolved or arbitrary labels. The report complete flag counts only literal unresolved rows.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1372 Historical hash matches override current owner inspection.md

findings.title: Any changed same-path file becomes a superseding owner
findings.body: When historical hash lookup misses, any existing current-root/source-path file becomes current_owner_exact if equal or current_owner_superseded if different. Changed content is automatically considered superseding without a policy rule or semantic evidence. First matching explicit rules apply only after this path lookup misses.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1373 Any changed same-path file becomes a superseding owner.md

findings.title: Historical reconciliation input hashes are later observations
findings.body: Source inventory paths and rule owner paths have no physical containment guard; lexical parent traversal and links can resolve outside the root. Most helpers parse input first and hash the path later, so mutable bytes can produce a digest unrelated to parsed data. Direct output writes and optional require-complete exit policies do not provide atomic or immutable custody.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1374 Historical reconciliation input hashes are later observations.md

findings.title: Skill identity joins use metadata rather than body equivalence
findings.body: Inventory and structured-text IDs are dictionaries with last duplicate wins. Canonical identity uses frontmatter name or parent path and catalog name membership, ignoring source body, catalog state and package hashes. A root SKILL.md without a name can raise IndexError. Completion compares matched metadata count with deduplicated skill count.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1375 Skill identity joins use metadata rather than body equivalence.md

findings.title: Skill alias and vendor routes have different target checks
findings.body: All declared specialty and alias targets are checked against catalog IDs, even unrelated entries, but empty lists pass and delivery/disposition labels are not validated. Vendor-prefix matches emit two hardcoded owner names without checking their catalog presence. Metadata can therefore complete without an active executable owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1376 Skill alias and vendor routes have different target checks.md

findings.title: Classified asset identity joins do not preserve row identity
findings.body: Classified IDs must occur in inventory and be unique, but their path, source tree and digest are not compared with inventory. Policy dictionaries update the result directly and may replace identity/hash/class fields. Skill dispositions join by ID alone, independent of either input hash or upstream complete flag.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1377 Classified asset identity joins do not preserve row identity.md

findings.title: Unresolved upstream skill labels escape the asset unresolved counter
findings.body: A skill disposition unresolved becomes skill_body_unresolved, while the aggregate only counts unresolved_class plus missing inventory IDs. Other arbitrary policy dispositions likewise avoid that counter. Complete asset accounting can therefore coexist with unresolved skill ownership.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1378 Unresolved upstream skill labels escape the asset unresolved counter.md

findings.title: Direct audit attachment and optional error logs are not global closure
findings.body: Direct audit records attach by declared source hash without validating audit completeness or outcome. The entire audit file is rehashed inside each record loop. Error logs are optional supplied files; omitted logs are not reconciled against an original summary. Error rule labels and exact default-label comparison drive completion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1379 Direct audit attachment and optional error logs are not global closure.md

findings.title: Mechanism ownership requires keys but not owners
findings.body: Every mechanism key must occur in mappings, but a mapped empty target list passes. Owner names, catalog lifecycle, source bytes, record uniqueness and scanner complete/errors are not checked. Expected count is caller candidate_count plus no_reusable_signal records, rather than an independent physical denominator.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1380 Mechanism ownership requires keys but not owners.md

findings.title: Oversize reconciliation relabels without scanning source bytes
findings.body: An oversize_review_required record with no missing mapping key becomes oversize_stream_scanned_and_mapped. This helper never opens the original source, so the new label does not establish a scan. CLI emits incomplete reports with exit zero unless require-complete is set.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1381 Oversize reconciliation relabels without scanning source bytes.md

findings.title: Planning coverage proves path existence with an optional denominator
findings.body: Allowed status labels and PC IDs are checked, and owner/test arrays need existing files, but there is no containment, content hash or test execution. Source comparison is optional and recognizes only level-two PC headings. Duplicate source headings collapse in set comparison; empty records with no source pass. Input hashes are taken after parsing.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1382 Planning coverage proves path existence with an optional denominator.md

findings.title: Staged policy enforces unique highest priority with a narrow absence rule
findings.body: Duplicate typed identities, no rules, equal top priorities, invalid dispositions and unknown owners fail. The absent-body rule rejects only ADOPT and SUPERSEDE when presence exactly equals manifest-only; other labels and presence strings are not schema-validated. A null kind/id becomes a nonempty string through coercion. Catalog names are checked, not active bodies.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1383 Staged policy enforces unique highest priority with a narrow absence rule.md

findings.title: Staged disposition preserves obligations without executing them
findings.body: Rationale, preserve lists and tests_required are copied from policy; they are not validated as evidence or executed. Empty candidate input can complete. CLI strict completion is optional, and reported input hashes are later reads. This is policy accounting, not capability admission.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1384 Staged disposition preserves obligations without executing them.md

findings.title: Manifest recovery ledger is a supplied-claim projection
findings.body: The producer intersects supplied missing_paths with manifest rows and copies expected sizes/hashes without inspecting physical files or comparing input provenance. Paths absent from the manifest are omitted; duplicate manifest rows remain. Artifact type comes from first path substring match, so nested scripts under skills classify as skill-component.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1385 Manifest recovery ledger is a supplied-claim projection.md

findings.title: Empty missing backlog fails after output creation begins
