findings.body: CSV fieldnames are taken from rows[0] after the CSV file is opened for writing. Zero missing rows raises IndexError and can leave a truncated file. Markdown is written later, and CLI compares row count with declared missing count only after both outputs; there is no paired atomic publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1386 Empty missing backlog fails after output creation begins.md

findings.title: Reconstruction planner binds a historical fixed denominator
findings.body: Only absent packs 01 through 07 and registry enter the missing set. Candidate count and recovery dictionary count must equal 260 and assigned paths 1133. Duplicate missing paths and multiply assigned paths fail, but slug-generated card IDs are not independently checked for collisions. Other pack declarations are outside this planner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1387 Reconstruction planner binds a historical fixed denominator.md

findings.title: Exact recovery branch trusts supplied flags and can accept an empty list
findings.body: Candidates with no missing paths are accepted when every supplied recovery row has exact_match truthy; bytes are not rehashed. With an empty sources list, both all checks pass vacuously. For candidates with some missing paths, other sources outside that set are filtered out without the exact-recovery check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1388 Exact recovery branch trusts supplied flags and can accept an empty list.md

findings.title: Support consolidation infers behavior from names
findings.body: Unassigned support paths group by artifact kind and slugged filename, with pack qualification only for certain kinds. Cross-pack contracts can therefore consolidate by stem. Behavior, targets and test filenames are generated strings, and the selected canonical owner is not checked for current existence or semantic equivalence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1389 Support consolidation infers behavior from names.md

findings.title: Reconstruction waves declare order without executing it
findings.body: The planner writes eight static waves and acceptance prose with all cards initially assigned_not_verified. It does not construct an executable dependency graph, verify target wiring or run tests. Generated JSON/Markdown do not bind input digests and are written independently.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1390 Reconstruction waves declare order without executing it.md

findings.title: Historical certifier checks generic plans and script dispatch
findings.body: The certifier asks every outcome for a positive and missing-constraints plan. Scripts additionally run with one shared synthetic payload. The runtime dispatches generic handlers by outcome words; skill/orchestration plans do not execute their domain procedures. Temporary sample creation occurs even without apply, so this command is not a purely read-only checker.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1391 Historical certifier checks generic plans and script dispatch.md

findings.title: Repeated script certification omits second validity
findings.body: The script check requires first.valid true and equal first/second result_sha256, but does not require second.valid true or a nonempty result hash. Its determinism claim is consequently narrower than two independently valid executions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1392 Repeated script certification omits second validity.md

findings.title: Support card certification does not evaluate per-card acceptance
findings.body: Support_ready checks fixed 18/3/257 registry counts, global contract validity and target existence. Directories can count as present, and missing implementation_targets entries are not independently required. Card required_tests, wiring_targets, behavior contract and acceptance text are not evaluated in this branch.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1393 Support card certification does not evaluate per-card acceptance.md

findings.title: Historical final gates trust supplied aggregate fields
findings.body: Final readiness accepts historical minimum test counters, booleans and failed-zero fields. It hashes the supplied gate file but does not validate source revision, installed artifact identity, execution logs, timestamps or current processing-order receipts. This legacy helper is distinct from current governed release certification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1394 Historical final gates trust supplied aggregate fields.md

findings.title: Certifier hashes evidence before later replacing it
findings.body: Evidence cards inspect and hash their target before apply may regenerate pack evidence. First application cannot create a missing target and count it in the same preceding check; existing recorded hashes can describe bytes replaced later. Invalid cards are not reset from a prior implemented_verified state, so persisted states can disagree with fresh counters.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1395 Certifier hashes evidence before later replacing it.md

findings.title: Certifier valid status and card closure are independent
findings.body: Summary valid and exit success depend only on accumulated errors; invalid support/evidence cards can remain open without adding errors. Receipt status depends only on open count and can say complete despite unrelated errors. The helper has no single predicate combining all closure obligations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1396 Certifier valid status and card closure are independent.md

findings.title: Failed certification can still publish certified owner states
findings.body: Confirmed with extracted main and all I/O intercepted in memory: one invalid operational card and an error produce valid=false, one open card and exit 1, yet passing final fields write implemented_verified owners/recovery and certified packs. Apply publication is guarded by final_ready, not global success. Nineteen synthetic writes were intercepted; no product state was changed. Sequential publication has no WAL or joint rollback.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1397 Failed certification can still publish certified owner states.md

findings.title: Reconciliation fixtures leave cross-helper authority gaps
findings.body: Mechanism tests cover unknown versus named mapping; staged tests cover one MERGE, manifest ADOPT denial and priority tie; reconstruction tests cover 260/1133 synthetic assignment and retained 375-card receipts/current package body hashes. Existing support tests call validate_operational, not main publication. These useful assertions do not establish end-to-end semantic reconstruction or failed-apply safety.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1398 Reconciliation fixtures leave cross-helper authority gaps.md

findings.title: Sort JSON streaming does not preserve JSON token boundaries
findings.body: Confirmed using in-memory readers: [12345] at chunk size two yields three records [1,23,45]. raw_decode accepts a numeric prefix before the next chunk arrives. The parser also accepts missing/repeated/leading/trailing commas and ignores text after the closing bracket; [,1 2,,,] ignored yields [1,2].
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1399 Sort JSON streaming does not preserve JSON token boundaries.md

findings.title: Sort sample bounds do not bound total parsing work
findings.body: Reservoir record count is bounded, but the entire source stream is parsed and type-checked and later fully hashed. A single huge record or incomplete JSON value can grow the buffer without a byte limit. No input size, deadline or candidate timeout is enforced.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1400 Sort sample bounds do not bound total parsing work.md

findings.title: Sort coercion and type policy distinguish compatible numeric shapes
findings.body: Every key must have exactly the same Python type, so int/float mixtures fail even when numerically ordered. String coercion applies only to strings; number policy leaves existing integers unchanged. Boolean keys are allowed only as a homogeneous class. Auto coercion can retain non-finite-looking strings as text after numeric conversion fails.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1401 Sort coercion and type policy distinguish compatible numeric shapes.md

findings.title: Reservoir replacement changes stability requirements for specialized sorts
findings.body: Reference comparison sorts use original source ordinal as tiebreaker. Reservoir replacement does not keep the sample in ordinal order. Counting and radix preserve sample order within equal keys, and all-equal bucket sort returns sample unchanged, so those candidates can fail the declared reference after sampling despite ordinary stable behavior on their input order.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1402 Reservoir replacement changes stability requirements for specialized sorts.md

findings.title: Numeric sort compatibility is not a full resource or precision gate
findings.body: Counting sort has a span limit, but radix passes scale with integer magnitude and bucket conversion may overflow huge integers or overflow finite float ranges. Exceptions are captured as failed candidate evidence. quick-3way compares key plus unique ordinal, so duplicate scalar keys do not form a large equal partition.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1403 Numeric sort compatibility is not a full resource or precision gate.md

findings.title: Sort correctness checks ordinal order without payload preservation
findings.body: Confirmed in memory: replacing key1/payload-original with key99/payload-changed at the same ordinal passes validate_output for a one-record reference. The validator compares length, ordinal sequence and output tie stability, not keys or payload equality. Candidate list copies are shallow and can share nested records.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1404 Sort correctness checks ordinal order without payload preservation.md

findings.title: Direct zero-repeat benchmark reports success without running a candidate
findings.body: CLI enforces repeats1-25, but public benchmark/build_receipt do not validate it. A direct zero-repeat benchmark returns correct=true and stable=true with empty timings and null median/p95. The in-memory probe verified the candidate function was never called.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1405 Direct zero-repeat benchmark reports success without running a candidate.md

findings.title: Sort ranking measures a fixed pilot and three finalists
findings.body: Pilot is the first at most4096 reservoir slots, one run per candidate in fixed order; only three correct pilots advance. Final choice uses fastest correct/stable median. No warmup, order randomization, uncertainty, memory measurement or runtime fingerprint is retained. A deterministic sample does not imply deterministic timing/winner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1406 Sort ranking measures a fixed pilot and three finalists.md

findings.title: Sort receipt fingerprints can follow different source bytes
findings.body: Sampling and benchmarking precede input stat and full SHA read, so mutable input can diverge from sampled records. Sample hash includes only keys and ordinals, not payloads. Output can alias the input and overwrite it despite dry_run=true, because no separate output identity is enforced.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1407 Sort receipt fingerprints can follow different source bytes.md

findings.title: Model normalization selects first alias and infers defaults
findings.body: First present alias wins even if null; contradictory aliases are not compared. Hidden/query/KV divisibility is checked and missing KV heads default to query heads with a warning. Explicit head_dim and architecture-specific projection dimensions are not consumed; returned formulas use hidden/query.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1408 Model normalization selects first alias and infers defaults.md

findings.title: Model parameter estimates are a simplified dense formula
findings.body: Parameter count uses standard attention projections, two or three FFN matrices and embedding/norm assumptions. Expert count changes only an active fraction, not total FFN weight parameters. Unknown activation is treated as gated, and truthy tie_word_embeddings strings affect embedding count. These are estimates, not a loaded-model inventory.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1409 Model parameter estimates are a simplified dense formula.md

findings.title: Architecture status mixes missing optional fields and unknown strings
findings.body: Unresolved includes None fields such as absent expert metadata even for a dense model, while unknown model/position/norm/activation strings are not unresolved. Context limits do not reject a requested token count above configured context. Required_runtime_validation remains an unevaluated list.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1410 Architecture status mixes missing optional fields and unknown strings.md

findings.title: Architecture input checks have conditional and falsy paths
findings.body: Falsy non-dict workloads such as an empty list are accepted through workload or {}. bits_per_weight is validated only if all parameter-estimate dimensions are present. Public arithmetic helpers themselves do not enforce the inspect integer bounds. CLI can emit review status with normal success and does not bind source config bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1411 Architecture input checks have conditional and falsy paths.md

findings.title: Deployment planner accepts non-finite numbers and truthy strings
findings.body: Numeric validation rejects negative values and booleans but not NaN/infinity. Architecture, streaming, privacy and remote flags use bool coercion rather than boolean types. Confirmed supplied strings false for architecture_supported and remote_fallback_allowed produce native feasible and remote conditional under fitting memory; no effects occur.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1412 Deployment planner accepts non-finite numbers and truthy strings.md

findings.title: Deployment feasibility omits some artifact and cache prerequisites
findings.body: Missing KV cache defaults zero. A transformed weight size zero falls back to original size. Disk preflight gates streaming only; native/quantized/offload can be labeled feasible or conditional with failed disk budget. Streaming does not check minimum working memory or task throughput, and zero model weights are accepted.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1413 Deployment feasibility omits some artifact and cache prerequisites.md

findings.title: Deployment complete means only bandwidth metadata is present
findings.body: The only blocking_unknowns entry is missing sustained_disk_read_mib_s. Supplying zero marks complete even with failed disk preflight and unmeasured compatibility/quality. Rankings use fixed strategy scores and heuristic memory fractions. Required validation and global release lists are declarations, not receipts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1414 Deployment complete means only bandwidth metadata is present.md

findings.title: Model estimate and deployment schemas require an explicit handoff
findings.body: Architecture helper emits parameter/byte estimates from config; deployment helper expects separate hardware/model/workload GiB and support flags. Neither imports or calls the other, converts units or probes actual hardware. Both remain nonexecuting planning helpers, distinct from local model admission/server owners.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1415 Model estimate and deployment schemas require an explicit handoff.md

findings.title: Sort and model fixtures exercise selected formulas and policies
findings.body: Sort tests cover seeded JSONL sampling, CSV conversion and mixed-key rejection. Model tests cover MHA KV arithmetic, two dimension errors, private remote denial and missing disk bandwidth. They omit parser chunk/grammar defects, payload preservation, zero direct repeats, MoE sizing, non-finite numbers and string flags. Sources read; tests not run.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1416 Sort and model fixtures exercise selected formulas and policies.md

findings.title: Behavior extractor privacy is limited identifier substitution
findings.body: Only three configured name patterns are replaced. Source aliases pass through unchanged; headings, test descriptions and frontmatter text are copied with that limited substitution. Those fields can contain private paths or secrets. secret_indicator_count counts words rather than redacting values, so the broad privacy label is not a general sanitization guarantee.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1417 Behavior extractor privacy is limited identifier substitution.md

findings.title: Behavior extraction reads broad mutable source trees without size bounds
findings.body: It enumerates all is_file paths with rglob and no exclusion policy or error denominator, follows file links, hashes then stats then reads entire text separately. Large files and full record lists are unbounded. Missing/unreadable hash paths abort rather than entering parse_failure_count; changing files can break hash-to-metadata identity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1418 Behavior extraction reads broad mutable source trees without size bounds.md

findings.title: Python syntax failure is counted as parsed behavior text
findings.body: The AST symbol extractor catches SyntaxError and returns empty symbol/test lists. The caller still sets parse_status=text_parsed, so parse_failure_count covers only text read failure, not syntactically unparsed Python. Lexical behavior/effect tags may still be emitted.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1419 Python syntax failure is counted as parsed behavior text.md

findings.title: Behavior metadata extraction has explicit lexical coverage limits
findings.body: JS/TS regexes omit many arrow/property/method forms; PowerShell matching is line-based; Markdown frontmatter is a simple single-line name/description regex. Symbols/tests are truncated to500 and headings100 without a truncation receipt. Whole-text substrings detect effects without resolving actual calls, and can count comments or miss equivalent syntax.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1420 Behavior metadata extraction has explicit lexical coverage limits.md

findings.title: Behavior tree identity depends on aliases and sanitized path strings
findings.body: Tree digest concatenates alias:path:hash lines in caller root order after path sanitization. Aliases/delimiters are not constrained and normalized path collisions are not rejected. The digest does not bind extractor version or extraction configuration. Output inside a scanned tree can enter later scans.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1421 Behavior tree identity depends on aliases and sanitized path strings.md

findings.title: Content-addressed extraction is not an atomic multi-file publication
findings.body: Destination mkdir uses exist_ok=false, so repeated identical input fails rather than verifies/reuses existing output. Index is created exclusively, but later summary/candidate/duplicate files are separate writes; interruption leaves a partial directory that blocks a same-digest rerun. CLI returns zero even with text-read failures.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1422 Content-addressed extraction is not an atomic multi-file publication.md

findings.title: Exact metadata names can claim existing semantic coverage
findings.body: Confirmed _catalog_match returns score1 for an identical normalized name despite unrelated tokens and deferred catalog state. Jaccard token equality can also return1. build_plan calls score1 already_covered_exact, without body, behavior or active-admission verification. At zero overlap the nearest owner still becomes the lexicographically first catalog ID.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1423 Exact metadata names can claim existing semantic coverage.md

findings.title: Staged priority is selected by a hardcoded source alias
findings.body: Only source-12 gets clean_room_contract_candidate for unmatched recognized families and enters priority_staged_candidates. Alias is caller-controlled metadata, not a provenance or authority check. Family and match decisions use token overlap with deterministic lexical tie-breaking, not semantic review.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1424 Staged priority is selected by a hardcoded source alias.md

findings.title: Admission plan trusts supplied index identity and denominators
findings.body: Summary tree_sha256 and file_count are copied without recomputing the behavior-index or joining candidate rows to source records. Catalog hash is read after catalog parsing. The output plan hash binds generated content, but does not prove input consistency or current source equivalence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1425 Admission plan trusts supplied index identity and denominators.md

findings.title: Metadata duplicate grouping does not validate source hash identities
findings.body: Planner groups str(item.get(sha256, empty)) without digest grammar or row uniqueness checks. Missing/default and null values differ; a null becomes the nonempty string None and can form a duplicate group. Duplicate source rows remain separate candidates. Repeated same plan output fails at exclusive directory creation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1426 Metadata duplicate grouping does not validate source hash identities.md

findings.title: External requirement integration is a fixed filename mapping
findings.body: Only source-12 records enter; rule files use the exact persistant_rules prefix and first two stem characters, while SKILL.md uses its parent name. Fixed RULE_OWNERS/SKILL_OWNERS membership plus catalog IDs decides integrated/reference labels. It does not inspect original behavior, package hashes or active catalog status.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1427 External requirement integration is a fixed filename mapping.md

findings.title: External requirement cards have positional rather than stable identity
findings.body: Card IDs use sorted record sequence, so adding an earlier path renumbers subsequent cards. Duplicate paths/rows and declared hash grammar are not checked. validation=complete follows integrated/reference labels, and bool(cards) only prevents vacuous empty completion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1428 External requirement cards have positional rather than stable identity.md

findings.title: External disposition digest does not bind its input artifacts
findings.body: The digest covers produced cards but omits index and catalog file digests. Report can remain unchanged across different unreferenced catalog/index content. Content-addressed output uses exclusive creation and CLI returns zero even when complete=false and cards are blocked.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1429 External disposition digest does not bind its input artifacts.md

findings.title: Mining migration mutates catalog before confirming skill bodies
findings.body: update_catalog runs first; missing body later raises after catalog mutation and perhaps earlier package writes. Packages list resources from scripts/references/assets, excluding bytecode but without resource hashes or link containment. Existing package files are overwritten with fixed version/status/effects rather than reconciled through an admission transaction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1430 Mining migration mutates catalog before confirming skill bodies.md

findings.title: Catalog text matching is narrower than TOML identity
findings.body: The migration detects existing IDs only with an exact double-quoted id = line regex. Equivalent TOML quoting/spacing can be missed and append duplicates; an existing matched entry is not updated for status/body/version changes. Catalog is rewritten even if no new entry was added.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1431 Catalog text matching is narrower than TOML identity.md

findings.title: Mining admission writes success and freshness claims without executing validation
findings.body: Every fixed skill receives active status, validation passed2/failed0 and package validation_freshness=current. Five scan receipts and their counts/hashes are constants. The script does not invoke those tests, verify raw scan reports or establish current operational behavior before publishing these labels.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1432 Mining admission writes success and freshness claims without executing validation.md

findings.title: Mining migration refreshes every package body digest
findings.body: After the fixed wave and lifecycle updates, every registry/skill_packages JSON is loaded and its declared body read and hash replaced. This extends mutation beyond the twenty added skills, follows unguarded body paths and does not compare expected previous hashes or validation freshness. A failure late in this sweep retains prior writes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1433 Mining migration refreshes every package body digest.md

findings.title: Mining workflow definitions preserve order but do not execute it
findings.body: Five workflows declare assimilation, secure service release, retrieval readiness, failure/recovery and external tool lifecycle. Assimilation branches incompleteness/relationships/boundaries after inventory, derive waits on relationships/boundaries, certify waits on incompleteness/derive. Other chains are linear. Producer replaces the whole workflow registry and emits a JSON-shaped YAML projection; it does not schedule the steps.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1434 Mining workflow definitions preserve order but do not execute it.md

findings.title: Mining receipt uses historical maximum coverage and fixed oversize disposition
findings.body: The receipt uses the maximum declared scan file count and separately sums focused observations, correctly avoiding naive additive coverage claims but not verifying nested membership or raw hashes. Fixed411 oversize records are labeled reference_only. Receipt hashes the generated admission registry; that proves document identity, not source reconstruction.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1435 Mining receipt uses historical maximum coverage and fixed oversize disposition.md

findings.title: Mining publication can stop between independently written control surfaces
findings.body: Order is catalog; per-skill packages; admission ledger; mining admission; workflow registry/projection; mining receipt; source coverage; engineering lifecycle; every package hash refresh. Direct writes have no joint preflight, lock, WAL or rollback, and overwrite retained wave entries. Idempotent wording does not imply transactional recovery or preservation of newer metadata.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1436 Mining publication can stop between independently written control surfaces.md

findings.title: Contract ID normalization rewrites identifiers without reconciling consumers
findings.body: All contracts/**/*.json are treated as schema objects. A changed ID requires $schema and otherwise raises after earlier writes; already matching ID skips that check. The path-derived URI is written directly, without updating absolute references, registries or provenance hashes or validating schema compatibility. Missing contracts directory returns zero changes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1437 Contract ID normalization rewrites identifiers without reconciling consumers.md

findings.title: External intake fixtures do not validate all claims in their names
findings.body: Extractor test checks one Python symbol/body-marker fixture, planner test uses an arbitrary supplied tree hash and inspects nonexecution flags, and staged requirement test reads retained75-card/6353-file counts without rebuilding owner dispositions. It does not execute the fixed admission migration or check broad metadata privacy.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1438 External intake fixtures do not validate all claims in their names.md

findings.title: Downstream assimilation validation remains a declaration check
findings.body: The consumer verifies scan IDs, positive counts, complete/error fields and hash grammar; target catalog membership; selectable workflow skills; dependency identities and acyclicity; and admission document hash/maximum denominator. It does not open the raw scan reports or execute the declared skill workflows, so producer constants remain claims at this boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1439 Downstream assimilation validation remains a declaration check.md

findings.title: CLI parser and dispatch denominators are independently accounted
findings.body: Pure parser construction yields69 top-level commands and169 leaf parsers. AST inspection finds a corresponding top-level dispatch branch for every command. Leaf count retains positional action choices rather than counting them as executed routes. Hardcoded section/profile choices are an additional CLI exposure boundary over registry data.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1440 CLI parser and dispatch denominators are independently accounted.md

findings.title: Four CLI paths fail on a branch-local JSON loader
findings.body: Confirmed with unchanged main AST and intercepted dependencies: declared-suite plan, declared-suite run-script, metacognitive run and scheduling simulate raise UnboundLocalError before invoking their owner. load_json is imported inside other mutually exclusive branches, making it a local variable not initialized in these paths. The exception is not in the CLI JSON-error catch tuple.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1441 Four CLI paths fail on a branch-local JSON loader.md

findings.title: Startup emits a tooling command that the parser rejects
findings.body: Startup guidance emits python -m runtime.cli tooling --project path, but tooling requires the assess subcommand. Pure parser probe returns exit2 for that emitted shape. Existing startup test checks deferred metadata but does not parse or execute its suggested command.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1442 Startup emits a tooling command that the parser rejects.md

findings.title: CLI argument semantics vary across command families
findings.body: Several file inputs are interpreted from process cwd while others are rebased under framework or project root. plan --effect appends to the default read_local list. skill-backup --verify is parsed but not consulted; default nonrestore path always verifies. audit --write-report affects licensing only. These distinctions are retained in the complete argument index.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1443 CLI argument semantics vary across command families.md

findings.title: Processing project mutation can use a different orchestration lock root
findings.body: Confirmed in isolated main: the orchestration lock receives framework root, while processing-order --project claim-release-stage passes the selected project root to the release owner. This does not remove the release owner own state checks/locks, but the repository-wide orchestration exclusion is not scoped to that mutated project.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1444 Processing project mutation can use a different orchestration lock root.md

findings.title: Inherited test ownership is restricted to one immediate stale-group child
findings.body: Only run-stale with matching owner and supervised-child environment values requests inherited ownership. The child marker is removed after claim so descendants cannot reuse that one-generation path. Managed project group runs additionally require an active exact full_profile claim, inspected structurally without rehashing live source.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1445 Inherited test ownership is restricted to one immediate stale-group child.md

findings.title: Stale-group child timeout expands to cover the full queue
findings.body: Refresh finds noncurrent groups, requires each in registered topology and uses max(requested timeout,sum group timeouts plus max60 or15 seconds per group). It launches one owned run-stale child with three workers and aggregate disk budget. This is intentionally larger than a single profile budget, not a global wall-time cap shared with the subsequent coexistence run.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1446 Stale-group child timeout expands to cover the full queue.md

findings.title: Stale-group resource closure is scoped to newly unresolved identities
findings.body: Baseline unresolved ephemeral IDs are excluded from the final new-resource check. Late current/parent PIDs and exact release-owner run/lane identities are also exempted. Reconciliation can return globally invalid while refresh succeeds when only prior/exempt resources remain. This is a scoped closure predicate, not a claim that the entire resource ledger is clean.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1447 Stale-group resource closure is scoped to newly unresolved identities.md

findings.title: Contained child failure is interpreted through fresh group receipts
findings.body: An exited, tree-terminated, nontimed-out child can have valid=false/exit1 without immediately aborting refresh. The owner checks receipt freshness, then returns all fresh failed groups. Full profile still runs cross-group checks and forces final valid=false if that failure list is nonempty. Noncontainment and unresolved new resources fail earlier.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1448 Contained child failure is interpreted through fresh group receipts.md

findings.title: Section owner invalidates the aggregate before launching work
findings.body: Section execution first requires processing stage and current dependencies, then writes a failing in-progress aggregate receipt before any child launch. This prevents an older passing section receipt from surviving an interrupted attempt as current authority. Final receipt follows all reused/executed chunks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1449 Section owner invalidates the aggregate before launching work.md

findings.title: Section chunk reuse depends on stored receipt integrity and declared input hash
findings.body: Caller reuses only passed receipts matching section, chunk ID and input_sha256. The reader separately checks exact keys/schema, member count, bounded output-evidence shape and an unkeyed content digest. Reuse is tied to declared inputs and retained evidence; it is not a fresh execution or an authenticated external attestation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1450 Section chunk reuse depends on stored receipt integrity and declared input hash.md

findings.title: Section chunk scheduling preserves all pending results rather than failing fast
findings.body: All pending chunks are submitted under max_parallel_chunks and individual timeouts. Worker Exceptions become failing chunk receipts while siblings continue. Aggregate duration measures scheduling time; no separate aggregate deadline or cancellation-on-first-failure exists here. BaseException and failure while publishing the failure receipt escape this per-worker conversion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1451 Section chunk scheduling preserves all pending results rather than failing fast.md

findings.title: Group reruns do not invalidate prior group receipts before execution
findings.body: Unlike sections, execute_group checks index freshness, runs the child, then writes the group receipt. A failure before that write can leave an older passing receipt untouched. Direct run can select an already current group, so interruption semantics differ between group and section owners.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1452 Group reruns do not invalidate prior group receipts before execution.md

findings.title: Group scheduling can stop before collecting the full selected denominator
findings.body: Parallel-safe futures are consumed with future.result without a per-group exception conversion, followed by serial groups. An exception in one future causes pool context shutdown and exits before later serial execution; other completed receipts may exist without a complete result report. Ordinary returned failed executions do not take this exception path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1453 Group scheduling can stop before collecting the full selected denominator.md

findings.title: Completion projection refresh has a specific place in serial group order
findings.body: The CLI writes completion projection immediately before a serial group containing test_completion_status.py, and once after the serial loop if any selected group contains that member. Parallel-safe groups run first. The second refresh occurs after all serial group receipts, not necessarily immediately after the derived-integrity group.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1454 Completion projection refresh has a specific place in serial group order.md

findings.title: Full profile claim precedes section validation and uses required group status
findings.body: Full/release claims full_profile before checking current section receipts, so later gate failure follows the failed-stage path. group_status.valid only checks configured required groups; if those are current, optional noncurrent groups do not trigger refresh. The executed profile command becomes the cross-group coexistence command, rather than the original full member command.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1455 Full profile claim precedes section validation and uses required group status.md

findings.title: Full-profile refresh keeps freshness and passing status distinct
findings.body: Post-refresh remaining detection tests fresh rather than current so failed fresh receipts can be gathered explicitly. Returned valid depends on failed rows, while status contains the required-group predicate. That status is retained in the profile output; its overall valid is not independently rechecked after refresh before coexistence execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1456 Full-profile refresh keeps freshness and passing status distinct.md

findings.title: Successful release preflight retains the certify claim for finalize
findings.body: Authoritative preflight checks certify processing stage and claims certify once. On valid=true it reports completion_deferred_to release finalize and clears only the local variable, leaving the durable claim. Finalize can reuse matching active certify claim or claim one if absent, then delegates actual artifact finalization.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1457 Successful release preflight retains the certify claim for finalize.md

findings.title: CLI failure receipts do not cover every exception or final output failure
findings.body: Only OSError, ValueError, KeyError, RuntimeError and JSONDecodeError enter failed-stage handling. TypeError, NameError/UnboundLocalError, KeyboardInterrupt and serialization errors can escape. Finally releases orchestration ownership; output serialization and print occur afterward, following any successful finish_release_stage. A stage can therefore finish before response delivery fails.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1458 CLI failure receipts do not cover every exception or final output failure.md

findings.title: Registry validation and doctor expose different completion contracts
findings.body: validate returns registry validity with operational_state and certification_claim=false; unavailable completion projection does not change registry valid. It claims ordered validate only when the release-identity pointer file exists, preserving installed registry checking. doctor instead sets exit0/2 from requested syntax/operable/ready/certification-ready predicate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1459 Registry validation and doctor expose different completion contracts.md

findings.title: CLI successful evaluation does not always mean an approved decision
findings.body: Claims-only admission/outcome evaluation, authorization simulation and security/hook authority decisions can return valid=true and exit0 for a denied or nonauthoritative decision. Authoritative admission/outcome paths use explicit disposition codes; retry maps allowed to valid. Default output without valid is treated as successful. Consumers must use the command-specific contract.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1460 CLI successful evaluation does not always mean an approved decision.md

findings.title: Hardware admission fingerprint omits decision-relevant inputs
findings.body: Confirmed isolated dispatch: changing batchable, estimated-device-bytes and operation-id leaves hardware_input identical. Those values are passed to WorkloadProfile but omitted from work identity. The shared work plane can join matching in-flight results, so cache_seconds=0 on route does not make the omitted fields irrelevant to concurrent identity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1461 Hardware admission fingerprint omits decision-relevant inputs.md

findings.title: Hardware report caching and timeout are work-plane contracts
findings.body: Hardware report uses a60-second cache while route uses0; both declare a10-second work-plane timeout. The reviewed work plane applies timeout to admission waiting, not interruption of the hardware callback. Benchmark file bytes are fingerprinted separately before the callback parses that file, leaving a mutable-input gap.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1462 Hardware report caching and timeout are work-plane contracts.md

findings.title: Bounded CLI output does not imply bounded input hydration
findings.body: Visibility ingress caps stdin at4MiB and requires a batch/event-object shape. Most file-based commands read entire JSON/text payloads before owner validation, including transcript record lists. Audit --summary runs the full audit first, then retains counts and at most100 error entries; error strings and hygiene dictionaries are not byte-bounded.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1463 Bounded CLI output does not imply bounded input hydration.md

findings.title: Visibility ingress chooses its allowed root from caller bus location
findings.body: The CLI resolves --bus-root, chooses its parent as allowed_root and creates that directory before constructing OperationalEventBus. This is a caller-selected publication boundary, not containment under the framework root. Batch validity does not independently confer event authority; the downstream bus owns its checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1464 Visibility ingress chooses its allowed root from caller bus location.md

findings.title: Some descriptive CLI operations publish artifacts without an apply flag
findings.body: Every placement action publishes its result through publish_placement_artifact, including advisory decisions and failed promotion results. Audit always invokes hygiene analysis, with actual application controlled separately; full/release profiles and selected release-audit groups apply hygiene automatically. Tool-intake scan suppresses recording apply but can still execute explicitly requested/approved scanners.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1465 Some descriptive CLI operations publish artifacts without an apply flag.md

findings.title: Plan effect declarations are descriptive rather than execution authorization
findings.body: plan passes goal and available input labels to navigation, then adds sorted declared_effects and an unload-plan string. Effects are not sent as navigation constraints and no authorization or task execution occurs. Selection, routing, hydration and specialist prompt compilation are distinct branches with different success predicates.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1466 Plan effect declarations are descriptive rather than execution authorization.md

findings.title: Cognitive freshness validation is confined to status in the CLI
findings.body: All cognitive actions load the index, but only status calls validate_cognitive_index and integration_healthcheck. Query and hydrate-plan use the loaded index directly; run also requires the index file even though dispatch uses a separate facade. Agent list valid is based on matches before limit, so limit0 can return valid=true with no agents.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1467 Cognitive freshness validation is confined to status in the CLI.md

findings.title: CLI fixtures cover ownership well but leave dispatch and publication gaps
findings.body: Tests exercise real lock exclusion, one-generation ownership, scoped resource exceptions, two concurrent missing chunks, decision codes and selected bounded routes. Four broken loader branches and hardware fingerprint omissions are absent. Preflight/finalize tests assert source strings rather than executing the claim lifecycle. test_bootstrap_cli calls underlying APIs directly, not parser/main. No product tests were run for this report.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1468 CLI fixtures cover ownership well but leave dispatch and publication gaps.md

findings.title: Pytest plugin loading has two entry paths
findings.body: Root conftest loads tests.pytest_guards for direct discovery, while the governed runner adds explicit -p loading for tests outside that discovery tree. The test package initializer contains only a docstring.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1469 Pytest plugin loading has two entry paths.md

findings.title: Per-test reclamation inherits ownership rather than checking it
findings.body: The hook resolves the environment marker once and snapshots child names. It does not query the resource ledger, verify a cleanup receipt, bind root identity after yield, or classify every new child. The normal runner supplies a registered workspace; direct calls with an arbitrary marker would rely on that caller assertion. Audit performed no cleanup.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1470 Per-test reclamation inherits ownership rather than checking it.md

findings.title: Name baselines are not per-test content or producer identity
findings.body: Existing child names are preserved even if their contents change. Every newly named child is selected, including one produced concurrently after the baseline. Directory existence after yield does not establish the same root identity. This is a lifecycle assumption, not demonstrated destructive behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1471 Name baselines are not per-test content or producer identity.md

findings.title: Cleanup retry is bounded but narrowly typed
findings.body: Only PermissionError receives six attempts with delays totaling2.65 seconds. Nested permission failures chmod entries to read/write before retry; other OSError values propagate to fixture aggregation. Tests cover transient retry, non-permission failure and read-only children, not root replacement or concurrent producers.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1472 Cleanup retry is bounded but narrowly typed.md

findings.title: Thread leak failure does not terminate leaked threads
findings.body: The shutdown hook compares object IDs of live non-daemon threads with an initial snapshot, prints their names and changes exitstatus. It does not join or stop them and cannot by itself guarantee process exit; preexisting and daemon threads are outside this predicate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1473 Thread leak failure does not terminate leaked threads.md

findings.title: Shared pytest base guard observes only a directory during call
findings.body: The runtest_call wrapper obtains the shared base, then recreates it and forces an exception if it is no longer a directory. It does not verify contents, identity, or deletion during all setup/teardown phases.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1474 Shared pytest base guard observes only a directory during call.md

findings.title: Bytecode suppression has startup timing limits
findings.body: sitecustomize sets sys.dont_write_bytecode when Python loads it. The package initialization test explicitly allows at most one __init__ cache file, showing that later package suppression is not a guarantee of zero startup bytecode. The second test only inspects CLI hygiene call ordering as source text.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1475 Bytecode suppression has startup timing limits.md

findings.title: Fixture copy preserves selected receipt metadata
findings.body: canonical_copy_ignore prunes generated patterns, every case-insensitive .lock suffix and external environment paths. The scope test confirms exclusion of local gate fixtures while retaining a current section receipt. Retention is a copy boundary, not a fresh receipt for the clone.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1476 Fixture copy preserves selected receipt metadata.md

findings.title: Quickstart timeout is per child rather than aggregate
findings.body: Eight sequential CLI calls each have a60-second bound, while the end-to-end test bounds the entire demonstration at90 seconds. No aggregate deadline or registered child-process custody appears in the demo owner; an earlier failure leaves the already-created output tree without the final receipt.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1477 Quickstart timeout is per child rather than aggregate.md

findings.title: Quickstart validity and selection rely on result shape
findings.body: The demo treats absent valid as true and applies bool to present values, then assumes selection capability_ids has an element. Its framework_validation label contains processing-order status rather than full validation. This is explicitly a pre-validation demonstration.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1478 Quickstart validity and selection rely on result shape.md

findings.title: Quickstart hash binds an envelope rather than complete effects
findings.body: The canonical unkeyed digest covers the receipt before its digest field. Nested step outputs are retained and may include absolute paths despite the relative project label. changed_paths lists project and receipt, not every possible runtime control-plane write.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1479 Quickstart hash binds an envelope rather than complete effects.md

findings.title: Declared wrapper is a projected executable template
findings.body: Installed imports take precedence and any ModuleNotFoundError triggers fallback imports after inserting parents[4]. Argument parsing executes at module import. Input JSON is read without a byte bound and malformed shape/owner exceptions are uncaught. The directory-depth assumption belongs to projected wrappers, not arbitrary direct template execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1480 Declared wrapper is a projected executable template.md

findings.title: Supabase scaffold does not implement authentication or idempotent work
findings.body: The handler only requires a nonempty idempotency header and any non-null JavaScript object, including arrays. JWT/signature validation and bounded idempotent work remain comments; the key is echoed without persistence or deduplication. OPTIONS returns before body checks, other methods are not restricted, malformed JSON becomes500, and CORS uses a placeholder origin without an allow-methods header. This is a template, not a deployed service claim.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1481 Supabase scaffold does not implement authentication or idempotent work.md

findings.title: Ownership tests exercise two declared records
findings.body: The builder tests assert semantic-memory and local-model owners, producer lists, enforcement labels and named tests. They do not invoke those producers or cover every schema-owner entry.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1482 Ownership tests exercise two declared records.md

findings.title: Graph manifest tests include real rejection paths
findings.body: Ten graph declarations must validate; duplicate path, missing source revisions and a stale graph hash must fail. Distinct purpose strings and ten paths are also asserted. This is stronger than presence-only checks but does not independently inspect all semantics represented by those graphs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1483 Graph manifest tests include real rejection paths.md

findings.title: Historical audit test checks presence and a weak status exclusion
findings.body: The retained audit test requires exactly30 unique A01-A30 IDs and zero stored open_count. Each status must omit pending_review and evidence paths must exist; it does not require a closed allowlist, bind hashes or validate evidence content.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1484 Historical audit test checks presence and a weak status exclusion.md

findings.title: Source migration receipt tests trust recorded disposition
findings.body: Tests require complete/runtime_loaded flags, every recorded batch unresolved=0, owner path existence and absence of externalized directories. They do not fetch or hash external payloads, verify historical scans, or reject an empty batches list through that all predicate alone.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1485 Source migration receipt tests trust recorded disposition.md

findings.title: Candidate and specialty tests preserve honest metadata distinctions
findings.body: Candidate records with runtime_symbols must remain partial_semantic_coverage; counts are recomputed internally. Specialty entries must cover queue IDs exactly once, and active IDs/counts must match catalog intersections. Neither test verifies runtime symbol behavior or original external source identity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1486 Candidate and specialty tests preserve honest metadata distinctions.md

findings.title: Research contract tests establish candidate-only shape admission
findings.body: Every declared research contract is tested with a generated minimal instance and must remain candidate_only with auto_activate false; one empty research-record must raise. Source coverage testing separately asserts a valid summary and a minimum control count, not each control execution.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1487 Research contract tests establish candidate-only shape admission.md

findings.title: Historical revocation tests preserve certificate bytes and reject authority
findings.body: The0.6.1 and0.6.2 tests hash retained certificates against revocation records and constrain project lifecycle labels; the0.6.2 test additionally calls the certificate verifier and expects invalid. Hardcoded public wording and release paths are historical policy fixtures, not live marketplace status.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1488 Historical revocation tests preserve certificate bytes and reject authority.md

findings.title: Fault campaign aggregate test does not call the aggregate owner
findings.body: One test loads campaign metadata and checks dimensions, command tokens and referenced test paths. The failed-lane test writes its own two-row JSON fixture and asserts Python all is false; it never invokes run_release_fault_campaign publication or its failure handling.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1489 Fault campaign aggregate test does not call the aggregate owner.md

findings.title: Supply-chain writer test uses declared artifact hashes
findings.body: The test passes invented wheel/sdist digests and no artifact files, then checks output types, one checksum, version and a provenance subject. Its final hash assertion merely checks a nonempty computed string. It does not verify real artifact bytes, signatures or complete source provenance.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1490 Supply-chain writer test uses declared artifact hashes.md

findings.title: Platform policy fixtures do not execute a multi-platform matrix
findings.body: Tests validate declared Python3.11-3.14 and three OS policies, synthetic version bounds, current-host Unicode paths/read-only bits/lock creation, and LF attributes. The POSIX host check only requires policy intersection with Linux or Darwin; this does not prove which OS or all CI jobs ran.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1491 Platform policy fixtures do not execute a multi-platform matrix.md

findings.title: Publication workflow tests inspect local strings and retained bindings
findings.body: Tests hash local certificate/signature files against a stored public receipt and compare artifact metadata; they do not cryptographically verify the signature or retrieve remote assets. Workflow ordering, OIDC, exact VSIX values and manual transport are checked as strings, not parsed/executed CI behavior. User-reported marketplace publication remains a separate fact.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1492 Publication workflow tests inspect local strings and retained bindings.md

findings.title: Completion tests mix formula checks with historical state expectations
findings.body: The tests bind stored projection to a fresh builder result and compare readiness/certified formulas, but also require fixed historical counts and explicit open-gap labels. A mock proves compact head use without loading snapshot. These assertions exercise declared projection semantics, not exhaustive feature completion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1493 Completion tests mix formula checks with historical state expectations.md

findings.title: Completion writer tests mutate authoritative fixture paths
findings.body: Both writer tests call owners against ROOT, then restore target bytes in finally. They assert final JSON and absence of prepared files; they do not inject mid-write crashes or concurrent changes. Restoration itself is a write and can overwrite intervening state. These tests were read only.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1494 Completion writer tests mutate authoritative fixture paths.md

findings.title: Adversarial routing test uses a fixed synthetic catalog
findings.body: Twelve hand-built summaries cover ambiguous terms, negative matches, unsafe risk and supersession. The fixed corpus checks top1, exclusions and deterministic ties with synthetic revision labels. No live catalog drift, adversarial corpus expansion or runtime capability execution is established.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1495 Adversarial routing test uses a fixed synthetic catalog.md

findings.title: Hybrid retrieval test signals are supplied rather than computed
findings.body: Each optional signal changes an unrelated baseline into a hit by replacing one input field. This proves fusion consumes six signal types, not that an embedding model, graph scorer or external service computed them. The adapter subprocess fixture has no timeout; import portability is also checked by source strings.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1496 Hybrid retrieval test signals are supplied rather than computed.md

findings.title: Memory fabric tests keep scope and trust separate from address encoding
findings.body: Fixtures exercise exact structured route priority, project/ACL/expiry/trust rejection, canonical semantic roundtrip and adaptive address expansion. The provider test explicitly requires disabled even when all seven self-attested booleans are true. Correction checks a rebuild plan and transfer_exports membership, not actual rebuilding of every derived surface.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1497 Memory fabric tests keep scope and trust separate from address encoding.md

findings.title: Capture tests verify proposal state without proving durable accepted origin
findings.body: The semantic candidate fixture uses a dry-run capture and supplied semantic envelope, then checks candidate/proposal/retrieval-disabled state and rejection of a quarantined label. Capture apply testing checks schema and repeat event ID, not a crash/restart chain or byte-for-byte immutability of every repeated file.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1498 Capture tests verify proposal state without proving durable accepted origin.md

findings.title: Promotion tests use evidence and reviewer identifiers as fixtures
findings.body: The high-impact constraint is held without reviewer IDs and becomes validated with human-1 plus two supplied evidence strings. This demonstrates the decision branch; the test does not authenticate a human or establish independent evidence provenance.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1499 Promotion tests use evidence and reviewer identifiers as fixtures.md

findings.title: Memory queue retry fixture does not establish exactly-once effects
findings.body: The first callback raises before performing a recorded effect; the same PersistentWriteQueue object then flushes through an append callback once. Stable idempotency key and ready status do not test process restart or a crash after the external writer commits but before queue publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1500 Memory queue retry fixture does not establish exactly-once effects.md

findings.title: Memory context and offload tests include actual tamper rejection
findings.body: Tests enforce L0 pointer-only assembly, a character bound, deterministic scenes and same-project borrowed-agent limits. Offload preview leaves no file; apply restores the original body; altered stored bytes raise hash mismatch. These are bounded fixtures, not proof of all storage/concurrency or injection cases.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1501 Memory context and offload tests include actual tamper rejection.md

findings.title: Scheduler tests certify simulated policy rather than execution
findings.body: Metadata counts assert30 capabilities/owners, five workflows, three policies and eight schemas. Simulation tests reject cycles/missing dependencies and approval/resource/privacy/budget/retry blocks, and assert deterministic would_dispatch plans with execution_authority none. They call Python directly and do not cover CLI load_json failure found in batch89.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1502 Scheduler tests certify simulated policy rather than execution.md

findings.title: Agent replay tests distinguish immutable artifacts from allowed run evidence
findings.body: Eighteen receipt mutations plus altered builder artifacts and undeclared topology are rejected. A well-shaped run filename containing empty JSON is accepted for reopen, while rogue.txt is rejected. Legacy creation receipt reopens without graph backfill; modern missing triplet fails. This tests definition topology, not every retained run payload.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1503 Agent replay tests distinguish immutable artifacts from allowed run evidence.md

findings.title: Worker success and host-model success have different fixture origins
findings.body: The owned harness test requires process_started/exited/tree_closed and worker_invoked true with model_invoked false. Host-model tests instead supply completion status, output and model/token metadata directly to complete_host_run. These establish terminal envelope handling, not a real Copilot/model request.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1504 Worker success and host-model success have different fixture origins.md

findings.title: Agent structural admission can coexist with blocked runtime memory
findings.body: The unresolved-memory fixture passes candidate tests and admission but marks runtime_ready false; preview blocks and invocation must fail before adding a run. Host tool preflight likewise tests structural attestation and authority preview, not an actual external host tool invocation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1505 Agent structural admission can coexist with blocked runtime memory.md

findings.title: Worker diagnostic fallback tests intercept storage and stderr
findings.body: Primary diagnostic failure is injected before a second durable write. When both writes fail, os.write is intercepted and the JSON payload inspected. No real supervised stderr transport, short-write loop or total diagnostic failure is exercised by these tests.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1506 Worker diagnostic fallback tests intercept storage and stderr.md

findings.title: Agent lifecycle test observes autonomous publication directly
findings.body: The real-lifecycle fixture starts through one-shot authority, denies unapproved pause, then pauses/resumes one run and cancels another. It polls run_control.read for up to45 seconds rather than session_status, verifying publication does not depend on that API. Observer inactive and worker reclaimed assertions are fixture requirements; no fresh cross-platform result is claimed here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1507 Agent lifecycle test observes autonomous publication directly.md

findings.title: Dashboard timeout assertion does not measure producer execution
findings.body: The snapshot test mocks RuntimeWorkPlane.execute, returns connected true immediately, and inspects timeout_seconds=60. It proves argument plumbing, not an enforced60-second total callback or end-to-end UI latency bound.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1508 Dashboard timeout assertion does not measure producer execution.md

findings.title: Dashboard runnable counts are stored-state observations
findings.body: Tests create unsigned minimal admission JSON with decision admitted/runnable_state runnable and minimal session/run state JSON, then expect runnable revision and run counts. Display totals therefore must not be interpreted as authenticated admission, current executable readiness or completed operations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1509 Dashboard runnable counts are stored-state observations.md

findings.title: Dashboard graph tests establish bounded presentation behavior
findings.body: Tests cover global typo ranking, qualified ambiguous IDs, aggregate cluster accounting, endpoint membership, depth clamp6 and node/edge limits500/1000. Oversized bytes are rejected before JSON decode; excessive node count is rejected after parsing but before graph materialization. A single-node repository fixture lacks freshness metadata, so its current-project-map test name does not establish current source identity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1510 Dashboard graph tests establish bounded presentation behavior.md

findings.title: Completion display tests separate source hashing from mocked selection
findings.body: One fixture changes actual authority bytes and verifies stale detection with a mocked ledger head. Several runtime/registry preference tests mock _completion_projection_current true, while stale fallback tests require green claims revoked and the builder uncalled. Host source identity excludes a generated bundle while binding source/action contract changes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1511 Completion display tests separate source hashing from mocked selection.md

findings.title: Hardware dashboard fixtures test cache integrity with a mocked probe
findings.body: Tests check miss/hit/forced/expired states, malformed JSON rebuild, tampered report hash, future timestamps and an upper TTL rejection. hardware_report is mocked, so these are cache lifecycle tests rather than measurements or hardware compatibility evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1512 Hardware dashboard fixtures test cache integrity with a mocked probe.md

findings.title: Provider LIVE display classification can come from budget state alone
findings.body: One test expects the local ollama budget projection to have provenance class LIVE. Another writes sealed synthetic reservation/settlement metadata and checks30 percent use, seven units remaining and redacted fallback details. No provider call, token observation or billing reconciliation occurs in those fixtures.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1513 Provider LIVE display classification can come from budget state alone.md

findings.title: Memory dashboard states are classification fixtures rather than attachment operations
findings.body: Tests distinguish detached, configured empty, expired and new-project onboarding; mocked workspace-monitor and project-map values suppress unrelated attention for new repositories while retaining invalid existing-map warnings. They do not initialize, attach or renew actual memory sessions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1514 Memory dashboard states are classification fixtures rather than attachment operations.md

findings.title: Cache discovery fails closed on walker limits but excludes by a distinct policy
findings.body: The Python cache owner uses100000 files, depth128 and2GiB observed file size, with links skipped. Repository-root pytest cache and canonical external custody are pruned after removing cache components from the classification path. Directory matching itself is case-sensitive while suffix matching is casefolded. This differs from the extension scanner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1515 Cache discovery fails closed on walker limits but excludes by a distinct policy.md

findings.title: Whole cache directory moves can carry uninventoried descendants
findings.body: The walker can skip links and excluded subtrees while still selecting their containing cache directory. shutil.move then relocates the entire selected directory, including entries not in covered_files. Post-move verification checks only recorded inventory, so it is not a complete moved-object denominator.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1516 Whole cache directory moves can carry uninventoried descendants.md

findings.title: Nested cache moves can invalidate expected destination layout
findings.body: Targets sort deepest-first. Moving an inner cache creates its destination parent; later moving the outer cache to that existing parent makes shutil.move append the source basename. Recorded expected paths can then fail reconciliation after earlier effects. An isolated unchanged-stdlib probe confirmed existing-directory destination behavior with rename intercepted; no directory was moved.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1517 Nested cache moves can invalidate expected destination layout.md

findings.title: Cache move receipt is published only after all effects
findings.body: Inventory hashes and size stats are separate reads; target containment is checked before inventory, not immediately before moves. No second matching tree snapshot, pre-move equality, durable intent or rollback exists in this owner. A move/reconciliation failure can leave partial quarantine without its final receipt. Caller quarantine roots may be external or even inside a selected subtree; only workspace/root equality is rejected.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1518 Cache move receipt is published only after all effects.md

findings.title: Cache CLI output is an additional unguarded publication path
findings.body: Even preview can write caller-selected --output, creating parents and replacing a file. This path has no collision/alias restriction against scanned input. Successful return always exits0 and the result has no valid field; errors raise before that return.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1519 Cache CLI output is an additional unguarded publication path.md

findings.title: Sanitizer traversal materializes excluded subtrees before filtering
findings.body: A complete rglob list is sorted deepest-first without file/byte/depth/time limits. Exclusions are applied in later loops, not traversal pruning. changed_nodes is built without exclusions and later adds renamed-node descendants to preservation, so excluded names can still be read/copied when selected by name transformation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1520 Sanitizer traversal materializes excluded subtrees before filtering.md

findings.title: Sanitizer preservation receipt hashes source after copy
findings.body: Apply creates an empty external preservation directory, scans readable UTF-8 candidates, copies affected files and then hashes/stat-checks each source. It never compares copied destination bytes against the source digest, nor checks immediate source equality before rewrite. Concurrent changes can make preserved bytes and receipt disagree. Preflight errors stop mutation but may leave the created preservation directory.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1521 Sanitizer preservation receipt hashes source after copy.md

findings.title: Sanitizer rename resolves links before applying the operation
findings.body: _extended_windows_path calls path.resolve for source and target, and _rename passes those resolved paths directly to os.rename. The owner does not reject symlink files or recheck resolved containment. An unchanged-function probe with fake resolution confirmed that an in-tree logical link resolving outside would pass the outside target as rename source; actual links/moves were not created.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1522 Sanitizer rename resolves links before applying the operation.md

findings.title: Sanitizer text classification and binary coverage differ
findings.body: The first64KiB NUL check decides binary versus UTF-8 treatment. A NUL-free binary with invalid UTF-8 raises preservation preflight failure under apply; later text errors are recorded. Binary scanning checks configured identifier patterns in Latin-1 chunks but does not rewrite binary content. Root names themselves are outside the rglob rename list.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1523 Sanitizer text classification and binary coverage differ.md

findings.title: Sanitizer text replacement and multi-file operation are not transactional
findings.body: Each text file uses a same-directory temporary, copied stat and os.replace; there is no file/directory fsync or concurrent-identity recheck. Finally retains a failed temp by move, which can itself fail and mask the original error. Later rename errors are outside the text-error catch. Earlier rewritten/renamed files remain changed if a later file fails.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1524 Sanitizer text replacement and multi-file operation are not transactional.md

findings.title: Sanitizer collision naming checks availability without reservation
findings.body: Overlong components use a deterministic name digest and limited suffix; collisions try widening source-name hash suffixes. Availability is checked before rename rather than reserved atomically, and preview does not reserve generated names. Path-change output hashes the original relative path and stores a sanitized target string; it is not a complete actual-path journal after ancestor renames.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1525 Sanitizer collision naming checks availability without reservation.md

findings.title: Identifier audit file and byte counts include unscanned binary contents
findings.body: Known binary suffixes bypass content scanning but add stat size to bytes_scanned. Unknown suffixes are fully decoded once for classification, then read again for scanning if admitted. Unknown-suffix OSError/UnicodeDecodeError returns false rather than recording the error; an isolated unreadable-file probe confirmed this classification result. Counts are visited/stat-accounted bytes, not universally inspected content bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1526 Identifier audit file and byte counts include unscanned binary contents.md

findings.title: Identifier audit has traversal and pattern scope limits
findings.body: The audit fully materializes rglob before exclusions and has no total resource bound. File symlinks can be followed by is_file/open without resolved-root containment. Nonexistent roots can yield empty scoped results. Pattern matching uses finite overlap, configured spellings and ASCII home-name grammar; ZIP detection is suffix-only and does not inspect archive content.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1527 Identifier audit has traversal and pattern scope limits.md

findings.title: Identifier-only audit intentionally never claims comprehensive validity
findings.body: Five controls are always not_run, so valid remains false even when scoped_valid passes. Four pattern/archive gate statuses depend on hit lists rather than errors; read failures can coexist with those individual passed gates while scoped_valid is false. CLI exits1 for noncomprehensive valid, not merely for identifier findings.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1528 Identifier-only audit intentionally never claims comprehensive validity.md

findings.title: Sanitation composition does not propagate identifier top-level errors
findings.body: build_sanitation_summary copies only identifier_audit.gates, replaces the five not-run controls and derives validity from gate statuses. It does not carry identifier_audit.errors or scoped_valid. A transient identifier-only read failure can therefore be lost if other scans pass and base gate hit lists are empty. Release/export callers use this compositor result; this is a source-derived failure path, not an executed release.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1529 Sanitation composition does not propagate identifier top-level errors.md

findings.title: Identifier provenance exemptions are path labels rather than content authentication
findings.body: Four fixed provenance paths receive host-home exemptions and one n8n template admits a fixed container home literal. Exemptions apply to home matches, not configured private identifiers. The audit itself does not verify append-only integrity or authenticate those paths before granting their typed exemption.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1530 Identifier provenance exemptions are path labels rather than content authentication.md

findings.title: Historical deletion scripts embed an old authority claim
findings.body: All three PowerShell receipts hardcode explicit_user_request_2026-08-13 and protected_data_touched=false. They do not consume a current admission, retention decision or resource ledger. Those source strings are historical labels and are not authorization to run deletion in this task.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1531 Historical deletion scripts embed an old authority claim.md

findings.title: Historical ownership discovery is based on names or fixture shapes
findings.body: One script selects four temp prefixes plus extension/.vscode-test; another selects every child of the user-wide pytest-of-USERNAME directory; the third matches temp names plus framework/repository/package/key-pair signatures. Generic tmp directories with repository/.git or a matching release-output suffix can qualify. These heuristics do not prove exclusive Pacify-X ownership.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1532 Historical ownership discovery is based on names or fixture shapes.md

findings.title: Historical live-process and reparse checks have time and resolution gaps
findings.body: Each script snapshots process command lines once and matches path substrings, missing users of files whose paths are absent from command lines and later processes. GetFullPath is lexical; relative link targets are resolved against current directory, not their containing link directory. Only the generated-fixture script explicitly rejects a top-level reparse target. No immediate content snapshot is compared before removal.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1533 Historical live-process and reparse checks have time and resolution gaps.md

findings.title: Historical deletion evidence is late and accounting is not physical reclamation proof
findings.body: The owned-cache script aborts on error and writes no final receipt after partial deletion. The other two catch per-target failures but retained targets may already be partly changed. Counts use logical file lengths; C-drive free-space differences are host-wide and can include unrelated activity or another target volume. Receipts are final direct writes without a durable per-effect journal.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1534 Historical deletion evidence is late and accounting is not physical reclamation proof.md

findings.title: Historical cleanup redaction claims exceed its verification
findings.body: The redactor replaces only current root/home/temp literal spellings in string values, not dictionary keys, other hosts, slash/case variants or arbitrary path patterns. It then unconditionally labels host_paths_removed and semantic_fields_preserved true. All four files are overwritten sequentially even if text did not change; no before-image, digest rebinding or verification scan is retained. Its nonauthoritative historical classification is explicit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1535 Historical cleanup redaction claims exceed its verification.md

findings.title: Extension cache custody differs from canonical repository custody
findings.body: The JS scanner skips .git/node_modules and root evidence/quarantine trees, but has no canonical exclusions for virtual environments, Python installations or preserved-skills trees. Any recognized cache basename can receive safe-to-delete and retentionRequired=false after structural inventory. Name classification does not establish content ownership or retention. Host requires explicit selection and modal approval, which remains a separate boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1536 Extension cache custody differs from canonical repository custody.md

findings.title: Extension scan bounds do not bound candidate hashing time
findings.body: maxDirectories/maxCandidates use Number(options.value || default), so nonfinite/nonnumeric truthy values can disable comparisons for direct callers. Each candidate permits50000 entries but has no byte/time bound; a large readdir is allocated before counting.
