Cancellation is checked between discovery entries, not inside inventoryDirectory/hashFileStable. Candidate failures are silently dropped without an unresolved list.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1537 Extension scan bounds do not bound candidate hashing time.md

findings.title: Extension main path binds multiple identities and snapshots
findings.body: Root lstat/realpath, every target ancestor, no-follow file open where available, file identity/size/mtime, hardlink rejection and directory identity checks support the normal path. Candidate, preflight, immediate, staged and final inventories must agree before adapter invocation. This is materially stronger than legacy cache mover, while remaining userspace pathname operations with a final check-to-effect interval.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1538 Extension main path binds multiple identities and snapshots.md

findings.title: Extension candidate IDs are selectors rather than authorization tokens
findings.body: IDs are truncated root/path hashes and execution verifies basename/name/relativePath/classification/retention plus inventory. directoryIdentity is optional in executeCleanup, but the normal host retains its nonenumerable scan object and only sends display fields to the webview. The host passes its own candidates after modal approval, so a webview cannot directly substitute arbitrary candidate objects through that route.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1539 Extension candidate IDs are selectors rather than authorization tokens.md

findings.title: Extension staging protects a replaced original path but not all OS races
findings.body: A random sibling stage becomes the adapter target, preserving a concurrently recreated original path. Identity/hash checks occur before rename/disposal, but no filesystem handle-based atomic compare-and-remove exists. A receipt write occurs between immediate inventory and stage rename. Claims of no remaining pathname race would exceed the implementation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1540 Extension staging protects a replaced original path but not all OS races.md

findings.title: Extension recycle fallback validates leaf but omits ancestor containment
findings.body: Fallback forms .quarantine/cleanupId with lexical isInside checks, recursively creates it and verifies only that leaf is a plain directory. It does not call assertPlainDirectoryUnderRoot or compare realpath with rootGuard for this route. An existing linked .quarantine ancestor can redirect the destination outside the root. This is a conditional source finding; no symlink or move was executed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1541 Extension recycle fallback validates leaf but omits ancestor containment.md

findings.title: Extension restoration has a narrower guard than disposal
findings.body: restoreUnchangedStage checks stage/plain-directory, original absence and matching inventory, then renames. It receives no root guard and does not repeat ancestor containment or reserve the absent original destination. A concurrent path/ancestor change can invalidate those checks before rename. Failed quarantine verification after a successful move can also leave an unrecorded quarantine location while stage-based restore finds nothing.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1542 Extension restoration has a narrower guard than disposal.md

findings.title: Extension receipts distinguish adapter uncertainty but can themselves fail after effects
findings.body: The owner explicitly separates partial retention, disappearance after adapter error, unchanged restoration and successful fallback. Phase receipts flush a temporary file then rename, with directory fsync only off Windows. A write outside the per-candidate try or terminal write failure aborts the loop/return after prior effects; no restart reconciler is defined here. Callback temporary-file removal errors are suppressed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1543 Extension receipts distinguish adapter uncertainty but can themselves fail after effects.md

findings.title: Extension reclaimed byte totals include preserved local quarantine
findings.body: Confirmed results include moved-to-local-quarantine as well as recycle/permanent disposition. bytes_reclaimed sums original logical candidate sizes, so it can be positive when bytes remain in the same project. The host announces reclaimed count. This is removal from the active cache location, not demonstrated freed disk capacity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1544 Extension reclaimed byte totals include preserved local quarantine.md

findings.title: Extension recycle tests use a deletion adapter rather than OS trash
findings.body: Success fixtures call fs.rm even when asserting useTrash=true; they prove adapter option plumbing and receipt logic, not recoverability through the operating-system recycle bin. Tests cover link/hardlink rejection, changed trees, partial/uncertain outcomes, original-path replacement and Unicode depth. They omit quarantine ancestor redirection and receipt publication failure after effects.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1545 Extension recycle tests use a deletion adapter rather than OS trash.md

findings.title: Sanitation tests preserve scanner scope rather than full secret assurance
findings.body: Identifier tests explicitly expect clean scoped_valid=true but comprehensive valid=false; they test chunk-boundary placeholder behavior, immutable provenance, binary exclusion and external custody. The summary test supplies passed base identifier gates and valid licensing while running local shape/email/magic checks. Matching PNG magic permits embedded email bytes without text PII review by design.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1546 Sanitation tests preserve scanner scope rather than full secret assurance.md

findings.title: Secret review tests bind content identity while allowing line movement
findings.body: Tests assert redacted literal credential shapes, selected false positives, complete private-key block detection and stale reviews after value changes. A separate fixture permits formatting-only movement to line3. These test deterministic identity policy; they do not prove detection of unknown secret encodings or provider revocation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1547 Secret review tests bind content identity while allowing line movement.md

findings.title: Sanitizer and cache tests leave several operational failure paths open
findings.body: Fixtures cover ordinary preview/apply, canonical expansion, long names, collisions, named exclusions, preflight read failure and single-level cache recovery. They do not cover nested cache targets, content drift between preservation and mutation, copy-byte verification, linked source rename or failed final receipt. Some sanitizer tests preserve a sibling directory outside their TemporaryDirectory context. None were run here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1548 Sanitizer and cache tests leave several operational failure paths open.md

findings.title: Global host lease can return without a successfully created lock
findings.body: The two-attempt loop removes a stale lock after each EEXIST. After the second removal it leaves the loop and constructs a lease even though neither exclusive create succeeded. A VM probe of unchanged source with fake fs confirmed two failed creates, two removals and a returned token. No real lock was touched.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1549 Global host lease can return without a successfully created lock.md

findings.title: Lease stale ownership is PID-based and release is best-effort
findings.body: Signal-zero EPERM means alive; other probe failures mean dead. There is no process birth identity, compare-and-unlink predecessor check or fsync. release sets its released flag before reading/unlinking and suppresses errors, preventing retry after a transient failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1550 Lease stale ownership is PID-based and release is best-effort.md

findings.title: Timeout followed by zero exit can report completed
findings.body: The worker records termination_reason=timeout but classifies numeric zero as completed. The explicit timeout error is limited to a null code. Unchanged source in a fake child/terminator VM produced status completed, timeout reason and both closure booleans true.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1551 Timeout followed by zero exit can report completed.md

findings.title: Termination rejection can escape timeout settlement
findings.body: Signal handlers discard the termination promise; timeout attaches then without a rejection handler. A rejecting terminator can produce unhandled rejection and a hanging one can leave the outer worker unresolved. Windows taskkill helper itself has no timeout. No live termination was attempted.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1552 Termination rejection can escape timeout settlement.md

findings.title: Process-tree closure changes meaning without an ownership token
findings.body: Without ownershipToken reconciliation equates tree closure to worker exit. With a token it scans command-line substring matches, requests termination, then scans once immediately. POSIX termination only sends SIGTERM; it does not await exit/escalate. Command-line token presence is not ancestry or PID-birth proof.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1553 Process-tree closure changes meaning without an ownership token.md

findings.title: Host output tail bound is characters rather than bytes
findings.body: The retained stdout/stderr tail limit is applied to JavaScript strings after independently decoding chunks, so UTF-8 boundaries can be replaced and memory bytes exceed the nominal character count. Forwarded output is not bounded by that tail. Callback or lease release exceptions in finally can replace the operation outcome.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1554 Host output tail bound is characters rather than bytes.md

findings.title: Cache marker creation and cache reads enforce different custody checks
findings.body: Read paths lstat root/marker and reject links, while ensure creates/writes through the selected root without equivalent root/ancestor identity checks. Existing marker owner/schema are checked, but direct read-modify-write has no lock or atomic publication and can lose concurrently retained versions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1555 Cache marker creation and cache reads enforce different custody checks.md

findings.title: Cached executable resolution does not bind executable bytes
findings.body: The resolver checks platform layout, directory/sentinel/executable plain-file state and marker owner/schema. It does not verify retained_versions includes requested version, sentinel contents, executable digest/signature/version or all ancestor realpaths. Darwin has no supported layout despite a macOS browser lane elsewhere.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1556 Cached executable resolution does not bind executable bytes.md

findings.title: Temporary host marker is a lexical ownership declaration
findings.body: Marker creation requires an immediate OS-temp child with pacify-x- prefix, then writes expected cleanup obligations. It does not establish physical root identity or register a current resource-ledger lease. Both smoke parents allocate and prepare before entering their execution try/finally and global lease.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1557 Temporary host marker is a lexical ownership declaration.md

findings.title: Installed smoke runtime identity checks a retained marker
findings.body: The optional engine identity path validates schema, hash shape and count fields from the runtime marker; it does not recompute all engine files. Expected VSIX SHA is checked if supplied; child hashes before and after install. Parent later trusts child result rather than independently rehashing the artifact.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1558 Installed smoke runtime identity checks a retained marker.md

findings.title: Installed fixture setup can retain unreceipted work before lease acquisition
findings.body: Marked temp creation, prepare and config write precede try and runOwnedHostWorker. Missing input, setup failure or duplicate lease can leave allocated paths before a cleanup lifecycle exists. Installed fixture git calls have no checked status or timeout; development fixture checks statuses but lacks timeouts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1559 Installed fixture setup can retain unreceipted work before lease acquisition.md

findings.title: Installed host network environment is not network containment
findings.body: The child inherits HTTP/HTTPS proxies pointed at localhost port 9 plus localhost bypass and a PX deny flag. These influence cooperative clients, not direct sockets or arbitrary process access. This route uses a pre-existing owned cache; development smoke can use test-electron downloading.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1560 Installed host network environment is not network containment.md

findings.title: Installed CLI execution and host results have separate checks
findings.body: Installation has a 120 second spawnSync limit, requires exit success and an English success string, and sets shell=true on Windows. The test suite writes a receipt; child checks existence and parent parses it. A retained file alone is not newly authenticated suite execution, and parent runtime-marker verification remains distinct from exact package checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1561 Installed CLI execution and host results have separate checks.md

findings.title: Smoke success receipt precedes workspace reclamation
findings.body: Both parents publish retained host evidence before finally writes lifecycle and conditionally fs.rm when process_tree_closed_verified. They do not verify absence afterward or bind workspace_reclaimed proof into the already written success receipt. Lifecycle write failure can prevent cleanup; prior retained receipts are not invalidated at start.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1562 Smoke success receipt precedes workspace reclamation.md

findings.title: Development portable receipt and console output differ
findings.body: Development receipt recursively rewrites strings resolving to engine root as dot, while stdout prints the original parsed result. Other absolute paths remain. Source and installed smoke files execute main at module load, so importing them is not a passive inspection operation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1563 Development portable receipt and console output differ.md

findings.title: Manual installer verifies a selected hash manifest rather than signed release authority
findings.body: The installer derives expected package/version, chooses first filename-regex match in SHA256SUMS and hashes the VSIX once. It does not authenticate the manifest, enforce exact whole-line filename membership or recheck bytes immediately after install. Hash integrity and certified publication authority are distinct.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1564 Manual installer verifies a selected hash manifest rather than signed release authority.md

findings.title: Manual installed verification is version observation
findings.body: Same exact version is refused, but other versions use force including downgrade. List-extensions exit status is not checked, and final verification searches exact extension/version text without inspecting installed file hashes. No prior installation snapshot or rollback is retained by this script.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1565 Manual installed verification is version observation.md

findings.title: Uninstaller uses a fixed identity and CLI exit status
findings.body: The uninstall script hardcodes mountain-nomad-bc.pacify-x-vscode, invokes the CLI and checks exit status without a subsequent absence query. Settings retention is stated but not independently verified in this owner. No uninstall was executed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1566 Uninstaller uses a fixed identity and CLI exit status.md

findings.title: Test profile partition can tolerate a missing isolated file
findings.body: Only top-level test files are discovered. Named isolated lists are filtered by existence and the profile fails only if empty; removal of one member can reduce coverage. Unit concurrency is four, UI lanes are serial, and child executions have no explicit timeout or resource registration in this runner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1567 Test profile partition can tolerate a missing isolated file.md

findings.title: UI browser lane identity is based on executable existence
findings.body: Windows requires Edge and Chrome; macOS Chrome lane can select Chromium; Linux Chromium lane may select Google Chrome. Selection tests existence without executable version/digest. Profile contract tests invoke lane resolution, so unit execution itself depends on browser availability.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1568 UI browser lane identity is based on executable existence.md

findings.title: UI matrix receipt can be absent after a spawn error
findings.body: Nonzero lane exits are collected and remaining lanes continue, but a spawn error throws before writing the final matrix. There is no start/partial receipt. Unit/performance profiles return child status without the UI matrix receipt; inherited environment is not filtered here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1569 UI matrix receipt can be absent after a spawn error.md

findings.title: Package contract assertions are mostly lexical
findings.body: All command IDs need only occur in extension source; presence does not prove registration, reachability or correct owner. Packaging pins, check scripts, hash guard text, contribution assets, marketplace-boundary defaults and ontology fields are asserted without executing those production flows.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1570 Package contract assertions are mostly lexical.md

findings.title: Host lifecycle tests omit the reproduced outcomes
findings.body: Tests cover duplicate active lease, one stale retry, fake worker success/error/timeout and residual process matches. They do not cover two stale failures or timeout followed by exit zero. A listenerCount>=0 assertion is tautological, and two matched PID fixtures do not establish a process-count bound.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1571 Host lifecycle tests omit the reproduced outcomes.md

findings.title: Fixture packaging is deterministic within the chosen runtime inputs
findings.body: The builder fixes UTC ZIP time, sorts names, deflates at level 9, stores CRC32 and produces two fixed identities. It directly overwrites VSIX files then publishes receipt, without transactional pair replacement or rollback; compression/runtime differences are not cross-version reproducibility proof. Import executes all builds.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1572 Fixture packaging is deterministic within the chosen runtime inputs.md

findings.title: Lifecycle fixtures are inert with a declared command conflict
findings.body: v1/v2 activation returns a frozen identity/version object and deactivate does nothing; installed harness activation is empty. The v2 manifest test asserts a contributed pacifyX.openDashboard command with no activationEvents. This supplies declarative conflict input, not real extension work.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1573 Lifecycle fixtures are inert with a declared command conflict.md

findings.title: Fixture tests prove repeatability without full independent ZIP validation
findings.body: The test runs builder twice at shared generated paths, compares file hashes and checks leading ZIP signature and size range. It does not independently extract every member/CRC, install in VS Code or impose a subprocess timeout. Shared paths can race under concurrent owners.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1574 Fixture tests prove repeatability without full independent ZIP validation.md

findings.title: Publication fixture replaces cryptographic and custody verification
findings.body: Positive/negative release tests mock verify_certificate_signature and reconstruct_evidence_custody as valid. Dummy wheel/sdist/VSIX bytes and literal signature fields exercise binding and expected asset checks, not real signing, archive extraction or remote publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1575 Publication fixture replaces cryptographic and custody verification.md

findings.title: Publication negative cases distinguish mutable subjects from certificate binding
findings.body: Tests reject changed candidate identity, substituted standalone VSIX, extra draft asset and changed summary whose custody subject hash is updated without matching certificate binding. This demonstrates the selected consumer comparison despite mocked cryptographic validation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1576 Publication negative cases distinguish mutable subjects from certificate binding.md

findings.title: Template completeness schema checker implements a subset
findings.body: The local helper checks type, const/enum, pattern/minimum, required/additionalProperties and items. It does not implement references, combinators, max/unique/minItems or format; successful fixtures are not full JSON Schema validation. Historical 318-file counters and completeness/index flags are retained metadata checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1577 Template completeness schema checker implements a subset.md

findings.title: All workflow fixture routes use supplied preflight and evidence authority
findings.body: The 17-workflow loop derives effect grants from the same handler registry and supplies all-true preflight, approved for non-read effects. Cross-project resolver returns fixed accepted source/destination evidence for every reference; many payloads provide true test/rollback flags and evidence strings. These exercise real handler routing when run, not independent trusted evidence acquisition.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1578 All workflow fixture routes use supplied preflight and evidence authority.md

findings.title: Missing operational owners are subtracted twice
findings.body: The duplicate filter selects any owner count other than one, including zero, while missing selects zero separately. owned_once subtracts both lengths. An unchanged-source VM with one unowned filesystem-write control reports total=1, owned_once=-1 and the same control in missing/duplicate. Exit remains correctly nonzero.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1579 Missing operational owners are subtracted twice.md

findings.title: Control owner coverage is a declared assignment test
findings.body: Eleven hardcoded direct controls and sixteen probe functions called with empty observations contribute records. A finite effect-name set selects the denominator. Exactly one record establishes assignment uniqueness, not successful admission, input handling, effect, persistence or recovery. New effect vocabulary outside this set is excluded.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1580 Control owner coverage is a declared assignment test.md

findings.title: CSS audit scope omits cascade layer identity
findings.body: Only media/supports/container preludes contribute scope. Layer and other at-rules are omitted; selector parsing strips comments lexically and splitSelectors tracks bracket/parenthesis depth without quote state. Matching selector strings can therefore collapse semantically distinct layer/declaration contexts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1581 CSS audit scope omits cascade layer identity.md

findings.title: CSS deduplication does not compare declarations
findings.body: The rewrite removes a legacy branch whenever its normalized selector/scope key exists in modular CSS. A pure probe with legacy red text plus white background and modular blue text in another layer removes the entire legacy rule, including unmatched background. This is selector migration, not proof of equivalent computed styles.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1582 CSS deduplication does not compare declarations.md

findings.title: CSS contrast gate is a finite literal-token check
findings.body: Two named text tokens are matched as six-digit hex literals and compared against three fixed backgrounds at 4.5. It does not resolve var fallback, theme overrides, opacity, rendered background or actual component text sizes. Missing numeric baseline maxima compare as undefined and do not independently fail.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1583 CSS contrast gate is a finite literal-token check.md

findings.title: CSS rewrite publishes directly without recovery custody
findings.body: Check mode exits one if generated rewrite differs; write mode directly overwrites dashboard.css. No atomic temp/rename, backup, before/after render comparison or collision with concurrent editor writes is managed here. The audit did not run write mode.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1584 CSS rewrite publishes directly without recovery custody.md

findings.title: Efficiency scan failure leaks its measurement interval
findings.body: measureScan starts setInterval and clears it only after successful await scanEnvironmentAsync. A fake-dependency VM forced rejection and observed zero clearInterval calls. A real failure could keep its process alive; no real timer or scan was created by the probe.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1585 Efficiency scan failure leaks its measurement interval.md

findings.title: Efficiency acceptance measures narrow synthetic loads
findings.body: Profiles use 200/400/1000/2500 files over a small reused directory pattern and a fabricated Python environment. Synchronous fixture creation is outside duration measurement; passed requires duration/lag below thresholds and uncapped tree but not any heartbeat tick or expected inventory count. A hundred identical held requests tests one single-flight case, not mixed-key contention.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1586 Efficiency acceptance measures narrow synthetic loads.md

findings.title: Efficiency ownership label exceeds the local implementation
findings.body: The function creates a temporary tree and deletes it in finally without registering a marker/lease here. Scan worker ownership belongs imported discovery code; governor disposal is not in a dedicated finally if its request loop fails. Standalone report publication occurs only after measurement and cleanup succeed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1587 Efficiency ownership label exceeds the local implementation.md

findings.title: Environment refresh uses a partial on-disk extension view
findings.body: The wrapper scans user .vscode/extensions and one Windows local installation builtin path. First encountered publisher/name wins across versions, directory order is not sorted before deduplication, and isActive=false is supplied for every extension. It does not query the active host or additional portable/Insiders/remote installations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1588 Environment refresh uses a partial on-disk extension view.md

findings.title: Environment manifest bounds precede a following stat/read
findings.body: Entry directories reject symlinks, but manifest stat follows file links and a separate full read follows the 2 MiB stat check. Roots/ancestors are not physically bound. Errors silently omit manifests. Root validation only rejects filesystem root/non-directory; reason text says governed but wrapper itself performs no admission check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1589 Environment manifest bounds precede a following stat/read.md

findings.title: Outage ownership marker does not prove current disposable custody
findings.body: Outage validation resolves sibling engine and user-data paths, rejects selected links and checks marker schema/owner/classification. It does not require an OS-temp boundary, active lifecycle lease, current admission or complete inventory. Arbitrary similarly marked sibling trees satisfy this local contract.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1590 Outage ownership marker does not prove current disposable custody.md

findings.title: Engine outage publication is in-memory after rename
findings.body: begin renames the whole runtime before returning a receipt; no durable intent, startup reconciler or automatic finally exists in this helper. Only cli.py and dashboard_api.py hashes are retained, so exact restoration claim covers those bytes, not every runtime file. Caller must ensure restoration after failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1591 Engine outage publication is in-memory after rename.md

findings.title: Outage restore verification follows the effect
findings.body: Restore requires original absent, renames displaced runtime back, then checks two hashes. If a hash check fails, restored remains false but the original path now exists, so the next restore call fails its boundary guard. Parent/root identity is not revalidated immediately before either rename.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1592 Outage restore verification follows the effect.md

findings.title: Native input client checks lexical sibling paths once
findings.body: Configuration checks same parent, leaf existence/nonlink and request/results directories, but does not bind all ancestor realpaths or require token to be a directory/current owned marker. Passing options.config bypasses constructor checks. Atomic request write uses exclusive random temp then rename without fsync or failed-temp recovery.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1593 Native input client checks lexical sibling paths once.md

findings.title: Native approval keys are not bound to dialog semantics
findings.body: Cancel alone maps to Escape; any other label approves via Enter with zero/one/two Tab traversals. Correlation strings are retained but neither server nor client verifies the targeted modal label, control action or operation payload at send time. Process ownership constrains host, not intended UI decision.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1594 Native approval keys are not bound to dialog semantics.md

findings.title: Native input result is correlated but not authenticated
findings.body: Client accepts schema, exact request ID/sequence, sent status, positive foreground PID, owned_process=true, expected key count and boolean focus_recovered. It does not verify signature, process ancestry itself, timestamp freshness or result file link/size identity. A writer inside the result directory can supply these assertions; directory custody is therefore the trust boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1595 Native input result is correlated but not authenticated.md

findings.title: Native input retry and numeric bounds have limited validation
findings.body: Only the exact activation-refusal error is retried, with at most two numeric attempts and a new sequence each time. NaN/fractional option values are not explicitly rejected; NaN maximumAttempts can skip the loop and throw null. TTL is caller numeric input while server independently restricts lifetime to ten seconds.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1596 Native input retry and numeric bounds have limited validation.md

findings.title: Native input server authenticates PID birth before foreground recovery
findings.body: Requests require secret equality, sequence above in-memory last value, exact root PID, allowed key/action and current ten-second-max interval. Each accepted request compares root process creation time. Ancestry walk is bounded to 128 parents; visible owned windows are preferred, hidden owned windows can be restored, and disabled modal owners are not excluded.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1597 Native input server authenticates PID birth before foreground recovery.md

findings.title: Native input focus and expiry checks are not atomic with SendInput
findings.body: Request expiry is checked before up to 0.75 seconds of focus recovery. Root birth is checked before recovery and foreground PID is observed before SendInput; focus can change in that gap. The helper verifies sent key-event count but cannot prove the intended dialog consumed or committed the action.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1598 Native input focus and expiry checks are not atomic with SendInput.md

findings.title: Native input crash can leave an effect without durable replay protection
findings.body: last_sequence advances after successful SendInput, before result write, and resets to zero at server startup. A crash after input but before durable result can permit replay on restart. Partial SendInput raises a refusal after some key events may have occurred. Result temp name uses PID and stale temp can block publication; no fsync or write-ahead intent exists.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1599 Native input crash can leave an effect without durable replay protection.md

findings.title: Native server directory custody is checked only at startup
findings.body: Config is read once for command token comparison and reread inside serve. Request JSON files are globbed/read without per-file link, size, filename-sequence or stable identity checks; existing result files suppress requests. Stop is any stop.json existence. Config/secret shape is not independently validated by serve. These are local same-directory trust assumptions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1600 Native server directory custody is checked only at startup.md

findings.title: Fault walk counts only controls already rendered in a prior UI receipt
findings.body: The selected set intersects supported UI kinds, rendered IDs in a zero-error UI receipt and required failure/recovery policy. It binds current source manifest and emits input receipt/matrix hashes, but unrendered controls never enter this denominator. A zero eligible set can still produce a successful process.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1601 Fault walk counts only controls already rendered in a prior UI receipt.md

findings.title: Fault acceptance can use an unrelated or hidden alert
findings.body: failureContained accepts nonempty alert text even if exact control text is unchanged. The collector uses allTextContents across alert/loading/empty selectors without a visibility or control-association check. Therefore unrelated/hidden fallback text can credit containment. Disappearance and changed text also lack semantic error-state validation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1602 Fault acceptance can use an unrelated or hidden alert.md

findings.title: Recovery can credit a freshly prepared page
findings.body: After restoring original test snapshot, if the exact control is not visible, the walker calls prepare and revealControl again before checking visibility. RecoveryObserved only requires baseline/recovered visibility and zero new page errors, not original state/text, same page lifecycle or successful operation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1603 Recovery can credit a freshly prepared page.md

findings.title: Fault walk exit success does not mean every required stage passed
findings.body: Final exit is nonzero only for pageErrors or thrown exceptions. Missing failure/recovery stages and unattempted controls are reported but do not independently fail. Browser/pages close in finally, while receipt is published only after all workers finish; an early exception leaves no partial receipt.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1604 Fault walk exit success does not mean every required stage passed.md

findings.title: Operational bootstrap retains ready receipt after later failure
findings.body: The bootstrap awaits activation, actual command registration and command return, writes ready with wx, then waits up to fifteen minutes for a sentinel. Catch writes failed only if receipt does not exist, so release timeout leaves the earlier ready record. Activation/command awaits have no local timeout and sentinel contents/identity are not checked.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1605 Operational bootstrap retains ready receipt after later failure.md

findings.title: Native and fault helper tests use synthetic effects
findings.body: Native client tests manufacture sent/refused JSON; Python tests use parent maps/window fakes and construct Win32 bindings but do not send keys. Fault tests simulate DOM/keyboard events and selected command helpers; direct element.click fallback is accepted. They demonstrate logic contracts, not current installed-host operation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1606 Native and fault helper tests use synthetic effects.md

findings.title: Native Python test portability is constrained before skip checks
findings.body: The helper imports WinDLL and WINFUNCTYPE at module import, while the test imports the module before its Windows-only test decorator. On platforms lacking these ctypes names, collection fails before the skip. ABI checks alone do not prove foreground or SendInput effects.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1607 Native Python test portability is constrained before skip checks.md

findings.title: Outage tests verify only selected happy and refusal paths
findings.body: Tests create real temporary trees, confirm ordinary/idempotent restoration and reject mismatched token root or linked runtime. Link test can skip for host permissions. They do not cover crash after displacement, restore hash mismatch, root substitution or unrelated runtime-file drift.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1608 Outage tests verify only selected happy and refusal paths.md

findings.title: MCP mutation fixture uses real signing with a narrow negative set
findings.body: Generated approval keys and launch authority are exercised to replace forged actor/session/harness inputs. Other-project replay, changed token and unadmitted operation are rejected. No expiry, mutated signature, changed trusted key or process transport case is asserted in this file.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1609 MCP mutation fixture uses real signing with a narrow negative set.md

findings.title: Team Fabric test claims are narrower than full registry nonmutation
findings.body: Tests hash a three-file pack, count two entities and one collision, use one async worker and stage a renamed candidate. canonical_registry_mutated=false is asserted from receipt without before/after registry byte comparison. Worker adapter readiness/authentication is based on supplied host flags and labels, not a real login attempt.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1610 Team Fabric test claims are narrower than full registry nonmutation.md

findings.title: Late-card worker combines physical probes with injected authority
findings.body: Physical occupancy/link probes and independent framed hash are meaningful when the worker runs; inspection denial is injected and external-authenticated allocation uses supplied digest strings. Scaffold overwrites registry files under caller root, promotion calls approved=true and no local disposable-root gate exists. completed aggregates booleans but does not set nonzero exit on false.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1611 Late-card worker combines physical probes with injected authority.md

findings.title: Late-card framed hash and rollback checks cover distinct moments
findings.body: Independent hash is computed after rollback against the earlier promotion hash, alongside exact first-projection byte restoration. Preserved provenance is checked at draft/validation/admission/promotion/projection stages. Authenticated committed transaction is verified for second promotion; rollback_projection_authenticated itself compares path sets, with receipt authentication owned elsewhere.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1612 Late-card framed hash and rollback checks cover distinct moments.md

findings.title: Studio crash worker covers one explicit publication boundary
findings.body: The helper monkeypatches _atomic_bytes to os._exit(91) before first skill-index projection in promotion or rollback. A separate recovery command verifies a signed receipt and computes canonical tree hash, but prints expected canonical version without reading/comparing canonical manifest version here. Parent must check actual crash exit and recovery details; all crash points are not covered.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1613 Studio crash worker covers one explicit publication boundary.md

findings.title: Audit bundle wrapper delegates completion to clean export
findings.body: The wrapper requires existing output directory and VSIX, checks package version, calls clean_source_export and checks exit code before hashing resulting archive and writing sidecar. It has no own subprocess timeout or rollback for sidecar failure; wrapper valid=true depends on the child contract rather than independently reopening all archive evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1614 Audit bundle wrapper delegates completion to clean export.md

findings.title: Deep host tool input bypasses target checking
findings.body: visit returns any value at depth greater than eight without examining it. An unchanged selected-function VM with fake filesystem rejects a top-level C:/outside/secret path but retains the same target nested nine times and records no validated target pointers. No tool or filesystem effect was invoked.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1615 Deep host tool input bypasses target checking.md

findings.title: Host tool policy constrains declared inputs rather than actual implementation effects
findings.body: The owner unions all grant effects and scope roots, rejects effects outside read/inspect/query/observe and requires non-billable, deny/loopback-only and no credential namespace. Recognized path/URI strings are checked and rewritten to physical paths, but the tool implementation receives no OS/network sandbox from this function. Undeclared internal effects remain outside these input checks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1616 Host tool policy constrains declared inputs rather than actual implementation effects.md

findings.title: Host input scope relies on heuristic locator discovery and a pathname interval
findings.body: Keys ending in path/file/folder/directory/root/cwd/target/source/resource/uri/url or path-shaped strings trigger scope checks; ordinary strings may pass unchanged. Existing ancestor realpath is joined with nonexistent suffix. A path can change after check and before tool use. These are input normalization boundaries, not stable opened handles.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1617 Host input scope relies on heuristic locator discovery and a pathname interval.md

findings.title: Live tool interface hash is observed rather than matched to admitted bytes
findings.body: Registered tools are matched by name and required to expose an object schema; canonical name/description/schema are hashed before model execution. The digest is placed in receipts but not compared to an expected admitted interface digest, and registered interface is not re-read before each invokeTool.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1618 Live tool interface hash is observed rather than matched to admitted bytes.md

findings.title: Exact model identity checks are explicit but initial calls precede the deadline
findings.body: The route must contain exact model ID, pacify-local must bind exact vendor, and selected ID/vendor/family/version are checked. selectChatModels and initial countTokens occur before starting the bounded request timer. A stalled initial host API call is therefore outside that local deadline.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1619 Exact model identity checks are explicit but initial calls precede the deadline.md

findings.title: Host model output budget is checked after full stream accumulation
findings.body: Each stream is consumed into responseText, streamedText and responseParts before countTokens compares accumulated output to a clamped cap. Tool-call argument content is not counted as responseText output tokens. Requested maxOutputTokens itself is constructed before clamp. A noncooperative/large stream can exceed memory/time expectations before the check.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1620 Host model output budget is checked after full stream accumulation.md

findings.title: Host model cancellation is cooperative rather than an enforced race
findings.body: The deadline cancels a token and wall time is checked between rounds. Awaited host token-count/request/invoke calls and stream iteration are not raced against a rejecting timeout. Cancellation requested before listener registration is not explicitly inspected at that point. The host API must honor the linked token for timely completion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1621 Host model cancellation is cooperative rather than an enforced race.md

findings.title: Host output schema is a prompt here and a downstream contract elsewhere
findings.body: The prompt includes an output schema, but this helper parses final text or wraps invalid JSON as text and non-object values as value. It returns completed without JSON Schema validation locally. Authoritative acceptance belongs complete-host-run and its runtime consumer, not this return label.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1622 Host output schema is a prompt here and a downstream contract elsewhere.md

findings.title: Tool call receipts are collected in memory before final host completion
findings.body: At most eight requested calls are permitted and each exact binding is policy-checked. Started receipt is appended before invoke; failed invocation annotates error and propagates all collected receipts. Completed input/result hashes are unkeyed observations held in memory until backend completion; no per-call durable journal is written here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1623 Tool call receipts are collected in memory before final host completion.md

findings.title: Prepared host run can outlive initial webview failure
findings.body: The backend prepares a durable run before the running result is posted. That post occurs before creating activeHostRuns cancellation state and before the try wrapping model execution. A disposed/erroring webview can leave the prepared run without executing/completing it through this local branch; external reconciliation remains necessary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1624 Prepared host run can outlive initial webview failure.md

findings.title: Host completion publication can fail after model execution
findings.body: After model work, the controller signs and submits complete-host-run and only then posts terminal result and refreshes. Failure in signing, backend completion, reply or refresh follows already observed model/tool work. The terminal run result omits the original requestId, while initial running result includes it.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1625 Host completion publication can fail after model execution.md

findings.title: External host run cancellation is classified differently from progress cancellation
findings.body: Progress UI cancellation sets hostCancelled=true and cancels token; pause/cancel/stop routes first call backend then cancel activeHostRuns token without setting that local boolean. A resulting thrown model error can be labelled failed by this helper rather than cancelled. Backend run-state reconciliation may impose the final state separately.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1626 External host run cancellation is classified differently from progress cancellation.md

findings.title: Chat participant model execution is a separate authority and budget route
findings.body: Status/skills/context commands do not invoke a model. Ordinary prompt uses request.model supplied by VS Code, checks input against maxInputTokens, streams text and records provider activity as effect observe. It does not call the Studio model selector/tool policy/output budget or a local timeout, and does not consult the imported provider policy report here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1627 Chat participant model execution is a separate authority and budget route.md

findings.title: Host asset identity omits modular styles and the shipped host bundle
findings.body: extensionAssetIdentity includes dashboard JS, src JS excluding extension.bundle.js, legacy dashboard CSS, sidebar assets and action inventory. The loaded modular media/styles files and generated bundle bytes are absent from asset digest. This host/source identity is selected-source parity, not complete installed-package byte identity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1628 Host asset identity omits modular styles and the shipped host bundle.md

findings.title: Package hash is emitted but excluded from host/source match
findings.body: identityMatches compares version, asset hash, asset protocol and message schema, not package_sha256. Version comes from require(packagePath), potentially cached, while hash reads current disk. Equal selected assets/protocols can still yield a match across other package metadata changes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1629 Package hash is emitted but excluded from host/source match.md

findings.title: Workspace selection and canonical memory root are distinct
findings.body: workspaceRoot uses first open folder or engine fallback; settings.workspaceRoot resolves separately for canonical memory. Dashboard state keys lowercase paths on every platform and keep eight entries. Case-distinct POSIX workspaces can share a state key. The activation coordination watcher is bound once to its initial root.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1630 Workspace selection and canonical memory root are distinct.md

findings.title: Host context cache does not carry a workspace key
findings.body: Five-minute hostContextCache and governor key host-context are shared inside activation. Current environment is also reused through currentEnvironment || readEnvironmentInventory(root). Configuration/extension events clear context, but there is no workspace-folder-change handler in this file. A changed first workspace can reuse context/environment until another invalidation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1631 Host context cache does not carry a workspace key.md

findings.title: Portable context snapshot retains absolute locators
findings.body: The named portable snapshot includes repository fsPath and environment current path. Its memory_refs branch dereferences workspace.uri when coordination paths exist, although workspace may be absent under engine fallback. Guarantee flags describe content choices but do not establish locator portability.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1632 Portable context snapshot retains absolute locators.md

findings.title: Opening cached context does not force a fresh read
findings.body: openContextSnapshot uses currentContextEnvelope when present. continueWithCodex sets the objective-bearing envelope, opens it, then publishSnapshot(false) can replace global context with cached host-context envelope. The displayed document and later global context can differ; cancellation clears only local context, not an external Codex session.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1633 Opening cached context does not force a fresh read.md

findings.title: Snapshot composition catches only the canonical bridge snapshot call
findings.body: Memory lease ensure runs before try; host-context, enterprise initialization, environment read, identity hashing and sidebar publication can throw afterward. currentSnapshot is assigned before composition completes. The promise finally resets joining state but does not roll back partial shared fields or guarantee an error snapshot to all callers.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1634 Snapshot composition catches only the canonical bridge snapshot call.md

findings.title: Forced snapshot refresh joins or follows the current publication
findings.body: A forced caller waits for an in-flight nonforced promise then requests a forced pass; ordinary callers share one promise. Each awaiting caller posts to its own target afterward. Rejection of the first promise prevents that forced retry path. There is no workspace generation binding around assigning shared currentSnapshot.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1635 Forced snapshot refresh joins or follows the current publication.md

findings.title: Validation cache is keyed to snapshot identity at publication time
findings.body: Validation runs against current configured engine root, then stores result under validationCacheKey(currentSnapshot) after completion. If snapshot/root changes while validation runs, this local code does not compare the validated source identity with that later snapshot key. Cached result is reused without a TTL in this owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1636 Validation cache is keyed to snapshot identity at publication time.md

findings.title: Selected host action receipts are latest in-memory observations
findings.body: durableHostActionTypes controls storage in activeRuntime.lastHostActionRequest/Result, not a persistent journal. Only one latest request/result survives; no per-request idempotency check or history exists. Setting a terminal result before reply preserves it across later delivery failure, but extension restart loses this local memory.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1637 Selected host action receipts are latest in-memory observations.md

findings.title: Graph rendered acknowledgement is client-supplied state
findings.body: The graphRendered branch directly replaces activeRuntime.dashboardGraph with supplied request ID, view and counts after general message validation. It does not correlate to current delivered graph request/result or verify actual DOM itself. Query-delivered status and client-rendered acknowledgement are different evidence sources.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1638 Graph rendered acknowledgement is client-supplied state.md

findings.title: Canonical memory setup can be partially applied before cancellation
findings.body: Workspace initialization and discovery can write before project-name/selection dialogs; project creation/activation and workspace config update are separate effects. Later cancellation or memory/refresh failure does not compensate earlier writes. Detach clears workspace configuration but does not itself show an explicit lease-release call in this branch; lease controller handles subsequent state.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1639 Canonical memory setup can be partially applied before cancellation.md

findings.title: Enterprise policy toggle has two separate persistence effects
findings.body: The toggle updates VS Code workspace billable.enabled, then writes enterprise execution policy. Configuration change listener can also write policy. Failure after configuration update leaves the earlier effect in place; a returned operation error is not evidence of rollback.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1640 Enterprise policy toggle has two separate persistence effects.md

findings.title: Owned-harness flags select multiple approval shortcuts
findings.body: Two PX_OWNED flags switch confirmations from modal, choose fixture paths, bypass selected Studio/memory/toggle approvals and write exports into fixture paths. Studio setup optionally requires a physical marker when exercising approval. These test-only routes are controlled by inherited environment; they are not independent user-presence proof.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1641 Owned-harness flags select multiple approval shortcuts.md

findings.title: Environment lifecycle uses typed-target UI approval rather than another host prompt
findings.body: Unlike native extension install/update/uninstall/rollback branches, environment execute and restore directly pass approved=true with exactTarget from the message to their manager. The dashboard owns typed target/acknowledgement interaction, while manager owns token/identity checks. These are distinct approval boundaries.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1642 Environment lifecycle uses typed-target UI approval rather than another host prompt.md

findings.title: Lifecycle refresh can hide a completed manager receipt
findings.body: Native install/update/uninstall/rollback and environment move/restore await refreshEnvironment after action but before posting result. If discovery/publication fails, outer operationError follows the completed effect and the manager receipt may not reach that webview. Recovery should inspect authoritative manager state rather than infer no effect from reply error.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1643 Lifecycle refresh can hide a completed manager receipt.md

findings.title: Enablement observation explicitly records temporal association only
findings.body: A single pending handoff with five-minute expiry is consumed by next extension-change event, then refreshed only if a view is visible. The emitted receipt says temporal-pending-handoff-only, enablement_observed=null and activation_is_not_enablement=true. Multiple concurrent handoffs overwrite this single slot; arbitrary extension change can consume it.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1644 Enablement observation explicitly records temporal association only.md

findings.title: Studio create origin trust has explicit bounds and detach semantics
findings.body: Active create map rejects duplicate kind/request and more than 64 operations. Host-origin proof ownership, initial physical absence, source reauthentication and postcommit warning handling are delegated explicitly. Closing panel disposes origin trust and marks create operations detached; it does not cancel already committed or running work.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1645 Studio create origin trust has explicit bounds and detach semantics.md

findings.title: Editor source token can be consumed before a later failed recheck
findings.body: Skill next-version consumes source-selection token, then verifies requested identity/version, rereads package, checks hashes/provenance and asks backend for allocation. A mismatch/read/backend failure can consume the token without producing allocation, requiring new selection. Catalog lookups are limited to first 100 matching results and require exact uniqueness.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1646 Editor source token can be consumed before a later failed recheck.md

findings.title: Dashboard readiness is distinct from successful rendered snapshot
findings.body: ready resolves panel readiness before awaiting initial snapshot publication. openDashboard waits at most fifteen seconds, then forces snapshot/deep link. Timeout throws without disposing panel here; later callers can await same ready promise. Panel disposal releases origin and detaches creates, while other asynchronous handlers may continue and encounter delivery errors.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1647 Dashboard readiness is distinct from successful rendered snapshot.md

findings.title: Activation transaction cannot own values before argument evaluation finishes
findings.body: Output channel/publisher/catalog are created before their first transaction.own call. Multiple registrations are passed as function arguments to one own call; if a later argument throws, earlier-created disposables from that expression may not yet be registered with transaction. Explicit rollback helps only resources already enrolled.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1648 Activation transaction cannot own values before argument evaluation finishes.md

findings.title: Startup zero-effect counters are declarations rather than measurements
findings.body: startup records elapsed activation time but subprocesses_started=0, discovery_started=false and project_writes=0 are hardcoded. Canonical memory lease start and listener/provider registration precede this assignment; imported owners determine actual deferred behavior. These constants are not independently observed effect counts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1649 Startup zero-effect counters are declarations rather than measurements.md

findings.title: Deactivation clears some state but leaves other module globals
findings.body: Lifecycle dispose clears selected timers/listeners/bridge/publisher; deactivate clears runtime/environment/lifecycle fields. It does not clear currentSnapshot, currentContextEnvelope, panel, dashboard view cache or activeHostRuns in this function. VS Code subscription disposal and process exit may close them elsewhere; same-module reactivation should not assume all state reset.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1650 Deactivation clears some state but leaves other module globals.md

findings.title: MCP definition creation is distinct from a verified server invocation
findings.body: Providing definitions signs a new project/session authority and creates public JWK file only if absent. Existing path contents/link identity are not checked here before reuse. Server is launched by VS Code from generated bundle with explicit identity/env and cwd; registration remains registered_unverified until invocation evidence exists.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1651 MCP definition creation is distinct from a verified server invocation.md

findings.title: Configuration fault once markers differ from host-action markers
findings.body: Configuration fault injection only checks marker existence and does not consume it, so a .once filename can repeatedly fail until external removal. Host-action fault injection checks plain-file JSON schema/operation/effect, unlinks then throws. Both routes are gated by owned-host flags but implement different failure lifetimes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1652 Configuration fault once markers differ from host-action markers.md

findings.title: Working draft recovery is exact-bound local state, not authority
findings.body: The dashboard stores editable overlay and a source binding, then reloads the exact catalog predecessor and host allocation before reopening. Persisted local view state takes precedence when nonempty; a source/candidate mismatch preserves the overlay rather than applying it. Canonical JSON buffer is sliced to 524288 characters, not bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1653 Working draft recovery is exact-bound local state, not authority.md

findings.title: Editor presentation retries measure presence rather than complete visibility
findings.body: Accepted editor presentation carries identity/version token and is checked by microtask, animation frame and 100/500ms timers. Matching DOM controls and baseline are inspected, not a rendered screenshot. Timers are guarded by presentation identity rather than cancelled as a group.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1654 Editor presentation retries measure presence rather than complete visibility.md

findings.title: Save detachment preserves host commit ownership
findings.body: Close while a save is active records a detached request and sends detach rather than release of proof owned by the host commit. Matching detached result refreshes catalog and history but does not clear or replace the current editor. The detached request set is bounded to 64, so very late results can become unmatched.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1655 Save detachment preserves host commit ownership.md

findings.title: Some rejected editor replies remain pending without a timeout
findings.body: Agent/workflow editor replies require exact request, catalog record, identity, version, revision/content hash and allocation proof. A matching but malformed reply releases incoming proof and leaves the original request pending. No timeout clears this local pending request; explicit closure or later result is needed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1656 Some rejected editor replies remain pending without a timeout.md

findings.title: Information modal metadata changes before replacement is accepted
findings.body: showInformationModal assigns shared title/record/copy fields before showModal checks whether a live Studio editor may be replaced. A refused replacement can therefore update shared metadata while leaving prior DOM present. Separately, operationalCardResult and operationalInventoryResult explicitly closeModal before showing uncorrelated details, which can detach a newer in-flight save.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1657 Information modal metadata changes before replacement is accepted.md

findings.title: Workflow approval can be attached to a different current session
findings.body: The pending approval records workflow ID/version, but response matching compares only requestId, nodeId and nonempty approval_id. Later code assigns to any current workflow studioSession. An unchanged listener in a VM accepts approval for workflow A and writes it into current workflow B. This is transient UI contamination; backend approval capabilities remain separately authoritative.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1658 Workflow approval can be attached to a different current session.md

findings.title: Studio lifecycle result matching is uneven across operations
findings.body: Run queries match request/kind/operation and expected run ID; skill lifecycle matches subject/version; preview binds exact subject/version and effects_executed=false. Generic agent test/admit/register-authority and start/run result paths do not have the same pending request matching. They can update history/catalog/modal after current session changes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1659 Studio lifecycle result matching is uneven across operations.md

findings.title: Generic lifecycle success accepts an empty object
findings.body: Operation-specific checks explicitly require passed/admitted/eligible/run identity for many operations. The fallback merely rejects failure words in status/state/decision, so an empty object for recover is accepted. VM probe confirms this; it does not establish recovery or durable outcome correctness.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1660 Generic lifecycle success accepts an empty object.md

findings.title: Workflow trace remains an identity projection
findings.body: The browser trace uses workflow/version/run identity, with a hash optional unless both compared records provide one. Node receipts are placed by node ID, so the final duplicate replaces earlier entries. Missing receipt list can clear node state. This projection does not validate event chains/signatures.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1661 Workflow trace remains an identity projection.md

findings.title: Workflow zero positions and edge positions disagree
findings.body: Node layout preserves zero using nullish fallback, while drawWorkflowCanvasEdges uses position.x || 40 and position.y || 40. An inert DOM probe produces source endpoint M 218 76 for a node at 0,0 instead of 178,36. The source discrepancy affects visual connection alignment.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1662 Workflow zero positions and edge positions disagree.md

findings.title: Layout rule cap is per call rather than global retained ownership
findings.body: Constructable stylesheet applies fixed numeric clamped attributes, reducing CSS injection through those attributes. However its 2048 limit counts this apply invocation; retained rules for still-connected elements can exceed that across partial calls. querySelectorAll materializes candidates before the cap is applied.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1663 Layout rule cap is per call rather than global retained ownership.md

findings.title: Graph virtualization hides eagerly created nodes
findings.body: materializeGraphGeometry creates all node foreignObjects and minimap dots before frame processing. Virtualization chunks 280 frames and 420 edges per animation frame but does not defer DOM allocation. The selected node is forced visible even outside the viewport; an edge crossing the viewport can be hidden if both endpoint frames are hidden.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1664 Graph virtualization hides eagerly created nodes.md

findings.title: Graph rendered acknowledgement does not prove paint completion
findings.body: reportGraphRender counts DOM elements and calculates node rectangles from model positions. Visible count prefers non-virtualized frames, including forced selected frames. The 250ms fallback prepares geometry and reports without awaiting frame chunks; a suspended renderer can therefore report before virtualization finishes. Host stores supplied counts as rendered without independent request correlation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1665 Graph rendered acknowledgement does not prove paint completion.md

findings.title: Full graph pagination has no aggregate termination guard
findings.body: Each request has 12-second timeout and max page sizes, but load-all repeats while backend has_more is true. No maximum total pages, aggregate deadline, repeated-cursor rejection or accumulated-node cap is enforced here. Merge matches only full mode and view, not snapshot hash or full filter identity.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1666 Full graph pagination has no aggregate termination guard.md

findings.title: Late graph success is accepted after local timeout
findings.body: The 12-second timeout clears graphPending and renders an error but retains graphRequestId. A later result with that same ID passes the response guard, clears the error and replaces data. Timeout is therefore a display deadline, not cancellation or terminal rejection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1667 Late graph success is accepted after local timeout.md

findings.title: Knowledge browse can overwrite a newer browser view
findings.body: requestKnowledge and learning operations share kind knowledge without request tracking. Any knowledge browse response replaces knowledgeData; an unchanged listener VM accepts an obsolete request result. Environment subject results and several detail modals likewise lack exact request-generation checks, unlike catalog/memory/activity queries.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1668 Knowledge browse can overwrite a newer browser view.md

findings.title: Snapshot updates do not invalidate all subject caches
findings.body: Snapshot clears memory only when canonical retrieval_ready becomes false. Settings/coordination may be retained if absent and environment/catalog/knowledge projections are not invalidated by a snapshot root/revision identifier here. A new snapshot can coexist with older lazily loaded details.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1669 Snapshot updates do not invalidate all subject caches.md

findings.title: Pending host actions are bounded memory with latest snapshot replay
findings.body: Browser retains at most 64 pending host actions and matches direct reply operation/request. Snapshot can replay latest host request/result into globals and clear a matching pending item. These globals and host fields are memory, not a persistent complete action journal; no per-action timeout exists here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1670 Pending host actions are bounded memory with latest snapshot replay.md

findings.title: A global search debounce crosses independent surfaces
findings.body: Activity, memory query/project/source and catalog search share one searchTimer. Typing on another surface before 250ms cancels the earlier scheduled query; callbacks retain the old input object. This is a single browser scheduling lane, not independent surface work.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1671 A global search debounce crosses independent surfaces.md

findings.title: UI readiness and metric labels have limited evidence domains
findings.body: readinessLiveBlockers checks source identity, MCP runtime verification, invalid available map, runtime failures and stale environment; unavailable environment is not itself a blocker there. Coordination summary counts claims array and board selects first task claim without filtering active lifecycle. Unknown Git uses its local fallback presentation; these values are not certification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1672 UI readiness and metric labels have limited evidence domains.md

findings.title: Browser authority declarations require downstream admission
findings.body: Workflow new bindings/grants are initialized with state admitted and human-approval reference strings; agent additions use candidate. These are editable payload declarations. Register-authority/admission/backend checks remain distinct from setting those JSON fields.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1673 Browser authority declarations require downstream admission.md

findings.title: Candidate JSON changes need explicit application
findings.body: Typing canonical JSON marks draft dirty and saves a buffer, but studioEditorPayload uses structured draft while kind matches. Only studioApplyJson parses, normalizes and applies the text; predecessor-bound identity/version change is rejected. Save can therefore use the last applied structured definition, not newly typed raw text.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1674 Candidate JSON changes need explicit application.md

findings.title: Workflow local graph edits use closed typed semantics
findings.body: Connection checks require existing exact ports, equal data type, no self edge, duplicate, second input driver or cycle. Supported task adapters are explicit deterministic operations, not arbitrary agent execution. Retyping a node clears all incident edges; removing a binding leaves references for later validation rather than silently rebinding them.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1675 Workflow local graph edits use closed typed semantics.md

findings.title: Human workflow sequence may be a synthesized presentation
findings.body: When declared steps are absent workflowHuman synthesizes a sequential display from the skill list. ImportCatalogDefinition creates an independent basic workflow and preserves original source_definition/source_import; it does not compile all original workflow semantics. Explicit admission and operation remain separate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1676 Human workflow sequence may be a synthesized presentation.md

findings.title: Legacy agent topology is separate from the active graph renderer
findings.body: upgradeLegacyAgentTopology and drawLegacyAgentTopologyEdges remain defined, but the modern upgradeAgentTopology route uses typed builder graph. Legacy edge selector expects data-agent-section while legacy created nodes use data-legacy-agent-section. The mismatch is a dormant helper boundary, not evidence that modern graph edges fail.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1677 Legacy agent topology is separate from the active graph renderer.md

findings.title: Agent model selection and local graph status can diverge from final authority
findings.body: Model provider change resets model_id/version to auto, while host execution requires an exact model. updateAgentValidationBox always replaces persisted-verified with working/Python-compile-required, even after validation-only updates. These labels describe browser state; final model route and compiled graph are backend-owned.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1678 Agent model selection and local graph status can diverge from final authority.md

findings.title: Studio error and cancellation re-enable save without rerunning all local checks
findings.body: studioDraftCancelled and createStudioDraft error set save.disabled=false directly. During an in-flight save other editor input handlers can also recompute availability. The browser button is not an exactly-once commit gate; submit revalidates and host create coordinator owns immutable occupancy and trust.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1679 Studio error and cancellation re-enable save without rerunning all local checks.md

findings.title: Knowledge proposals distinguish cached canonical update from new candidate
findings.body: Single cached matching canonical head supplies supersedes_sha256 and duplicate or malformed heads block. No cached match produces a proposal without predecessor. Current canonical verification must therefore occur downstream when the browse cache is partial or stale. The UI-provided bare source hash is evidence input, not proof of a new claim.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1680 Knowledge proposals distinguish cached canonical update from new candidate.md

findings.title: Learning forms record evidence assertions rather than independently running trials
findings.body: Observation captures outcome/metric/environment/evidence; pattern and hypothesis freeze declarations; trial records selected winner; research includes independent flags; final validation/reuse are explicit host requests. UI labels explain separate verify/approve/promote and non-destructive decay. Backend sources, confidence and dependency gates determine whether claims are accepted.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1681 Learning forms record evidence assertions rather than independently running trials.md

findings.title: Native lifecycle handoff has differentiated result claims
findings.body: Install/update/uninstall/rollback preview and response generally match exact pending request/action and token/target; enablement explicitly reports temporal observation rather than proof. Conflict resolution routes into a new separate governed install/uninstall/enablement preview. Conflict preview renderer does not test allowed here, so manager token authority remains essential.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1682 Native lifecycle handoff has differentiated result claims.md

findings.title: Environment action UI is exact-target gated but response identity is weaker
findings.body: showModal clears typed environment target and execute checks exact text plus consumer acknowledgement. Environment preview/result/restore messages have no pending request correlation; result-type captions assert moved/restored without checking status fields locally. Host manager remains authoritative. This audit reads those paths and performs no quarantine, restore or deletion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1683 Environment action UI is exact-target gated but response identity is weaker.md

findings.title: Coordination forms and release have different request evidence
findings.body: Plan parses pipe-separated declarations and sends numeric budgets; claim/progress/reconcile use host validation. Release uniquely requires a reason of ten characters, explicit checkbox, request ID and task-bound returned authorization. Other coordination results set complete without operation-specific matching here. Portable memory remains proposed/non-canonical.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1684 Coordination forms and release have different request evidence.md

findings.title: Deep links can use positional subtask fallback
findings.body: The resolver first tries exact task/subtask identity, then extracts digits from a dotted suffix and indexes a parent subtask list. A stale or noncanonical identifier can therefore display a positional sibling. The record is a read-only snapshot projection, not task identity authorization.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1685 Deep links can use positional subtask fallback.md

findings.title: Keyboard and frame liveness preserve partial rather than full visual guarantees
findings.body: Graph focus trap filters visible elements; modal focus trap does not. Graph arrow focus walks all graph-node DOM entries, including virtualized frames. Shared render defers while any modal exists, and ready posts immediately after render rather than after data, geometry or paint completion.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1686 Keyboard and frame liveness preserve partial rather than full visual guarantees.md

findings.title: Full walk completion trusts the complete-chain aggregate
findings.body: evaluateOperationalWalk checks control count/attempts and accepts complete_interaction_chains plus recovered boundaries at least equal to denominator. It does not recompute complete stages, inspect ordinary control errors, require rendered/visible, enforce unique IDs or cap inflated complete counts. Pure probe returns completed for one attempted control with empty stages and errors when aggregate says one complete.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1687 Full walk completion trusts the complete-chain aggregate.md

findings.title: Source verified is a supplied status at this evaluator boundary
findings.body: Explicit mismatch always blocks and unknown/reported-match are distinguished. However verified is accepted from source_identity.state without checking digests, method or artifact bytes. Upstream identity producer and downstream artifact validation remain separate proof owners.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1688 Source verified is a supplied status at this evaluator boundary.md

findings.title: Issue deduplication keeps the first blocking decision
findings.body: Issue key includes source/code/context/message, but not severity or blocking. Duplicate occurrence/recovered fields merge while first blocking/severity/details remain. Probe supplies a nonblocking issue then the same blocking issue and retains nonblocking. Truncating message/context before key creation can also merge distinct long observations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1689 Issue deduplication keeps the first blocking decision.md
