findings.title: Nonobject additional issues are silently discarded
findings.body: dedupeIssues skips values that are not objects. The isolated child pushes native helper termination/exit failures as strings, so those explicit failure signals vanish. A pure evaluator probe with the actual helper failure string returns completed. Other independently classified failures may still block, but these strings cannot.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1690 Nonobject additional issues are silently discarded.md

findings.title: Prior walker profile failures are lost during child recomputation
findings.body: The walker passes profileFailures as additionalIssues into its first status evaluation and stores status_truth. The isolated child reads that receipt but calls evaluateOperationalWalk again with only normalized processIssues. The evaluator ignores prior status_truth. It accepts expected nonzero exit derived from the original status. A pure reproduction changes original incomplete with a retained profile failure to completed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1691 Prior walker profile failures are lost during child recomputation.md

findings.title: Launcher ignores contradictory child terminal status
findings.body: evaluateLauncherTerminal copies child issues and checks owner tree/worker closure. It does not require recognized status schema, terminal completed, scope_complete or operationally_complete. A child object saying failed with an empty issue list is recomputed completed in the probe.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1692 Launcher ignores contradictory child terminal status.md

findings.title: Focused completion is promoted in the nested launcher flag
findings.body: A successful focused walk correctly returns operationally_complete=false and scope_complete=true. Launcher recomputation returns operationally_complete=true whenever no issues remain, losing that distinction. The outer report separately sets full_operational_completion_claimed=false for focused profiles, leaving conflicting nested scopes for consumers to interpret.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1693 Focused completion is promoted in the nested launcher flag.md

findings.title: Host-boundary focused profile accepts no interaction stages
findings.body: The host-boundary predicate uses Object.values(chain).every with no required key set; an empty object satisfies it. It checks record count, rendered/attempted and errors but not exact IDs/uniqueness. Probe with one rendered attempted empty-chain record returns completed. Its test positive case supplies only two stages.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1694 Host-boundary focused profile accepts no interaction stages.md

findings.title: Generic focused probe counts do not prove exact control identities
findings.body: completeOwnedProbe requires positive eligible count, equal records length and thirteen stage states, but does not require unique IDs, admitted eligible ID set, visibility or stage evidence references. Most stages may be not_applicable without a reason. Error-indicators is stronger: two exact unique IDs and nonempty evidence for every named stage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1695 Generic focused probe counts do not prove exact control identities.md

findings.title: Focused configuration and Studio lifecycle predicates omit important denominators
findings.body: Configuration accepts any nonempty attempted error-free records without checking eligible_control_count equality. Studio lifecycle requires each kind with one or more valid operations, but no exact lifecycle operation sequence. The positive test deliberately uses only an inspect operation for each kind and still completes the scoped predicate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1696 Focused configuration and Studio lifecycle predicates omit important denominators.md

findings.title: Focused builder evidence is a selected flag contract
findings.body: Builder scope requires interaction_complete, durability.verified, closed modal, no saved candidate/runtime execution and two attempted control IDs. It does not independently inspect malformed JSON rejection, recovery evidence, all builder controls or errors array despite its explanatory text. These are producer-trusted observations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1697 Focused builder evidence is a selected flag contract.md

findings.title: Surface capture checks labels rather than image bytes
findings.body: Surface capture requires exactly eighteen named records, navigation_active, matching capture surface and first/deep screenshot status captured. It does not read screenshot files, inspect image hashes, timing, visibility or dimensions. The test uses status-only screenshot objects and is a predicate fixture, not rendered evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1698 Surface capture checks labels rather than image bytes.md

findings.title: Recovered refusal coverage is distinct and less complete than execution coverage
findings.body: Ten exact control IDs can count as accepted coverage while terminal remains skipped_requires_authority, with rendered/visible/attempted, four nonempty explanation strings, failure/recovery observed and at least one noncomplete stage. Full stage set/evidence/unique IDs are not required. Stage Map takes last duplicate; nonarray errors are ignored in this helper.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1699 Recovered refusal coverage is distinct and less complete than execution coverage.md

findings.title: Process output normalization leaves unknown closure to callers
findings.body: normalizeProcessOutput only emits closure issue for explicit false, and only checks exit if walkerExit exists. Missing exit/closure yields zero issues in probe. Generic error-word matching examines stderr rather than stdout, while selected token/unresponsive patterns examine both. Launcher applies stricter explicit-true closure checks separately.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1700 Process output normalization leaves unknown closure to callers.md

findings.title: Diagnostic exceptions are exact lexical policy, not independent attribution
findings.body: Four console patterns and paired Windows Jump List output are downgraded as external warnings. They depend on message/location text rather than authenticated origin. A responsive line anywhere marks unresponsive observation recovered without chronological/PID pairing, but unresponsiveness correctly remains blocking.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1701 Diagnostic exceptions are exact lexical policy, not independent attribution.md

findings.title: Terminal severity precedence is source-driven
findings.body: Blocking process/page/console wins failed, source_identity/extension_host wins blocked, other blocking sources yield incomplete. Severity error itself does not force failed; profile errors become incomplete. Exit codes map completed/failed/incomplete/blocked to 0/1/2/3, so consumers must preserve both scope and issue provenance.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1702 Terminal severity precedence is source-driven.md

findings.title: Bootstrap completion is a narrower flag proof
findings.body: Bootstrap evaluator requires ready plus extension found, activation, command registered/executed and storage verified. It does not check exact extension/command identity, signature, source hash, receipt schema or screenshot. Its operationally_complete means bootstrap predicate passed, not the complete product walk.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1703 Bootstrap completion is a narrower flag proof.md

findings.title: Status tests model predicate inputs rather than physical operational evidence
findings.body: completeReceipt has six attempted controls with terminal strings and aggregate counts but no stages/evidence. Focused cases construct booleans and mutate selected failure fields. These test predicate behavior, including exact diagnostic exceptions; they do not execute installed host, verify signatures or independently establish every represented lifecycle.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1704 Status tests model predicate inputs rather than physical operational evidence.md

findings.title: Disposable engine copy is not a consistent full-tree snapshot
findings.body: Copy excludes current coordination locks, evidence/caches and links. Afterwards only runtime/cli.py and registry/engine_identity.json are re-copied and checked with three before/after attempts. Other copied files lack identity comparison or two matching whole-tree snapshots. Counters describe initial enumeration and can differ after the re-copy.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1705 Disposable engine copy is not a consistent full-tree snapshot.md

findings.title: Copy and fixture path checks leave pathname intervals
findings.body: Engine source/root lstat then realpath checks reject root links; cp filter checks child entries at enumeration time. Later copy/read/removal occurs by path, allowing changes after checks. Some fixture helpers realpath first then lstat the resolved result, which does not reject a linked caller-supplied root, and lexical inside does not inspect every ancestor.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1706 Copy and fixture path checks leave pathname intervals.md

findings.title: Loopback port readiness is not process identity
findings.body: reserveLoopbackPort listens on port zero then closes before VS Code starts, leaving a reuse race. probeCdp accepts HTTP200 and any truthy webSocketDebuggerUrl without matching expected host/PID/port. Its 1-second timeout is socket inactivity, not an overall response deadline; an ongoing body is sliced to 16KiB while waiting for end.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1707 Loopback port readiness is not process identity.md

findings.title: Storage isolation is inferred from chunk-local stdout text
findings.body: storageBoundaryObserver recognizes shared-storage database paths only within each stdout chunk and accumulates paths without a cap. Split log text can be missed; classified paths are lexical rather than physical. Recognized in-memory or owned path plus no observed external path becomes verified, not an independent inspection of all host storage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1708 Storage isolation is inferred from chunk-local stdout text.md

findings.title: Proxy flags and denial sentinels are not network containment
findings.body: Launch environment sets HTTP(S) proxies to dead loopback and NO_PROXY loopback after billing-key filtering. Sentinel checks only uppercase proxy strings; clients can ignore proxy environment or use other protocols. Native helper and runtime fixture invocations use nonBillableEnvironment rather than the same proxy wrapper. No network attempt was made by this audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1709 Proxy flags and denial sentinels are not network containment.md

findings.title: Selected Python is not used by every child
findings.body: resolveOwnedPython accepts arbitrary requested string or a plain certification executable before system fallback. VS Code and walker receive config.pythonPath, but native helper always spawns python and runtime fixture command chooses system python/python3. Existence is not dependency/version/digest verification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1710 Selected Python is not used by every child.md

findings.title: Installed VSIX hash check proves archive stability during install only
findings.body: Child hashes VSIX before install against prepared digest, invokes native CLI with a 120-second bound and English success substring, then rehashes archive. It does not independently compare all installed bytes here. Ordinary source mode runs live extensionRoot while engine is a prior copy, so separate source identity checks are necessary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1711 Installed VSIX hash check proves archive stability during install only.md

findings.title: Ordinary operational host and bootstrap host follow separate activation routes
findings.body: Bootstrap-only supplies extensionTestsPath and waits for ready JSON/registered/executed flags. Ordinary host records deferred-to-operational-walker and relies on walker to open dashboard. It waits for CDP and recognized storage first. Native profiles require Windows/cached executable and receive native secret/root/PID; other modes may download pinned host.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1712 Ordinary operational host and bootstrap host follow separate activation routes.md

findings.title: Local host waits rely partly on the outer owner deadline
findings.body: Initial cache/download and walker exit have no child-local total timeout; outer worker is thirty minutes or explicitly one hour. JSON receipt wait reads existing file before checking host exit and has no size/link/atomic-read guard. No correlation schema is required by generic waitForJsonFile itself.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1713 Local host waits rely partly on the outer owner deadline.md

findings.title: Sequential child finalization can prevent later cleanup
findings.body: Finally writes sentinel, terminates walker, writes progress, requests native stop, awaits/races helper, terminates VS Code then publishes result. Some awaited termination/progress/receipt writes are not independently caught; an early failure can skip later cleanup and child-result. Parent timeout/process owner may still reconcile independently.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1714 Sequential child finalization can prevent later cleanup.md

findings.title: Natural walker exit is recorded as termination verification
findings.body: After waitForExit the child sets walker_termination_verified=true without descendant verification in that branch. Helper natural exit considers no signal termination verified even when nonzero; it adds separate failure string later, which normalizer drops. Full parent process-tree proof is a different owner and must not be conflated.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1715 Natural walker exit is recorded as termination verification.md

findings.title: Walk cleanup marker and retry boundaries are partial
findings.body: Cleanup requires supplied tree closure, direct os.tmpdir child with fixed prefix, root not symlink and marker owner/classification. Marker itself is not checked for symlink, schema, session/PID binding or retention obligations. Retry loop does not recheck root identity, and caller options attempts/delay are Number-converted without finite upper bounds. No cleanup was executed in this audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1716 Walk cleanup marker and retry boundaries are partial.md

findings.title: Owned acquisition fallback can remove a custom root without the normal gate
findings.body: acquireWalkOwnership obtains lease before temporary allocation, a useful duplicate-owner boundary. If marking a custom makeTemporaryRoot result fails, catch directly rmSync recursively on that returned path rather than using safeOwnedEphemeralCleanup. Default allocation is mkdtemp; custom injection can widen this fallback target. Lease release follows best-effort removal.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1717 Owned acquisition fallback can remove a custom root without the normal gate.md

findings.title: Post-worker failures can bypass cleanup and final receipt
findings.body: After runOwnedHostWorker returns/releases its lease, owner reads child/fixture JSON and hashes source without an encompassing finally. Parse/hash failures occur before settleOwnedEphemeralCleanup. Successful cleanup removes temp root before final wx report write, so a report collision can lose the child evidence kept only there. Final worker assertion also occurs after report publication.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1718 Post-worker failures can bypass cleanup and final receipt.md

findings.title: Evidence output scope is lexical and prior walk output may be reused
findings.body: main checks repository-relative paths and refuses existing reportPath, but does not require walkOutput absent or check every ancestor for links. prepare recursively creates output, progress appends and walker receipt overwrites its fixed name. Existing output can mix prior progress/artifacts with new run; exact timestamp/ownership correlation is not enforced here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1719 Evidence output scope is lexical and prior walk output may be reused.md

findings.title: Final source labels are sampled after the host run
findings.body: Final report hashes live extension entry, walker, bootstrap and VSIX after child execution. These are not compared with initial copies/loaded bytes in this report builder. Required engine file digests describe earlier staging. Source mutation during execution can mix evidence generations unless separate identity consumers reject it.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1720 Final source labels are sampled after the host run.md

findings.title: Fixture construction changes multiple authorities before a complete receipt
findings.body: Knowledge fixture creates workspace directories/files then validates/writes engine registry. Host-boundary fixture writes coordination plan, initializes workspace/project, activates, ingests and transitions up to 64 memory IDs twice before provider policy change. Failure late leaves earlier disposable changes; no transactional rollback exists inside these helper functions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1721 Fixture construction changes multiple authorities before a complete receipt.md

findings.title: Fixture memory certification and provider readiness are scoped assertions
findings.body: Runtime fixture helper checks valid/applied flags for transitions with literal evidence labels, then reports lifecycle certified. Provider fixture copies an enabled Ollama budget and adds zero-charge deny-unknown row. This prepares a fixture rather than proving independent research, billing behavior, model availability or production canonical quality.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1722 Fixture memory certification and provider readiness are scoped assertions.md

findings.title: Progress retention has a read/hash interval and no lifecycle chain
findings.body: Readers cap file size and validate schemas/states but then hash by a separate file read, not the parsed bytes. Profile reader accepts empty input and checks no profile start/end pairing, timestamps or owner; last record is copied without field sanitization. Host writer whitelists pid/ready_after_ms but appends by path without rejecting a linked existing target.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1723 Progress retention has a read/hash interval and no lifecycle chain.md

findings.title: Focused lane isolation is an explicit alternate lease key
findings.body: main rejects multiple focused modes and restricts post-audit long-running to full. A validated lane name with any focused profile selects a separate temp lock rather than global host lock; same profile can run in distinct lanes. Root/fixture separation is still required; lane string alone does not prove independent scopes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1724 Focused lane isolation is an explicit alternate lease key.md

findings.title: Isolated launcher tests mix real narrow fixtures with source regex contracts
findings.body: Tests physically copy small trees, hash source fixtures, exercise lease collision and prelaunch failure, and open a loopback test server. Many profile/native/network guarantees are assertions that source contains specific strings. Canonical memory runtimeCommand is mocked to return valid/applied, so that test proves call order and local fixture bytes rather than backend certification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1725 Isolated launcher tests mix real narrow fixtures with source regex contracts.md

findings.title: Cache subprocess test isolation is platform-dependent and unbounded
findings.body: runIsolatedCacheOwner changes TEMP/TMP but not HOME/cache override; cache owner uses home-based root on Linux. Its subprocess has no timeout or nonbilling environment filtering. The test writes fixed cache-layout fixtures and removes a temp directory afterwards; it is not evidence of universally isolated cache behavior.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1726 Cache subprocess test isolation is platform-dependent and unbounded.md

findings.title: Storage and native finalizer tests leave operational gaps
findings.body: Storage tests toggle in-memory flags rather than parsing split real output; native finalizer test checks source regex and waits one millisecond. They do not exercise helper exit errors passing through status normalization or failures interrupting sequential cleanup. Those gaps were found by caller review and pure status probes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1727 Storage and native finalizer tests leave operational gaps.md

findings.title: Source manifest does not close complete loaded-byte identity
findings.body: currentSourceManifest hashes only source_refs declared by the matrix, before browser work. It rejects outside lexical paths and leaf links, but does not reject linked ancestors or bind all preview/controller/harness assets. There is no final source equality check. sourcePath splits the first colon, so Windows absolute references are not supported.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1728 Source manifest does not close complete loaded-byte identity.md

findings.title: Equal matrix digest bypasses changed source and chain verification
findings.body: resumeReceiptCompatible returns after checking record count and ordered control IDs when matrix_sha256 matches. It does not compare current source manifest or check surface, kind, evidence mode, interaction chain or operational boolean on that branch. Pure exported probe accepted changed source with an absent chain.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1729 Equal matrix digest bypasses changed source and chain verification.md

findings.title: Metadata-change resume validates policy parity rather than evidence truth
findings.body: The slower branch compares manifests and exact record identity plus thirteen stage keys and not-applicable parity. It does not recompute operational, require legal states for required stages, verify evidence references, dates or error types. Copied records retain prior assertions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1730 Metadata-change resume validates policy parity rather than evidence truth.md

findings.title: Default resume leaves incomplete error-free controls untouched
findings.body: Without a pattern, resume selects only rows whose errors have length. A row with missing stages, operational=false and errors=[] is never rerun. This is confirmed by exact filter reproduction. A pattern may select only part of inherited evidence.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1731 Default resume leaves incomplete error-free controls untouched.md

findings.title: Predecessor digest may describe later bytes than parsed receipt
findings.body: Resume JSON is read before browser launch and the predecessor path is read again for its digest after browser work. Concurrent changes can make the retained records and predecessor_sha256 disagree. Neither read bounds size or rejects a linked path.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1732 Predecessor digest may describe later bytes than parsed receipt.md

findings.title: Control selectors can alias distinct indicators
findings.body: Multiple indicators resolve to the same metric card, provider container, cleanup summary or graph-state element. Direct resolution proves the first selector match is visible, without validating the requested state/value. Semantic fallback ranks substrings; the token id matches invalid with score one.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1733 Control selectors can alias distinct indicators.md

findings.title: Row variant is not an exact repeated-row identity
findings.body: variantsMatch accepts row if any dataset key contains id, index, row or key; even invalid is accepted. Other variants may match any dataset value or visual context. resolveAction returns first compatible item without uniqueness or target-row verification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1734 Row variant is not an exact repeated-row identity.md

findings.title: Preview fixtures are declared inputs rather than host observations
findings.body: prepare injects loading/error/catalog/project/plugin/runtime/task/Studio states using window.eval and synthetic MessageEvents. Sidebar fixture includes connected execution/provider billing state. The receipt correctly limits authority to contained browser evidence; maps must preserve that boundary.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1735 Preview fixtures are declared inputs rather than host observations.md

findings.title: Preparation reuse can mix state across semantic controls
findings.body: preparationKey isolates a selected regex of state-bound IDs; other field/editor/indicator controls reuse a surface. Mutating input handlers, local drafts and uncaught restoration differences can influence subsequent controls. revealControl false does not prevent exercise; it only contributes to resetting the cache.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1736 Preparation reuse can mix state across semantic controls.md

findings.title: Prerequisite setup uses direct DOM actions and synthetic authority previews
findings.body: Studio prerequisites call element.click with no visibility check and choose first matching dataset; graph endpoint pairs are selected by type text. Plugin preview grants/tokens and environment exact-target acknowledgements are fixture-generated. These make controls reachable without verifying native authority.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1737 Prerequisite setup uses direct DOM actions and synthetic authority previews.md

findings.title: Action validation credit follows successful click dispatch
findings.body: exercise sets validationObserved=true after click and a fixed delay, without testing invalid input or reading a validation result. contained_ui_interaction acknowledgement is unconditional after that; other modes only require outbound message count growth, not a correlated accepted response.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1738 Action validation credit follows successful click dispatch.md

findings.title: Field restoration does not prove logical state rollback
findings.body: Fields are edited and reset, then attempted is promoted to validation and acknowledgement. No post-value or model-state comparison is performed. If an earlier edit or restoration throws, only disclosure-open state is in finally, so earlier changes may remain.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1739 Field restoration does not prove logical state rollback.md

findings.title: Absent numeric bounds are converted to zero
findings.body: Number(await getAttribute(min/max)) converts null to zero. For ordinary number inputs without attributes, alternate selection may fail to exercise the field despite a valid editable control. The harness needs explicit missing-bound semantics.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1740 Absent numeric bounds are converted to zero.md

findings.title: Form failure test validates browser custom validity rather than product rejection
findings.body: The first visible editable field is changed/restored, then setCustomValidity injects a temporary failure and clears it. This verifies local browser validity and field value, not the product validator, persistence or runtime recovery. Re-rendering may leave the captured field detached from current DOM/model.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1741 Form failure test validates browser custom validity rather than product rejection.md

findings.title: Form restoration can disturb coupled controls and derived state
findings.body: Checkbox/radio assignment, select changes and input events may alter other fields, derived draft state or retained working history. Only the chosen field object and validity flags are compared. Event-triggered dispatch is not counted, yet host stages are declared not applicable.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1742 Form restoration can disturb coupled controls and derived state.md

findings.title: Unknown stage policy fails open to not applicable
findings.body: Only the literal required makes a stage required. Missing, misspelled or unsupported policy values produce not_applicable rather than rejecting malformed matrix. completeChain accepts those states. Main parses JSON without a schema validation call.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1743 Unknown stage policy fails open to not applicable.md

findings.title: Contained form policy overrides explicitly required host stages
findings.body: stageResult sets authorization, backend_dispatch and runtime_effect not_applicable whenever evidence_mode is contained_ui_form, even if stage_policy requires them and probe is not attempted. A pure predicate probe confirms the override; this is a local interaction scope decision, not full control coverage.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1744 Contained form policy overrides explicitly required host stages.md

findings.title: Visible error-named indicator receives failure credit without error content
findings.body: Failure handling is marked present when an indicator is visible and the control ID/label matches an error word. It need not expose an actual failure value or request identity. Progress reporting similarly follows indicator visibility. The test endorses this predicate.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1745 Visible error-named indicator receives failure credit without error content.md

findings.title: Fallback editor and gesture checks can acknowledge swallowed input errors
findings.body: Generic menu/editor probes catch key/click errors and still set all three attempted/validation/acknowledged flags. Unrecognized non-knowledge graph gesture focuses, catches ArrowRight error and returns true. Drag-existing-workflow-node also returns true without comparing coordinates.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1746 Fallback editor and gesture checks can acknowledge swallowed input errors.md

findings.title: Graph gesture evidence is narrower than named gesture families
findings.body: plusMinus tests plus only and zeroOrHome tests zero only. Arrow focus checks inequality, which can pass if focus leaves nodes. Synthetic wheel/pointer events do not independently prove native input routing. Other graph cases use before/after transform datasets, a useful but bounded observation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1747 Graph gesture evidence is narrower than named gesture families.md

findings.title: Operational boolean and process success use different predicates
findings.body: Per-record operational depends solely on completeChain, ignoring probe.errors. Receipt operationally_complete compares operational count to all records; process exitCode is set only for aggregate errors. Missing controls/chains can therefore leave exit zero, while errors may coexist with operational true.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1748 Operational boolean and process success use different predicates.md

findings.title: Parallel browser preparation failures lose partial receipt publication
findings.body: prepare/reveal failures escape the per-control exercise catch. Promise.all rejects, browser finally closes, but the final receipt write is skipped. No progress receipt/checkpoint is written between controls. Browser launch/newPage and cleanup failures have separate partial-resource windows.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1749 Parallel browser preparation failures lose partial receipt publication.md

findings.title: Output is exclusive but path and read scope are not constrained locally
findings.body: output/resume resolve arbitrary CLI paths; output uses wx after recursive directory creation, protecting existing leaf files but not linked ancestors. Worker count is clamped but not required integer. User regex has no complexity bound; matrix/receipt/source sizes are unbounded in this owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1750 Output is exclusive but path and read scope are not constrained locally.md

findings.title: Exhaustive walker tests mostly certify helper predicates and text
findings.body: Tests assert CSS strings, fixture fields, stage states and source regex. Help is a real bounded subprocess. No test runs the complete browser main, resumes stale same-matrix source, or compares model rollback with DOM restoration. Tests were fully read, not run in this report audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1751 Exhaustive walker tests mostly certify helper predicates and text.md

findings.title: Dashboard end-to-end tests are preview browser tests
findings.body: Every page loads file preview.html and uses fixture messages. Even installed Studio adversarial profile is invoked through page.evaluate on preview. Tests exercise real browser controller behavior but not an installed VS Code host, physical Python effects, canonical persistence or authority verification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1752 Dashboard end-to-end tests are preview browser tests.md

findings.title: Approval correlation tests omit current workflow replacement
findings.body: The two-node approval case tests stale/duplicate request IDs and distinct nodes within one unchanged workflow session. It does not switch workflow/version while a response is pending, leaving the cross-session assignment reproduced in batch96 uncovered.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1753 Approval correlation tests omit current workflow replacement.md

findings.title: Screenshot manifest can include stale evidence from earlier runs
findings.body: writeVisualManifest enumerates every PNG in fixed extension/evidence/screenshots. Two tests overwrite named screenshots and rewrite one manifest without an exact expected set, per-run directory or source digest. Surviving old PNGs acquire the new manifest timestamp/browser label.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1754 Screenshot manifest can include stale evidence from earlier runs.md

findings.title: Visual assertions cover geometry rather than all rendered accessibility
findings.body: Checks assert containment/overlap, finite CSS transforms, target widths, forced-color media and screenshot byte length. They do not perform pixel-baseline comparison, comprehensive contrast/readability or assistive-technology verification. The 720px/DPR2 case is a reflow proxy, not an actual browser zoom setting.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1755 Visual assertions cover geometry rather than all rendered accessibility.md

findings.title: Suspended-frame test accepts render acknowledgement without completed frame work
findings.body: Test replaces requestAnimationFrame with a no-op and waits for a graphRendered message with positive counts/dimensions. It proves the fallback acknowledgement remains live, not that all chunked graph rendering or paint completed. This matches the graph evidence boundary recorded in batch96.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1756 Suspended-frame test accepts render acknowledgement without completed frame work.md

findings.title: Long browser scenario shares state and aborts later checks on first failure
findings.body: The large 300-second test combines eighteen route screenshots, Studio lineage/editing, graph gestures, scopes, memory, environment and seven width sweeps. Assertions are sequential: early failure prevents later coverage and final manifest. Fixed sleeps depend on preview timing; evidence retained before failure may remain for later runs.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1757 Long browser scenario shares state and aborts later checks on first failure.md

findings.title: Draft and lineage tests preserve useful browser-side rejection boundaries
findings.body: Tests reject substituted catalog revision, wrong-family/cross-kind allocation replies, lineage changes through JSON and detached stale save outcomes; they retain overlays and check proof-release requests. Hashes/proofs are fixture values. This is meaningful controller coverage, separate from authenticating host proofs or physical commit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1758 Draft and lineage tests preserve useful browser-side rejection boundaries.md

findings.title: Preview tests intentionally accept uncorrelated knowledge browse fixture
findings.body: Knowledge head test dispatches studioOperationResult browse without requestId to seed malformed head and asserts proposal refusal. It does not assert rejection of obsolete browse responses; the stale cache boundary observed in batch96 remains.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1759 Preview tests intentionally accept uncorrelated knowledge browse fixture.md

findings.title: Responsive route coverage is finite and does not equal all interaction coverage
findings.body: Eighteen route headers/screenshots and selected high-risk actions are checked at one wide viewport; dashboard/graph seven-width sweeps and seven other mobile routes follow. Control matrix membership is not used to derive this test denominator, so the broad test name is not exhaustive control proof.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1760 Responsive route coverage is finite and does not equal all interaction coverage.md

findings.title: Successive incomplete scenarios can merge into a complete installed chain
findings.body: applyInstalledProbeObservations keeps already observed stages and promotes later present stages without a scenario/run identity. Complementary failed scenarios can therefore union into a complete chain although no scenario completed it. The report-only exported predicate probe reproduces this; separate child profile issues mitigate locally but the parent status reconstruction drops those issues.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1761 Successive incomplete scenarios can merge into a complete installed chain.md

findings.title: Later failure does not revoke prior observed stages
findings.body: The merger does not downgrade an existing observed stage when a later record reports missing or failed evidence. A previously complete record remains complete after a total-failure observation. Completion is chosen ahead of error/authority disposition, so retained stage state and latest outcome can disagree.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1762 Later failure does not revoke prior observed stages.md

findings.title: Merged control records lose profile errors and exact evidence custody
findings.body: Input record errors are used for a terminal branch but not copied into the resulting control errors array. Stage records have no enforced source/run/request/time binding and preserve base observation timestamps. Exact thirteen input keys do not authenticate evidence references or the preexisting stage denominator.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1763 Merged control records lose profile errors and exact evidence custody.md

findings.title: Applicability can be widened during installed evidence composition
findings.body: An incoming not-applicable observation can replace a missing stage without rechecking matrix policy. Inline command inheritance fills every required target stage once its source chain is complete, even when the corresponding source stage was not applicable. Inline entrypoints are not physically exercised by this copy.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1764 Applicability can be widened during installed evidence composition.md

findings.title: Builder observation projects shared success onto individual controls
findings.body: Builder attribution sets exact resolver/render/attempt flags from broad draft observations, shares screenshot references across builders and credits stages when a digest exists rather than when it changes. Same-webview resume and shared durability flags are not separate persistence/reload proof for each action.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1765 Builder observation projects shared success onto individual controls.md

findings.title: Raw asset verification is narrower than complete installed-code identity
findings.body: The identity enumerates top-level dashboard/src JavaScript and selected fixed assets, excluding generated host code and missing nested CSS/server deployment code. Host manifest hash difference is explicitly intentional because packaging changes main; it needs complementary generated/installed byte provenance, not raw equality. This predicate alone cannot certify all loaded code.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1766 Raw asset verification is narrower than complete installed-code identity.md

findings.title: Verified installed source is not rebound to final current bytes
findings.body: The local identity is sampled once and cached through refreshes. Only unknown state receives late refresh; verified identity is not rechecked after effectful profiles or against final source bytes. Host matches=true can coexist with mismatch reasons, and protocol strings are not compared to exact supported values.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1767 Verified installed source is not rebound to final current bytes.md

findings.title: Source mismatch is not a universal stop before effectful profiles
findings.body: Main gates initial captures/builders and late checks on mismatch but still schedules project, configuration, Studio, Knowledge, Learning, coordination, cleanup and plugin effects from authority flags. The final limitation text saying mismatch blocks further interaction is broader than the implemented schedule. Unknown identity also permits work.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1768 Source mismatch is not a universal stop before effectful profiles.md

findings.title: Proof-matrix preflight compares counts rather than exact contracts
findings.body: Before effects, main compares only proofMatrix.controls.length and inventory.control_count. Equal-count substituted IDs, policy/evidence modes, duplicate controls or manifest drift are not rejected there. The matrix file is reread for a final digest after effects, which can describe different bytes than the parsed schedule.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1769 Proof-matrix preflight compares counts rather than exact contracts.md

findings.title: Owned-host flags do not themselves prove exact host authority
findings.body: Child authority derives from PX_OWNED_VSCODE_HOST and an argv token prefix plus effect flags. This is not marker/PID/birth/root custody and some prefix checks admit an empty token. The parent and individual helpers have additional checks; their proof cannot be inferred solely from these booleans.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1770 Owned-host flags do not themselves prove exact host authority.md

findings.title: Timeout returns without cancellation or reconciliation of underlying UI work
findings.body: boundedOwnedUiAction and content/locator boundaries use Promise.race. On timeout the original operation may continue mutating browser/product state while restoration or a later profile begins. Reacquisition clears failure latches without joining prior tasks. Tests use never-resolving promises and do not exercise a late completion after reset.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1771 Timeout returns without cancellation or reconciliation of underlying UI work.md

findings.title: Local phase budgets do not guarantee whole-operation elapsed bounds
findings.body: Several helpers start deadlines after navigation or await predicates outside timeout ownership; nested phases receive fresh full budgets. Content handle acquisition occurs before the evaluation timeout. Invalid numeric options are not consistently rejected. A bounded inner wait does not prove aggregate operation duration.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1772 Local phase budgets do not guarantee whole-operation elapsed bounds.md

findings.title: Profile health and prerequisite failure can diverge
findings.body: timedProfile collects errors but generally does not require completed=true or an exact observation denominator. Pre-builder baseline failure is returned and ignored; builder outer catch is usually bypassed because timedProfile swallowed the exception. Studio candidate watchdog can return only an attempted prefix; later candidates never enter its denominator.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1773 Profile health and prerequisite failure can diverge.md

findings.title: Late diagnostics are omitted from earlier fault partitions
findings.body: faultDiagnostics is computed before late identity refresh and worker/controller/bridge profiles. New hostErrors appended later do not enter retained/recovered arrays used by final receipt and late-card completeness input. Initial page listeners also do not cover pages created later.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1774 Late diagnostics are omitted from earlier fault partitions.md

findings.title: Receipt publication precedes owned browser closure and is not atomic
findings.body: Main overwrites the final receipt before viewport detach/browser.close, so closure failure can leave a completed-looking artifact with process exit1. Early failure may leave an older receipt in place. Progress appends to a preexisting path without a new exclusive run envelope. No final cleanup receipt binds released frame/listener ownership.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1775 Receipt publication precedes owned browser closure and is not atomic.md

findings.title: Native fallback accepts operation type without exact request target
findings.body: nativeWorkbenchRequestFallbackAdmitted checks request.type and allowed label/type mapping, not a nonempty request ID, target, current terminal state or authority token. After750ms an observed request can trigger keyboard-only fallback even with no visible native blocker. Pure probe accepted permanent-delete mapping with only type. Physical helper PID checks are separate and do not restore missing effect-target binding.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1776 Native fallback accepts operation type without exact request target.md

findings.title: Native dialog selection can escape exact dialog identity
findings.body: Dialog discovery searches all context pages by text and may fall back to an actionable ancestor or body. Click resolution searches matching labels in dialog and workbench, selecting a visible candidate without uniqueness or exact request-to-dialog identity. Escape cancellation can report success without proving the expected modal was active.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1777 Native dialog selection can escape exact dialog identity.md

findings.title: Palette disappearance can reuse a stale command identity
findings.body: Command selection normalizes visible labels rather than contributed command IDs/publisher. When the palette disappears the decision helper may retain last valid identity and continue Enter dispatch; acceptedPrompt can accept closure without observing that prompt. Focus or tab changes can redirect keyboard effects.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1778 Palette disappearance can reuse a stale command identity.md

findings.title: Harness event interception is weaker than production authority refusal
findings.body: Workbench/sidebar/control/validation failure scenarios inject capture handlers or custom validity, then assert blocked input. This proves the harness can suppress an event or force browser invalidity, not that product policy rejects the unauthorized request at the backend. Maps distinguish synthetic refusal from governed rejection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1779 Harness event interception is weaker than production authority refusal.md

findings.title: Generic control acknowledgement can accept unrelated state change
findings.body: Local acknowledgement follows attempted/restored flags; host acknowledgement can follow any response count increase or body-text change. Conditional recovery matches type/kind/operation without exact request ID or success state. Attempted input broadly yields validation credit, while first/broad/fuzzy selectors can alias controls.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1780 Generic control acknowledgement can accept unrelated state change.md

findings.title: Body-text fingerprints do not cover editor and graph state restoration
findings.body: Editor/gesture probes compare body-text FNV/length, which can remain constant when values, transforms, graph geometry or model state change. Field probes restore captured elements without guaranteed finally or replacement-node/model equality. Numeric suffix editing can become empty while still counted attempted.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1781 Body-text fingerprints do not cover editor and graph state restoration.md

findings.title: Synthetic failures share instrumentation with real host messages
findings.body: Bridge listeners record every message and custom outbound event in the same arrays, including injected operation errors and fixture snapshots. No provenance distinction marks synthetic versus actual host results; arrays are unbounded and listeners are not removed by the instrumentation owner.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1782 Synthetic failures share instrumentation with real host messages.md

findings.title: Frame retry and tab recovery do not prove previous effect closure
findings.body: Cached webview identity does not always recheck outer visibility. Selected frame errors can retry an operation after it already affected state; reacquisition resets latches without closure. Failed tab focus can be caught before Ctrl+W closes the currently active tab. Label/selector/time-origin checks are narrower than exact process custody.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1783 Frame retry and tab recovery do not prove previous effect closure.md

findings.title: Stable samples need valid counts and stable identity
findings.body: Settlement counts consecutive boolean acknowledgements, not the same element or source revision. Required sample count0 or negative can accept unacknowledged state; the report pure probe reproduces zero-sample acceptance. Scope/capability references can also become detached after preparatory clicks.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1784 Stable samples need valid counts and stable identity.md

findings.title: Host action durable naming describes in-memory retention
findings.body: Host result waiters consult current response arrays, controller globals and latest snapshot, matched by request/operation and a lower time bound. Extension state is in memory, not a persisted journal; tests explicitly forbid globalState retention. This can support webview reconstruction while not proving extension-process restart durability.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1785 Host action durable naming describes in-memory retention.md

findings.title: Configuration acknowledgements have weaker branches than host-action receipts
findings.body: Enterprise response matching uses operation and Boolean(master_enabled), not exact request/status, allowing absent state to resemble disabled. Approval may return a read acknowledgement before final disposition validation. Fault marker errors are operation-matched rather than request-bound and the config marker differs from the consumed host-action marker.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1786 Configuration acknowledgements have weaker branches than host-action receipts.md

findings.title: Host prerequisite failure can lose its restoration record
findings.body: Preparation makes changes before returning the scenario, so throwing during preparation can leave the caller without baseline state. A repeated preparation result is discarded. Activity settings restore writes original bytes without intermediate compare-and-swap and may overwrite concurrent edits; root/link ownership is not fully established here.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1787 Host prerequisite failure can lose its restoration record.md

findings.title: Canonical memory normalization can precede reliable predecessor capture
findings.body: Attached state is disconnected before its previous root is fully validated. On failure, an already attached state may be marked restored without comparing root; failure before baseline capture leaves a false detached default and may disconnect a preexisting attachment. Restoration checks selected UI/target fields rather than exact registry state.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1788 Canonical memory normalization can precede reliable predecessor capture.md

findings.title: Setup and candidate evidence are attributed beyond exact exercised controls
findings.body: Setup has useful exact request-to-terminal matching, but one agents setup action and generic positive counts credit multiple controls/indicators. Candidate invalid-identity fallback uses harness customValidity if product validation does not reject it. Typed receipt checks verify identity/version/hash shape, not persisted artifact hash equality.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1789 Setup and candidate evidence are attributed beyond exact exercised controls.md

findings.title: Revision preservation does not compare pre-save predecessor hashes
findings.body: predecessor_preserved checks original owner and hash shape in the predecessor read after save. It never compares those hashes with pre-save allocation/source/candidate hashes. Changed predecessor content can therefore satisfy preserved if selected owner remains. Reopened editor comparison checks owner/identity/version, not complete saved content bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1790 Revision preservation does not compare pre-save predecessor hashes.md

findings.title: Revision stale-response and conflict fixtures omit complete predecessor restoration
findings.body: Skill stale_result_rejected is preset, while agent/workflow cases inject malformed unmatched allocation responses. Conflict/fork scenarios assign globals and synthetic hashes then clear selected request state; no full original draft/proof/catalog restoration or valid late concurrent response is demonstrated.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1791 Revision stale-response and conflict fixtures omit complete predecessor restoration.md

findings.title: Lifecycle result predicates omit expected run and revision identity
findings.body: Many predicates accept operation schema/status and any run ID. Pause/cancel/stop durable-run receipts need no expected terminal state; rollback accepts a rolled-back object. Pure probe accepted another run with failed state for pause. Later status waiting adds checks but earlier operation.valid remains true after subsequent failure.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1792 Lifecycle result predicates omit expected run and revision identity.md

findings.title: Lifecycle stage attribution can survive failed sequencing
findings.body: The builder credits all required stages from one valid same-operation observation or shared invalid-transition flag; missing action is treated as rejected transition. Run-control selectors omit exact run/kind, and the profile has no universal finally to stop/release unfinished work. Per-kind merge can replace prior identity observations.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1793 Lifecycle stage attribution can survive failed sequencing.md

findings.title: Learning effectiveness evidence is supplied by the fixture
findings.body: The installed Learning profile hashes deterministic labels, supplies six challenger wins, an independent:true reference and12/12 reuse outcomes. These are valid UI state-machine inputs, not independently retained observation artifacts or measured causal improvement. Shared completion credits fields/actions not individually exercised.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1794 Learning effectiveness evidence is supplied by the fixture.md

findings.title: Knowledge and coordination waiters are not uniformly request-bound
findings.body: Knowledge operations/browse and coordination results often match type/kind/operation after an offset. Browse may precede the mutation and another same-operation result may match. Selected proposal/head/hash and task/confirmed checks are useful but do not establish all request/state ordering or full durable content.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1795 Knowledge and coordination waiters are not uniformly request-bound.md

findings.title: Coordination and Codex error exits can leave partial durable state
findings.body: Plans, task claims, memory and context are created; claim release and normal restoration occur on the success path without a universal failure finally. Context tab text or cleared receipt does not independently establish saved-context absence. Shared flags credit many fields and entrypoints beyond their individual actions.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1796 Coordination and Codex error exits can leave partial durable state.md

findings.title: Query and pagination restoration resets defaults rather than the predecessor
findings.body: Catalog restoration writes blank query/status, label sort and limit50 without capturing original filters. Returned offsets do not verify complete item order, overlap or total identity coverage. Hydration accepts string ID/hash without comparing exact selected ID and recomputed body bytes. Error paths may leave state changed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1797 Query and pagination restoration resets defaults rather than the predecessor.md

findings.title: Conditional input scenarios may exercise invented operating conditions
findings.body: Local select probes inject an alternate option if none exists; invalid value rejection is native select behavior. Memory pagination sets memoryOffset=-59 to align a fixed60-step UI with a one-item query. Other cases seed project rows, zero-hash learning history and literal failure/recovery flags. They are renderer fixtures, not authoritative production scenarios.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1798 Conditional input scenarios may exercise invented operating conditions.md

findings.title: Temporary observation fixtures lack complete failure restoration
findings.body: Several branches clear preexisting working drafts, assign snapshot/catalog/pending state and restore only marker absence or one field on success. Exceptions can bypass restore; select finally may reset DOM value without dispatching model restoration. Later errors can leave completed flags true.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1799 Temporary observation fixtures lack complete failure restoration.md

findings.title: Graph identity ignores labels weights and rendered attributes
findings.body: graphProjectionIdentity hashes sorted node keys and edge source/relation/target triples. Labels, node/edge weights, other attributes and layout are excluded, while empty graphs/duplicate IDs and inconsistent total counts are not fully rejected. Pure probe changed labels and weights without changing identity. This matters directly to the requested weighted navigable map.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1800 Graph identity ignores labels weights and rendered attributes.md

findings.title: Saved-view restart proof does not bind all saved presentation state
findings.body: Graph profile resets baseline rather than preserving prior filters/layout. Restart compares a reduced graph identity and saved-view name, not every normalized preset field. Delete restoration checks current memory/DOM absence without another storage reconstruction; failure can leave the view and baseline altered.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1801 Saved-view restart proof does not bind all saved presentation state.md

findings.title: Request-bound system snapshot helper has no request identifier binding
findings.body: requestBoundSystemSnapshotIdentity verifies refresh/snapshot types and a projection tuple, but does not compare request IDs. Empty map, extension and campaign identity fields can pass the tuple. Pure probe accepted an unrelated snapshot request; test explicitly uses no request ID.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1802 Request-bound system snapshot helper has no request identifier binding.md

findings.title: Snapshot selection can return older matching state after a newer contradiction
findings.body: selectLatestMatchingInstalledSnapshot retains the latest predicate match separately from latest observed snapshot. If a newer snapshot fails the predicate, it still returns the earlier match and callers may accept it. Pure probe shows revision1 success selected after revision2 failure. Existing test covers only stale-then-good ordering.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1803 Snapshot selection can return older matching state after a newer contradiction.md

findings.title: Project reconstruction equality is selected metadata rather than graph content
findings.body: Project identity compares path, revision, inventory digest and counts, not graph bytes or validation/errors. Build result acceptance is broadly truthy. Initialization cancellation from one entry is shared across two attempted controls; a common build result contributes across multiple entrypoints.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1804 Project reconstruction equality is selected metadata rather than graph content.md

findings.title: Sidebar bounded journals use length offsets that stop advancing at capacity
findings.body: Full snapshots are capped at20 and outbound requests at80, but subsequent scenario waits use previous array length and slice offsets or require length growth. At capacity new entries cannot increase length, so new evidence is missed or recovery times out. Synthetic snapshots also enter the same host journal.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1805 Sidebar bounded journals use length offsets that stop advancing at capacity.md

findings.title: Sidebar restoration and reconstruction cover selected state only
findings.body: Preference identity binds wave/expanded plus integer revision without freshness. Stable reconstruction intentionally excludes volatile task progress, and conditional completion can be true despite failed conditional flags. Error finally restores outage/sidebar visibility but not all wave/task preferences or original projection.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1806 Sidebar restoration and reconstruction cover selected state only.md

findings.title: Cleanup receipt accepts claimed reclamation with an empty resource list
findings.body: validCleanupResult requires reclaimed count but uses resources.every, which passes for an empty array. It does not bind each resource to the exact selected fixture/source digest or rehash quarantine destination. The report pure probe accepted one reclaimed resource with resources=[]. Inventory absence after restart is not restored destination custody.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1807 Cleanup receipt accepts claimed reclamation with an empty resource list.md

findings.title: Cleanup preexistence rejection can still recursively remove existing fixture parents
findings.body: runInstalledCleanupProfile rejects preexisting fixed fixture paths but its finally recursively removes both fixture parents whenever present. It has no created-this-run guard, so rejection itself can lead to deletion of preexisting contents. This was source-reviewed only; no cleanup was executed.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1808 Cleanup preexistence rejection can still recursively remove existing fixture parents.md

findings.title: Environment fixture preexistence rejection still reaches recursive cleanup
findings.body: The environment lifecycle finally removes its target even when an initial exists check rejected that target. The temporary_registered flag is literal, not a checked ownership receipt. Restored marker/path and inventory observations do not themselves prove equal snapshots, exact tree restoration or failed quarantine reconciliation.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1809 Environment fixture preexistence rejection still reaches recursive cleanup.md

findings.title: Enterprise team fixture cleanup lacks exact creation custody
findings.body: Fixed team fixture preexistence is rejected, but finally removes an existing in-root fixture regardless of creation ownership. A staged path supplied by a result is accepted if within workspace/existing, not bound to an exact owned candidate. Target configuration uses hardcoded values without full baseline restoration; nonnull toggle result is weaker than exact state equality.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1810 Enterprise team fixture cleanup lacks exact creation custody.md

findings.title: Plugin pending receipt plus visible version is not terminal durable custody
findings.body: Mutation can accept a pending-host-reload receipt and mark physically reconciled after workbench restart/version observation. No new terminal journal/tree receipt is required by that path. Current-version polling may reuse a cached result, and most execution waiters omit request ID despite stronger preview binding.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1811 Plugin pending receipt plus visible version is not terminal durable custody.md

findings.title: Plugin failure cleanup can uninstall a preexisting fixture
findings.body: The initial absent check happens after manager entry actions. If it fails because fixture v1/v2 already exists, catch may uninstall that version as failure cleanup without a created-by-this-run marker. Final absent inventory also leaves retained rollback custody, so it is not complete initial state restoration.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1812 Plugin failure cleanup can uninstall a preexisting fixture.md

findings.title: Plugin source and manager denominators have incomplete custody
findings.body: Fixture VSIX bytes are checked against receipt SHA/size, a useful boundary, but receipt schema/provenance and path ancestor containment are not fully admitted before reads. Four manager entry IDs receive shared evidence after at least two positional actions. Physical version scan ignores malformed manifests/duplicates and does not bind complete installed tree bytes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1813 Plugin source and manager denominators have incomplete custody.md

findings.title: Exact preview confirmation is a strong local boundary with separate downstream obligations
findings.body: Plugin confirmation binds preview request ID, token, exact target, enabled visible modal and rechecks control identity at click. Tests exercise stale/substituted and transient replacement cases with fake DOM. This proves the local selection contract; native focus, execution request, installed bytes and durable custody remain separate and must not inherit that proof automatically.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1814 Exact preview confirmation is a strong local boundary with separate downstream obligations.md

findings.title: Validation profile ordering is not bound to the registered campaign oracle
findings.body: Actual validation requires two independent environment flags, but no local processing-order check precedes it. Main invokes it before later graph, cleanup, plugin, outage and late adversarial work. One shared validation result credits both UI entrypoints; source regex counting one click does not prove global single-owner campaign sequence. Backend enforcement must be checked separately.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1815 Validation profile ordering is not bound to the registered campaign oracle.md

findings.title: Expected-fault filtering assumes historical marketplace and cancellation state
findings.body: Console classification suppresses a hardcoded PX marketplace404 as unpublished although user says extension is published/verified. Other text-based network/config classifications are broad. Native recovery requires three project cancellation keys while the current profile includes initialization keys too, creating a stale denominator. These are classifier assumptions, not independently attributed causes.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1816 Expected-fault filtering assumes historical marketplace and cancellation state.md

findings.title: Late-card closure uses fixed historical artifacts rather than current findings
findings.body: all_report_findings_reconciled reads specific August closure/findings files without binding the current atlas denominator/hash. Empty repair disposition can pass a negative regex; implemented_pending_remote_os_execution is accepted. post_repair_incompleteness_audit derives from prior booleans and host errors rather than a new independent audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1817 Late-card closure uses fixed historical artifacts rather than current findings.md

findings.title: Worker envelope validation is weaker than physical worker evidence
findings.body: Crash/late worker wrappers accept status/schema/hash-shaped summaries without rehashing canonical outputs or requiring complete nonempty recovery actions. Missing engine root resolves to cwd, defeating empty-root check. Late worker errors can be normalized away. Independently reviewed worker internals provide evidence only for their exact scope.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1818 Worker envelope validation is weaker than physical worker evidence.md

findings.title: Bridge conflict helper counts fixture invocations rather than mutation retries
findings.body: Two child commands emit an error envelope with exits2 and1. no_mutation_retry is inferred from attempts==2 across those fixture calls, not from exercising a mutating operation retry path. request_bound_reason checks text rather than exact original request custody. Keep its claim limited to exit classification.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1819 Bridge conflict helper counts fixture invocations rather than mutation retries.md

findings.title: Late controller adversarial fixture restores only selected globals
findings.body: Synthetic proofs/hashes and MessageEvents exercise stale/cross-kind/detached save handling. Saved globals are partly references, and final closeModal after restoration can consume restored state. Catalog/request arrays, detached maps and all proof/presentation state are not fully restored. Object.values(checks).every lacks a separately enforced expected check denominator at this producer.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1820 Late controller adversarial fixture restores only selected globals.md

findings.title: Test names exceed the behavioral scope of many installed assertions
findings.body: The4277-line suite includes useful pure predicate, callback DOM, exact plugin substitution and spawned worker cases. Many claims about ordering, restoration, authority, source gating and exact denominators merely search source text. Reducer tests apply one probe only; timeout tests never resolve old work after reset; no product tests were run by this report audit.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1821 Test names exceed the behavioral scope of many installed assertions.md

findings.title: Bundle identity lacks a retained complete producer-input receipt
findings.body: build-mcp uses no sourcemap/metafile, strips legal comments and writes one bundle. Existing check mode would compare fresh build bytes, but has not run during this audit because campaign order forbids speculative build reconciliation. Report partition and normalized AST prove narrower correspondence only.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1822 Bundle identity lacks a retained complete producer-input receipt.md

findings.title: Generated source correspondence does not preserve module-relative worker locations
findings.body: Bundled exported inventoryTeamPackAsync and scanEnvironmentAsync still use __dirname plus worker filenames. In server/index.js that resolves under server; both physical worker files are under src. Current registered routes call synchronous inventory and stored reads, so no current tool failure is asserted. The dormant helper contract must be resolved before route reuse.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1823 Generated source correspondence does not preserve module-relative worker locations.md

findings.title: SDK cancellation signal is discarded before PX handler execution
findings.body: executeToolHandler invokes executor(args,ctx), but mcpActivityIntegration returns async(input) and calls handler(effectiveInput). ctx.mcpReq.signal and exact transport request identity never reach PX handlers. Synchronous spawnSync can also block receipt of cancellation; SDK aborted replies do not roll back already executed effects.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1824 SDK cancellation signal is discarded before PX handler execution.md

findings.title: Cancellation with valid numeric request ID zero is ignored
findings.body: The wire RequestIdSchema accepts integer IDs, but Protocol._oncancel returns on falsy requestId. The extracted-method pure report probe shows ID0 yields no abort while1 and a string abort their fake controllers. This is a bundled dependency behavior, not a whole SDK operational test.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1825 Cancellation with valid numeric request ID zero is ignored.md

findings.title: Inbound request concurrency is not bounded by the raw stdio buffer
findings.body: ReadBuffer limits raw accumulated bytes to10MiB. Decoded messages enter an unbounded queue, and _onrequest schedules handler promises without a configured global in-flight bound. Async callbacks can overlap and parsed request memory can outlive the byte buffer. Synchronous PX handlers add event-loop blocking instead of cooperative admission.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1826 Inbound request concurrency is not bounded by the raw stdio buffer.md

findings.title: Duplicate request IDs replace cancellation controller ownership
findings.body: _onrequest stores a new controller at request.id without rejecting an existing active entry. A duplicate ID displaces cancellation ownership for the prior handler; finally protects against deleting the replacement but does not prevent the duplicate effects. No duplicate-ID operational proof was run.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1827 Duplicate request IDs replace cancellation controller ownership.md

findings.title: Stdout backpressure and close have no aggregate deadline
findings.body: StdioServerTransport.send waits for drain/error after a false write result without a timeout. closeAll awaits subscription writes, product.close and wire.close without an aggregate bound. Application shutdown ownership cannot be inferred from a bounded inbound frame size or3-second probe-answer wait.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1828 Stdout backpressure and close have no aggregate deadline.md

findings.title: PX does not retain the serving handle or integrate application shutdown
findings.body: The final serveStdio call discards its close handle and supplies only onerror. Stdio transport attaches data/error callbacks, not stdin end/close callbacks in this implementation. No source-level application hook reconciles PX effects on EOF/signal here; generic SDK closure only aborts cooperative handlers.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1829 PX does not retain the serving handle or integrate application shutdown.md

findings.title: Domain result validity is not supplied by MCP input schemas
findings.body: The SDK validates output only when outputSchema exists. PX registers strict input schemas but no output schemas, and wraps arbitrary values into structuredContent. A normal unavailable/failure object can be logged as completed/success by instrumentation because it did not throw. Wire result shape and domain success are different contracts.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1830 Domain result validity is not supplied by MCP input schemas.md

findings.title: Malformed JSON lines can be discarded without a parse-error receipt
findings.body: ReadBuffer catches SyntaxError from JSON.parse and continues to the next line. Schema-invalid messages reach transport.onerror, but syntax-invalid lines disappear at this boundary. Diagnosis and client retry must not assume every rejected request generates a typed error response.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1831 Malformed JSON lines can be discarded without a parse-error receipt.md

findings.title: Protocol fallback can instantiate PX authority and instrumentation twice
findings.body: A modern discover probe creates a server, and a later legacy opener discards it and constructs another. Factory buildServer recreates authority/instrumentation state. The SDK waits for answered probe requests but does not prove application-owned resource disposal beyond product.close. This matters to future factory side effects and registration ownership.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1832 Protocol fallback can instantiate PX authority and instrumentation twice.md

findings.title: Embedded dependency origins are not fully described by direct dependency names
findings.body: Bundle has80 Zod regions, MCP core types, protocol/stdio implementation and an SDK AJV chunk containing validator engines and format support. Lock lists SDK/core/Zod versions but AJV is embedded upstream. Origin accounting and retained dependency notices need to describe these shipped contents rather than treating all4383 functions as PX-authored.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1833 Embedded dependency origins are not fully described by direct dependency names.md

findings.title: Packaged dependency notice custody is missing from the reviewed inputs
findings.body: MCP build strips legal comments. Custom VSIX packaging copies root LICENSE/NOTICE and selected directories, while root NOTICE describes branding only; SDK/core/Zod license files remain in node_modules, which is excluded. This is a source-observed release-documentation gap for review, not a legal opinion or a claim about a remotely published artifact.
findings.note: 05 Findings/D1834 Packaged dependency notice custody is missing from the reviewed inputs.md
